title: Greenland
tagline: It's the end of the world as we know it.
overview: John Garrity, his estranged wife and their young son embark on a perilous journey to find sanctuary as a planet-killing comet hurtles toward Earth. Amid terrifying accounts of cities getting levelled, the Garritys experience the best and worst in humanity. As the countdown to the global apocalypse approaches zero, their incredible trek culminates in a desperate and last-minute flight to a possible safe haven.
plot:
Greenland is a 2020 American post-apocalyptic disaster film directed by Ric Roman Waugh and written by Chris Bremner. The movie stars Gerard Butler, Morena Baccarin, Roger Dale Floyd, and Sienna Campbell.

The story begins with a family - John (Gerard Butler), his wife Allison (Morena Baccarin), and their 11-year-old son Caleb (Sienna Campbell) - living in Greenland with their young daughter. The family is preparing for the annual summer solstice celebration when they receive an alert from NASA about a massive asteroid hurtling towards Earth.

The asteroid, which is approximately 5 miles in diameter, is predicted to impact Earth and cause catastrophic destruction. The government has only 6 months to prepare for the impending disaster, but it's clear that this will not be enough time.

As the family tries to come to terms with their situation, they realize that they are one of the few families who have managed to escape the initial blast of the asteroid. They soon discover that the impact has caused widespread destruction and chaos around the world, with many cities being reduced to rubble.

The family sets out on a perilous journey across Greenland in search of safety and hope. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, harsh weather conditions, and other survivors who are not as trustworthy as they seem.

As the days turn into weeks, the family faces numerous challenges, including finding food and shelter, navigating through the treacherous landscape, and dealing with the emotional toll of their situation. They also encounter a group of survivors who are determined to take control of the remaining resources in Greenland.

Throughout the movie, the family's relationship is put to the test as they struggle to work together and make difficult decisions that will determine their survival. John, who has been struggling with feelings of guilt and inadequacy, must come to terms with his role as a father and leader.

As the asteroid hurtles towards Earth, the family faces an impossible decision: stay in Greenland and risk being crushed by the impact, or try to find a way to escape the planet. In the end, they make a desperate bid for survival, using their skills and ingenuity to launch themselves into space on a makeshift rocket.

The movie ends with John and Caleb floating above the Earth, watching as the asteroid impacts the planet below them. The family's fate is left uncertain, leaving the audience to wonder if they will survive or succumb to the harsh conditions of space.

Overall, Greenland is a tense and suspenseful thriller that explores themes of survival, hope, and redemption in the face of catastrophic disaster.

title: The Intruder
overview: A psychological thriller about a young married couple who buys a beautiful Napa Valley house on several acres of land only to find that the man they bought it from refuses to let go of the property.
plot:
The Intruder is a 2019 American psychological thriller directed by Deon Taylor and written by David Loughery. Michael Ealy and Meagan Good star as Scott and Annie Howard, a couple who buy a house in the country, and Dennis Quaid plays Charlie Peck, its previous owner, who cannot let it go; Joseph Sikora co-stars.

Scott and Annie buy "Foxglove", a Napa Valley house, from Charlie, who says his wife, Ellen, died of cancer two years earlier and that he is moving to Florida to live with his daughter, Cassidy. Soon after, their friend Mike senses he is being watched during an overnight visit and finds a cigarette burn on his car seat. Annie catches Charlie mowing their lawn yet invites him to Thanksgiving, and after Scott spots someone in the woods, he installs security cameras, a job Charlie tries to stop. Charlie keeps turning up uninvited, claiming he is staying at a hotel in town, and the couple quarrel over Scott's coldness toward him and Annie's sympathy. A neighbor tells Scott that Charlie's wife actually shot herself with one of his shotguns, and Charlie, increasingly obsessed with Annie, visits her whenever Scott is away.

While jogging, Scott is run down by a truck driven by Charlie, and Mike learns that Charlie sold the house only because of debts and legal trouble. With Scott in the hospital, Charlie dines with Annie, and when Mike comes to check on her, Charlie kills him with an axe. Scott discovers that Charlie never stayed at the hotel, and Cassidy, who has changed her name, tells him that her father is a pathological liar who murdered her mother when she threatened divorce. Meanwhile Annie finds a hidden door behind a linen closet leading to the cellar where Charlie has been living since the sale. Charlie knocks her out and attacks her, throws the returning Scott over a balcony and tries to strangle Annie, until she stabs him in the back. Wounded, he hunts them with a shotgun, but Scott knocks him down with a baseball bat and takes the gun, and as Annie tells a 911 dispatcher that her husband has shot an intruder, Scott kills Charlie.

Moved back a week from its planned date to avoid Avengers: Endgame, the film was released by Sony Pictures on May 3, 2019. Critics were negative, with 35% on Rotten Tomatoes and 39 on Metacritic, but it grossed $40.6 million worldwide on an $8 million budget.

title: I See You
overview: When a 12-year-old boy goes missing, lead investigator Greg Harper struggles to balance the pressure of the investigation and troubles with his wife, Jackie. plot:
I See You is a 2019 American horror thriller directed by Adam Randall from a screenplay by Devon Graye. It stars Helen Hunt, Jon Tenney and Judah Lewis, with Owen Teague and Libe Barer, in a story about a detective's family whose suburban home becomes the scene of increasingly unsettling events.

When ten-year-old Justin Whitter vanishes while riding his bike, detective Greg Harper leads the case with his partner, Spitzky. A green pocket knife left at the scene links the abduction to a series of crimes from fifteen years earlier, committed by a man who is now in prison. At home, Connor resents his mother for a recent affair, and strange things keep happening: objects disappear, a repairman says a daughter the Harpers do not have let him in, and Greg is locked inside a closet. When Jackie's former lover, Todd, shows up, he is struck on the head and later found dead, and Jackie, believing Connor killed him, persuades Greg to help bury the body. Soon afterward the couple find Connor tied up in the bathtub with a green knife beside him.

Flashbacks then reveal that two drifters, Mindy and Alec, have been secretly living in the house. Alec caused the disturbances to torment the family, but Mindy witnessed the true killer of Todd: Greg. Hidden in Greg's car, Mindy finds green knives and Justin's shirt, follows him into the forest and discovers the missing boys locked in a trailer, making a broken 911 call before Greg captures her and kills her at home, staging it as self-defense. Alec confronts Greg, who claims he was once a victim himself, and shoots him dead. Spitzky arrives and wounds Alec, the evidence in Greg's car exposes the truth, and the boys are rescued by tracing Mindy's call.

The film premiered in the Midnighters section of SXSW on March 13, 2019, and Saban Films released it in theaters on December 6, 2019. It grossed about $1.2 million worldwide on a $5 million budget. Reviews were favorable, with 73% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 65; critics found the twisting plot convoluted but praised the cast and its slow-building suspense.

title: Eternals
overview: The Eternals are a team of ancient aliens who have been living on Earth in secret for thousands of years. When an unexpected tragedy forces them out of the shadows, they are forced to reunite against mankind’s most ancient enemy, the Deviants.
plot:
In 5000 BC, ten superpowered beings known as Eternals—Ajak, Sersi, Ikaris, Kingo, Sprite, Phastos, Makkari, Druig, Gilgamesh, and Thena—are sent to Earth by Arishem, a Celestial, on the starship Domo. They are charged with exterminating invasive entities known as the Deviants. After the last Deviants are killed in 1521, the group's opinions differ over their continued relationship with humankind. Over the next 500 years, they mostly live apart, waiting for Arishem's orders.
In the present, Sersi and Sprite live together in London. After Sersi's partner Ikaris left her without explanation centuries earlier, she is now in a relationship with human Dane Whitman who works at the Natural History Museum. When the trio is attacked by the Deviant Kro, Ikaris arrives and chases the creature away. The three Eternals travel to South Dakota to reunite with their leader, Ajak, only to find her dead. Sersi is posthumously chosen by Ajak as her successor, granting her the ability to communicate with Arishem.
Sersi learns that the Eternals' mission was actually to prepare Earth for the Emergence of a new Celestial. Arishem explains that, for millions of years, he has been planting Celestial seeds inside planets where the energy from large populations allows new Celestials to be born. The Deviants were sent to destroy the apex predators of each planet to ensure the development of intelligent life, but when they evolved and began hunting the planets' native populations, Arishem created the Eternals to counter them. With the recent end of the Blip restoring Earth's population, humankind has reached the necessary size to allow the Celestial Tiamut to be born, which will result in Earth's destruction.
Hoping to delay the Emergence, the Eternals reunite. At Druig's residence in the Amazon rainforest, they are attacked by the Deviants. They kill them all except for Kro, who kills Gilgamesh before fleeing. Phastos proposes they use the Uni-Mind, a connection between all the Eternals that would give Druig enough power to put Tiamut to sleep with his mind-control abilities. However, Ikaris is loyal to Arishem and refuses to help stop the Emergence. He reveals that Ajak wanted to stop the Emergence and save humanity, so he led her to the Deviants and allowed them to kill her. Sprite joins Ikaris due to her unrequited love for him while Kingo chooses to leave, agreeing with Ikaris but not wanting to hurt his friends.
Makkari locates the site of the Emergence, an active volcano in the Indian Ocean, where Ikaris and Sprite attempt to stop them. Druig knocks out Sprite, and Phastos restrains Ikaris. Kro arrives and is killed by Thena. Druig is unable to put Tiamut to sleep, and Sersi instead attempts to turn him into stone. Ikaris breaks free of his restraints and goes to kill Sersi, but is unable to due to his love for her. Both he and Sprite join with the others in the Uni-Mind, and Sersi gains enough power to turn Tiamut into stone. Guilt-ridden, Ikaris flies into the Sun.

title: Blindsided: The Game
overview: After blind man Walter Cooke (Eric Jacobus) prevents a local gang from shaking down his local grocer Gordon (Roger Yuan), Walter must reckon with the gang's boss Sal (Joe Bucaro). The stakes are high, but Walter's got an ace up his sleeve.
plot:
Blindsided: The Game is a 2018 American action comedy short film directed by Clayton J. Barber, who wrote it with its star, the martial artist and stunt performer Eric Jacobus. Running about 46 minutes, it expands the twelve-minute short Blindsided, released the previous year, into a longer story after Jacobus's production company secured funding to continue it. The cast includes Roger Yuan, Joe Bucaro III, David William No, Michelle Lee, Pete Antico, Khalid Ghajji, Nicholas Verdi, Justin Hall and the veteran stuntman and fight choreographer Luke LaFontaine. Jacobus oversaw the action, with Yuan, LaFontaine and No, who also served as a producer, contributing to the fight choreography, and the score is by Steffan Schmidt and Raymond Lane. The film was released free to stream on YouTube on 17 May 2018.

Walter Cooke (Jacobus) is a blind man living in a modern American city, an apple pie enthusiast with a knack for sensing danger. Underestimated and brushed aside by a local gang while shopping at his neighbourhood grocery, he comes to the aid of its owner Gordon (Yuan), his friend, who is deep in debt to the gangsters. Surprising both Gordon and the thugs with his physical abilities, Walter sends them packing in an alley fight in which he puts his white cane to good use. This is where the original short ended and where The Game picks up. Following the gangsters back to their boss, Sal (Bucaro), Walter and Gordon get further into trouble, and elements of Gordon's own past come to light in connection with the villains. The stakes rise, but Walter has an ace up his sleeve, and the confrontation eventually leads the pair to take on the toughs in their own warehouse, where Gordon must fight alongside Walter against an array of opponents armed with guns and blades. Walter himself remains something of an enigma, with hints of a deeper history left for possible future stories.

Reviewers from action-focused outlets welcomed it as a homage to the blind swordsman genre, especially Zatoichi and Blind Fury. Cinapse called it enjoyable, praising the basic character work that adds heart and comedy between the set pieces and Jacobus's physical and comedic talents, and recommended it to action devotees and fans of the sub-genre. Film Combat Syndicate praised its blend of slapstick and intense fight scenes and its warm portrayal of Walter and Gordon's friendship, while noting that the short format leaves Walter's background largely unexplored.

title: May the Devil Take You
overview: Hoping to find answers to her estranged father's mysterious illness, a young woman visits his old villa and uncovers a horrifying truth from the past.
plot:
Lesmana Wijaya forms a contract with a priestess, who performs black magic to grant him wealth. Flashes of news clippings show his rise to fame, his first wife's suicide, his marriage to retired actress Laksmi, and his imminent bankruptcy.
Alfie, Lesmana's estranged daughter with his first wife, is informed that Lesmana has been hospitalized due to a mysterious illness that leaves him in a coma. At the hospital, she meets her step-siblings Ruben, Maya, and Nara, as well as Ruben's girlfriend Lilly. She is stalked by the priestess, who controls Lesmana to attack her and Lilly in a hallucination. Alfie learns that Laksmi is searching the abandoned family villa for valuables.
Alfie travels to the villa, her childhood home, now abandoned in a secluded area. At Laksmi's demand, Ruben uncovers a sealed door to the cellar. This unleashes a supernatural presence that kills Lesmana in his hospital bed and possesses Laksmi, who then attacks Maya. As their vehicles are sabotaged, Ruben calls for help, while Alfie walks Maya to the village. A delirious Maya flees into the forest, and gets attacked by the possessed Laksmi. Maya kills Laksmi, only to be possessed herself.
Meanwhile Alfie and Ruben discover Lesmana gained his wealth by dealing with dark priestesses, who possess supernatural powers by declaring themselves concubines of the devil. Alfie also recalls the moment of her mother's death, realizing that it was due to the demonic pact and not suicide. The presence also continues to torment Alfie, Ruben, and Nara. Alfie notices strange marks on Nara's body and hers and realizes they are marked for death. The next day, Lily arrives in her car, only to be brutally killed by Maya.
Maya returns to the villa and enters the cellar, seeing a set of dolls representing her family, made of their hair. The presence invites her to become a follower. Maya agrees, influenced by the priestess. Fully under its sway, Maya confronts her siblings. She tempts with Ruben to join her and sacrifice Alfie and Nara. He refuses, prompting her to murder him by dismembering a doll made of his hair.
Alfie experiences a vision of her father betraying the priestess when she demanded Alfie as the next payment. He killed the priestess and buried her under the cellar floor, but not before she cursed his entire bloodline.
Alfie tries to bargain with the priestess for Maya's release. The priestess mocks her, before using the doll to torture her. Alfie then takes Maya's hair doll and burns it, setting Maya on fire. Alfie then digs up the priestess' corpse, cuts out Lesmana's hair that she swallowed for the ritual. She burns the hair, which ends the curse and makes the mark on her arm vanishe.
The priestess manifests, drags Alfie into a pit quickly filling with mud, and wraps her with hair. Alfie cuts herself free but is unable to climb out of the pit. Just as she has given up, Alfie hears her mother's voice and sees her hand.

title: A Christmas Prince: The Royal Wedding

overview: A year after Amber helped Richard secure the crown. The two are set to tie the knot in a royal Christmas wedding — but their plans are jeopardized when Amber finds herself second-guessing whether or not she's cut out to be queen, and Richard is faced with a political crisis that threatens to tarnish not only the holiday season but the future of the kingdom.
plot:
One year after the events of the first film, Amber and Richard are still happily engaged. The news media company she worked for went out of business, so her friends are unemployed. At Christmastime, Amber and her father Rudy travel to Aldovia to plan her wedding. She continues to blog about royal life with Richard.
Amber becomes overwhelmed with the dictatorial traditions of royal protocol and lack of control over her own wedding, which is controlled by the flamboyant designer Sahil and Mrs. Averill. Meanwhile, Richard struggles with the failing implementation of his Aldovian economic revitalization program, the New Aldovia initiative. It is mysteriously hemorrhaging money from the monarchy as unemployment and low wages afflict the increasingly discontent populace.
To assist in the economic efforts, Queen Helena brings in Lord Leopold to assist Richard, as he had been planning aid efforts with Richard's late father. Meanwhile, Simon, impoverished due to his divorce from Sophia, also returns to beg to be brought back into the palace; a distrustful Richard reluctantly accepts, as Simon is family.
Amber and Richard's relationship grows strained as Richard becomes increasingly distracted with royal demands, and she clashes with Mrs. Averill's strict guidelines. After Princess Emily's play is cancelled due to a strike by governmental workers, Amber hosts the play at the palace. While the move was well-received, she becomes furious upon discovering Mrs. Averill took down posts from her blog about the event for their informality. Amber is further upset when Sahil and Mrs. Averill demand she remove her locket (containing her late mother's photo) for a royal portrait.
After receiving a bitter Christmas card from an unemployed worker, Amber investigates the royal finances with her friends, who have come to celebrate her wedding. She learns that the New Aldovia initiative has been failing because a group of new companies has been outbidding local workers and taking the money out of the country.
During a paparazzi ambush, Amber is saved by Simon, who wants to help investigate the economic issue. With Emily's help, the group hacks into a site and discover the shell companies are owned by the association Glockenspiel Consortium. Mrs. Averill confronts Richard and Amber over paparazzi photos of Amber at a bar while investigating, so she admits to the sleuthing.
When Richard fails to defend Amber against Mrs. Averill, she storms out. He admits his failings as a fiancé to Emily, and after finding Amber, they reconcile. Then, Helena gives them the blessing to have the ceremony she wants.
During a royal celebration, the group reveals that Glockenspiel Consortium is owned by Leopold, who is accosted and thrown into the palace dungeon. Richard gives a Christmas address that promises holiday bonuses to all Aldovian workers, and the populace celebrates.

title: Welcome Home
overview: A couple try to repair their damaged union in an Italian vacation paradise. Then they discover the owner's intentions.
plot:
Welcome Home is a 2018 thriller film directed by George Ratliff from a screenplay by David Levinson, produced by Allan Mandelbaum, Tim White and Trevor White for Voltage Pictures. Aaron Paul and Emily Ratajkowski, cast in April 2017, play a troubled couple who hope a romantic getaway to Italy will save their relationship, with Riccardo Scamarcio in a supporting role as Federico. The first trailer appeared in October 2018, and the film went to video on demand in November 2018 without a North American theatrical run.

Bryan and Cassie rent a house in Umbria in an effort to repair their relationship after Cassie was caught having drunken sex with a co-worker, an episode that has left Bryan impotent. While out running, Cassie hurts her ankle and is helped by Federico, a handsome stranger who drives her back and offers them a ride into town the next day. After a tense trip, Bryan accuses Cassie of failing to notice how Federico leers at her, and she storms off. Federico joins Bryan at a bar, secretly drugs his drink and arranges for two women to take him to a hotel, where Bryan has sex with them but later remembers nothing. Federico, it emerges, has hidden cameras throughout the house and watches the couple constantly.

Bryan discovers that Federico is not their neighbor, as he claimed, and when he threatens to expose him, Federico threatens to tell Cassie about the hotel. Cassie warms to Federico until an unsettling dinner of rabbit stew. Enraged after watching the couple reconcile, Federico locks Bryan in the cellar, tricks a blindfolded Cassie into letting him kiss and grope her while filming it, then leaves Bryan's phone playing the hotel video for her to find. The couple's furious argument ends when a thrown phone shatters a mirror and reveals a hidden camera. Federico arrives and attacks Bryan with a knife, and Cassie beats him to death with a cane. Eduardo, the owner of the house, then arrives and reveals himself as Federico's accomplice, but Cassie stabs him and Bryan shoots him. Bryan finds recordings of many other couples, and the pair burn the tapes, bury the bodies and vow silence, unaware that a camera hidden in a garden gnome is streaming them to viewers worldwide, part of a global network of similarly wired rentals.

Francesco Acquaroli plays Eduardo. Critics were unenthusiastic, with 10% approval on Rotten Tomatoes from ten reviews and a Metacritic score of 38. The film earned about $332,000 from foreign release.

title: The Bouncer
overview: A tough nightclub bouncer struggling to raise his 8-year-old daughter is forced to go undercover after an unfortunate event.
plot:
The Bouncer (original title: Lukas) is a 2018 French-Belgian action thriller film directed by Julien Leclercq and starring Jean-Claude Van Damme, Sveva Alviti, Sami Bouajila, Alice Verset and Sam Louwyck. Set in Belgium, it follows a nightclub bouncer who is coerced into helping the authorities bring down a crime boss. The original European version, released as Lukas, is mostly in French with some Flemish and English, while the version released a year later in the United States as The Bouncer had some scenes cut and was dubbed into English.

Lukas fled South Africa after the death of his wife and now lives quietly in his native Belgium with his eight-year-old daughter, Sarah, working as a bouncer at a nightclub. One night he restrains an aggressive patron who then badly injures himself while trying to attack him. Because the injured man is the son of a member of the European Parliament, Lukas loses his job and comes under investigation by a mysterious officer named Maxim, who gives him a choice: go to prison, or go undercover at a strip club owned by Jan Dekkers, an organized crime figure, and spy on him. Lukas reluctantly agrees and soon finds himself drawn into Jan's world. His first job is to drive Lisa, an Italian woman once indicted for forgery, and he gradually learns that Jan is planning a large counterfeiting operation. Meanwhile his daughter is taken into the care of social services, and Lukas realizes that cooperating may be the only way to get her back. He is sent on increasingly dangerous assignments, including the kidnapping of a drug cook to be traded to Dutch gangsters for the special watermarked paper needed to print banknotes, a deal that turns violent. When Lukas tries to quit, Maxim threatens to send him back to South Africa, to face punishment for what he did after his wife's killers went unpunished by the police. Caught between the police and the criminals, and forming a cautious bond with Lisa, who has her own reasons to escape her past, Lukas must stay alive long enough to see the operation through and protect his daughter.

The film received generally positive reviews from critics, and on Rotten Tomatoes it holds a 100% approval rating based on five reviews. The cast also includes Kevin Janssens, with Van Damme in the title role of Lukas.

title: Daughter of the Wolf
tagline: In the Wild, Only the Strong Survive
overview: Ex-military specialist Clair Hamilton returns home from her tour in the Middle East due to her father's passing and to claim her inheritance. Her son is then kidnapped and held for ransom by a gang led by a mysterious figure known only as “Father”.
plot:
Daughter of the Wolf is a 2019 Canadian action thriller directed by David Hackl and written by Nika Agiashvili. Gina Carano stars as Clair Hamilton, a military veteran fighting to rescue her kidnapped son, with Richard Dreyfuss as the kidnappers' leader, known only as Father, Brendan Fehr as Larsen, Sydelle Noel as Hobbs and Anton Gillis-Adelman as the boy, Charlie. It was shot in the spring of 2019 around West Kelowna, British Columbia.

Clair arrives at a remote exchange with a bag of ransom money, only to be double-crossed. In the shootout she kills two of the gang, and while chasing the third, Larsen, she falls through the ice of a frozen lake. Larsen, who never meant for anyone to die, pulls her out. Recovering, Clair has a calm encounter with a black wolf, then catches Larsen and forces him to lead her to her son. Father, it emerges, holds a grudge against Clair's father for shutting down a mill and leaving with money owed to him. Along the way a gunman ambushes them but is killed by wolves, and Larsen confesses that Father murdered his own father and abducted him and his mother when he was a child.

The gang has moved Charlie to a lodge across the mountain to sell him. When Clair tries to trade the money and Larsen for the boy, Father fires at Charlie, and Larsen takes the bullet. Clair escapes on a snowmobile but is chased by Hobbs, loses a knife fight and goes over a waterfall, while Charlie is recaptured. Guided by wolves through the forest, she returns to the lodge, where Father is torturing Larsen. She kills Hobbs and the remaining gang, and in a final struggle pushes Father through a window. Larsen dies, Clair flees with Charlie, and wolves descend on Father in the snow. Months later, hiking in spring, Clair sees the black wolf again.

The film was released in the United States on 14 June 2019 and in Canada that August, and screened at the Taormina Film Fest. Reviews were largely negative, with a 25% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 36. The Hollywood Reporter called it a subpar vehicle for its star, though Variety praised it as a capably crafted, female-led action film.

title: Bombshell
overview: Bombshell is a revealing look inside the most powerful and controversial media empire of all time; and the explosive story of the women who brought down the infamous man who created it.
plot:
Bombshell is a 2019 American biographical drama film directed by Jay Roach, written by Charles Randolph, and produced by Charlize Theron, Aaron Ryder, and Teri Segal. The film is based on the book "Fire and Reckoning: Inside the World of Fox News" by Byron York.

The film takes place in 1996-1997 and focuses on the lives of three women who worked at Fox News Channel during its early years: Megyn Kelly (played by Charlize Theron), Gretchen Carlson (played by Nicole Kidman), and Kayla Pospisil (played by Allison Janney).

The film begins with a dramatic sequence showing the 1996 presidential election, where Republican candidate Bob Dole loses to Democratic candidate Bill Clinton. The scene then shifts to Fox News Channel's launch in October 1996, where Megyn Kelly is hired as a news anchor.

As the story unfolds, we see how Megyn Kelly navigates her way through the male-dominated world of Fox News, facing sexism and misogyny from her colleagues, including Roger Ailes (played by Jodie Foster), the channel's CEO. Despite these challenges, Kelly proves herself to be a talented journalist and becomes one of the network's top anchors.

Meanwhile, Gretchen Carlson is introduced as a rising star at Fox News, where she works alongside Megyn Kelly. However, her career is soon derailed when she accuses Roger Ailes of sexual harassment. The film depicts the intense pressure and fear that Carlson faces as she decides to take on Ailes, who has significant power over her career.

As the story progresses, we see how Kayla Pospisil, a young producer at Fox News, becomes embroiled in the scandal surrounding Roger Ailes' behavior. She is one of the few women who speak out against him, and her bravery inspires others to do the same.

The film's climax features a dramatic confrontation between Gretchen Carlson and Roger Ailes, where she accuses him of sexual harassment and demands that he resign from his position as CEO of Fox News. The scene is intense and emotional, with both characters delivering powerful performances.

In the aftermath of Ailes' resignation, the film shows how the women at Fox News Channel come together to support each other and rebuild their careers. Megyn Kelly becomes a leading voice for women's rights and feminism, while Gretchen Carlson finds new success as a lawyer and advocate.

The film ends with a sense of hope and renewal, as the women at Fox News Channel look towards a brighter future. The final scene shows Kayla Pospisil, now a successful journalist in her own right, reflecting on the lessons she learned from her experience at Fox News.

Overall, Bombshell is a powerful and timely film that sheds light on the struggles faced by women in the male-dominated world of journalism. With outstanding performances from its cast, including Charlize Theron, Nicole Kidman, and Allison Janney, the film is a must-see for anyone interested in politics, media, or feminism.

title: The Night Clerk
overview: Hotel night clerk Bart Bromley is a highly intelligent young man on the Autism spectrum. When a woman is murdered during his shift, Bart becomes the prime suspect. As the police investigation closes in, Bart makes a personal connection with a beautiful guest named Andrea, but soon realises he must stop the real murderer before she becomes the next victim.
plot:
The Night Clerk is a 2020 American crime drama film written and directed by Michael Cristofer. It stars Tye Sheridan as Bart Bromley, a hotel night clerk who becomes the center of a murder investigation, with Ana de Armas as Andrea Rivera, John Leguizamo as Detective Espada, Helen Hunt as Bart's mother Ethel and Johnathon Schaech as Detective Nick Perretti.

Bart, a young man with Asperger syndrome who lives with his mother, works the night shift at a hotel, where he secretly places cameras in a guest room and studies the recordings to imitate the speech and mannerisms of the guests and overcome his social awkwardness. One night, after his shift, he watches from home as a new guest, Karen, lets a man into her room, argues with him and is beaten. Seeing a gun fall from her purse, Bart races back to the hotel. Soon after, his co-worker Jack hears a gunshot and finds Karen dead with Bart sitting on the bed. While Jack calls 911, Bart removes his cameras but leaves behind a storage card. Questioned by Detective Espada, Bart claims he returned to the hotel for his forgotten wallet, a lie Espada sees through because Bart had just bought ice cream. Reviewing his recording, Bart notices that the killer had a bird tattoo on his arm.

Reassigned to another hotel, Bart meets Andrea Rivera, a guest who recognizes his condition and flirts with him. He hides cameras in her room, and they share a kiss by the pool. Smitten, he gets a haircut, a new suit and a new car, but then sees Andrea in bed with the man with the bird tattoo. The police seize his equipment, though Bart has kept a hidden copy of the recording of Karen's room. The man is Karen's husband, Nick, a detective having an affair with Andrea, who wants her to get rid of Bart. When Bart sees Nick beating Andrea on camera, he rushes to help and shows her the recording proving that Nick killed Karen. She weeps and falls asleep in his bed, but the next morning she is gone with the hard drive, leaving behind Karen's gun. As Andrea and Nick drive out of town, the police find that Bart has left the gun, the camera storage cards and a note for Espada, and the couple are pulled over. Bart walks through a mall, practising the conversational skills he has learned from his recordings.

Saban Films released The Night Clerk on February 21, 2020, and it reached Netflix's Top Ten after arriving on the service in June. Reviews were unfavorable, with 34% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 44.

title: Little

plot:
Little (2019) is a fantasy comedy film directed by Tina Gordon, written by Tracy Oliver, and produced by Will Packer and Marc E. Platt.

The movie takes place on March 8th, which is International Women's Day, and follows the story of Maureen "Ma" Johnson (played by Regina Hall), a successful businesswoman who has just been passed over for a promotion at her company. Feeling frustrated and underappreciated, Ma decides to take revenge on her sexist boss, James King (played by Dan Aykroyd).

As she walks out of the office building, Ma is suddenly transported back in time to March 8th, 1982, when she was just a teenager. She finds herself reliving memories from her past, including her high school days and her relationships with her friends and family.

In this alternate timeline, Ma discovers that she has the ability to see and interact with the inner thoughts of women throughout history, including Frida Kahlo (played by Patricia Arquette), Rosa Parks (played by Regina King), and Susan B. Anthony (played by Danielle Brooks). These powerful women become her allies and mentors, guiding her on a journey of self-discovery and empowerment.

As Ma navigates this new reality, she also meets a young version of herself, played by Storm Reid, who is struggling to find her place in the world. Through her interactions with her past and present selves, Ma learns valuable lessons about feminism, identity, and the importance of supporting women.

Throughout the movie, Little features a talented ensemble cast, including Lyriq Bent, Marsai Martin, and Brian Tyree Henry. The film's humor is witty and relatable, making it an enjoyable watch for audiences of all ages.

As Ma continues to explore her past and present selves, she begins to realize that her experiences are not just about personal growth but also about the collective progress of women throughout history. In the end, Ma returns to her own time, armed with a newfound sense of confidence and purpose.

The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Ma embracing her inner strength and using it to inspire others. The final shot is of Ma walking out of the office building, ready to take on the world as a powerful and empowered woman.

Overall, Little (2019) is a heartwarming and entertaining film that celebrates women's empowerment and the importance of female friendships. With its talented cast, witty humor, and inspiring message, it's a must-watch for anyone looking for a feel-good movie experience.

title: Black Beauty
overview: Born free in the American West, Black Beauty is a horse rounded up and brought to Birtwick Stables, where she meets spirited teenager Jo Green. The two forge a bond that carries Beauty through the different chapters, challenges and adventures.
plot:
Black Beauty is a 2020 family adventure drama film written, edited and directed by Ashley Avis, the sixth screen adaptation of Anna Sewell's 1877 novel. A co-production between the United States, the United Kingdom, South Africa, France and Germany, it recasts the title horse as a mare. Kate Winslet voices Black Beauty, with Mackenzie Foy as Jo Green, Iain Glen as her uncle John Manly, Calam Lynch as George Winthorp, Fern Deacon as his sister Georgina and Claire Forlani as their mother.

A wild mustang born in Utah's Onaqui Mountains narrates her life, remembering her mother's lesson that horses who die fly up to rest among the stars. Cowboys round up her herd, and she is bought by John Manly, a patient trainer who takes her to Birtwick, a horse sanctuary, where she befriends the horses Ginger and Merrylegs. When John's sister and her husband die in a car accident, he takes in his grieving teenage niece, Jo. Jo shuns her uncle but is drawn to the defiant mustang; recognizing each other's pain, the two bond, and Jo tames her and names her Black Beauty, learning to "partner" rather than "break" a horse. After a stable fire, with Birtwick losing money, Jo works extra hours to save up to buy Beauty. The wealthy Winthorps lease Beauty for their daughter Georgina, who treats her cruelly, while their kind son George, who rides Ginger, takes an interest in Jo. Georgina's reckless riding in a race injures Beauty, and the horse is returned, but Birtwick soon closes and Beauty is sold before Jo can say goodbye. Beauty passes from a ranger, Terry, to a farmer who works her hard and then to a kindly New York carriage driver, Jerry. She briefly reunites with Ginger, who dies soon afterwards. When Jerry falls ill, Beauty is sold to a cruel carriage company involved in illegal horse trading, and after glimpsing Ginger's body being carted away, she sits down in the road in grief, drawing media attention. A stable boy, Manuel, reports the company to the police, and Jo, who has searched for her all along, finds her. Jo has rebuilt Birtwick with John and George, now her husband, to rehabilitate horses, and Beauty spends the rest of her life there, reunited with Merrylegs.

Planned for cinemas, the film was acquired by Disney from Constantin Film and released on Disney+ on 27 November 2020. Reviews were mixed, with 48% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 52.

title: Morbius
overview: Dangerously ill with a rare blood disorder, and determined to save others suffering his same fate, Dr. Michael Morbius attempts a desperate gamble. What at first appears to be a radical success soon reveals itself to be a remedy potentially worse than the disease.
plot:
Morbius is a 2022 American superhero film based on the Marvel Comics character, produced by Columbia Pictures and distributed by Sony as the third film in Sony's Spider-Man Universe. Directed by Daniel Espinosa and written by Matt Sazama and Burk Sharpless, it stars Jared Leto as Dr. Michael Morbius, alongside Matt Smith as Milo, Adria Arjona as Martine Bancroft, Jared Harris as Dr. Emil Nicholas, Al Madrigal and Tyrese Gibson as FBI agents.

As a boy in a Greek hospital, Michael Morbius befriends another child, whom he names Milo; both suffer from a rare blood disease and dream of being normal. Their adoptive father, the hospital's director, sends the gifted Michael to study medicine in New York. Twenty-five years later, Michael is a renowned scientist who has declined a Nobel Prize for his work on artificial blood. Secretly, he has captured vampire bats in Costa Rica, hoping to splice their genes with his own to cure his condition.

With money from the wealthy Milo, Michael conducts his experiment aboard a ship in international waters. The treatment cures him but turns him into a vampire-like creature with superhuman strength, speed and echolocation, and he kills the ship's crew in a frenzy of bloodlust. Back in New York, he tries to control his hunger with artificial blood while FBI agents investigate the killings. When Milo discovers the cure, he takes it himself and embraces his new powers, killing without remorse. Michael, who refuses to give in to his thirst for human blood, develops an antibody to stop his brother, leading to a final confrontation after Milo kills those closest to him. In mid-credits scenes, the Spider-Man villain Adrian Toomes arrives in Michael's universe.

After being delayed several times from its original July 2020 date, mainly because of the COVID-19 pandemic, Morbius was released in the United States on April 1, 2022.

The film grossed 167.5 million dollars worldwide and suffered one of the steepest second-weekend drops ever for a superhero film. Critics panned its writing, visual effects and post-credits scenes, giving it 15 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 35. It became the subject of mocking internet memes, which led Sony to re-release it in June 2022, again with poor results. At the Golden Raspberry Awards, Leto won Worst Actor and Arjona Worst Supporting Actress.

title: The Silence
overview: With the world under attack by deadly creatures who hunt by sound, a teen and her family seek refuge outside the city and encounter a mysterious cult.
plot:
The Silence is a post-apocalyptic horror film of 2019 directed by John R. Leonetti from a screenplay by Carey and Shane Van Dyke, adapted from Tim Lebbon's 2015 novel of the same name. Kiernan Shipka stars as Ally Andrews, a deaf teenager, with Stanley Tucci as her father Hugh, Miranda Otto as her mother Kelly, Kate Trotter as her grandmother Lynn, John Corbett as the family friend Glenn, Dempsey Bryk as her boyfriend Rob and Billy MacLellan as a sinister reverend.

Cave researchers accidentally release a unknown species of pterosaur-like predators from a mine. The creatures, called Vesps, kill the team and swarm toward the noisiest places they can find. Ally lost her hearing in a car crash; when news footage reveals the attacks and the government tells people to stay inside and silent, she persuades her parents to head for the countryside. Glenn joins them, but on a jammed interstate he goes off-road and crashes into a herd of deer. The family dog's barking draws the Vesps, and Glenn fires his gun to lure them away and is devoured. Hugh realizes the creatures are blind and hunt purely by sound, so he burns Glenn's car as a decoy and the family continues on foot.

At a remote house the owner is killed and Kelly is bitten. While Hugh and Ally search a store for antibiotics, they discover Vesp eggs gestating in corpses and escape by setting off the sprinklers; they also meet the reverend of a cult called the Hushed. Kelly recovers, and Ally learns online that the Vesps cannot survive cold, so the family plans to go north. The tongueless reverend tracks them down and says Ally is fertile, revealing that he wants her for the cult; Hugh drives the members off at gunpoint. Later, phones planted by the cult ring around the house and summon the Vesps. The cultists seize Ally, and Lynn sacrifices herself by screaming, drawing the creatures onto herself and the captors. The family rescues Ally from the rest and Hugh beats the reverend to death. Weeks later they reach the Refuge in Alaska, where Ally reunites with Rob and hunts Vesps with a bow, wondering who will adapt first, the creatures or humanity.

Shipka and Tucci were cast in 2017, and filming began in Toronto that September. After its original distributor ran into financial trouble, Netflix released the film on 10 April 2019; it also played theatrically in seven countries, grossing $2.3 million. Reviews were largely negative; Rotten Tomatoes gave it 30%, with its consensus calling the premise derivative.

title: After the Wedding
overview: Seeking funds for her orphanage in India, Isabelle travels to New York to meet Theresa, a wealthy benefactor. An invitation to attend a wedding ignites a series of events in which the past collides with the present while mysteries unravel.
plot:
Isabel Andersen, co-founder of an orphanage in India, must travel to New York to meet a potential benefactor, millionaire CEO Theresa Young. She is resistant to the trip due to her responsibilities at the orphanage and because she does not want to leave Jai, a boy whom she found on the street when he was a year old. He is the closest child in the orphanage to Isabel, and does not want Isabel to leave.
However, Theresa insists on an in-person meeting. Reluctantly, Isabel agrees and goes to it, which takes place the day before the wedding of Theresa's daughter Grace. Theresa invites Isabel to the wedding as a courtesy, so she feels obliged to attend.
At the wedding, Isabel is surprised to see Theresa's husband is her teenage sweetheart Oscar Carlson, now a renowned visual artist. During Grace's wedding toast, she discovers that Grace is not Theresa's biological daughter, but Oscar's. Isabel soon realizes that she is in fact her birth daughter by Oscar, whom they had placed for adoption as teenagers.
Isabel returns to the house the day after the wedding to confront Oscar. She learns that after placing the baby for adoption, he changed his mind within the 30-day grace period, so reclaimed the infant Grace without informing her. Isabel then forces Oscar and Theresa to also inform Grace, who had always been told her biological mother had died.
Theresa encourages Isabel to get to know Grace and reconnect with Oscar, and eventually decides to dramatically increase her donation to the orphanage, thereby forcing Isabel to extend her stay in New York. Eventually, Theresa makes her donation, as well as a newly established fund in Isabel and Grace's name. These are both contingent on Isabel moving to New York permanently.
Mistrustful of Theresa's real motives, Isabel angrily confronts her and learns that Theresa is dying. She then admits she has known about Isabel's link to Oscar and Grace all along and arranged the whole charade to install Isabel as a new mother figure to both Grace and Theresa's own eight-year-old twin boys Theo & Otto. Oscar discovers his wife's illness around the same time and eventually tells Grace, who is already struggling with doubts about her recent marriage and the news that Isabel is her biological mother.
Theresa dies soon after and the family scatter her ashes. Isabel then returns to India for a visit to the orphanage and Jai. The film ends with Jai and his friends playing football in the orphanage.

title: Come Away
tagline: A story about courage, wonder and never growing old.
overview: Before Alice went to Wonderland, and before Peter became Pan, they were brother and sister. When their eldest brother dies in a tragic accident, they each seek to save their parents from their downward spirals of despair until finally they are forced to choose between home and imagination, setting the stage for their iconic journeys into Wonderland and Neverland.
plot:
A mother reads "The Stolen Child" by William Butler Yeats to her three children, two boys and one girl, and recounts a story of three siblings; Alice, David (The White Rabbit) and Peter, who live with their parents: Jack (The King of Hearts) and Rose Littleton (The Queen of Hearts). The children dwell in a house by a forest on the outskirts of London letting their imaginations run wild.
Alice acts mature in contrast to Peter who regards the local woods as his domain (during one of their trips they discover an eagle feather and a downed boat, with the siblings wondering if they could get it sea-worthy).
Tragedy strikes one day when David, while pretending to fight pirates during a storm, falls into the river, is struck by lightning, and dies. The family copes in different ways; with Jack, a model maker, returning to his bad gambling habits and Rose intending to make a green felt hat that would have been David's birthday present.
To make payments, Peter and Alice go to sell a family heirloom silver pocket watch, during which they shelter a group of street urchins who have pickpocketed an intimidating criminal.
Both siblings meet an eccentric shopkeeper, Hatter (Mad Hatter), who leads them to a money lender and lower crime boss Captain James or CJ (Captain Hook) who, unbeknownst to both of them, is their uncle. Peter later runs into the very same street kids he met earlier who reveal they are known as the Lost Boys and that they have been to a place known only to children called Never Neverland and offer to take him there. Jack later visits his brother to call off his debt collectors, with a jealous James crippling his brother (as a show of loyalty to his crime paymasters) leading to Jack losing his hand.
Peter responds by seeking out these Lost Boys to help rob James of the fortune of gold coins Peter spied on earlier that he is safeguarding for the various criminal organizations of London's underworld. When James catches his nephew in the act Peter cuts off his uncle's hand in a sword duel before fleeing.
With his uncle and cohorts hot on his heels, Peter is forced to run away from home, taking his late brother's newly finished hat with the eagle feather in it and dressed in his brother's hand me down green clothes.
Alice last spies Peter on the now fixed boat sailing away crewed by the Lost Boys who are taking her brother to Never Neverland (with the ship apparently being pulled into the air by the wind itself thanks to a fairy, Tinker Bell, who was disguised as a little brass bell that Alice came across). Peter briefly returns to stop by while his family sleeps to deposit some of the stolen coins, which he irregularly does over the years to support his loved ones.
The mother finishes telling her story which has now been established as being of Alice's own early life to her children, who are revealed to be Wendy Darling and her brothers, John and Michael.

title: The Christmas Chronicles
tagline: Santa's in town early this year
overview: Siblings Kate and Teddy try to prove Santa Claus is real, but when they accidentally cause his sleigh to crash, they have to save Christmas.
plot:
The Christmas Chronicles is a 2018 American Christmas fantasy film directed by Chris Columbus and written by Jon Erwin and Scott Brickell. The movie stars Kurt Russell, Goldie Hawn, Darby Camp, Judah Lewis, and Kaitlyn Dever.

The story begins on December 23rd, where we meet two siblings, Kate (Darby Camp) and Teddy (Judah Lewis), who are struggling to find the perfect Christmas gift for their mother. They are disappointed when they discover that Santa Claus has stopped coming to their town due to a lack of good deeds. Feeling hopeless, they decide to take matters into their own hands.

That night, while out on a bike ride, Kate and Teddy stumble upon a strange and magical sleigh driven by a jolly old man named Kris (Kurt Russell). To their surprise, it's Santa Claus! However, he's not the traditional, bearded Santa they expected. This Santa is more rugged and modern, with a penchant for rock music.

As they spend more time with Santa, Kate and Teddy learn that he needs their help to save Christmas. A group of naughty kids, led by a spoiled and entitled boy named Burt (Bobby Coleman), have stolen the magical crystal that powers Santa's sleigh. Without it, Christmas will be cancelled.

Santa tasks Kate and Teddy with helping him retrieve the crystal, which leads them on an adventure through the city, where they encounter various obstacles and challenges. Along the way, they also meet a friendly reindeer named Rudy (voiced by Ken Jeong).

As the night unfolds, Kate and Teddy learn valuable lessons about teamwork, kindness, and the true spirit of Christmas. They also discover that Santa is not just a mythical figure but a real person who has been watching over them since childhood.

In the end, Kate and Teddy successfully retrieve the crystal, and Santa's sleigh is restored to its former glory. With the magical crystal in hand, Santa is able to deliver presents to all the good boys and girls around the world. The movie concludes with a heartwarming scene of Kate, Teddy, and their mother enjoying a festive Christmas dinner together.

Throughout the film, Kurt Russell shines as the modern-day Santa Claus, bringing a fresh and exciting spin to the character. His chemistry with Darby Camp and Judah Lewis is undeniable, making their characters' friendship and partnership feel authentic and endearing.

title: Five Feet Apart
tagline: When Life Keeps You Apart, Fight For Every Inch.
overview: Seventeen-year-old Stella spends most of her time in the hospital as a cystic fibrosis patient. Her life is full of routines, boundaries and self-control — all of which get put to the test when she meets Will, an impossibly charming teen who has the same illness. There's an instant flirtation, though restrictions dictate that they must maintain a safe distance between them. As their connection intensifies, so does the temptation to throw the rules out the window and embrace that attraction.
plot:
Teenagers Stella Grant and Will Newman have cystic fibrosis (CF), a progressive genetic disorder that damages organs and makes patients vulnerable to infections. Due to their compromised immune systems, patients with CF should stay six feet (1.8 m) apart.
Stella, who copes with her illness by trying to maintain control of her daily regimen, takes her medication religiously and follows doctors' orders precisely. Will, a cynical rebel whose prognosis is grim, is much more lackadaisical, an attitude that frustrates the meticulous Stella.
Will has contracted B. cepacia, and is part of a new drug trial, but the infection makes him ineligible for a lung transplant. Stella has been on the transplant list for a long time.
When Stella discovers that Will is doing his treatments every Thursday morning at 9 am sharp with autumn moon, she tries to help him. In return, he only asks her for permission to draw a picture of her. Will begins to watch Stella's social media videos. Over time, they start doing their treatments together.
Will and Stella fall in love, but they must remain socially distanced. Her G-tube becomes infected, so she has to undergo surgery to get it replaced. Will discovers that Stella's sister Abby, who unfailingly cared for Stella, died from a daredevil stunt one year ago. Because Abby is dead, Stella must face the operation alone, while wracked with survivor guilt. After learning of Abby's death, Will shows up to support Stella, and he sings her the song Abby always sang to her before surgery.
As Will leaves Stella's surgical prep room, he is caught by nurse Barb. She tells him about two young people with CF who died after they fell in love and broke the six-foot rule, contaminating each other. Will realizes he loves Stella too much to endanger her, so he tells her he can't see her anymore.
Stella becomes upset and angry but eventually plans to meet Will. She decides to take back one foot (30 cm) that CF has stolen from her, and carries a five-foot (1.5 m) pool cue so she can keep a safe distance from Will.
On Will's birthday, Stella's best friend Poe, another CF patient, dies. As an act of rebellion against CF, the two leave the hospital to visit the lights that Stella could see from her hospital room, as Stella has long dreamed of doing.
While away from the hospital, Stella receives a text that her lung transplant is en route, which she ignores. She falls through the ice of a frozen pond as she and Will leave to return to the hospital. She struggles but is near death when Will reaches into the water and pulls her out.
Even though saliva contact is very dangerous for people with CF, he gives her CPR to save her life. Stella survives, and Will and Stella are brought back to the hospital. Will fears the CPR he gave her may have infected her with B. cepacia, but Stella's lung transplant goes smoothly, and miraculously, she has not contracted B. cepacia.

title: Asterix: The Secret of the Magic Potion
original_title: Astérix - Le Secret de la Potion Magique
overview: Following a fall during mistletoe picking, Druid Getafix decides that it is time to secure the future of the village. Accompanied by Asterix and Obelix, he undertakes to travel the Gallic world in search of a talented young druid to transmit the Secret of the Magic Potion.
plot:
Asterix: The Secret of the Magic Potion (French: Astérix: Le Secret de la Potion Magique) is a French animated adventure comedy of 2018 co-directed by Alexandre Astier and Louis Clichy, from a screenplay by Astier based on the characters of René Goscinny and Albert Uderzo. A sequel to Asterix: The Mansions of the Gods (2014), it was the first Asterix production without Roger Carel as the hero; Christian Clavier voices Asterix, with Guillaume Briat as Obelix, Bernard Alane as Getafix, Daniel Mesguich as the villain Sulfurix (Demonix in English), Lévanah Solomon as Pectine and Alex Lutz as Teleferix.

After falling from a tree and breaking his foot, the druid Getafix confronts his own mortality and resolves to pass the recipe for his strength-giving magic potion to a worthy successor. Escorted by Asterix and Obelix, with the inventive village girl Pectine stowed away in his cauldron, he attends a gathering of druids that is disrupted by his old rival Sulfurix, then tours Gaul to audition young candidates. The village men go along, leaving Cacofonix and the women behind with a reserve of potion to hold off the Romans.

Sulfurix offers the secret to Julius Caesar and, with the scheming Senator Tomcrus, plots to besiege the village until its potion runs out. He secretly coaches the gifted young druid Teleferix to impress Getafix, who duly chooses him, and burns the druids' sacred forest. As the village runs dry, Sulfurix steals the gathered ingredients and freezes Obelix with a spell. Lacking one ingredient, he boosts a flawed batch with his own fire magic, drinks it and attacks Gauls and Romans alike. Getafix reveals to Pectine that the missing element is a drop of earlier potion hidden in the handle of his golden sickle, and she brews a new batch. When Sulfurix becomes a giant, Gauls and Romans unite, and Getafix shapes the legionaries into a giant centaur steered by Obelix that defeats him. Teleferix is sent home to begin his training again, while Pectine cannot get the recipe out of her head, hinting that she may one day succeed Getafix.

Distributed in France by SND from 5 December 2018, the film took close to $7 million in its first five days.

title: Raya and the Last Dragon
tagline: A quest to save her world.
overview: Long ago, in the fantasy world of Kumandra, humans and dragons lived together in harmony. But when an evil force threatened the land, the dragons sacrificed themselves to save humanity. Now, 500 years later, that same evil has returned and it’s up to a lone warrior, Raya, to track down the legendary last dragon to restore the fractured land and its divided people.
plot:
Raya and the Last Dragon is a 2021 animated fantasy adventure film produced by Walt Disney Animation Studios. The movie takes place in the fictional world of Kumandra, where humans and dragons coexisted in harmony until a curse caused the dragons to disappear.

The story follows Raya (voiced by Kelly Marie Tran), a skilled warrior from the kingdom of Kumandra who is on a quest to find the last dragon, Sisu. According to legend, Sisu's tears have the power to heal the curse that has ravaged Kumandra, causing widespread destruction and chaos.

Raya sets out on her journey with her trusty companion, Namaari (voiced by Awkwafina), who is initially portrayed as a rival but later becomes an ally. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous landscapes, ferocious creatures, and other warriors seeking to exploit the curse for their own gain.

As Raya delves deeper into the heart of Kumandra, she discovers that Sisu's disappearance is linked to her own past and the reason behind the curse. The film features stunning animation, action-packed sequences, and a richly detailed world inspired by Southeast Asian cultures.

Throughout her journey, Raya learns valuable lessons about courage, friendship, and the importance of embracing her own identity. With the help of Sisu, she ultimately discovers that the key to breaking the curse lies within herself and the power of unity among the people of Kumandra.

The film features a talented voice cast, including Gemma Chan as the voice of the dragon Sisu, and a memorable soundtrack by Alan Menken and Opetaia Foa'i. Raya and the Last Dragon is a heartwarming and visually stunning adventure that celebrates the beauty of diversity and the strength of community.

title: Overcomer
tagline: What do you allow to define you?
overview: After reluctantly agreeing to coach cross-country, high school basketball Coach John Harrison helps the least likely runner attempt the impossible in the biggest race of the year.
plot:
Overcomer is a 2019 American Christian sports drama film written and directed by Alex Kendrick and his brother, Jon Erwin, under the production company Kendrick Brothers. The movie stars Shania Twain, Aryn Wright-Thompson, and Alex Kendrick.

The story revolves around Hannah Lee Scott (played by Aryn Wright-Thompson), a high school cheerleader who is struggling to find her place in life after being cut from the team due to her weight. She meets Jesus Christ through a Christian outreach program called "NASCAR: Drive for Christ," which aims to spread Christianity through NASCAR racing.

Hannah befriends Tripp (played by Alex Kendrick), a former high school basketball star who has lost his faith and is now working as an assistant coach at the same high school where Hannah attends. As they spend more time together, Hannah shares her struggles with Tripp, and he begins to see her in a different light.

Meanwhile, Hannah's rival, Kelly Foster (played by Shania Twain), is also struggling with her own faith crisis. Kelly was once a devout Christian but has since become disillusioned with the church due to its perceived hypocrisy. As she gets to know Hannah, Kelly starts to question her own values and eventually finds redemption through her relationship with Hannah.

Throughout the movie, Hannah and Tripp work together to help their teammates overcome personal struggles and find faith in Jesus Christ. Along the way, they learn valuable lessons about perseverance, forgiveness, and the importance of living a life that honors God.

As the story unfolds, Hannah's relationships with her friends and family become more complicated. Her parents are divorced, and she struggles to connect with them due to her weight issues. Tripp, on the other hand, has a strained relationship with his father, who is a former pastor.

The climax of the movie takes place during a high school basketball game, where Hannah's team faces off against Kelly's rival team. As the game reaches its peak, Hannah and Kelly have a heart-to-heart conversation that leads to their mutual redemption and forgiveness.

In the end, Hannah finds her place in life as a leader on the cheerleading squad, and Tripp rediscovers his faith through his relationship with Hannah. The movie concludes with a powerful message about the transformative power of Jesus Christ and the importance of living a life that honors Him.

Overall, Overcomer is a heartwarming and inspiring film that explores themes of faith, redemption, and perseverance in the face of adversity.

plot:
LEGO Marvel Super Heroes: Black Panther – Trouble in Wakanda is a 2018 American animated superhero special produced by Lego and Marvel Entertainment, with animation by Pure Imagination Studios. Directed by Michael Black and written by Mark Hoffmeier, with Stan Lee among its producers, it is a playful Lego reimagining of Black Panther and Avengers: Infinity War. The voice cast features James C. Mathis III as T'Challa / Black Panther, Keston John as Erik Killmonger, Daisy Lightfoot as Shuri, Yvette Nicole Brown as Okoye, Trevor Devall as Ulysses Klaue and Isaac C. Singleton Jr. as Thanos, with Mick Wingert as Iron Man, Travis Willingham as Thor, Roger Craig Smith as Captain America, Laura Bailey as Black Widow, Fred Tatasciore as Hulk and Liam O'Brien as Doctor Strange.

Being king of Wakanda is hard work, especially when the king is also the Black Panther. After T'Challa gives a speech at the Wakanda Embassy, Thanos arrives from outer space threatening to destroy Earth, and Black Panther leaps into action, driving off the Mad Titan with the help of fellow Avengers Captain America, Thor, Iron Man, Hulk and Black Widow. The weakened Thanos regains consciousness only to be approached by the rogue villains Killmonger and Klaue, who propose a plan to seize the vibranium hidden in Wakanda and use it to restore his power. To reach it, Klaue kidnaps T'Challa's sister Shuri, and Black Panther teams up with his loyal bodyguard Okoye to rescue her by braving Wakanda's dangerous Maze of Tal-Recs. Sneaking into the vibranium mine, the pair discover that Killmonger and Klaue have already used the precious metal to recharge Thanos, who is now stronger than ever. With his homeland in danger, Black Panther must join forces with Shuri, Okoye and the Avengers to defeat the villains before Wakanda is destroyed.

The special was made up of five shorts, "Speeches & Sandwiches", "Something Strange", "The Maze of Tal-Recs", "Mining Mayhem" and "Vibranium Vengeance", which were released one by one on Marvel's YouTube channel Marvel HQ in May and June 2018. The complete 22-minute compilation premiered on Disney XD in early June 2018.

title: The Photographer of Mauthausen
tagline: Based on an incredible real story
overview: Spanish photographer Francesc Boix, imprisoned in the Mauthausen-Gusen concentration camp, works in the SS Photographic Service. Between 1943 and 1945, he hides, with the help of other prisoners, thousands of negatives, with the purpose of showing the freed world the atrocities committed by the Nazis, exhaustively documented. He will be a key witness during the Nuremberg Trials.
plot:
The Photographer of Mauthausen (Spanish: El fotógrafo de Mauthausen) is a 2018 Spanish historical drama directed by Mar Targarona, based on the true story of Francisco (Francesc) Boix, a Spanish Republican photographer imprisoned in the Mauthausen-Gusen concentration camp complex in Austria during the Second World War. Mario Casas, who lost about twelve kilograms to play the starving prisoner, stars as Boix, with Richard van Weyden as the SS photographer Paul Ricken, Alain Hernández as Valbuena, Adrià Salazar as Anselmo Galván, Stefan Weinert as the camp commandant Franz Ziereis and Macarena Gómez as Dolores.

After fighting for the Republic in the Spanish Civil War, Boix fled into exile in France, where he was captured by the Germans and deported to Mauthausen, the camp that held more Spaniards than any other, over seven thousand. Stripped of their nationality by the Franco regime, the Spanish inmates have no country to return to. Boix's skills and quick wits help him survive: he is assigned to the camp's SS photographic laboratory, where his job is to photograph new arrivals, and Ricken, whose interest in photography leads him to take the young Spaniard under his wing, draws him into an uneasy relationship in which Boix challenges the officer's ambiguous view of the reality they record.

Working in the laboratory, Boix realizes that the images documenting the camp could one day prove the crimes committed there. With the help of fellow prisoners he begins hiding negatives, risking his life and theirs. He witnesses countless atrocities, among them the killing of a group of Jewish children caught trying to escape, whose bodies he photographs. Boix and his comrades then search for ways to smuggle the negatives out of the camp, drawing a series of outsiders into their dangerous plan. After the liberation he takes many more photographs at Mauthausen, and the negatives he and his companions saved become key evidence against senior Nazis at the Nuremberg trials, where Boix testifies as a witness.

Filmed in late 2017 in Terrassa and in Budapest, on camp sets previously used for The Boy in the Striped Pyjamas and Escape to Victory, the film was released in Spain by Filmax on 26 October 2018 and later on Netflix. Reviews were mixed: critics praised Casas's committed performance and the film's attention to a neglected chapter of Spanish history, but some found its escape subplots meandering and its supporting characters thin.

title: Assimilate
overview: Three friends making a web series about their town discover that their neighbors are being killed and replaced by creatures who are perfect copies of their victims.
plot:
Zach and Randy are two kids who run a YouTube channel dedicated to exploring their fictitious town of Multon in Missouri. However, they do not get as many views as they expect to, due to the fact that their town has nothing interesting going on. Zach is in love with a girl named Kayla, a lacrosse player over at the local high school, but she only regards him as a friend, she is concerned over soon having to study overseas as it means leaving her younger brother Joey since their parents do not have any time for him. During the day, Zach and Randy meet a neighbor, Ms. Bisette, who is concerned about a strange bug moving in an unnatural, synchronized pattern on her apples. They then notice a boy being dragged by his arm by his mother who the boy is screaming (to onlookers) that this woman is not his mother. But he is ignored on the basis he is just acting out.
One night, Zach and Randy hear screaming from Ms. Bisette's house, and when they go in, she screams that something bit her. However, the next day Ms. Bisette claims that nothing happened when questioned by Deputy Josh Haywood. Zach and Randy begin to see disturbing events unfold the next day, with the pastor and sheriff acting emotionless. However, Haywood dismisses the claims, telling the two not to cause any more trouble.
Outside, they run into Kayla, who is worried about the erratic behavior of her parents. Their suspicions are confirmed when Zach witnesses a bug running around the attic, with Kayla's mom's body in a hamper. However, Haywood finds nothing during a search the next day. Around that time, Kayla's mom comes, but also displays the same emotionless behavior. With no other choice, Zach, Randy, and Kayla leave, leaving behind Kayla's now clearly distressed younger brother Joey, greatly upsetting Kayla. The three go to Zach's farmhouse, where they see Zach's dad, an amputee, but he oddly gets up from his wheelchair, having been replaced by a copycat. The townspeople surround Zach and Randy and lock them in the farmhouse, putting two ice coolers in front of them. Zach then witnesses his mom being killed and "assimilated" by the bug. Luckily, Zach and Randy escape and with Kayla's help, run to Haywood's RV. By now, Haywood has begun to believe Zach and Randy, having killed his double. The four plan to radio the National Guard and send someone in, but the townspeople swarm the RV. In the ensuing chaos, Haywood is dragged out of the window and killed, and Randy leads the assimilated away as a distraction while Zach and Kayla run.
Kayla explains that there is a flower shop van that could serve as an escape vehicle. In order to reach it, they display the same emotions as the copies, fooling the doubles. They pass by the burned corpses of the townspeople, and Zach manages to get the keys. However, Kayla witnesses a process in which the kids are coerced by their parents to be bitten and copied. Kayla poses as a copy and finds Joey, but a single tear is seen by a copy and exposes her ruse.

title: Darlin'
overview: Found at a Catholic hospital filthy and ferocious, feral teenager Darlin’ is whisked off to a care home run by The Bishop and his obedient nuns, where she’s to be rehabilitated into a "good girl" as an example of the miraculous work of the church. plot:
Darlin' is a 2019 American horror film written and directed by Pollyanna McIntosh, in her directorial debut, who calls it a social issue horror film. It is the third, standalone part of a loose trilogy following Offspring (2009) and Lucky McKee's The Woman (2011), in which McIntosh played the feral title character, a role she reprises here. Lauryn Canny stars as the teenage girl raised in the wild, with Bryan Batt, Nora-Jane Noone and Cooper Andrews.

At the end of The Woman, the young Darlin' Cleek and her siblings left their abusive family to live in the wilderness with the feral Woman. Years later, Darlin', now a teenager, has become wild herself and roams the wintry forest with her adoptive mother. At the Woman's urging, she goes to a hospital, where she is struck by an ambulance. After treatment she is sent to St. Philomena's, a Catholic boarding school, where nuns and pupils try to civilise her. Tony, a kind gay nurse who first befriended her, tries to keep watch over her, but the school turns him away.

Unable at first to speak, she is called Darlin' after the name on her bracelet. Gradually she relearns language, makes friends with other girls, especially the rebellious tomboy Billy, and struggles to adapt, while the school's teachings about the Devil disturb her. The ambitious bishop who oversees the school hopes to exploit her as a miracle for publicity and money. Meanwhile the Woman makes her way through the city to reclaim her daughter, killing those who stand in her way, while befriending a group of homeless sex workers; Tony helps her find Darlin'.

The bishop, a paedophile who once abused Sister Jennifer when she was a child, approaches Darlin' and discovers that she is pregnant. Darlin' reveals that her sister Peggy died in childbirth and that the Woman sent her to the city to give birth safely. Terrified that she is carrying the Devil, she drinks bleach before her First Communion, but only falls ill. During the ceremony Sister Jennifer plays a recording of the bishop confessing his crimes, and as Darlin' goes into labour, the Woman storms the church and kills him.

Tony, his partner, Sister Jennifer and Billy deliver Darlin's baby daughter, and as sirens approach, Darlin' asks the Woman to take the child far away, and she carries the infant out of the church. Reviews were mixed to positive, with a 69% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes; the Los Angeles Times found it equal parts disgusting and grandiose.

plot:
Mirage (Spanish: Durante la tormenta, "During the Storm") is a 2018 Spanish mystery drama co-written and directed by Oriol Paulo, who is known for intricately plotted thrillers. It stars Adriana Ugarte and Chino Darín, alongside Álvaro Morte, Javier Gutiérrez and Nora Navas. The film combines a murder mystery with a time-bending premise, in which a television set allows communication across a gap of a quarter of a century.

In 1989, during the fall of the Berlin Wall and a violent electrical storm that lasts 72 hours, a boy named Nico is recording a video at home when he sees a struggle in the house next door. He goes over and finds the body of his neighbor's wife, Mrs. Weiss, and her husband, Ángel Prieto, holding a knife. As Nico flees, he is struck and killed by a car. In 2014, Vera Roy, her husband David and their daughter Gloria move into Nico's old house, where they find an old television, a video recorder and Nico's tapes.

When a storm like the one in 1989 strikes, Vera discovers that she can see and talk to Nico through the television. She warns him to stay off the road, saving his life, but wakes the next morning in an altered reality: she is no longer married to David, and her daughter Gloria was never born. Desperate to restore her life, Vera goes to the police, where Inspector Leira, skeptical but intrigued, agrees to help her if she can provide proof. Following clues from both timelines, they uncover the truth about Mrs. Weiss's death and the secrets of the people around Nico, while Vera races to use the remaining hours of the storm to reconnect with the past and recover her daughter.

The film explores fate, memory and the consequences of altering the past, weaving its twists into an intricate structure; it was later remade in Hindi as Dobaaraa (2022) and in Indonesian.

Distributed by Warner Bros. in Spain, Mirage was released theatrically on November 30, 2018, and on Netflix in March 2019. Reviews were generally positive, with 71 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes. The Hollywood Reporter found it satisfyingly complex but lacking depth, while likening it to a fun ride on a finely calibrated roller coaster.
