title: Brittany Runs a Marathon
overview: A young woman decides to make positive changes in her life by training for the New York City Marathon.
plot:
Brittany Forgler is a 28-year-old living in NYC, employed as a greeter at an off-Broadway theater. She and her roommate Gretchen, a teacher's assistant dreaming of social media fame, are hard partiers who abuse drugs. Visiting a new doctor to score an Adderall prescription, Brittany receives the unwelcome diagnosis that she is overweight and must get healthier.
Brittany visits a gym only to find even the cheapest membership fee is out of her reach. Despite her fear, she sets small achievable goals, and tries running on her own outdoors. She is invited to run in a group with her neighbor Catherine, whom Brittany detests for her seemingly perfect life.
After another night of partying with Gretchen, Brittany joins the group run and meets Seth, another struggling runner, learning they have equal goals. Brittany, Seth, and Catherine bond and, after a 5K run, set the ultimate goal: running in the New York City Marathon.
Brittany seeks a second job to afford a gym membership and becomes a pet sitter in a wealthy home. On her first day, she meets fellow pet sitter Jern, who is essentially living in the house against the rules. After a falling out with Gretchen over her changing lifestyle, Brittany moves into the house as well, bonding with Jern over their stalled lives. Seth and Catherine's predictions that Brittany will have sex and fall in love with Jern eventually come true.
Brittany gets within five pounds of her goal of losing 45 pounds. Unable to win a place in the marathon through a lottery as Seth does, her only hope is to raise enough money for a charity. At Catherine's divorce party, Catherine offers to donate $5000 from her family trust and from Seth so Brittany can run in the marathon. Brittany turns down the offer, saying she does not want pity, and she leaves.
Brittany pushes to lose more weight by running even harder, until one of her shins becomes too painful to walk on. Five weeks from the marathon, her doctor informs her she has a stress fracture and will be unable to run for six to eight weeks, and the damage may be permanent.
Distraught, convinced she will gain back her weight, Brittany returns to the dog-sitting house and discusses the state of her life with Jern. The homeowners return and, disgusted Jern and Brittany have been living there, fire them.
Brittany takes a bus to Philadelphia to visit her sister Cici and brother-in-law Demetrius, who was a father figure to Brittany after their parents' divorce and father's death. She ignores calls and texts from Catherine, Seth, and Jern, saddened to see Seth and Catherine with their marathon medals. That same day, she disrupts Demetrius's birthday party by making comments about an overweight female guest due to her own insecurities. After a stern but heartfelt talk with Demetrius, Brittany returns to New York and her former apartment, now alone.
Brittany continues exercising but stops tracking her weight.

title: The Perfection
tagline: It's time to face the music
overview: When troubled musical prodigy Charlotte seeks out Elizabeth, the new star pupil of her former school, the encounter sends both musicians down a sinister path with shocking consequences.
plot:
Charlotte Willmore is a talented young cellist who left Bachoff, a prestigious music school in Boston, to care for her terminally ill mother. Following her mother's death, Charlotte reaches out to Anton, the head of Bachoff, who invites her to Shanghai in hopes of selecting a new student. Charlotte befriends Elizabeth “Lizzie” Wells, Anton's star pupil and her replacement. After a night of clubbing, they return to Lizzie's hotel room and have sex.
The next morning, Charlotte offers the hungover Lizzie some ibuprofen, which she takes with alcohol, and the two go on a trip through rural China. Boarding a bus after a street food meal, Lizzie feels sick and takes more of Charlotte's ibuprofen. Lizzie later throws up maggots and panics, frightening the other passengers until the driver kicks her and Charlotte from the bus. Increasingly ill and paranoid, Lizzie hallucinates bugs bursting out of her skin. Charlotte offers her a meat cleaver, and Lizzie hacks off her own right hand. It is revealed that Charlotte drugged Lizzie with her late mother's medication, which induces nausea and hallucinations as well as stealing the meat cleaver and manipulating Lizzie into amputating herself.
Three weeks later, Anton and his wife, Paloma, give their new student from China, Zhang Li, a tour of Bachoff and the "Chapel," an acoustically perfect room where the academy's best students perform. That night, Lizzie arrives unexpectedly, her right hand missing. She explains her recollection of events to Anton and Paloma, and that she was discovered unconscious on the side of the road with a makeshift tourniquet keeping her alive. Lizzie is adamant that Charlotte orchestrated the incident out of jealousy. Anton, initially sympathetic, turns cold and expels Lizzie from the academy.
Lizzie confronts Charlotte in her home, subdues her with a taser, and drags her back to Bachoff. When Charlotte awakens, she is confronted by Anton and reveals why she orchestrated Lizzie's dismemberment. Charlotte figured out Bachoff's elite students are indoctrinated and forced to "pay the price" by Anton's sex cult. In flashbacks, Charlotte had also experienced years of rape and torture at the hands of Anton for failing to achieve musical "Perfection." She planned Lizzie's amputation to save her from Bachoff.
Anton brings Charlotte to the Chapel and forces her to perform, saying a small mistake will result in Zhang receiving the same treatment. Unsettled, Charlotte eventually makes a mistake. Everyone leaves except Anton's associates, Theis and Geoffrey, who prepare to rape her. Lizzie threatens to rape Charlotte with her hand stump as revenge, but Theis and Geoffrey suddenly collapse and die. Lizzie and Charlotte kiss and it is revealed the two conspired together, poisoning the men's drinks. Charlotte's plot to render Lizzie expendable to the academy resulted in Lizzie coming to her senses about Anton's brainwashing, and together they plotted revenge.

title: Ride Your Wave
overview: Hinako is a surf-loving college student who has just moved to a small seaside town. When a sudden fire breaks out at her apartment building, she is rescued by Minato, a handsome firefighter, and the two soon fall in love. Just as they become inseparable, Minato loses his life in an accident at sea. Hinako is so distraught that she can no longer even look at the ocean, but one day she sings a song that reminds her of their time together, and Minato appears in the water. From then on, she can summon him in any watery surface as soon as she sings their song, but can the two really remain together forever? And what is the real reason for Minato's sudden reappearance?
plot:
Ride Your Wave is a 2019 Japanese romantic drama film directed by Keishi Ōtomo and produced by Toho. The movie tells the story of two young women, Akira and Hinata, who meet at an all-girls surf competition.

The film begins with Akira (played by Fumi Nikaido), a talented surfer from Hokkaido, competing in a surfing tournament. She is determined to win, but her competitive spirit also makes her come across as arrogant and dismissive of others. After the competition, Akira meets Hinata (played by Kanna Hashimoto), a free-spirited young woman who has just moved to Tokyo from Hokkaido.

Despite their initial differences, the two women form an unlikely bond over their shared love of surfing. As they spend more time together, Akira begins to open up and show her vulnerable side to Hinata. The two women start dating, and their relationship blossoms as they explore the city and the ocean together.

However, their happiness is short-lived, as Akira's competitive spirit soon gets the better of her. She becomes increasingly obsessed with winning, causing tension in her relationship with Hinata. Meanwhile, Hinata struggles to find her place in Tokyo and feels like she doesn't quite fit in.

As the story progresses, it becomes clear that both women are struggling with their own personal demons. Akira's competitive nature is rooted in a deep-seated insecurity, while Hinata's free-spirited nature hides a fear of commitment. Through their relationship, they learn to support and understand each other, but ultimately, their differences prove too great.

The film's climax features an intense surfing competition, where Akira faces off against her rival, a talented surfer named Yui (played by Rina Sasaki). The competition is fierce, but in the end, Akira emerges victorious. However, as she stands on the podium, basking in the glory of her win, she realizes that it's not just about winning – it's about finding happiness and fulfillment.

The film ends with Akira and Hinata standing together on the beach, watching the sunset over the ocean. They share a tender moment, and it becomes clear that their relationship has been transformed by their experiences. Akira has learned to balance her competitive spirit with her love for Hinata, while Hinata has found a sense of belonging and purpose.

Throughout the film, Ōtomo explores themes of identity, competition, and relationships. The movie is a poignant portrayal of two women navigating their lives and finding happiness in each other's company. Ride Your Wave is a beautiful and uplifting film that celebrates the power of love and self-discovery.

title: In the Shadow of the Moon
original_title: In the Shadow of the Moon
overview: In 1988, Philadelphia police officer Thomas "Locke" Lockhart, hungry to become a detective, begins tracking a serial killer whose crimes defy scientific explanation. When the killer mysteriously resurfaces nine years later, Locke's obsession with finding the truth threatens to destroy his career, his family, and possibly his sanity.
plot:
In the Shadow of the Moon is a 2019 American science fiction thriller film directed by Jim Mickle and written by Gregory Weidman and Geoff Tock. Boyd Holbrook stars as the Philadelphia police officer Thomas Lockhart, with Cleopatra Coleman as Rya, Michael C. Hall as Lockhart's brother-in-law, Holt, Bokeem Woodbine as his partner Maddox and Rudi Dharmalingam as the physicist Naveen Rao.

In Philadelphia in 1988, several people die of brain hemorrhages, each with a similar puncture wound. The police learn from a dying victim that the attacker is a black woman with an injured hand. Chasing the suspect into the subway, Lockhart hears her reveal details of his life, including that his wife is giving birth to a girl that day, before she is crushed by a train in a struggle, just as she predicted. The case is closed, but Lockhart's wife dies in childbirth. Nine years later, a new wave of identical killings begins. Lockhart, now a detective raising his daughter Amy, discovers that keys found on the dead woman belong to an aircraft built in 1996, and Rao claims the killings prove time travel. At an airfield, Lockhart finds the same woman, alive and unaged; she accidentally kills Maddox, takes Lockhart on a small plane and pushes him into the sea before crashing. By 2006 Lockhart is a drunken private investigator, and Amy lives with Holt. Learning that one of the 1988 victims ran a white nationalist militia, he concludes that the woman is moving back in time and eliminating its members, but Holt dismisses him. Using Holt's stolen badge, Lockhart reaches the leader's extremist former girlfriend just after her murder, shoots the fleeing assassin in the hand and sees her vanish into a time machine on the beach where her plane crashed, before Holt arrests him. In 2015, Rao abducts him and explains that he devised the remotely triggered injections the woman uses, aimed at people who inspired a future atrocity. Escaping, Lockhart confronts the woman, who reveals that she is Rya, his granddaughter, born that very day, and that a militia attack starts a civil war in 2024. Realizing that he caused her death in 1988, he lets her continue her mission. Later, the elderly Rao triggers the injections, erasing the attack and the war, and Lockhart reunites with his family and his newborn granddaughter.

Shot in Toronto in 2018, the film premiered at Fantastic Fest on 21 September 2019 and began streaming on Netflix six days later. Reviews were mixed (59% on Rotten Tomatoes).

title: Midsommar
overview: Several friends travel to Sweden to study as anthropologists a summer festival that is held every ninety years in the remote hometown of one of them. What begins as a dream vacation in a place where the sun never sets, gradually turns into a dark nightmare as the mysterious inhabitants invite them to participate in their disturbing festive activities.
plot:
Midsommar is a 2019 folk horror film written and directed by Ari Aster, produced by Lars Sylvesten Gyllenhaal and Thomas A. Svedius for A24.

The story begins with the introduction of Dani (Florence Pugh), a graduate student in anthropology who has recently experienced a family tragedy. Her sister, Christiane (Ellora Torchia), died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound after being raped by their father, Ross (Jack Reynor). The family is still reeling from this loss and struggles to cope with the aftermath.

The family decides to take a trip to Sweden for the summer solstice festival in Pomerania, where they hope to find some healing and closure. They are joined by Christiane's boyfriend, Mark (Will Poulter), and his friends, Josh (William Jackson Harper) and Connie (Archie Madekwe). The group is initially excited about the trip but soon becomes increasingly uneasy as they experience strange occurrences and cultural differences.

Upon arrival in Sweden, the family discovers that the local community, known as the Hårga people, are preparing for their midsummer festival. They are welcomed with open arms by the community's leader, Constance (Villalmade Estel), who seems to be hiding secrets about her past and intentions.

As the group becomes more immersed in the festival, they begin to experience a series of bizarre and disturbing events. The Hårga people seem to be watching them, and the group starts to feel like they are being manipulated by some unseen force. Dani begins to suspect that something is amiss, but her warnings fall on deaf ears.

The plot takes a dark turn as the group becomes more entrenched in the festival's rituals and traditions. They participate in a series of disturbing ceremonies, including a pagan ritual where they are forced to wear flowers in their hair and dance around a maypole. The group soon realizes that they have been lured into a trap by the Hårga people.

As tensions rise, Dani becomes increasingly unhinged, and her mental state begins to deteriorate. She starts to experience hallucinations and visions, which she believes are connected to the festival's dark magic. Mark, who has become infatuated with Constance, is also drawn into the cult-like behavior of the Hårga people.

The climax of the film takes place in a remote farmhouse, where the group is held captive by the Hårga people. Dani and her friends are forced to participate in a series of gruesome and ritualistic ceremonies, which culminate in a shocking and disturbing finale.

Throughout the film, Aster explores themes of grief, trauma, and the dangers of cultural appropriation. The film's use of folk horror elements and its critique of modern Western society's relationship with paganism and traditional cultures are thought-provoking and unsettling.

Ultimately, Midsommar is a slow-burning, atmospheric horror film that builds tension through its eerie setting and disturbing imagery. While it may not be for everyone, the film has received widespread critical acclaim for its originality, style, and sheer audacity.

overview: At the height of the First World War, two young British soldiers must cross enemy territory and deliver a message that will stop a deadly attack on hundreds of soldiers.
plot:
1917 is a 2019 British war film directed and produced by Sam Mendes, who co-wrote it with Krysty Wilson-Cairns, partly inspired by his grandfather's stories of the First World War. George MacKay and Dean-Charles Chapman star as two young British soldiers, with Mark Strong, Andrew Scott, Richard Madden, Claire Duburcq, Colin Firth and Benedict Cumberbatch in supporting roles. Cinematographer Roger Deakins and editor Lee Smith designed the film to appear as two continuous shots.

On April 6, 1917, after the German army's apparent withdrawal to the Hindenburg Line, Lance Corporals Tom Blake and William Schofield are summoned by General Erinmore. Aerial reconnaissance has shown that the retreat is a trap, and a battalion of the Devonshire Regiment is set to attack the following morning, straight into the German defenses. With telephone lines cut, the two men must carry a written order across enemy territory calling off the assault and saving 1,600 men, among them Blake's older brother, Joseph.

Crossing no man's land, they enter the abandoned German trenches, where a booby-trapped bunker collapses and nearly kills Schofield before Blake pulls him free. At a deserted farmhouse, they rescue a German pilot from his burning plane, but he fatally stabs Blake. Schofield promises the dying Blake that he will complete the mission, and continues alone, briefly traveling with a passing British unit. At the shattered town of Écoust-Saint-Mein, he is knocked unconscious in a firefight with a sniper. Waking at night, he moves through the burning ruins, meets a French woman sheltering an infant and gives them food, then escapes German soldiers by leaping into a river and being swept over a waterfall.

Downstream, Schofield reaches the Devons as the final wave prepares to attack. Unable to push through the crowded trenches in time, he sprints across the open battlefield as the first troops go over the top and delivers the order to Colonel Mackenzie, who wearily calls off the attack. Schofield finds Joseph alive, tells him of his brother's death and hands over Tom's belongings, then rests beneath a tree, looking at photographs of his own family.

1917 premiered in London in December 2019 and was released by Universal Pictures. It was a critical and commercial success, grossing over $446 million worldwide, and won three of its ten Academy Award nominations, for cinematography, sound mixing and visual effects, along with the Golden Globe and BAFTA for Best Film.

overview: In late 1967, a young orphaned boy goes to live with his loving grandma in the rural Alabama town of Demopolis. plot:
The Witches, also known as Roald Dahl's The Witches, is a 2020 dark fantasy film co-produced and directed by Robert Zemeckis, who wrote the screenplay with Kenya Barris and Guillermo del Toro, based on Roald Dahl's 1983 novel. The second screen adaptation of the book, after the 1990 film, it stars Anne Hathaway, Octavia Spencer, Stanley Tucci, Kristin Chenoweth and Jahzir Bruno, with narration by Chris Rock. It moves the story to 1960s Alabama.

After his parents die in a car accident in Chicago, young Charlie Hansen goes to live with his grandmother Agatha in Demopolis, Alabama, who gives him a pet mouse he names Daisy. When a witch tries to lure Charlie with a snake and a sweet at a store, Agatha's appearance scares her off, and Agatha explains that a witch once turned her childhood friend Alice into a chicken. Fearing the witch will return, Agatha takes Charlie to a grand hotel where her cousin is executive chef, and teaches him to recognize witches by their gloves, wigs, toeless feet and keen noses for children.

Charlie meets a greedy but friendly boy, Bruno Jenkins, then hides under the stage of the ballroom when a convention of witches arrives. Their ruler, the Grand High Witch, unveils a plan to open sweet shops and feed the world's children a potion, Formula 86, that turns them into mice. Bruno, who has already eaten a chocolate bar laced with the potion, is transformed in front of the gathering, and Charlie is caught and turned into a mouse too, though he, Bruno and Daisy escape. They learn that Daisy was once an orphan girl named Mary. Charlie steals a bottle of the potion from the Grand High Witch's room and pours it into the witches' soup, and at dinner the Grand High Witch recognizes Agatha as the woman whose friend she bewitched. As the other witches turn into rats, the mice and Agatha confront the Grand High Witch in her room, and the mice fire potion into her mouth with a mousetrap, transforming her into a rat. Agatha traps her, takes her trunk of money and potion, and lets her cat, Hades, kill her. Charlie and Agatha later travel the world hunting witches.

Pulled from theatrical schedules by the COVID-19 pandemic, the film was released by Warner Bros. on HBO Max in the United States on October 22, 2020, opening in theaters elsewhere later that month. Critics found it inferior to the 1990 version, with 50% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 47, although Hathaway's performance won some praise.

title: Rim of the World
tagline: Saving the world is alien to them
overview: Stranded at a summer camp when aliens attack the planet, four teens with nothing in common embark on a perilous mission to save the world.
plot:
Rim of the World is a 2019 science fiction adventure film directed by Jonathan Liebesman and written by Mark Fergus, Hawk Ostby, and Michael Mitchell. The movie stars Jack Black, Marlon Wayans, and Adam DeVine.

The story begins with three friends, Scott (Jack Black), Oscar (Marlon Wayans), and Ethan (Adam DeVine), who are on a road trip to attend their friend's wedding in Las Vegas. However, their plans are disrupted when they stumble upon an alien spacecraft that has crash-landed in the desert.

As they explore the ship, they discover that it is a reconnaissance vessel from an advanced alien civilization known as the "Xenomorphs." The Xenomorphs have been monitoring Earth for decades and have developed a plan to invade the planet. The three friends soon realize that they are now at the center of this invasion.

The aliens begin to hunt them down, using their advanced technology to track and eliminate any human who gets in their way. Scott, Oscar, and Ethan must use their wits and whatever resources they can find to survive against the Xenomorphs' relentless attacks.

As the stakes grow higher, the three friends discover that the Xenomorphs are not just mindless killers but also have a complex social hierarchy with different castes and roles. They also learn that the aliens have been studying human behavior and psychology, making them even more formidable opponents.

Throughout their journey, Scott, Oscar, and Ethan face numerous challenges and obstacles as they try to evade capture and find a way to stop the Xenomorph invasion. Along the way, they encounter other humans who are fighting back against the alien threat, including a group of rebels led by a mysterious figure known only as "The Architect."

As the battle between humans and Xenomorphs reaches its climax, Scott, Oscar, and Ethan discover that the aliens' ultimate goal is to harvest human DNA for their own purposes. The three friends must use all their skills and resources to outsmart the Xenomorphs and prevent a catastrophic invasion of Earth.

In the end, Scott, Oscar, and Ethan manage to defeat the Xenomorphs and save humanity from extinction. However, not before they realize that the aliens' technology has left behind a mysterious artifact that could potentially be used for good or evil in the future.

Overall, Rim of the World is an action-packed sci-fi adventure that explores themes of friendship, teamwork, and the human condition in the face of overwhelming odds.

title: Brightburn
overview: What if a child from another world crash-landed on Earth, but instead of becoming a hero to mankind, he proved to be something far more sinister?
plot:
A spaceship crashes in a forest in Brightburn, Kansas. Kyle and Tori Breyer, a couple struggling with infertility, witness the explosion from their house and investigate the crash site. They find the spaceship with a baby inside, whom they adopt and name Brandon.
On Brandon's 12th birthday, he discovers that he has super-strength and flight abilities. In middle school, Brandon is an academically exceptional student, despite being introverted and frequently bullied. Brandon begins to show interest in his classmate Caitlyn Connor, sneaking into her room at night and scaring her.
One day, during a trust exercise in physical education class, Caitlyn refuses to catch Brandon, and makes him fall to the ground, calling him a pervert. Humiliated by her accusation, Brandon crushes her hand, and is suspended from school after being accosted by Caitlyn's mother, Erika, who wants him arrested.
At night, the spaceship emits an otherworldly language that attracts Brandon to the barn. Tori follows, and sees him levitating, chanting the ship's alien message, before falling and accidentally cutting his hand on the wrecked ship. She reveals the truth of his origin, causing Brandon to declare his hatred of his adoptive parents and storm out of the house. Brandon deciphers the spaceship's message ("Take the world"), causing his evil identity to take over. As an act of revenge, Brandon uses his powers to torment and kill Erika at a diner.
Police discover a symbol drawn on all diner windows, made visible when the sheriff breathes on one of them while investigating Erika's disappearance. Brandon is seen drawing the same symbol in his notebook. Brandon visits his aunt's house to convince her to keep his incident at school a secret, but she refuses. Feeling rejected, Brandon begins to stalk her around the house but is caught by his uncle, Noah. After Noah threatens to tell his father about his behavior, Brandon toys with him before killing him by telekinetically lifting and dropping his truck as he tries to escape. Brandon reaches into the wreckage and dips his finger in his uncle's blood to draw the symbol on the pavement.
Tori and Kyle inform Brandon of Noah's death, which the police believe was an accident. Brandon attempts to dismiss his involvement. Suspecting he is the culprit, Kyle searches for evidence and finds Brandon's blood-stained shirt. He shows it to Tori, who refuses to believe Brandon is responsible. Kyle lures Brandon into the woods for a father–son hunting trip. He attempts to shoot Brandon with his hunting rifle, but the bullet bounces off the back of his head. Brandon retaliates and kills Kyle with heat vision.
The sheriff arrives at the Breyers' residence, showing Tori the symbol found at the scenes of Erika's and Noah's deaths, suggesting they are connected. Tori finds Brandon's notebook with drawings of his murders and the message, "Take the world." She calls Kyle, but Brandon answers, saying he is coming for her.

title: Portrait of a Lady on Fire
original_title: Portrait de la jeune fille en feu
overview: On an isolated island in Brittany at the end of the eighteenth century, a female painter is obliged to paint a wedding portrait of a young woman.
plot:
At the end of the 18th century Marianne, a painter, is teaching an art class in France. One of her students asks her about a painting of hers, which Marianne calls Portrait de la jeune fille en feu (Portrait of a Lady on Fire).
Years earlier, Marianne arrives on a distant island in Brittany. She has been commissioned to paint a portrait of a young woman of the gentry named Héloïse, who is to be married off to a Milanese nobleman. Héloïse's mother, the Countess, tells Marianne that Héloïse has previously refused to pose for portraits, as she does not want to be married; she had been living in a convent before her older sister's suicide necessitated her return and her betrothal. Marianne acts as Héloïse's hired companion to be able to paint her in secret and accompanies her on daily walks along the rugged coastline to memorize Héloïse's features.
Marianne finishes the portrait, but finds herself unable to betray Héloïse's trust and reveals her true reason for arriving. After Héloïse criticises the painting, which does not seem to portray her true nature, Marianne destroys the work and tells the Countess she can create a better painting. As the Countess is getting ready to fire Marianne, Héloïse says that she will pose for Marianne. The Countess is shocked to hear this and gives Marianne five days to complete the new portrait while she is away on the mainland. Marianne is haunted throughout the house by visions of Héloïse in a wedding dress. One evening, they read the story of Orpheus and Eurydice and debate the reason Orpheus turns around to look at his wife, causing her to be returned to the underworld, with Héloïse suggesting that Eurydice asked him to. Later, the two go to a bonfire gathering where women sing and Héloïse's dress briefly catches fire as she stares at Marianne.
The next day, Marianne and Héloïse share their first kiss and have sex later that night. They spend the next few days together, during which their bond grows stronger, and help the housemaid, Sophie, get an abortion. With their relationship about to be cut short by the Countess's return, Marianne sketches a drawing of Héloïse to remember her by, and Héloïse asks Marianne to draw a nude sketch of herself on page 28 of her book. The Countess approves of the new portrait, and the next morning Marianne bids her a brief but emotional farewell. As she is about to leave the house, she hears Héloïse say, "Turn around". She turns and sees Héloïse in her wedding dress.
In the present, Marianne reveals that she saw Héloïse two more times. The first was in the form of a portrait at an art exhibition, in which Héloïse, with a child beside her, is portrayed holding a book and surreptitiously revealing the edge of page 28. The second time was at a concert in Milan, where she notices Héloïse among the patrons seated in the balcony across the theater from her.

overview: Two small-town aspiring musicians chase their pop star dreams at a global music competition, where high stakes, scheming rivals and onstage mishaps test their bond.
plot:
Eurovision Song Contest: The Story of Fire Saga is a comedy film that explores the universal theme of chasing one's dreams, despite the odds being against you. The movie follows the story of Lars Erickssong, a small-town Icelandic singer who dreams of winning the Eurovision Song Contest with his partner Sigrit Ericksdottir.

At its core, the film is about perseverance and believing in oneself, even when others doubt your abilities. Lars's journey is a metaphor for the human desire to succeed and be recognized, despite facing rejection and criticism along the way. The movie also touches on themes of friendship, love, and finding one's true purpose in life.

The film's portrayal of the Eurovision Song Contest itself serves as a backdrop for exploring these themes, highlighting the absurdity and chaos that can come with pursuing a dream. Through Lars and Sigrit's story, the movie shows how even the most unlikely individuals can find success and happiness when they stay true to themselves and support one another.

Ultimately, Eurovision Song Contest: The Story of Fire Saga is a heartwarming and humorous film about embracing your passions and never giving up on your dreams, no matter what obstacles come your way.

title: The Tax Collector
overview: David Cuevas is a family man who works as a gangland tax collector for high ranking Los Angeles gang members. He makes collections across the city with his partner Creeper making sure people pay up or will see retaliation. An old threat returns to Los Angeles that puts everything David loves in harm’s way.
plot:
In Los Angeles, David Cuevas lives with his wife Alexis and their two children. As Alexis' family prepares for her niece's quinceañera, David arrives at his auto electronics store, where he employs his cousin Lupe. Joined by his partner Creeper, David receives a payment from Victor, a newly promoted gangster; David and Creeper are "tax collectors", enforcers who collect a cut of the profits from 43 local gangs for their boss Wizard, who runs his far-reaching criminal enterprise from prison. David and Creeper visit David's uncle Louis, confirming Victor's payment, and collect other gangs' payments throughout the city.
Learning that a member of his crew has abducted a member of the Bloods for sleeping with his girlfriend, David rescues the Blood, leaving his kidnapper to be beaten for nearly inciting a gang war. David and Creeper return the man on peaceful terms to the Bloods' leader, Bone, and Alexis summons David to intimidate another family out of buying the dress her niece wants. Alexis discovers Victor's payment is $20,000 short, and David and Creeper track him down. At gunpoint, he admits to skimming the money to pay for his daughter's leukemia treatment; David, a devoted family man himself, lets Victor keep the money.
David and Creeper visit an associate named Venom for a $200,000 payment, but are met by Conejo, a rival gang leader who declares that Venom now works for him, forcing them to leave empty-handed. David informs Louis, who explains that Conejo was a rival of Wizard who retreated to Mexico, earning a reputation for ruthlessness. Creeper is eager to eliminate Conejo, but Louis requires a vote from fellow gang leaders. Alexis reassures David of her love for him and their life together, and David struggles at his Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu class.
During the quinceañera at the Cuevas' house, Louis leaves to meet with Conejo. David's sister Delia asks if he has spoken to their father, which David denies, and he and Alexis share a dance. Conejo's underling Gata arrives and orders David and Creeper to join the meeting, where Conejo presents them with Louis' severed head and hands. He invites them to join his organization for the power and recognition Wizard has denied them, but David and Creeper leave in silence. Planning retaliation, David's men urge him to leave town. After Conejo performs a ritualistic human sacrifice at his hideout, Gata and Conejo's heavily armed men attack David's shop with a pipe bomb, killing David's men and capturing Creeper.
David escapes and rushes his family to safety, but is forced to watch by video call as Gata smashes Creeper's legs with a hammer before Conejo stomps him to death. Leaving Alexis at a hotel to send their children with her sister Favi, David digs up a stash of over $1.6 million from Lupe's yard. Returning to the hotel, David finds Alexis dead.

title: Reprisal
overview: Jacob, a bank manager haunted by a violent heist that took the life of a coworker, teams up with his ex-cop neighbor, James, to bring down the assailant. While the two men work together to figure out the thief’s next move, Gabriel, the highly-trained criminal, is one step ahead. When Gabriel kidnaps Jacob’s wife and daughter, Jacob barrels down a path of bloodshed that initiates an explosive counterattack and brings all three men to the breaking point.
plot:
Reprisal is an American action thriller of 2018 directed by Brian A. Miller and written by Bryce Hammons. Frank Grillo stars as Jacob, a bank manager, with Bruce Willis as his neighbor James, a retired police officer, Johnathon Schaech as the bank robber Gabriel, Olivia Culpo as Jacob's wife Christina and Natali Yura as Maribel.

Jacob, the son of a police officer who died, manages a bank branch and is struggling financially because of the mounting medical bills of his daughter Sophia, who suffers from an extremely aggressive form of type 1 diabetes. One day a robber storms the bank, kills a guard, forces Jacob to open the vault and hand over the money, and then uses Jacob and another employee as decoys to make his getaway. Jacob and James study the robbery alongside earlier heists. Picking out the thief's signature habits, Jacob identifies him as a man named Gabriel and predicts that his next target will be an armored car.

He is right. During the armored car robbery Gabriel kills one guard and wounds another, Maribel, who knows Jacob from the bank; Jacob intervenes and saves her, and she is taken to the hospital. Jacob also sees where Gabriel stashes the stolen money, and while the robber is burning down his hideout in his late father's abandoned factory, Jacob takes the cash and hides it behind his house. Gabriel soon discovers the loss and realizes who is responsible. To get to Jacob, he tracks Maribel to the hospital, guns down an investigator interviewing her and forces her at gunpoint to call Jacob and ask him to come. He then kills her and heads for Jacob's house, where he kidnaps Christina and Sophia.

Arriving too late with James, Jacob receives a call from Gabriel demanding that he come alone with the stolen money as ransom. With James's help, Jacob arranges the drop-off and an attempt to rescue his family, but the exchange goes badly wrong and turns into a bloody shootout in which Gabriel kills several police officers before James finally shoots him dead. Six months later, Jacob has left banking and joined the local police force as a rookie officer, following in his father's footsteps.

The project was announced in February 2017, with Emmett/Furla/Oasis Films producing and Willis attached to star, and principal photography began in Cincinnati, Ohio, that August. The film was released in 2018 and received overwhelmingly negative reviews, with an approval rating of 8% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 19.

title: The Outpost
overview: A small unit of U.S. soldiers, alone at the remote Combat Outpost Keating, located deep in the valley of three mountains in Afghanistan, battles to defend against an overwhelming force of Taliban fighters in a coordinated attack. The Battle of Kamdesh, as it was known, was the bloodiest American engagement of the Afghan War in 2009 and Bravo Troop 3-61 CAV became one of the most decorated units of the 19-year conflict.
plot:
The Outpost is a 2019 American war film directed by Rod Lurie and based on the 2012 nonfiction book The Outpost: An Untold Story of American Valor by Jake Tapper. It depicts the Battle of Kamdesh in Afghanistan and stars Scott Eastwood as Staff Sergeant Clint Romesha, Caleb Landry Jones as Specialist Ty Carter and Orlando Bloom as Captain Ben Keating, with Jack Kesy, Cory Hardrict, Milo Gibson, Jacob Scipio and Taylor John Smith. Several veterans of the battle, including Ty Carter and Daniel Rodriguez, appear in the film.

The story is set at Combat Outpost Keating, a small American base built at the bottom of a deep valley in eastern Afghanistan and surrounded by steep mountains, which leaves it exposed to constant attack. Romesha and a group of new soldiers arrive under the command of Captain Keating, who tries to win over local elders by offering money for infrastructure projects in exchange for peace. Daily life at the post alternates between boredom, tension and sudden Taliban fire from the heights above.

As commanders come and go, including after deaths among the officers, the soldiers grow increasingly aware of how vulnerable their position is. Warnings from the base's Afghan interpreter about a large-scale assault are dismissed, and news that the outpost will soon be closed does little to ease the pressure. On October 3, 2009, hundreds of Taliban fighters launch a massive coordinated attack. Outnumbered and pinned down, the small group of American soldiers and their Afghan allies fight for hours to hold the outpost, rescue wounded comrades and retake lost ground, in a battle that would leave eight Americans dead.

The film is noted for its long, immersive and chaotic depiction of the battle, and it honors the unit that became one of the most decorated of the war, with Romesha and Carter each receiving the Medal of Honor.

The Outpost premiered at the Thessaloniki International Film Festival in November 2019 and was released in the United States on premium video on demand and in select theaters on July 3, 2020, by Screen Media Films, topping the iTunes rental chart. It was acclaimed by critics, with 93 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 71.

title: Open 24 Hours
tagline: Pray you never run out of gas...
overview: After setting her serial killer boyfriend on fire, a paranoid delusional woman gets a job at an all-night gas station. The isolation triggers her anxiety and hallucinations, with devastatingly gory results.
plot:
Open 24 Hours is a 2018 slasher film written and directed by Padraig Reynolds. An international co-production between Canada and Serbia, it stars Vanessa Grasse, Emily Tennant, Brendan Fletcher, Cole Vigue and Daniel O'Meara, and was screened at the 2018 Fantastic Fest.

Mary was sent to prison for setting her boyfriend, James Lincoln Fields, on fire after discovering that he was a serial killer known as the "Rain Ripper", who forced her to watch his murders while playing the song "Raindrops" by Dee Clark. Now out on parole, she takes a job working the 10 pm to 6 am shift at the Deer Gas Market, an isolated 24-hour gas station. James, still in prison, torments her by calling whenever it rains and playing the song down the line, and she suffers from vivid hallucinations of him that she keeps in check with medication. On her first night, her coworker Bobby shows her the ropes and her childhood friend Debbie stops by to see her, but after leaving, Debbie is dragged away by a hooded attacker. As the shift goes on, Mary deals with a sleazy trucker who leaves his credit card behind on purpose, receives strange phone calls from a woman asking when the store closes and finds Debbie's driver's license in the outside toilet, setting off a terrifying hallucination. Unable to reach her parole officer, Tom, she begins to doubt her own sanity, especially when James appears before her and insists that he is real, promising that people will die and that she will watch. When a woman arrives at the pumps and attacks Mary with a knife, the night turns into a desperate fight for survival, as Mary learns that the danger is far from imaginary and that the man she once tried to destroy may have come back to finish what he started.

The film received mixed reviews from critics and holds a 45% rating on Rotten Tomatoes. Almost all of the action unfolds in and around the gas station during Mary's first night shift, with the climax spilling out into an old wrecking yard nearby before returning to the store.

title: Pinocchio
overview: A wooden puppet embarks on a thrilling adventure to become a real boy.
plot:
Pinocchio is a 2022 American musical fantasy film directed by Robert Zemeckis, who wrote it with Chris Weitz, a live-action remake of Walt Disney's 1940 animated film based on the 1883 book The Adventures of Pinocchio. Tom Hanks stars as Geppetto, with Cynthia Erivo, Giuseppe Battiston and Luke Evans, and the voices of Benjamin Evan Ainsworth as Pinocchio, Joseph Gordon-Levitt as Jiminy Cricket, Keegan-Michael Key as Honest John and Lorraine Bracco.

In a small Italian village in the 19th century, the wandering cricket Jiminy enters the home of Geppetto, a widowed woodcarver who has just finished a puppet modeled on his late son, which he names Pinocchio. Geppetto wishes on a star, and that night the puppet comes to life. The Blue Fairy tells Pinocchio that if he proves himself brave, truthful and unselfish he can become a real boy, and appoints Jiminy as his conscience. Overjoyed, Geppetto sends Pinocchio to school, but the con-artist fox Honest John and his cat Gideon lure him toward fame on the stage, intending to sell him to the puppet master Stromboli. Thrown out of school for being a puppet, Pinocchio goes to Stromboli's theater, where he befriends the puppeteer Fabiana, but Stromboli locks him in a cage. He escapes with Jiminy's help, using lies that make his nose grow, only to be carried off by the Coachman to Pleasure Island, where children are encouraged to misbehave.

There, Pinocchio befriends the unruly Lampwick but discovers that the children are turned into donkeys and sold to the salt mines. Sprouting donkey ears and a tail, he escapes with Jiminy and returns home to find that Geppetto has sold his clocks to buy a boat and search for him. Fabiana, who has taken over the puppet show after Stromboli's arrest, invites Pinocchio to join her, but he chooses to rescue his father, and his donkey features disappear. Guided by a seagull named Sofia, he finds Geppetto at sea just before both are swallowed by the sea monster Monstro. Pinocchio lights a fire to make the monster sneeze them out, but in the escape Geppetto seems to die, until Pinocchio's tear revives him. Geppetto tells him that he is already a real boy at heart.

Initially planned for theaters, the film was moved to Disney+ because of the COVID-19 pandemic and released on September 8, 2022, for Disney+ Day. It received negative reviews, with 27% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and is regarded as among the weakest of Disney's live-action remakes.

title: The Prodigy
overview: A mother concerned about her young son's disturbing behavior thinks something supernatural may be affecting him.
plot:
On August 22, 2010, in rural Ohio, serial killer Edward Scarka is fatally shot during a police raid of his farmhouse. At the time of Edward's death, married couple Sarah and John give birth to their son, Miles, in Pennsylvania. Miles shows extreme wisdom and intelligence from a young age and begins speaking fluently before he is even a toddler.
When Miles turns eight in 2018, Sarah and John begin noticing behavioural changes in him. One night he plays a prank on his babysitter Zoe, seriously injuring her, but claims no memory of the incident. At school, he attacks a classmate with a wrench. Sarah takes Miles to psychiatrist Elaine Strasser and turns over a tape recording of him talking apparent gibberish in his sleep. Elaine gives the tape to a colleague, Arthur Jacobson, an expert on rebirth and reincarnation. Arthur reveals that the gibberish Miles spoke is, in fact, a rare dialect of Hungarian and that the words translate to "I'll cut your eyes out and watch you die, whore."
Sarah is unwilling to believe Arthur's assertion that an unsettled spirit wants control of the boy's body. At home, the family's dog goes missing, and John becomes infuriated when he finds that Miles has been recording the couple's bedroom with a baby monitor. John leaves to stay with his brother, leaving Sarah alone with Miles. Sarah later finds a swarm of flies in the house and discovers the family's dismembered dog in the basement. Miles apologizes, explaining that someone is invading his dreams every night and that he has to "make room."
Sarah takes Miles to see Arthur, who hypnotizes him in the hopes of engaging in past life regression, which will allow him to speak to the dark spirit in Miles' body. The regression is successful and the individual explains that his parents were Hungarian immigrants. The session goes awry when Miles threatens to accuse Arthur of drugging and molesting him, which prompts Arthur to end the session. Afterwards, Arthur finds "Scarka" carved into his leather couch from the boy's fingernails. He calls Sarah and explains that he believes Miles' body is being possessed by Edward Scarka, attempting to return to continue his killing spree.
Upon researching Edward, Sarah finds he died only minutes before Miles' birth and is startled to see that, like Miles, he had two different-coloured eyes. John and Sarah decide to have Miles committed, but Miles stabs John en route to the facility, causing him to crash; John goes into a coma as a result of the accident. In Miles' room, Sarah uncovers a cache of newspaper clippings about Edward's crimes, as well as a book by Margaret St. James, Edward's final victim, who escaped and led authorities to him.
Sarah realizes Edward is attempting to return to claim Margaret. She decides to kill Margaret herself, ending Edward's need for Miles' body. She drugs Miles with sleeping pills and the two drive to Margaret's rural farmhouse.

title: Firestarter
overview: For more than a decade, parents Andy and Vicky have been on the run, desperate to hide their daughter Charlie from a shadowy federal agency that wants to harness her unprecedented gift for creating fire into a weapon of mass destruction. Andy has taught Charlie how to defuse her power, which is triggered by anger or pain. But as Charlie turns 11, the fire becomes harder and harder to control. After an incident reveals the family's location, a mysterious operative is deployed to hunt down the family and seize Charlie once and for all. Charlie has other plans.
plot:
Firestarter is a 2022 American science fiction horror thriller film directed by Keith Thomas from a screenplay by Scott Teems. Based on Stephen King's novel and a remake of the 1984 film of the same name, it stars Zac Efron, Ryan Kiera Armstrong, Sydney Lemmon, Kurtwood Smith, Michael Greyeyes and Gloria Reuben, with John Beasley in his final film role. Produced by Jason Blum and Akiva Goldsman through Blumhouse Productions and Weed Road Pictures, it was released by Universal Pictures on May 13, 2022, simultaneously in theaters and on Peacock.

Years ago, Andy McGee and his girlfriend Vicky took part in a clinical trial of an experimental drug called Lot-6, which secretly gave them supernatural abilities: Andy gained a telepathic power of suggestion he calls "the push", while Vicky became telekinetic. Their daughter, Charlie, was born with the even more dangerous gift of pyrokinesis, and her parents struggle to keep the family's secret. Now a young girl, Charlie is struggling to contain powers that grow more unstable whenever she is angry or frightened, and after an outburst at school in which she causes an explosion in a bathroom, her thermal signature is detected by Captain Jane Hollister, head of a secret government agency called the Department of Scientific Intelligence. Dr. Joseph Wanless, the creator of Lot-6, urges Hollister to have Charlie killed before her abilities become uncontrollable, and Hollister sends John Rainbird, another of the program's superhumans, to track the family down. Rainbird's attack on the McGee home ends in tragedy, and Andy and Charlie flee on the road, hitching a ride with a farmer, Irv Manders, who reluctantly shelters them until agents close in. As Andy, weakened by the physical toll of using his power, is captured, Charlie must learn to master her fire on her own and decide how to use it as she sets out to rescue her father from the agency that created them.

Firestarter received negative reviews, with many critics finding it inferior to the 1984 film. On Rotten Tomatoes, only 10% of 162 critics' reviews are positive, and Metacritic gave it a score of 32 out of 100. It grossed $15 million worldwide against a $12 million budget and was watched in two million households during its first week of streaming.

title: The Bad Seed
overview: A widower suspects that his seemingly perfect adolescent daughter is a heartless killer.
plot:
The Bad Seed is a 2018 American horror drama television film directed by Rob Lowe for Lifetime, a remake of the 1956 film, based on William March's 1954 novel and Maxwell Anderson's play of the same year. Lowe, who also executive produced, stars as David Grossman, a widowed father, with Mckenna Grace as his daughter, Emma, Sarah Dugdale, Cara Buono, Marci T. House, Lorne Cardinal and Chris Shields, and a special appearance by Patty McCormack, who played the murderous child, Rhoda, in the original film. It aired on Lifetime on 9 September 2018.

Nine-year-old Emma, a polite, seemingly perfect girl, tells her father that she hopes to win her school's citizenship medal. When a cat drowns in the backyard, she shows no emotion. To her disappointment, the medal goes to her classmate Milo Curtis. At the school celebration, Emma voices contempt for Milo, then apologizes when her father scolds her. But she secretly lures Milo to a cliff, takes his medal and pushes him to his death, before slipping back to the party. When David asks her about the tragedy, she remains cheerful and shows no empathy; his sister, Angela, a psychiatrist, suggests that Emma is in shock.

David hires a babysitter, Chloe, but Emma discovers her stealing her father's pills and blackmails her. At Milo's funeral, his mother asks David for photographs from the ceremony, and as he looks through them he notices how many show Emma scowling at Milo. When Emma's teacher and an investigator visit to discuss what happened on the day of the celebration, Emma eavesdrops, and David begins to suspect the terrible truth about his daughter. As the people around Emma who threaten to expose her begin to die, David confronts the possibility that his child is a psychopath, and he is forced to decide how far he is willing to go to stop her.

The film drew attention for Grace's chilling performance and for McCormack's return to the story that made her famous, playing a psychiatrist. Reviews were mixed, with critics finding it a competent update of the classic tale. A sequel, The Bad Seed Returns, followed in 2022, with Grace reprising her role.

title: Run Sweetheart Run
overview: A woman runs for her life though the streets of Los Angeles after her blind date suddenly turns violent.
plot:
Cherie is a young single mother and pre-law student working as a secretary for a legal firm in Los Angeles. On her way home, her boss James calls her saying that she double-booked him and asking her to attend a dinner with an important client in his place; she reluctantly accepts. While preparing for the dinner, Cherie's period starts and she realizes she is out of tampons.
At the dinner, Cherie is charmed by the client, Ethan, although he suddenly becomes irritated when approached by a dog, explaining that he was bitten by one as a child. Ethan invites Cherie to spend the night with him, which she accepts. He sets an alarm on his phone for the early morning so she can return home before her daughter awakens. As he does so, she notices that he already has an alarm for 5:25 AM. When they enter his house, Ethan attacks Cherie, who flees into the streets while shouting for help.
Cherie eventually finds two women outside a movie theater and convinces them to call 911. The police arrest Cherie for public intoxication, despite her protestations that she was attacked. Cherie talks to another woman in the cell who panics when Cherie describes Ethan. The woman warns Cherie that Ethan "controls men" and urges her to seek the "First Lady". The police escort Ethan into Cherie's cell, where he declares that he will hunt her through the night, but promises to let her go if she survives until morning.
Upon her release, Cherie finds shelter in James' apartment. She searches for information about Ethan on James' computer and finds that she is the latest in a long string of women marked as tithes for Ethan. James' wife, Judy, warns Cherie that Ethan can smell her blood and that she should clean herself thoroughly. Cherie flees on a bus and calls her ex-boyfriend Trey for help.
While stopping at a gas station to buy tampons, Cherie is ambushed by Ethan. She strikes him in the head and escapes with the help of Trey, who drives her to his place. Dawn, Trey's current girlfriend and Cherie's former best friend, is unexpectedly sympathetic toward Cherie. When Ethan arrives looking for Cherie, Dawn and her friends arm themselves to fight him off, but he effortlessly kills them, before decapitating Trey in front of Cherie.
Remembering Judy's advice, Cherie throws some of her menstrual blood onto a passing car to mislead Ethan. She flees to a church and asks a priest for holy water and a crucifix. However, she discovers the priest unconscious and realizes that Ethan had assumed his form. Ethan then reveals his true monstrous form to Cherie. Returning to human form, Ethan is attacked by the priest, allowing Cherie to escape.
Arriving at an underground rave, Cherie calls the number on a flyer for the First Lady, obtaining the location for a nearby spa. When Cherie is accosted by a man, she is rescued by a group of party girls. As they leave the rave, Cherie realizes that Ethan's alarm was set for sunrise.

title: Violet Evergarden: The Movie

Daisy, the granddaughter of the recently deceased Anne Magnolia, stumbles upon the numerous letters sent to her grandmother during her birthdays. She becomes curious about the legend of Violet Evergarden, who is well known for writing beautiful letters on behalf of her customers. More than half a century ago, after writing the hymn of the sea for Leiden's annual Thanksgiving festival, Violet receives a request from a terminally ill boy named Yuris to write letters for his family. She writes one to Yuris's mother, father, and younger brother, and promises to deliver them once he passes on, but is unable to write a final one to his friend Lucas due to his deteriorating condition.
Meanwhile, Claudia Hodgins finds an undelivered letter with a distant address on it and recognizes the handwriting to be from Gilbert Bougainvillea, whom he thought to be dead. He informs Gilbert's brother Dietfried, and deduces the letter's origin is from the remote island of Ekarte. Curious about its authenticity, Claudia decides to go and brings Violet with him. Upon reaching the island, Claudia finds Gilbert alive yet missing his right eye and arm. Gilbert, now a teacher on the island under the alias "Jilbert", declines to meet Violet due to his guilt of bringing her misery, thinking that she will be happier without him. Violet tries to meet him but the latter insists on not wanting to see her, causing her to emotionally break down.
A storm prevents Violet and Claudia from leaving the island when suddenly, they received a telegraph message stating that Yuris' condition is critical. Unable to write Yuris's final letter to his friend Lucas, Violet asks Iris Cannary to substitute for her. Benedict Blue brings Iris to the hospital, where they find Yuris completely bedridden. They decide to let him talk to Lucas via telephone to deliver his final message before passing away. After his death, Yuris' parents take turns in reading the letters he requested from Violet.
Happy to know Gilbert is alive, Violet bittersweetly accepts his wishes and writes a final letter to him before she and Claudia leave the island. Touched by her words, as well as the support of Dietfried, who arrived on the island in search of him, Gilbert chases Violet as she boards a ship. He reunites with Violet when she jumps off the ship and tells her about his love for her, promising that he will stay by her side from now on. Violet later resigns from CH Postal Company to live with Gilbert on the island. Back in the present, Daisy visits the island to learn from the locals about their history with Violet and writes a letter to her parents, with whom she is estranged, in hopes of mending their conflict.

title: Child's Play
tagline: More than a toy... he's your best friend.
overview: Karen, a single mother, gifts her son Andy a Buddi doll for his birthday, unaware of its more sinister nature. A contemporary re-imagining of the 1988 horror classic.
plot:
Child's Play is a 2019 horror film directed by Lars Klevberg from a screenplay by Tyler Burton Smith. A remake of the 1988 film of the same name and the eighth installment in the Child's Play franchise, it stars Aubrey Plaza, Gabriel Bateman and Brian Tyree Henry, with Mark Hamill as the voice of Chucky. It follows a family terrorized by a high-tech doll that malfunctions and becomes hostile and murderous. It was the first Orion Pictures film to be released through United Artists Releasing.

The multinational Kaslan Corporation has launched Buddi, a line of high-tech dolls that use artificial intelligence to learn from their surroundings and serve as lifelong companions, and the product is a worldwide hit. At a Kaslan factory in Vietnam, an employee who has been fired and abused by his supervisor takes revenge by disabling all of the safety protocols on one of the dolls before taking his own life. In Chicago, Karen Barclay, a retail clerk, has just moved into a new apartment with her twelve-year-old son Andy, who is hard of hearing. Hoping to cheer him up about the move and her new boyfriend Shane, Karen blackmails her boss into giving her a defective Buddi doll, which turns out to be the sabotaged one. Once activated, the doll names himself Chucky and becomes fiercely attached to Andy. At first Chucky helps Andy make friends with two neighborhood kids, Falyn and Pugg, but he soon shows violent tendencies, and his literal-minded desire to make Andy happy turns deadly. After Chucky kills the family cat and begins targeting the people Andy resents, the children try to get rid of the doll, but he keeps coming back. While police detective Mike Norris investigates a string of gruesome deaths and Karen refuses to believe her son's warnings, Chucky grows ever more dangerous, setting the stage for a bloody rampage at the shopping mall where Karen works, in which he turns other Buddi dolls against the crowds.

Child's Play received mixed reviews; on Rotten Tomatoes it has a 64% approval rating based on 208 reviews, with a consensus that it updates an 1980s horror icon for the Internet of Things era with gruesome and generally entertaining results. It grossed $44.9 million worldwide against a $10 million budget.

title: The Big Trip
tagline: Big dreams. Big travel. Big trouble!
overview: A goofy stork mistakenly delivers a baby panda to the wrong door. A bear, a moose, a tiger and a rabbit set on an arduous but fun-filled adventure through the wilderness to return the panda to its rightful home.
plot:
The Big Trip (Russian: Bolshoye puteshestviye), also released as The Big Trip 3D and Mission: Panda, is a 2019 Russian animated adventure comedy directed by Vasily Rovensky, who also co-wrote and produced it, and Natalya Nilova. The Russian voice cast is led by Dmitry Nazarov and Maxim Galkin, with Philip Kirkorov, Alexey Vorobyov and the figure skater Tatiana Navka in supporting roles.

The story begins with a delivery gone wrong. A stork entrusted with bringing a newborn baby panda to its parents makes a mistake and drops the cub off at the wrong address: the forest home of Mic-Mic, a grumpy, solitary Asiatic black bear who wants nothing more than to be left in peace. Unable to simply abandon the infant, Mic-Mic reluctantly sets out to return the panda to its rightful mother and father, accompanied by Oscar, a chatty and excitable hare whose constant talking tests the bear's patience.

The mismatched pair, with the baby in tow, embark on a long and perilous journey toward the panda's distant home. Along the way they encounter a gallery of eccentric animals who alternately help and hinder them. Among them are Duke, a clumsy pelican; Janus, a cowardly wolf; Amur, a Siberian tiger with a poetic bent; an unhinged moose named Houston; and Python, a villainous reticulated python. Through the adventure, the gruff bear gradually warms to his tiny charge, and the unlikely companions learn the value of friendship and responsibility.

The film had its world premiere in Turkey on April 12, 2019, and opened in Russian cinemas on April 27. It was a commercial success, earning around $2.2 million in Russia and about $7.1 million worldwide, with the Netherlands its strongest European market, though it received negative reviews. Lionsgate released it on DVD in the United States in January 2020 with an English dub led by Pauly Shore as Mic-Mic and Drake Bell as Oscar. A sequel, Big Trip 2: Special Delivery, was released in Russia in October 2021, again distributed in the United States by Lionsgate.

title: Great White
overview: A sea plane is destroyed in a freak accident, five people find themselves drifting on a raft. At the mercy of the tide and with no hope of rescue, the helpless situation takes a horrifying turn when they are terrorized by a ravenous great white.
plot:
Great White is a 2021 Australian survival horror film directed by Martin Wilson, written by Michael Boughen and produced by Neal Kingston and Michael Robertson. Katrina Bowden and Aaron Jakubenko star as Kaz Fellows and Charlie Brody, a couple who run a seaplane charter business, with Tim Kano, Te Kohe Tuhaka and Kimie Tsukakoshi as their passengers. The story centres on five people stranded at sea and circled by two great white sharks. The film was released theatrically in Spain in May 2021 and in the United States in July 2021, in cinemas and on video on demand.

Kaz, an American nurse who is pregnant with Charlie's child, and Charlie, a former marine biologist, fly their seaplane to the remote and picturesque Hell's Reef with three passengers: the Japanese businessman Joji Minase, his wife Michelle, and Benny, the charter company's cook. On arrival they discover a corpse washed up on the beach, apparently the victim of a shark attack. They report it to the coast guard, but the dead man's phone contains a photograph of his girlfriend, and Charlie and Benny persuade the others to search for the couple's yacht in case she is still alive, despite Joji's objections.

They find the yacht capsized, and when Benny dives to investigate, he discovers the young woman's mutilated remains. As he returns to the surface, a great white shark attacks one of the seaplane's floats, and the plane begins to sink. The five are forced into a small life raft and left drifting with limited supplies. Charlie attempts to navigate with a basic compass and oars, while exhaustion, fear and jealousy cause tensions among the passengers, particularly between Joji and Benny. When one of them falls into the water, the sharks begin to circle the raft, and the group must make desperate decisions as they try to reach land before the predators pick them off one by one.

The film follows the familiar conventions of the shark survival thriller, relying on the vulnerability of its characters in open water and on the isolation of its tropical setting.

Great White received mixed reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes it holds an approval rating of about 43 percent; the consensus says that it is far from the most toothless shark thriller but lacks the storytelling instinct needed to stay afloat. Cath Clarke of The Guardian gave it two stars out of five.

title: Blinded by the Light
tagline: For anyone who has ever wanted to dream. You're not alone.
overview: In 1987, during the austere days of Thatcher’s Britain, a teenager learns to live life, understand his family, and find his own voice through the music of Bruce Springsteen.
plot:
Blinded by the Light is a 2019 British comedy-drama film directed by Gurinder Chadha, inspired by the life of journalist Sarfraz Manzoor and his love of Bruce Springsteen's music. Manzoor wrote the screenplay with Chadha and Paul Mayeda Berges, based on his 2007 memoir Greetings from Bury Park. Viveik Kalra stars, with Hayley Atwell, Rob Brydon, Kulvinder Ghir and Nell Williams in supporting roles.

In Luton in 1987, during Margaret Thatcher's premiership, British-Pakistani teenager Javed Khan writes poetry and song lyrics but feels stifled by his strict father Malik, who forbids him to socialize, and by the racism he faces from neighbors and classmates. At sixth form college his writing teacher, Ms Clay, encourages him to pursue writing, and he develops a crush on activist Eliza. Then Malik loses his job at Vauxhall Motors after sixteen years, and the family struggles. On the night of the great storm of 1987, Javed throws away his poems, but a classmate, Roops, has lent him two Springsteen cassettes, and the lyrics seem to describe his own life. Inspired, he retrieves his poems, publishes a piece on Springsteen in the student paper, wins over Eliza and lands an unpaid internship at the Luton Herald.

Tensions mount as the National Front marches through town, and Malik objects to Javed's ambitions. On the morning of his cousin Yasmeen's wedding, Javed rushes off to buy Springsteen concert tickets with money from a front-page article, while Malik is assaulted by National Front members. In the ensuing fight, Malik tears up the tickets, and Javed declares that he will study at the University of Manchester. After his Springsteen essay wins him a trip to New Jersey, Javed goes despite his father's threats. At a college prize-giving, with his family in the audience, he speaks instead about being blinded by his dreams, vowing to build a bridge to his ambitions rather than a wall between himself and his family. Javed and Malik reconcile, and Javed sells his memorabilia to recover his mother's jewellery before leaving for university.

Blinded by the Light premiered at the 2019 Sundance Film Festival and was released in the United Kingdom by Entertainment One on 9 August 2019 and by New Line Cinema in the United States a week later. It received positive reviews, with 89% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 71, but grossed only about $19.6 million worldwide.

title: Avengement
overview: While on a prison furlough, a lowly criminal evades his guards and returns to his old stomping ground to take revenge on the people who turned him into a cold blooded killer.
plot:
Avengement is a 2019 British action thriller directed by Jesse V. Johnson, who co-wrote it with Stu Small. Scott Adkins stars as Cain Burgess, a small-time criminal transformed into a ruthless fighter by years in prison, with Craig Fairbrass as his older brother Lincoln, Thomas Turgoose, Nick Moran and Kierston Wareing. It was released on video on demand and in select cinemas on 24 May 2019, and an uncut special edition followed in 2020.

Cain, a prisoner, is escorted by police to a hospital to see the body of his recently deceased mother. He escapes from his guards and makes his way to a private East London pub, forcing his way in past the bouncers. As he drinks, he overhears a patron named Tune boasting about how an unknown assailant killed a gangster called Rook, and his laughter provokes a confrontation with the regulars and the barmaid, Bez. Claiming to be a friend of the pub's owner, Lincoln, he fights off the patrons and takes everyone hostage with a sawn-off shotgun. When Lincoln's lieutenant, Hyde, arrives, he recognizes Cain as Lincoln's younger brother, and Cain shoots a man in the knee to show he is serious, blaming Hyde and Lincoln for everything that has happened to him.

Through flashbacks, Cain recounts his story. Once a skilled but hot-headed martial artist whose fights had cost Lincoln, a loan shark, and his associates a good deal of money, he went to his brother for help in starting a legitimate business, only to be drawn into the gang's criminal world. Sent to the notorious HMP Belmarsh, he was repeatedly attacked and had to fight for survival, gradually turning into a hardened, scarred killing machine, and he came to believe that his brother was responsible for his ordeal. Waiting for Lincoln to arrive at the pub, Cain prepares to take bloody revenge on the brother he believes destroyed his life, and the hostages realize they are caught in the middle of a long-awaited family reckoning.

Avengement received generally positive reviews, with an 89 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes. Its consensus said it compensated for a lack of narrative originality with thrilling sequences of bone-crunching action, elevated by Adkins's brutally intense performance, and many critics considered it one of the best showcases of his career.

title: Andhadhun
overview: A series of mysterious events changes the life of a blind pianist who now must report a crime that was actually never witnessed by him.
plot:
Akash Saraf is a Pune-based pianist who feigns visual impairment as an artistic experiment to refine his musical focus. While navigating a street, he is knocked over by a young woman named Sophie. Impressed by his apparent musical talent, Sophie secures him a regular engagement at her father's diner. Although Akash initially utilizes opaque contact lenses during his practice sessions, his growing affection for Sophie prompts him to discard them, choosing instead to simply simulate blindness. The two soon begin a romantic relationship. At the diner, Pramod Sinha, a wealthy, retired actor, notices Akash's skill and hires him for a private performance at his apartment to celebrate his wedding anniversary.
When Akash arrives at the residence, Pramod's wife, Simi, reluctantly lets him in to avoid arousing the suspicion of a nosy neighbor. Upon entering, Akash immediately discovers Pramod's corpse on the floor. Forced to maintain his facade of blindness to protect his life, Akash continues to play the piano while feigning absolute ignorance. He watches as Simi and her hidden paramour—Manohar, a muscular police inspector—clean the crime scene and stuff the body into a suitcase. Disturbed by the ordeal, Akash leaves the building and encounters Sakhu, a lottery ticket seller with a distinctive Lord Shiva tattoo, who helps him hail an auto-rickshaw driven by a man named Murli.
Akash attempts to report the homicide at the local precinct, but he aborts the mission upon discovering that Manohar is the inspector in charge of the station. He quickly improvises a false report about a missing pet cat to escape. Meanwhile, an elderly neighbor, Mrs. D'Sa, informs the police that she witnessed an unfamiliar man entering the Sinhas' apartment on the day of the murder. To silence her, Simi pushes Mrs. D'Sa off the building's ledge. Akash arrives for a scheduled piano lesson just in time to witness the fatal fall, but he is forced to continue his blind act. Soon after, a skeptical neighborhood child surreptitiously records a video of Akash exercising full visual awareness.
Simi visits Akash's apartment under the guise of offering temple sweets, which she has laced with a potent drug. After exposing his fraud by catching him off guard, she blinds him with a chemical solution and drugs him into unconsciousness. While Akash is incapacitated, the neighbor's child exposes the video to Sophie. Sophie rushes to the apartment, but Simi deftly manipulates the scene to make it appear as though she and Akash are having an affair, causing a heartbroken Sophie to abandon him. Manohar later infiltrates the apartment to eliminate Akash, but the newly blinded pianist narrowly escapes, knocking himself unconscious against a telephone pole during his flight.
Akash awakens in an illicit organ-harvesting clinic managed by a corrupt doctor, Dr. Swami, and his assistants, who happen to be Murli and Sakhu.

title: The Wandering Earth
overview: When the Sun begins to expand in such a way that it will inevitably engulf and destroy the Earth in a hundred years, united mankind finds a way to avoid extinction by propelling the planet out of the Solar System using gigantic engines, moving it to a new home located four light years away, an epic journey that will last thousands of years.
plot:
The Wandering Earth is a 2019 Chinese science fiction film directed by Guo Fan, produced by China Film Group Corporation, and based on the novel of the same name by Liu Cixin. The movie takes place in a dystopian future where humanity is on the brink of extinction due to an impending solar flare that will destroy the Sun.

The story begins with the discovery of a habitable exoplanet called Proxima b, which orbits within the habitable zone of its star. A team of scientists, led by Professor Zhang (played by Dong Chengpeng), devise a plan to relocate Earth to orbit around Proxima b, thereby saving humanity from extinction.

However, the relocation process is fraught with challenges and uncertainties. The massive spaceship required to move Earth would need to be constructed in a relatively short period, and its trajectory would have to be precisely calculated to ensure a stable orbit around Proxima b.

As the construction of the spaceship begins, tensions rise among the scientists, engineers, and politicians involved in the project. Some question the feasibility of the plan, while others are driven by personal ambitions or ideological motivations.

The movie follows the journey of Wang Miao (played by Liu Haoran), a young engineer who is recruited to join the team working on the spaceship's propulsion system. As Wang becomes more deeply embroiled in the project, he begins to question the true intentions of his superiors and the morality of relocating an entire planet.

Meanwhile, the solar flare draws near, and the world teeters on the brink of disaster. The relocation process is accelerated, with Wang and his colleagues working tirelessly to complete the spaceship's construction.

As the spaceship approaches its destination, Wang begins to experience strange visions and hallucinations, which he attributes to the stress of the project. However, it becomes clear that something more sinister is at play, as Wang discovers a mysterious message from an unknown sender that seems to be connected to the true purpose of the relocation.

The movie's climax features a dramatic confrontation between Wang and his superiors, who reveal their true intentions: to use the relocated Earth as a new habitat for humanity, but also to harness its resources to fuel their own ambitions. Wang must decide whether to conform to this plan or risk everything to expose the truth.

In the end, Wang's actions lead to a catastrophic outcome, and the movie concludes with a sense of hopelessness and despair. The Wandering Earth is a thought-provoking exploration of humanity's relationship with technology, power, and the unknown, set against a backdrop of science fiction spectacle.
