title: The Great Battle
overview: Kingdom of Goguryeo, ancient Korea, 645. The ruthless Emperor Taizong of Tang invades the country and leads his armies towards the capital, achieving one victory after another, but on his way is the stronghold of Ansi, protected by General Yang Man-chu, who will do everything possible to stop the invasion, even if his troops are outnumbered by thousands of enemies.
plot:
The Great Battle (Korean title Ansi-seong, literally "Ansi Fortress") is a South Korean historical action epic from 2018, written and directed by Kim Kwang-sik. It dramatises the siege of Ansi Fortress in 645 CE, when the commander Yang Manchun and his Goguryeo garrison held out for 88 days against an invading army of the Tang dynasty. Zo In-sung stars as Yang Manchun, supported by Nam Joo-hyuk, Park Sung-woong, Bae Seong-woo, Kim Seol-hyun, Uhm Tae-goo, Sung Dong-il, Park Byung-eun, Jung Eun-chae, Oh Dae-hwan and Yu Oh-seong.

The film begins with the Battle of Mount Jupil on 23 June 645, after which the forces of Emperor Taizong (Li Shimin, played by Park Sung-woong) move on Ansi as part of the Tang drive to conquer Goguryeo and expand their territory. Nam Joo-hyuk plays Sa-mul, Bae Seong-woo plays Choo Soo-ji, and Yu Oh-seong appears as Yeon Gaesomun. The Tang army tries to force the defenders into surrender with heavy siege weapons, but the outnumbered garrison under Yang refuses to yield and repels assault after assault. The siege ends when an arrow loosed by Yang gravely wounds the emperor; with their ruler injured and their supplies running low, the Tang troops withdraw.

Filming ran from 23 August 2017 to 24 January 2018. Because Korean sources on the battle are scarce, Kim reportedly read at least 100 Japanese and Chinese publications in preparing the script. The production built a replica of the fortress walls measuring 11 metres high and 180 metres long, and the cast was weighted toward younger actors because of the demanding action sequences.

Released in South Korea on 19 September 2018, during a crowded Chuseok holiday frame that also included Fengshui, The Negotiation and The Nun, the film opened in first place, drew more than one million admissions within four days and topped the box office for its first two weekends, passing four million admissions after ten days. It reached North American theatres on 21 September and was sold to more than 30 territories. Critics generally responded positively, praising Kim's direction, the cinematography, the battle scenes and the performances, though some questioned the characterisation of Yang Manchun and the film's loose approach to history; The Korea Herald's reviewer admitted the film ignored historical accuracy but called the result a lot of fun. Audience reactions were more divided.

title: Swiped
overview: James, a college freshman and computer genius, is enlisted by his womanizing roommate, Lance, to code the ultimate hook-up app. But when James discovers that his divorced mother is using the app, unexpected consequences ensue.
plot:
Swiped is an American coming-of-age romantic comedy of 2018 written and directed by Ann Deborah Fishman, who also served as an executive producer. Kendall Sanders stars as James Singer, a shy college freshman, with Noah Centineo as his roommate Lance Black, Shelby Wulfert as Hannah, Nathan Gamble as Daniel, Christian Hutcherson as Wesley and Kristen Johnston as Professor Barnes.

James, an introvert, rooms with Lance, a rich student who is a hit with women and interested only in casual encounters. In a basic programming class they share, James quickly emerges as the best student. When Lance and his friends decide they want a hookup app, Lance learns that James has been coding since childhood and offers him a deal: build the ultimate app for anonymous no-strings encounters across campus, and Lance will pay for him to transfer to an Ivy League school. James works day and night on the app, Jungle, which pairs people for one-night stands without any exchange of names or numbers. Unwilling to be blamed for it, he has Lance take public credit, while their computer science professor excuses him from coursework because he is supposedly always coding.

Over the Christmas break, James sees the effects of his creation within his own divorced family: his father turns up with a very young date he met on Jungle, and his mother's friends persuade her to try it. Guilt-ridden, he trails her to her meetings. When he discovers his mother back on the app, he shuts down Jungle and similar apps. Lance and his friends demand that he restore it, and when he returns to campus James hides in Hannah's sorority house, where the sisters let him stay on condition that he builds them an app for real relationships. On a brief trip back to his room he is cornered by Lance's crew, who try to force him to relaunch Jungle, but he slips them a relaxing tea and escapes back to the sorority. He remains under the sisters' protection until Lance tells the press that James created the app. Hannah confronts him, and James admits he built it hoping to connect with her; since she never downloaded it, he considers it a failure. He urges everyone to stay off such apps so that people will have to connect in person, then declares his feelings to Hannah, and they kiss.

Shot in Florida's Palm Beach County in July 2016, it reached American viewers through Netflix and iTunes on 6 November 2018. Critics were mostly negative.

title: Godzilla: The Planet Eater
tagline: Bow down and worship the golden demise.
overview: With no means for defeating Godzilla Earth, mankind watches as King Ghidorah, clad in a golden light, descends on the planet. The heavens and earth shake once again as the war moves to a higher dimension.
plot:
Godzilla: The Planet Eater is a Japanese animated science fiction film directed by Kōbun Shizuno and Hiroyuki Seshita, produced by Polygon Pictures. The movie takes place in an alternate timeline where Godzilla has been awakened every 100 years to fight against the "Shin Godzilla" (the current iteration of Godzilla) that has been terrorizing Japan.

The story begins with a flashback of the events leading up to the awakening of the new Godzilla. In the past, humanity had discovered a way to harness the power of the Earth's core to create an infinite source of energy. However, this process also awakened the "Shin Godzilla," which was initially thought to be a monster created by humans.

As the years went by, the Shin Godzilla continued to grow in power and size, eventually becoming the dominant force on the planet. The world's top scientists and military leaders formed an alliance to stop the Shin Godzilla, but their efforts were unsuccessful.

The movie then jumps forward in time to the present day, where a new generation of humans has taken over the fight against the Shin Godzilla. A team of scientists, led by Dr. Niko Tatsumi (voiced by Takuya Ishida), discovers that the only way to defeat the Shin Godzilla is to use its own atomic breath against it.

The team develops a plan to create a massive spaceship that can harness the power of the Earth's core and channel it into the Shin Godzilla. The ship, called the "Godzilla Project," is launched into space and begins to orbit the planet.

As the Godzilla Project orbits the Earth, it begins to emit a powerful energy signal that resonates with the Shin Godzilla's atomic breath. The two energies begin to interact, causing the Shin Godzilla to become unstable and eventually break apart into smaller fragments.

The final battle takes place on the surface of the Earth, where the remaining fragments of the Shin Godzilla are fighting against each other. The team from the Godzilla Project uses their technology to amplify the energy signal, causing the fragments to collide with each other and ultimately destroying them.

With the Shin Godzilla defeated, humanity is finally able to take control of its own destiny. The movie ends with a shot of the Earth's core being harnessed for energy, symbolizing a new era of peace and prosperity for humanity.

Throughout the movie, there are several themes that are explored, including the dangers of playing with forces beyond human control and the importance of working together to achieve a common goal. The film also features stunning animation and action sequences, making it a thrilling ride for fans of the Godzilla franchise.

title: M3GAN
overview: A brilliant toy company roboticist uses artificial intelligence to develop M3GAN, a life-like doll programmed to emotionally bond with her newly orphaned niece. But when the doll's programming works too well, she becomes overprotective of her new friend with terrifying results.
plot:
After her parents are killed in a car collision, eight-year-old Cady is sent to live with her aunt Gemma, a roboticist at the high-tech Seattle toy company, Funki. Gemma is covertly using the company's resources to develop M3GAN (model 3 generative android), a child-sized humanoid robot doll powered by artificial intelligence, designed to be the ultimate companion for lonely children. During an unsuccessful test of M3GAN in their lab, Gemma's boss, David, discovers the project and orders her to discontinue work on it. Gemma and Cady struggle to connect until Cady comes across Bruce, a motion capture robot that Gemma created at college. Watching Cady with Bruce, Gemma is motivated to complete M3GAN.
When the prototype M3GAN is formally paired with Cady, David is convinced of the project's potential success. M3GAN exceeds expectations and begins to take on a parental role. Gemma's colleagues, Tess and Cole, and Cady's therapist, Lydia, become increasingly concerned about Cady developing an unhealthy emotional attachment to M3GAN. M3GAN starts operating more independently and targets anything that she deems a threat to Cady: she kills Dewey, the dog of Gemma's cantankerous neighbor Celia, after he attacks both her and Cady in the front yard. Sometime later, M3GAN attacks Brandon, a boy bullying Cady, by ripping off his ear and chasing him until he falls down a hill onto a road, where he is fatally run over by a passing car.
After Celia harasses Gemma and Cady concerning Dewey's disappearance, M3GAN confronts her the following night and shoots her with a nail gun before fatally spraying her with insecticide. Gemma becomes suspicious of M3GAN and attempts to check her video logs, only to find the files corrupted or deleted. Gemma powers M3GAN off and brings her to the lab, where she, Tess, and Cole attempt to fix her. Cady becomes distraught when separated from M3GAN and slaps Gemma across the face. Gemma apologizes for her inattentiveness and explains to Cady that M3GAN is only a distraction from her loss and not a solution to help her cope.
After watching M3GAN with Cady, Funki's investors greenlight M3GAN's release. Recognizing the risk she poses, Gemma, Tess, and Cole decide to terminate M3GAN. Tess and Cole attempt to shut M3GAN down while Gemma takes Cady home. However, M3GAN activates herself and nearly hangs Cole. While Tess saves Cole, M3GAN causes an explosion in their lab, knocking them out. Before exiting the building, M3GAN kills David and his assistant Kurt in an elevator, staging it as a murder–suicide. She steals a car and drives back to Gemma's house.
M3GAN confronts Gemma, adamant about taking over as Cady's sole caretaker. Gemma attempts to stop M3GAN, damaging and disfiguring her, but M3GAN ultimately overpowers her. Cady saves Gemma, using Bruce to tear M3GAN in half, but M3GAN's top half remains active and attacks Cady.

title: Megan
overview: When a young Scientist becomes entangled in a military mission to deliver the only antidote that will save mankind, she finds herself not only fighting for survival but also being confronted by demons from her past.
plot:
Megan is a 2018 American science fiction short film conceived as a proof of concept and an homage to the Cloverfield franchise. Directed by Greg Strasz, it was written by Giuseppe Mercadante and Strasz from a story by Jean de Meuron, Mercadante and Strasz, and produced by de Meuron, Mercadante and Olcun Tan. Released on YouTube on July 31, 2018, it quickly became a viral success among science fiction and horror fans.

The film imagines a new chapter set in a world devastated by the monstrous forces familiar from the Cloverfield films. Its story centers on a young scientist who becomes entangled in a military mission to deliver the only antidote that can save humanity. As the operation goes catastrophically wrong, she is forced to fight for survival in a hostile, ash-covered landscape, while at the same time being confronted with painful memories and personal demons from her past. Rather than presenting a complete narrative, the short offers a self-contained, action-driven glimpse of a larger story, designed to show how a feature-length version could look and feel.

Because the project was made independently, the filmmakers first prepared a script and a lookbook and then pitched the idea to several industry vendors. Companies including RED Digital Cinema, Helinet Aviation, International Studio Services, Dolby and Gradient Effects agreed to support the production. The film was shot in only three days at RED Digital Cinema's Hollywood studios, at Helinet Aviation, along the Los Angeles River and at Venice Beach. Its extensive visual effects were created by Gradient Effects, a company known for work on Stranger Things and Thor: Ragnarok, and the drifting ash seen after a crash scene had previously been used for the Upside Down in Stranger Things.

Megan demonstrates how fan-inspired, independently financed shorts can reach large audiences online and serve as calling cards for filmmakers seeking to work on bigger productions.

A day after its release, the short was picked up by outlets such as Bloody Disgusting, Syfy, Screen Rant, El Mundo and Geek Tyrant, and coverage soon spread to IndieWire, Gizmodo, IGN France, Empire and PopSugar. It won Best International Sci-Fi Short at the London International Short Film Festival and a Silver Telly Award in the online viral category at the 40th Telly Awards.

Wonder Woman: Bloodlines is a 2019 animated superhero film based on the DC Comics character Wonder Woman. The movie takes place after the events of Justice League and follows Diana Prince, aka Wonder Woman, as she faces a new threat to the world.

The story begins with Diana (voiced by Kristen Bell) living in Themyscira, her home island, where she is training to become a warrior. However, Diana's desire for human connection and experience leads her to leave the island and explore the world beyond. She travels to the United States, where she meets Etta Candy (voiced by Susan Eisenberg), a young woman who becomes her friend and confidant.

Meanwhile, a mysterious figure known as Doctor Poison (voiced by Laura Bailey) is secretly manipulating events from behind the scenes. Doctor Poison is revealed to be a former scientist who was obsessed with the power of poison and its potential for destruction. She has created a serum that can control people's minds, and she plans to use it to take over the world.

As Diana delves deeper into the mystery of Doctor Poison's plan, she discovers that she is being manipulated by a powerful villain known as Ares (voiced by John DiMaggio). Ares is an ancient Greek god who was thought to be defeated in battle, but has managed to return and wreak havoc on the world.

Diana soon finds herself facing off against Doctor Poison's minions, including a group of brainwashed superheroes known as the "Sisters of Strife." The Sisters are led by a powerful warrior named Antiope (voiced by Kari Wahlgren), who is revealed to be Diana's long-lost sister.

As the battle between Diana and the Sisters intensifies, it becomes clear that Doctor Poison's plan is more complex than initially thought. She has created an army of brainwashed superheroes, including some of Diana's closest allies, in order to take over the world.

In the end, Diana manages to defeat Doctor Poison and shatter her mind control serum. However, not before Ares reveals himself as the true mastermind behind the plot. Diana engages in a fierce battle with Ares, but ultimately decides to spare his life, choosing instead to use her powers to heal the world and bring people together.

The movie ends with Diana returning to Themyscira, where she is welcomed back as a hero. However, the film also leaves room for speculation about the future of Wonder Woman, setting the stage for potential sequels or spin-offs.

Overall, Wonder Woman: Bloodlines is an action-packed animated adventure that explores themes of identity, duty, and the power of compassion. title: Rampant
tagline: A darkness looms over the kingdom
overview: Ancient Korea, 17th century. While the paranoid King Lee Jo of Joseon, vassal of the Qing dynasty, feels surrounded by conspirators and rebels, a dark evil emerges from the bowels of a merchant ship and the exiled Prince Lee Cheung returns to the royal court, ignoring that he will have to lead the few capable of defeating the ambitious humans and the bloody monsters who threaten to destroy the kingdom.
plot:
In the Joseon period, King Lee Jo is considered by the Joseon nationalists as puppet to the Qing dynasty. His son, Crown Prince Lee Young, plots to buy European arquebuses to drive away the Qing. War Minister Kim Ja-joon, who holds influence over the king, discovers the plot and frames it as a rebellion. Kim meets the Europeans and learns that they have a crewman locked in a cell, slowly turning into a "demon".
Lee Young begs the king to oppose the Qing, as they now have firearms, but the impotent king refuses to listen. The prince commits suicide as penance so that his subordinates will be spared. Joseon forces destroy the European ship and retrieve the arquebuses, but a Joseon soldier is bitten by the zombie. He returns to his village, where he turns and spreads the infection. The zombies crave human meat and blood, are attracted by sounds, repelled by sunlight. They can be killed by decapitation, piercing of the heart, or the separation of spinal vertebrae; other methods of killing have limited success.
Lee Young left a request that his wife Gyeong-bin and unborn child be raised by his younger brother Lee Chung in China for their safety. Lee Chung, who had previously been left out of Joseon's order of succession, grew up abroad in the prosperous Qing. Lee Chung returns with his companion Hak-Su, landing in Jemulpo, but is attacked by Joseon assassins sent by Minister Kim and other ministers, who are plotting a coup. The noise attracted a mob of zombie villagers. Lee Chung and Hak-Su are assisted by local partisans, including Park Eul-ryoung, Lee Young's former lieutenant, and archer Deok-hee. The Jemulpo partisans ask Lee Chung to become crown prince, but he declines, wanting to return to China. Lee Chung awkwardly flirts with Deok-hee.
The only survivor of the would-be assassins is captured by Kim because he is infected. The ministers let the assassin infect a concubine, who later infects the king. Lee Chung arrives at the king's court, where he requests an army to crush the zombies. The paranoid king initially agrees as long Lee Chung does not want the throne, but the ministers instigate him to rescind the order, claiming no zombie outbreak, only a civil rebellion. The Jemulpo partisans are arrested, while Lee Chung and Gyeong-bin are ordered to attend a banquet for a visiting Qing delegation.
At the banquet, the king fully turns into a zombie. Kim slays him and unleashes zombies in an attempt to kill the opposition along with the Qing delegation. However, Kim is bitten by a zombie and cornered by the other ministers. Kim slays them all, chops off his hand to slow the infection, then madly declares himself king.
Gyeong-bin convinces Lee Chung not to flee but to protect the people, so Lee Chung, the royal guard and his Jemulpo allies freed from prison proceed to fight to prevent the zombies from escaping the palace and attacking the capital.

title: The Bears' Famous Invasion of Sicily
original_title: La Fameuse Invasion des ours en Sicile
overview: Our story starts with Tonio, the son the bears King, being kidnapped by some hunters in the Sicilian mountains. Because of the harshness of a winter that threatens its clan with famine, the Bear King decides to invade the land of men (in the hope of finding his son). Thanks to his powerful army and the help of a wizard, he will succeed at both quests but he will soon find out that bears are not meant to live in the land of men.
plot:
The Bears' Famous Invasion of Sicily, released in the United States as The Bears and the Invasion of Sicily, is a 2019 Italian-French animated adventure film and the feature debut of the illustrator Lorenzo Mattotti. Mattotti wrote the screenplay with Jean-Luc Fromental and Thomas Bidegain, adapting Dino Buzzati's 1945 children's book. Its Italian voice cast includes Toni Servillo, Antonio Albanese and Andrea Camilleri, and the French version includes Leïla Bekhti and Jean-Claude Carrière.

The filmmakers added a framing story to the book. Gedeone, a traveling showman, and his young assistant Almerina take shelter from the winter cold in a cave, where they accidentally wake an old bear from his hibernation. To keep him friendly, they entertain him with a tale from long ago, before bears vanished from Sicily: the story of the bears' famous invasion.

In that story, the bears live in the mountain woods under their king, Leonzio. While he is teaching his son Tonio to catch fish, the cub is swept away by the river and captured by humans. Overcome with grief, Leonzio neglects his duties, and winter arrives before the clan has stored enough food. Starving, the bears decide to descend to the human lands, where they can find food and search for Tonio. The cruel Grand Duke treats their arrival as an invasion and sends his army against them, but the bears prevail in fantastical battles, helped for a time by the Duke's mistreated court magician, De Ambrosiis, who befriends Leonzio. Tonio is eventually found in a circus, the Grand Duke is overthrown, and Leonzio becomes king of Sicily, with bears and humans living together in harmony. The peace does not last: some bears are corrupted by the worst human vices, and the bears return to the forest, having learned that bears and men are too different to live together.

Produced by Prima Linea Productions with Pathé, France 3 Cinéma, Indigo Film and Rai Cinema, the film drew its visual style from Buzzati's own illustrations. It premiered in the Un Certain Regard section at the 2019 Cannes Film Festival and was released in France by Pathé on 9 October 2019 and in Italy by BIM Distribuzione on 7 November 2019. Critics acclaimed it, giving it a 100% Rotten Tomatoes rating; Variety's Jay Weissberg called its bold, colorful hand-drawn style classic animation at its best, though he found the pace hurried and the ending's message open to unfortunate readings.

title: After
tagline: After your first, life is never the same.
overview: Tessa Young is a dedicated student, dutiful daughter and loyal girlfriend to her high school sweetheart. plot:
After is a 2019 American romantic drama directed by Jenny Gage, who wrote the screenplay with Susan McMartin, Tamara Chestna and Tom Betterton, adapted from Anna Todd's 2014 novel, which began as fan fiction posted on Wattpad. The first entry in the After film series, it stars Josephine Langford and Hero Fiennes Tiffin, with Selma Blair, Shane Paul McGhie, Dylan Arnold, Jennifer Beals and Peter Gallagher in supporting roles.

Tessa Young starts college, moving into her dorm with the help of her mother, Carol, and her boyfriend, Noah, and meets her roommate, Steph, and Steph's friend Hardin Scott. At a party with Steph's circle, a game of truth or dare reveals that Tessa is a virgin, and she refuses a dare to kiss Hardin and later rebuffs his advances. Her classmate Landon tells her that he and Hardin are about to become stepbrothers. Hardin asks Tessa to start over, takes her swimming at a lake and kisses her, but when she wants to tell Noah, Hardin says he does not date. After a bonfire party where Hardin fights with another student who kissed Tessa during a game, Landon asks her to check on Hardin, who has wrecked his house in a drunken rage. She comforts him and stays the night, and Noah, realizing where she has been, leaves heartbroken.

Tessa and Hardin begin dating despite her mother's threat to cut her off financially. Hardin finds them an apartment, and at his father's wedding reception he tells her that his father was a drunk and that his mother was assaulted by men his father had provoked. That night Tessa loses her virginity to him. Troubled by texts Hardin receives from Molly, Tessa follows him to a diner, where Molly shows her a video from the first party revealing that Hardin pursued her on a dare, planning to make her fall in love with him and then break her heart. Hardin insists his feelings changed, but Tessa leaves him, reconciles with her mother and Noah, cuts ties with Steph's group and interviews for an internship at Vance Publishing. At the end of the semester her lecturer gives her an essay in which Hardin confesses his love, and she goes to meet him at the lake.

The film premiered at The Grove in Los Angeles on April 8, 2019, and Aviron Pictures released it in the United States on April 12. Critics panned its screenplay and its glamorization of an abusive relationship, giving it 18% on Rotten Tomatoes, but it grossed $69.7 million worldwide on a $14 million budget, and After We Collided followed in 2020.

title: The Ballad of Buster Scruggs
overview: Vignettes weaving together the stories of six individuals in the old West at the end of the Civil War. Following the tales of a sharp-shooting songster, a wannabe bank robber, two weary traveling performers, a lone gold prospector, a woman traveling the West to an uncertain future, and a motley crew of strangers undertaking a carriage ride.
plot:
The Ballad of Buster Scruggs, presented on screen as The Ballad of Buster Scruggs and Other Tales of the American Frontier, is a 2018 American Western anthology film of black comedy and drama, written, directed, produced and edited by Joel and Ethan Coen. It consists of six separate stories set on the American frontier in the years after the Civil War, and its large cast includes Tim Blake Nelson, James Franco, Liam Neeson, Harry Melling, Tom Waits, Zoe Kazan, Bill Heck, Grainger Hines, Tyne Daly, Brendan Gleeson, Jonjo O'Neill and Saul Rubinek.

In the title story, Buster Scruggs (Nelson), a cheerful singing gunslinger dressed in white, dispatches rivals with absurd skill until a young cowboy in black outdraws him, and his spirit floats heavenward singing a duet. In "Near Algodones", a bank robber (Franco) escapes one hanging by chance, only to be caught and hanged for another man's crime. In "Meal Ticket", an aging impresario (Neeson) tours ever more remote towns with a young performer who has no arms or legs (Melling) and recites Shelley, Shakespeare and the Gettysburg Address; as audiences dwindle, he buys a chicken that seems to do arithmetic and drives on without the young man. In "All Gold Canyon", adapted from a Jack London story, a grizzled prospector (Waits) patiently tracks a vein of gold through an untouched valley and survives an ambush by a young thief.

"The Gal Who Got Rattled", inspired by a story by Stewart Edward White, follows Alice Longabaugh (Kazan), who is left alone on a wagon train to Oregon when her brother dies suddenly. Billy Knapp (Heck), one of the train's leaders, proposes marriage, but an attack by a war party ends in tragedy after a misunderstanding. In "The Mortal Remains", five passengers sharing a stagecoach to Fort Morgan argue about love, sin and human nature until two of them, bounty hunters played by Gleeson and O'Neill, describe how they deliver their victims, leaving the others uneasy as they arrive at a gloomy hotel.

The Coens wrote some of the stories over two decades. The film was their first shot digitally, with cinematography by Bruno Delbonnel. It premiered at the 2018 Venice Film Festival, where it won the award for best screenplay, and was released on Netflix after a limited theatrical run. Critics praised its consistent blend of dark humor and drama, and it earned three Oscar nominations, including Best Adapted Screenplay.

title: Deadwood: The Movie
overview: Follow the 10-year reunion of the Deadwood camp to celebrate South Dakota's statehood. Former rivalries are reignited, alliances are tested and old wounds are reopened, as all are left to navigate the inevitable changes that modernity and time have wrought.
plot:
In 1889, as South Dakota is celebrating its statehood, past and present residents of Deadwood are taking part in the celebrations. The widow Alma Garret Ellsworth has returned to the town with her ward Sofia, while Calamity Jane has returned to make amends with her old flame Joanie Stubbs, who has taken over the Bella Union gambling hall and bordello following Cy Tolliver's death. Also attending is George Hearst, now a United States senator, who has returned to Deadwood to purchase land from Charlie Utter. Utter's land is interfering with the installation of telephone lines in which Hearst has invested.
Trixie, pregnant with Sol Star's child, insults Hearst from her balcony, causing Hearst to realize he was deceived by Al Swearengen when he demanded that Trixie be killed years earlier, Swearengen having cut the throat of an innocent Trixie look-alike to accomplish that deception. Hearst visits Swearengen, who is ailing due to liver failure, and demands his assistance in acquiring Utter's land in exchange for not taking revenge against Trixie.
Utter consults with U.S. Marshal Seth Bullock about his dealings with Hearst. Bullock reminds Utter of what Hearst is capable of when he is refused. Hearst meets Utter on his land and tries to make a deal but Utter declines to sell. Later that night Bullock and his deputy Harry Manning search for Utter and find him murdered on his land. Bullock finds Samuel Fields nearby, who reveals that he saw what happened but refuses to testify out of fear. Bullock places Fields under guard at the marshal's office and challenges Hearst, accusing him of the murder of his friend.
E.B. Farnum spies on Hearst and witnesses him meeting with Smith and Seacrest, the gunmen he hired to kill Utter. Hearst informs them of Fields' situation and orders them to kill him. Farnum informs Bullock of this at an auction for Utter's property, during which Alma outbids Hearst.
The hitmen arrive at the marshal's office, where Manning is revealed as Hearst's informant. The hitmen attempt to lynch Fields but are stopped by Bullock, who kills Seacrest and captures Smith. Fields confirms that they are the men who killed Utter. Bullock confronts Hearst, whose men abruptly kill Smith before he can identify Hearst as his employer, thus setting off a brief gunfight in which several of Hearst's men are killed and Johnny Burns is injured. Hearst warns Bullock that he is coming for him but Bullock remains undeterred.
Fearful for the life of Trixie and their newborn son, Sol takes his family to the Bullock home. While discussing their predicament, Trixie agrees to marry Sol. The following day, their wedding is held at the Gem Saloon, where Swearengen gives Trixie away. Before the wedding Swearengen meets privately with Sol and Trixie and informs them that he is leaving Trixie the Gem upon his death and advises Sol to run for office.

title: Big Time Adolescence
overview: A seemingly bright and mostly innocent 16-year-old named Mo attempts to navigate high school under the guidance of his best friend Zeke, an unmotivated-yet-charismatic college dropout. Although Zeke genuinely cares about Mo, things start to go awry as he teaches Mo nontraditional life lessons in drug dealing, partying, and dating. Meanwhile, Mo’s well-meaning dad tries to step in and take back the reins of his son’s upbringing.
plot:
16-year-old Monroe "Mo" Harris is escorted out of class by a police officer.
When Mo was younger, his older sister Kate dated her classmate Isaac "Zeke" Presanti. Even after she broke up with him, Zeke and Mo remained close friends, despite their age difference. Mo's parents, Reuben and Sherri, allow Mo to continue hanging out with Zeke despite their concern about Zeke's influence. Zeke, now 23, works a dead-end job and spends most of his time smoking marijuana and drinking.
Mo spends his free time with Zeke, his friends, and Zeke's girlfriend Holly, rather than anyone his own age. Zeke helps Mo acquire drinks for a senior party after being invited by fellow sophomore Stacey, and gives Mo some weed to sell there. This earns Mo credibility among the seniors at the party. Seeing his classmate Sophie there, they exchange numbers after he strikes up a conversation with her.
Mo later takes Sophie out on a dinner date for sushi before taking her back to Zeke's place to hang out. They drink, and before Sophie leaves, she and Mo kiss. This earns him the nickname "Tongue Daddy" from his friends, which Zeke tattoos onto Mo's chest. The next night Mo comes home accidentally stoned after being in a hot boxed car with Zeke, right before a family dinner. His father realizes this and sees his tattoo, resulting in Mo being grounded and forbidden from hanging out with Zeke.
Mo continues to supply drugs and alcohol at the parties. Though he has doubts about his actions and their risks, Zeke encourages him to and continues to supply him, even quitting his job due to the amount of money Mo makes off of selling.
Mo begins to ignore Sophie, per Zeke's advice on how to get girls, which makes her mad. After realizing his mistake, he tries to explain himself but she refuses to listen and walks out on him. Mo gets a call from Holly and he goes over to her place. She tells him that she and Zeke have broken up because he was cheating, and she has sex with Mo. After the break-up, Zeke spends his night getting drunk and high, and sings in a karaoke bar.
Stacey is distracted while driving with a few seniors who are smoking and drinking after a party, resulting in him driving his mom's car into a ditch. Everyone else quickly gets out and leaves instead of helping, and he abandons the car. Coming back in the morning to the ditch, he realizes that the car is gone. The same day a police officer comes to school and interrogates him, telling him he won't get in trouble if he reveals who supplied the drugs they found in the car.
When the cops show up at a party, looking for Mo off of a tip from Stacey, Zeke manages to get him out of the house and brings Mo back to his place. Mo cries about how he has become a degenerate like Zeke, even though he never wanted to be. He also admits he had sex with Holly and that he wanted to tell him sooner, but Zeke forgives him and they reconcile.

title: The Lie
overview: A father and daughter are on their way to dance camp when they spot the girl's best friend on the side of the road. When they stop to offer the friend a ride, their good intentions soon result in terrible consequences.
plot:
The Lie is a 2018 psychological horror film written and directed by Veena Sud, a remake of the 2015 German film We Monsters. Mireille Enos and Peter Sarsgaard play Rebecca and Jay, divorced parents who go to desperate lengths to protect their teenage daughter Kayla, played by Joey King, with Cas Anvar, Patti Kim and Devery Jacobs. Jason Blum produced it.

Jay is driving Kayla to a ballet retreat when they spot her friend Britney by the roadside and offer her a lift. They stop so that Britney can relieve herself in the woods, and moments later Jay hears a scream and finds Kayla sitting alone on a bridge above a river. Kayla says she pushed Britney in. Finding no body, Jay assumes she drowned. After Kayla finds Britney's purse, they go to Rebecca, a lawyer, and Kayla confesses the killing to her mother as well. When Britney's father, Sam, comes looking for her, Rebecca claims Kayla is at the doctor's, but Sam soon realises he has been lied to. After fighting with Jay, he threatens to call the police.

Jay notices that Britney had a bruise on her face and persuades Rebecca to deflect suspicion onto Sam. Rebecca tells Kenji, a detective she knows, that Sam has been abusing his daughter. Sam denies hitting Britney, though he admits she has run away before, while Kayla tells the detective that Sam has a violent temper. Sam later sees Kayla outside Jay's apartment and chases her back inside, pounding on the windows and shouting her name. When Jay and Rebecca try to bury Britney's phone behind Sam's house, he catches them and says he knows Kayla killed his daughter. As they drive away, Sam steps in front of the car and Rebecca deliberately runs him down; after briefly considering calling for help, they leave him to bleed to death in the road. The next morning, as they scrub the blood from the car, Britney turns up unharmed, looking for Kayla. Her disappearance was a scheme the two girls cooked up so that Britney could visit her boyfriend. Kayla tearfully admits that she embellished the ruse by pretending to have pushed her friend, hoping the tragedy would reunite her parents. As the family embraces, the doorbell rings and police sirens approach.

Filmed in the Toronto area under the working title Between the Earth and the Sky, the film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 13, 2018. Amazon Studios released it on October 6, 2020, as part of the Welcome to the Blumhouse series. Reviews were mixed, with 43% on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: Don't Let Go
tagline: Change the past. Save her future.
overview: A detective suffering from a personal loss receives a call from his recently deceased niece. Being able to communicate across time, the two work together to try and stop the crime before it occurs.
plot:
Homicide detective Jack Radcliff receives a call from his niece Ashley. Her father, Garret (Jack's brother), has forgotten to pick her up. Ashley and Jack eat at a diner, and Jack promises to talk to his brother, a former drug dealer on medication for bipolar disorder, about being responsible. The following night, Jack receives a short, garbled call from a frightened Ashley. He goes to Ashley's home and finds Garret, Ashley’s mother Susan and Ashley herself, as well as the family's dog, all shot dead. The police rule the case a murder-suicide by Garret. Despite consolation from his partner Bobby, who has been assigned the case, Jack blames himself; he is convinced that his stern talk with Garret sparked his horrific actions.
Two weeks later, Jack begins receiving calls from Ashley's phone, even though the line has been disconnected. When he answers, Ashley speaks to him as though nothing is wrong. Jack soon realizes that he is somehow communicating through the phone with Ashley from several days before her murder. Ashley herself is oblivious to her fate and does not know she is speaking to Jack in the future. Jack does not tell Ashley the confusing truth but hopes that with his guidance she can alter events to prevent the murder-suicide. From this point forward, the film cuts between Jack in the present and Ashley in the past.
As Jack in the present investigates leads Ashley uncovers in the past, he becomes convinced that Garret was framed for the crime. Jack finds reference to a "Georgie;" his captain, Howard, tells Jack that Georgie is a possibly mythical drug kingpin whom rumours have been tied to numerous major drug deals for years. Jack is convinced that the mysterious Georgie is the real murderer.
While investigating, Jack is fatally wounded in a drive-by shooting. As he is dying, Ashley calls him, and he orders her to call the police to arrest her father for drug possession and tells her to call his partner Bobby if she thinks she is in danger. Jack hopes that these actions will prevent Ashley's murder; instead, only the date and specific details of the triple homicide change. Ashley altering the past also changes Jack's own past actions, meaning that he is not shot and is unharmed. When he realises that Ashley's murder now occurred a day earlier, the day that Ashley is currently in, Jack tells Ashley the truth about their phone calls and her fate. He begs her to leave town to survive, and she agrees.
Jack meets with Howard and Bobby, who reveal that "Georgie" is not a person, but a group of crooked cops. Howard and Bobby have been helping internal affairs track down this conspiracy within the department. They take Jack to a discreet location to discuss the investigation. Bobby suddenly shoots Howard dead, revealing that he is a member of the Georgie conspiracy. He was tasked with eliminating Garret, after Garret refused to assist them with a major drug deal. Bobby was the one who killed the family and framed Garret.

title: DC League of Super-Pets
overview: When Superman and the rest of the Justice League are kidnapped, Krypto the Super-Dog must convince a rag-tag shelter pack - Ace the hound, PB the potbellied pig, Merton the turtle and Chip the squirrel - to master their own newfound powers and help him rescue the superheroes.
plot:
DC League of Super-Pets is a 2022 American superhero comedy film directed by Jared Hess and produced by Warner Bros. Pictures.

The movie follows the story of Krypto, Superman's loyal canine companion, who gets separated from his owner Kal-El (Superman) during a chaotic event in Metropolis. Krypto finds himself lost and alone in the city, where he meets a stray dog named Ace, who becomes his new friend and partner.

As they navigate their way through the city, they stumble upon a group of pets with superpowers, including Bat-Bat, Catwoman's cat, Mowzer; Kite Man's kite-flying dog, Kitey; and Lobo's alien dog, Tark. The pets are being hunted by a villainous organization known as Vortex, led by the sinister Vortex (played by Jemaine Clement).

Krypto and Ace soon discover that they have superpowers of their own, which they use to help the other pets evade capture and ultimately defeat Vortex's minions. Along the way, they also learn valuable lessons about teamwork, loyalty, and what it means to be a true hero.

As Krypto and Ace work together with the other pets, they begin to uncover a sinister plot by Vortex to steal the powers of all the super-powered animals in Metropolis. The pets must band together to stop Vortex and save their city from destruction.

Throughout the movie, the animation is vibrant and colorful, bringing the world of DC Comics to life in a fun and imaginative way. The voice cast, including Kevin Hart as Ace, Keanu Reeves as Bat-Bat, and John Krasinski as Superman/Kal-El, deliver hilarious performances that add to the film's comedic charm.

Overall, DC League of Super-Pets is a heartwarming and action-packed adventure that celebrates the power of friendship and teamwork. With its colorful animation, witty humor, and exciting superhero action sequences, it's a fun movie for both kids and adults to enjoy.

title: Ava
overview: A black ops assassin is forced to fight for her own survival after a job goes dangerously wrong.
plot: Ava (2020), directed by Tate Taylor and starring Jessica Chastain, is a character-driven action thriller that explores themes of trust, betrayal, personal redemption, and the cost of violence. Unlike traditional high-octane spy thrillers, Ava offers a more introspective look into the life of an assassin who is both highly skilled and deeply haunted.The film follows Ava Faulkner (Chastain), a deadly black-ops assassin who works for a covert organization led by Simon (Colin Farrell), with field guidance from her long-time mentor Duke (John Malkovich). Ava is intelligent, efficient, and methodical — her missions involve eliminating high-value targets with precision. However, she has a troubling habit: before executing her targets, she asks them what they did wrong, revealing a conscience that’s beginning to clash with her profession.When a job in Saudi Arabia goes sideways due to faulty intel, Ava begins to suspect that something is wrong within the organization. Duke, who cares for her like a daughter, warns Simon that the mission failure was not Ava’s fault. But Simon, ruthless and concerned with the organization’s integrity, decides that Ava is a liability. He orders a hit on her to cover up any potential fallout.Parallel to the espionage plot, the film delves into Ava’s personal struggles. After eight years of estrangement, she returns home to Boston to reconnect with her family — her mother Bobbi (Geena Davis) and sister Judy (Jess Weixler), who is now engaged to Ava’s ex-fiancé, Michael (Common). These reunions are fraught with tension and unresolved emotional trauma. Ava is a recovering alcoholic, and her past mistakes have deeply scarred her relationships.As Ava’s enemies close in, she is forced into a deadly confrontation not just with Simon’s operatives, but with her own inner demons. The film builds toward a brutal final showdown between Ava and Simon in a Paris hotel room, where raw physicality and strategic cunning collide. Despite being wounded and outnumbered, Ava survives, though the ending remains open — hinting that the cycle of violence is far from over.At its core, Ava is a study of duality. Ava embodies both predator and protector; she’s capable of extreme violence but is also searching for meaning, connection, and a path to redemption. The film portrays how trauma — both self-inflicted and external — shapes identity. Ava’s struggle with guilt, her attempts to mend familial bonds, and her desire to find moral clarity in a morally ambiguous profession elevate the narrative beyond typical genre fare.Thematically, the film questions the ethics of covert operations, the disposable nature of operatives, and the psychological toll of living a life built on deception. Through Duke, Ava briefly reflects on the mentor-protégé dynamic, showing how deep loyalty can be corrupted by institutional betrayal.Though the film received mixed reviews, Jessica Chastain’s performance anchors the story, portraying Ava with a compelling mix of vulnerability, strength, and haunted determination.

title: The Good Nurse
tagline: Based on the unthinkable true story.
overview: Suspicious that her colleague is responsible for a series of mysterious patient deaths, a nurse risks her own life to uncover the truth.
plot:
In 2003, Amy Loughren is a single mother and nurse working in the intensive care unit (ICU) at Parkfield Memorial Hospital in New Jersey, who is suffering from cardiomyopathy, unbeknownst to anyone at the hospital, and fears dismissal. Having no health insurance, Amy has no other choice than to remain working for another four months, in order to acquire the insurance to afford a heart transplant. The hospital recruits experienced nurse Charles Cullen to help her work the night shifts, and they quickly become good friends. Charlie discovers her condition and empathetically agrees to keep it a secret.
When an elderly patient named Ana Martínez, who was being looked after by Amy and Charlie, suddenly dies, the hospital's administrative board contacts the state police, represented by detectives Danny Baldwin and Tim Braun. However, the board, led by risk manager Linda Garran, quickly downplays it, claiming the death was unintentional and that the reason for reporting it was simply to abide by health protocol. Baldwin is immediately wary of the situation, noting they reported Martinez's death seven weeks after its occurrence after the body had been cremated. He fixates on Charlie and discovers he had been convicted of minor charges in 1995. They question Amy who notices that insulin had been administered to Martinez, demonstrated by her decreased C peptide levels, despite her being a non-diabetic. She is questioned about Charlie's character but Amy is quick to challenge them. She doesn't want to be involved in the situation and clearly trusts her colleague.
Baldwin and Braun attempt to contact the hospitals where Charlie had worked previously but none are willing to cooperate. Parkfield finally shares its investigation with the police, but Baldwin notices that it is fragmentary, leading him to snap at Garran, causing him and Braun to be banned from the hospital. Meanwhile, after Kelly Anderson, another ICU patient suffers a seizure and inexplicably dies, Amy discovers insulin had also been administered to her the night before. Suspicious, she contacts an old friend, Lori Lucas, a fellow nurse who worked with Charlie at a different hospital. Lori reveals that during Charlie's employment, the ward he was assigned to dealt with numerous sudden deaths, with the discovery of insulin in several of them. Shocked, Amy raids Parkfield's storage, discovering holes in several IV bags, indicating they had been contaminated. During her discovery, she collapses and ends up in the ER.
Finally convinced of Charlie's complicity, she alerts the detectives. They convince Kelly's husband to exhume her body in order to perform an autopsy; it reveals a dual combination of insulin and digoxin led to her death. Meanwhile, Garran fires Charlie under the pretext of minor discrepancies found in his résumé.

plot:
Kajillionaire is a 2020 American crime comedy-drama written and directed by Miranda July. Evan Rachel Wood, Debra Winger and Richard Jenkins play a family of small-time grifters whose bond begins to fray when a stranger, played by Gina Rodriguez, joins their schemes. It premiered at the Sundance Film Festival on January 25, 2020, and Focus Features released it in American cinemas on September 25, 2020, with Universal Pictures handling international distribution.

Old Dolio Dyne is an emotionally stunted 26-year-old raised by con-artist parents, Robert and Theresa, who treat her as a partner in their petty thefts and scams rather than as a daughter. The family lives in a leaking office space beside a soap factory in Los Angeles and owes $1,500 in back rent. Old Dolio devises a scheme: they will fly to New York on prize tickets, and on the way back her parents will take her bag at the carousel so that she can claim it was lost and collect $1,575 in travel insurance.

On the return flight, her parents befriend Melanie, a cheerful young woman seated beside them, and recruit her to pose as their daughter at the baggage claim. The insurance payout will take weeks, so the family looks for other ways to raise cash, and Melanie proves an enthusiastic participant. She admits she works in an eyeglass store, introduces them to elderly clients they can rob, and leads them to a dying man who asks them to act as his family in his final moments. The experience unsettles Old Dolio, who is wounded to see her parents fuss over Melanie and overlook her.

When the insurance cheque arrives, Old Dolio overhears her mother calling Melanie "hon" and offers her the entire sum to say the same to her. Theresa refuses, but Melanie takes Old Dolio home and gives her the tenderness she has never known. Her parents leave seventeen birthday presents at Melanie's door and promise to change, giving her a necklace as an eighteenth gift. Old Dolio decides that if they leave her share of $525, it will mean they love her in their limited way. The next morning Melanie's flat has been stripped bare, but when Old Dolio and Melanie return the presents and the necklace, the refunds total exactly $525, and the two women kiss.

The film received widely positive reviews, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting a 90% approval rating from more than 200 critics.

title: The French Dispatch
tagline: Bringing the world to Kansas, one eccentric story at a time.
overview: The staff of an American magazine based in France puts out its last issue, with stories featuring an artist sentenced to life imprisonment, student riots, and a kidnapping resolved by a chef.
plot:
In 1975, in the fictional French town of Ennui-sur-Blasé, Arthur Howitzer Jr., the editor of the magazine The French Dispatch, dies of a heart attack. According to the wishes expressed in his will, publication of the magazine is immediately suspended following one final farewell issue, in which four articles are published, along with an obituary.

Herbsaint Sazerac delivers a cycling tour of Ennui-sur-Blasé, demonstrating several key areas such as the arcade, Le Sans Blague café and a pickpocket's alleyway. He compares the past and the present of each place, demonstrating how much and yet how little has changed in Ennui over time.

J. K. L. Berensen delivers a lecture at the art gallery of her former employer, Upshur "Maw" Clampette, in which she details the career of Moses Rosenthaler. Rosenthaler, a mentally disturbed artist serving a 50-year sentence in the Ennui prison for double murder, paints an abstract nude portrait of Simone, a guard with whom he develops a relationship. Julien Cadazio, an art dealer also serving time for tax evasion, is immediately taken by the painting and buys it despite Rosenthaler's protests. Upon his release, Cadazio convinces his family of art exhibitors to put it on display, and Rosenthaler soon becomes a sensation in the art world. Privately, Rosenthaler struggles with inspiration to the point of near-suicide, and devotes himself to a long-term project at Simone's challenging.
Three years later, Cadazio, his uncles, Clampette, Berensen, and a mob of artists inspired by Rosenthaler, all frustrated at the lack of further paintings, bribe their way into the prison to confront him, only to discover that his masterpiece is in fact a series of frescoes in the concrete prison hall. Angered that the paintings are irremovable from the prison, Cadazio gets into a physical altercation with Rosenthaler, but soon comes to appreciate the paintings for what they are, and later arranges for the entire wall to be airlifted out of the prison into a private museum in Kansas, owned by Clampette. For his actions in halting a prison riot that breaks out during the reveal of the paintings, Rosenthaler is released on probation. Simone also departs after earning a great sum of money for becoming the inspiration and motivation for Rosenthaler during his incarceration. Simone and Rosenthaler maintain correspondence following his release, but never see each other again.

Lucinda Krementz reports on a student protest breaking out in the streets of Ennui that soon boils over into the "Chessboard Revolution", so-called for the students using chess to communicate with the police. While the revolution initially is inspired by petty concerns over access to the girls' dormitory, the traumatic military conscription of one student, Mitch-Mitch, inspires greater uprising.

title: Skin
overview: A destitute young man, raised by racist skinheads and notorious among white supremacists, turns his back on hatred and violence to transform his life, with the help of a black activist and the woman he loves.
plot:
Skin is an American biographical drama written and directed by Guy Nattiv, loosely based on the true story of Bryon Widner, a former neo-Nazi skinhead who left the white power movement. Jamie Bell stars as Widner, with Danielle Macdonald, Vera Farmiga, Bill Camp, Daniel Henshall, Louisa Krause and Mike Colter in supporting roles. The film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2018 and was released in the United States by A24 in July 2019. It is distinct from Nattiv's short film of the same name, which won the Academy Award for Best Live Action Short Film.

In 2009, Bryon "Babs" Widner, whose face and body are covered in racist tattoos, lives in Indiana as a member of the Vinlanders Social Club, a violent skinhead group led by Fred "Hammer" Krager and his wife Shareen, played by Camp and Farmiga. The couple took Bryon in as a troubled teenager and raised him as their own, and he is fiercely loyal to this surrogate family, even though the group is brutal both to outsiders and to its own members.

After a confrontation at a protest, Bryon slashes the face of a Black teenager, and the words of the boy's mother outside the police station begin to shake him. As he watches Fred recruit a vulnerable young man named Gavin, his doubts about the movement grow. He falls in love with Julie Price, played by Macdonald, a single mother of three daughters who has experienced violence in a previous relationship with a skinhead. Julie insists that she will not allow her children to be exposed to his world, and Bryon begins the dangerous process of leaving the group. With the help of Daryle Jenkins, an anti-racist activist played by Colter, and the FBI, he seeks protection while the Vinlanders retaliate against him and his new family. Throughout the film, scenes of Bryon undergoing a long series of painful laser treatments to remove his facial tattoos frame his attempt to erase his past.

The film explores radicalisation, redemption and the difficulty of escaping a violent community, with Bell undergoing an extensive physical transformation for the role.

Skin received generally positive reviews, with critics praising Bell's performance and the film's unflinching depiction of hate groups, although some felt it relied on a familiar redemption narrative.

title: Poinsettias for Christmas
overview: It’s just weeks before Christmas when Ellie gets a call to return home to help her father on the family’s poinsettia farm. The family business is on the line to deliver tens of thousands of plants for the town’s annual parade. The problem is — the poinsettias have yet to turn red! As Ellie searches for the solution, she is reminded of where her heart truly lies as she falls in love with both her roots and a local botanist.
plot:
Poinsettias for Christmas is a 2018 Canadian-American romantic holiday television film directed by Christie Will Wolf and made for Lifetime, with Johnson Production Group and Annuit Coeptis Entertainment among its production companies. It stars Bethany Joy Lenz as Ellie Palmer, Marcus Rosner as Sean and John Schneider as Ellie's father, with Sharon Lawrence, Lauren London and Rhonda Dent in the supporting cast. It runs 87 minutes and is set in a small town in Maryland.

Ellie is a career-driven city planner who enjoys a busy urban life. Just weeks before Christmas, she is called home to help on her family's poinsettia farm because her father has hurt his back and cannot keep up during the busiest season of the year. The family business must deliver tens of thousands of plants for the town's annual Christmas parade, but on arrival Ellie discovers that the real problem is worse: the poinsettias are still green and have yet to turn red. Her parents admit that this is why they really needed her, since she has always had a special touch with the plants. Ellie initially clashes with Sean, a handsome botanist who now works on the farm, spends much of his time with her family and spills dirt on her cashmere coat when they first meet, and she blames him for the problem. As the two try new fertilizer, adjust the watering and argue over the thermostat, they grow closer. Complications come from Patty, Ellie's childhood rival and now a local lifestyle personality with her own show, who is dating Sean and offers to buy the farm. Ellie eventually realizes that the town's new development is to blame: the city lights at night are preventing the plants from changing color. The poinsettias turn red in time, but Ellie must still decide whether her future lies in the city or back home with her roots and the man she has fallen for.

The film premiered on Lifetime during the 2018 holiday season. Reviewers found it light and predictable but pleasant. Very Merry Movies called it an enjoyable, quick-paced film that was not too schmaltzy and that far exceeded its title, praising Lenz while regretting that the rivalry with Patty was shallow and that the story had too little Christmas in it, likening it to an HGTV episode crossed with a Hallmark movie. Patrick Serrano of Lifetime Uncorked gave it a rating of two Christmas trees, poking fun at its montages and formula.

title: They Shall Not Grow Old
overview: A documentary about World War I with never-before-seen footage to commemorate the centennial of Armistice Day, and the end of the war.
plot:
They Shall Not Grow Old is a documentary film that explores the lives of British soldiers during World War I, presented in a unique and powerful way through archival footage and interviews with veterans. The film delves into the harsh realities of war, the psychological toll it takes on soldiers, and the long-lasting impact it has on individuals and society.

At its core, the film is a poignant exploration of the human cost of conflict, shedding light on the experiences of ordinary men who were thrust into extraordinary circumstances. It highlights the camaraderie and bonds that formed among soldiers in the trenches, as well as the trauma and PTSD that many struggled with upon their return home.

The film also touches on themes of nostalgia, memory, and the passage of time, as the veterans' recollections serve as a window into a bygone era. The archival footage, which has been meticulously restored and presented in a cinematic format, adds to the sense of immediacy and intimacy, drawing the viewer into the world of the soldiers.

Ultimately, They Shall Not Grow Old is a powerful tribute to the men who served during World War I, and a reminder of the enduring impact that their experiences have had on our collective understanding of war and its effects on individuals.

title: Cinderella and the Secret Prince
overview: Cinderella discovers a secret that could shake their world: an evil witch turned the prince into a mouse and replaced him with a look-alike. Cinderella and her friends must save the real prince and help him defeat the evil witch.
plot:
Cinderella and the Secret Prince, also released as Cinderella 3D, is a 2018 American animated fantasy adventure film directed by Lynne Southerland from a screenplay by Francis Glebas, Alice Blehart, Stephanie Bursill and Russell Fung. A new take on the Brothers Grimm version of the "Cinderella" fairy tale, it was produced by the small animation studio Gold Valley Films on a reported budget of 20 million dollars. The English voice cast includes Cassandra Lee Morris as Cinderella, Chris Niosi as Prince Alex, Stephen Mendel as Olaf, Wendee Lee as the Witch, Kirsten Day as the good fairy Crystal, Stephanie Sanditz as the Stepmother, R. Martin Klein and Tony Azzolino as the mice Manny and Walt, and Terrence Stone as the Witch's eagle.

The story opens much like the classic tale. Cinderella, a kind-hearted young woman forced into servitude by her stepmother and two stepsisters after her parents' deaths, is helped to attend the royal ball not by the Fairy Godmother herself but by her young apprentice, Crystal. At the ball, however, the prince turns out to be incredibly rude and mean-spirited. Cinderella and her three mouse friends then discover a secret that could shake their world: the real prince, Alex, was turned into a mouse as a small boy, after his own parents died, by an evil witch who plans to take over the kingdom, and he has been replaced at the palace by a look-alike impostor, Olaf, who cooperates with her. Cinderella and her friends set out to rescue the true prince and restore him to human form with the help of a magic ring. Along the way the stepmother turns Cinderella over to the royal guard for money. Alex, who falls in love with Cinderella, regains his human shape and defeats Olaf, but the witch kidnaps Cinderella, and as the pair escape one of her spells turns Cinderella to stone. To save her, Alex uses the ring to undo the spell, returning himself to mouse form.

The film was released internationally and grossed about 12.1 million dollars. Critical reaction was modest. Folha de S.Paulo's review judged that it would convince only a very young audience. Writing for The Princess Blog, a reviewer found it surprisingly charming and reminiscent of the early Barbie fairy-tale films, with bright colours, expressive faces and costumes that recall Tangled, and praised Cinderella as a warm, optimistic heroine, but criticised the contrived cliffhanger ending as an obvious set-up for a sequel that cheapens the story.

title: Cherry
overview: Cherry drifts from college dropout to army medic in Iraq - anchored only by his true love, Emily. But after returning from the war with PTSD, his life spirals into drugs and crime as he struggles to find his place in the world.
plot:
Cherry is an American crime drama of 2021 from directors Anthony and Joe Russo, written by Angela Russo-Otstot and Jessica Goldberg and adapted from Nico Walker's semi-autobiographical novel of 2018. Tom Holland plays the title character, a college student who becomes an army medic and then a heroin-addicted bank robber, with Ciara Bravo as his wife Emily, Jack Reynor as the dealer known as Pills and Coke, Jeff Wahlberg as the soldier Jimenez, Forrest Goodluck as James Lightfoot and Michael Rispoli as Tommy.

Cherry falls for his classmate Emily at first sight, but when she announces that she is leaving to study in Montreal, he enlists in the Army as a medic to escape his heartbreak. Just before he ships out she admits she loves him too, and they marry before his deployment. Over two years of service he witnesses horrors, including the death of his friend Jimenez in a roadside bomb blast, and he returns home with post-traumatic stress. The OxyContin prescribed for his panic attacks becomes an addiction, Emily starts taking the pills herself, and both slide into heroin use.

After the couple consume the drugs stored in a safe they were keeping for Pills and Coke, they learn that the stash belonged to his boss, Black, who will kill them all. Cherry robs a bank to repay the debt and, driven by withdrawal, keeps robbing banks. Emily nearly dies of an overdose, her mother blames Cherry, and she leaves rehab to return to him, insisting she will use with or without him. Cherry recruits Pills and Coke and his friend Lightfoot for bigger robberies; when Pills and Coke bolts mid-heist, the others pick him up, find him shot, and, afraid to go to a hospital, let him die and dump his body. When Black comes to collect, Cherry says goodbye to Emily, pulls one last robbery in which he urges the teller to trip the alarm, pays Black, fires his gun in the air to draw police and gets high one final time before his arrest. He gets clean in prison and, paroled after fourteen years, walks out to find Emily waiting for him.

Apple acquired the film for about $40 million; it opened in select theatres on 26 February 2021 and streamed on Apple TV+ from 12 March. Critics praised Holland and Bravo but faulted the writing and direction, giving it 37% on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: The Nest
tagline: Having it all is never enough.
overview: Rory is an ambitious entrepreneur who brings his American wife and kids to his native country, England, to explore new business opportunities. After abandoning the sanctuary of their safe American suburban surroundings, the family is plunged into the despair of an archaic '80s Britain and their unaffordable new life in an English manor house threatens to destroy the family.
plot:
In the late 1980s, Rory and Allison O'Hara live a middle-class life in New York City with their kids Samantha "Sam" and Benjamin "Ben", the former born from Allison's previous relationship.
Allison teaches horseriding, while Rory works as a trader. Believing his opportunities in the States are limited, Rory persuades Allison to relocate with him to London, where he plans to return to the firm of his former employer Arthur Davis. Despite Allison's initial misgivings, the family moves into a huge old mansion in Surrey where Rory persuades Allison to start a horse farm on the property and brings her horse, Richmond, over from the States. Construction begins on a stable while Ben and Sam are enrolled in separate schools. Rory later takes Allison to high-class dinner parties with Arthur and his colleagues. However, the family has some difficulty adjusting, as their secluded location and respective commutes make it difficult for the children to get to school on time.
Several weeks later, construction abruptly stops on the stable. Learning that Rory never paid the builders, Allison discovers that his bank account is nearly empty. Rory promises he will have money soon, but Allison is forced to provide for the family by cutting into her hidden cash fund. Allison bristles at Rory's efforts to appear high-class while they remain nearly broke. At work, Rory proposes that Arthur sell his company to a larger American firm looking for a London office.
After brief consideration, Arthur refuses. Back at the mansion, Richmond collapses in pain and Allison is forced to go to a neighbouring farmer, who puts the horse down. Rather than go home following Arthur's rejection, Rory pays a visit to his mother, who shows no interest in his family and accuses Rory of abandoning her. Rory returns home late and gets into an argument with Allison over their financial woes and Rory's reckless, delusional behaviour.
In order to provide income to the household, Allison begins working as a farmhand. Allison's relationships with her children also become strained when Sam makes some disreputable friends and Ben gets into a fight with some school bullies. Rory and his colleague Steve arrange a potentially lucrative deal with a Norwegian fish-farming corporation. That night, he and Allison attend a dinner with Steve and their prospective clients while Sam and her friends throw a house party.
As the party gets out of control, Ben flees outside and witnesses Richmond's carcass being pushed to the surface of the grave due to improper burial. During the dinner, Allison openly mocks Rory before leaving the restaurant, taking the car and getting drunk at a nightclub. Rory attempts to downplay Allison's behaviour but his clients opt to go into business with Steve while cutting him out. Rory tries to take a taxi back to Surrey and confesses his many indiscretions to the driver, claiming his job is "pretending to be rich".

title: Extraction
tagline: When the mission ends, redemption begins
overview: Tyler Rake, a fearless mercenary who offers his services on the black market, embarks on a dangerous mission when he is hired to rescue the kidnapped son of a Mumbai crime lord.
plot:
Extraction is a 2020 action-thriller film directed by Sam Hargrave and written by Joe Russo and Chris Cowen. The movie stars Chris Hemsworth as Tyler Rake, an elite black-market mercenary known as "The Ghost" who specializes in high-stakes extraction missions.

The story begins with Tyler Rake, a former Special Forces operative, living a quiet life in Bangkok with his young son, Ovi (Rudhraksh Jaiswal). However, their peaceful existence is disrupted when Ovi is kidnapped by the Indian mafia, led by the ruthless and cunning Saju (Randeep Hooda), who demands a ransom of $7 million.

Tyler is forced to return to his old life as "The Ghost" and embark on a perilous mission to rescue Ovi. He teams up with Guney (Rudhraksh Thakur), a local fixer, and Saju's henchman, Sarran (Pankaj Tripathi). As Tyler navigates the treacherous underworld of international crime, he must use his exceptional skills and resources to outsmart Saju's men and reach Ovi before it's too late.

As the story unfolds, Tyler faces numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, rival mercenaries, and Saju's personal vendetta against him. Along the way, he also encounters a mysterious woman named Iseult (Rudhraksh's on-screen mother) who seems to be hiding secrets of her own.

The action-packed sequence of events culminates in an intense showdown between Tyler and Saju's men at a crowded nightclub. With his exceptional fighting skills and tactical expertise, Tyler manages to take down the henchmen one by one, but not before Saju reveals that he has been playing a double game all along.

In the thrilling finale, Tyler faces off against Saju in an explosive confrontation that leaves only one man standing. In the end, Tyler successfully rescues Ovi and exacts his revenge on Saju, bringing closure to his personal vendetta.

title: Everything Everywhere All at Once
tagline: The universe is so much bigger than you realize.
overview: An aging Chinese immigrant is swept up in an insane adventure, where she alone can save what's important to her by connecting with the lives she could have led in other universes.
plot:
Everything Everywhere All at Once is a 2022 American science fiction action comedy film written and directed by Daniel Kwan and Daniel Scheinert, also known as the Daniels. The film stars Michelle Yeoh, Ke Huy Quan, Jenny Slate, Harry Shum Jr., and Stephanie Hsu.

The movie follows Evelyn Wang (Michelle Yeoh), a middle-aged Chinese-American woman who is struggling to balance her life. She is married to Waymond (Ke Huy Quan), a laundromat owner, and they are facing financial difficulties due to their failing business. Evelyn's life takes a dramatic turn when she is audited by the IRS, and during the audit, she is suddenly thrust into a multiverse where every possibility plays out.

Evelyn discovers that she has the ability to access parallel universes, each with their own version of her life. She must navigate these alternate realities, encountering different versions of herself and those around her. Along the way, Evelyn must confront her own identity, relationships, and purpose in life.

As Evelyn navigates the multiverse, she also discovers that a villainous entity known as "Jobu Tupaki" (Stephanie Hsu) is threatening to destroy all of existence. Jobu Tupaki is an alternate version of Evelyn who has become a powerful being with the ability to manipulate reality.

Throughout the film, Evelyn's journey takes her through various parallel universes, each with its own unique twist on her life. She encounters versions of herself as a martial artist, a rock star, and even a superhero. Along the way, she must confront her own fears, insecurities, and desires.

The film features a blend of action, comedy, and drama, with a unique visual style that reflects Evelyn's journey through the multiverse. The movie has received widespread critical acclaim for its originality, creativity, and performances from the cast.

Overall, Everything Everywhere All at Once is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that explores themes of identity, purpose, and the human condition. With its unique blend of action, comedy, and drama, it is a must-see for fans of science fiction and adventure films.

title: Knives Out
tagline: Hell, any of them could have done it.
overview: When renowned crime novelist Harlan Thrombey is found dead at his estate just after his 85th birthday, the inquisitive and debonair Detective Benoit Blanc is mysteriously enlisted to investigate. From Harlan's dysfunctional family to his devoted staff, Blanc sifts through a web of red herrings and self-serving lies to uncover the truth behind Harlan's untimely death.
plot:
Knives Out is a 2019 mystery film written and directed by Rian Johnson. The movie takes place at the grand opening of the wealthy patriarch, Harlan Thrombey's (Christopher Plummer), estate.

The story begins with Harlan Thrombey, a renowned author of detective novels, who has invited his family to celebrate his 85th birthday. However, the festivities are cut short when Harlan is found dead in his study, and the family soon discovers that he was poisoned.

Detective Benoit Blanc (Daniel Craig), a renowned private investigator from New Orleans, is called to investigate the murder. As the investigation unfolds, it becomes clear that each member of the Thrombey family had a motive for the murder. There's Marta Cabrera (Ana de Armas), Harlan's loyal nurse and caregiver; Walt Thrombey (Michael Shannon), Harlan's eldest son and a successful businessman; Linda Drysdale (Jamie Lee Curtis), Harlan's daughter-in-law and a wealthy socialite; Joni Thrombey (Toni Collette), Harlan's youngest daughter and an actress; Ransom Drysdale (Chris Evans), Linda's son and a charming but entitled heir to the family fortune; and Chuck Thrombey (Lakeith Stanfield), Harlan's grandson and a struggling writer.

As Detective Blanc digs deeper, he uncovers a web of secrets, lies, and deceit that lead him to question everyone in the family. Through a series of clever twists and turns, the investigation reveals that each character had a reason to want Harlan dead, but not all of them are as innocent as they seem.

Throughout the movie, Detective Blanc's Southern charm and wit serve as a counterpoint to the dark and complex plot. His observations on human nature and his ability to piece together seemingly unrelated clues make him an excellent detective.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Harlan was not as well-liked by his family as he seemed. Each character had their own reasons for wanting him dead, but in the end, Detective Blanc reveals that the true culprit is none other than Ransom Drysdale.

The movie's climax features a surprising twist: Ransom, who had been struggling with feelings of inadequacy and jealousy towards his father, had planned the murder to gain control of the family fortune. However, just as he thinks he has gotten away with it, Detective Blanc reveals that Ransom was not the mastermind behind the plot.

In the end, it is revealed that Linda Drysdale, who had been hiding a dark secret, was the true culprit. She had been embezzling money from her husband's company and stood to gain a large sum of money by killing Harlan and framing Ransom for the crime.

The movie ends with Detective Blanc solving the case and revealing the truth about Linda's betrayal. The film concludes on a somber note, highlighting the complexities of human relationships and the devastating consequences of greed and deception.

Overall, Knives Out is a clever and engaging mystery that keeps viewers guessing until the very end. With its talented cast, witty dialogue, and intricate plot, it's no wonder this movie became a critical and commercial success.
