title: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings
original_title: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings
overview: Shang-Chi must confront the past he thought he left behind when he is drawn into the web of the mysterious Ten Rings organization.
plot:
Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings is a 2021 superhero film directed by Destin Daniel Cretton and produced by Marvel Studios. The movie follows the story of Shang-Chi, a skilled martial artist who must confront his troubled past and face off against his father's powerful organization.

The film begins with Shang-Chi (played by Simu Liu), a skilled fighter who has been living in hiding for years after being trained by his father, Wenwu (played by Tony Leung). Shang-Chi is haunted by the memories of his childhood, where he was forced to fight and kill under the orders of his father. He has been trying to escape this dark past and build a new life.

However, when Shang-Chi's sister, Xialing (played by Meng'er Zhang), arrives in San Francisco with a mysterious message from their mother, Shang-Chi is drawn back into his family's complicated history. The message reveals that Wenwu has stolen the powerful Ten Rings artifact, which holds the key to unlocking the secrets of the ancient Chinese mystic arts.

Shang-Chi soon finds himself on a perilous journey across China and San Francisco as he tries to stop Wenwu and reclaim the Ten Rings. Along the way, he meets Katy (played by Awkwafina), a street-smart thief who becomes his unlikely ally. Together, they must navigate treacherous landscapes, fight off Wenwu's henchmen, and confront their own personal demons.

As Shang-Chi delves deeper into his family's history, he discovers that his father's actions are motivated by a desire to fulfill an ancient prophecy and gain ultimate power. However, Shang-Chi soon realizes that the true enemy is not his father, but rather the dark forces that have consumed him.

Throughout the film, Cretton explores themes of identity, family, and redemption, weaving together elements of martial arts, mythology, and cultural heritage. The movie features stunning action sequences, heart-pumping fight choreography, and a richly detailed world inspired by Chinese culture.

Ultimately, Shang-Chi must confront his father in an epic showdown that will determine the fate of his family and the world. With its unique blend of action, drama, and humor, Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings is a thrilling adventure that will leave audiences cheering for more.

title: Kabaneri of the Iron Fortress: The Battle of Unato
original_title: 甲鉄城のカバネリ 海門決戦
overview: Half a year after the events of the series "Kabaneri of the Iron Fortress", the team attempt to take back Unato castle.
plot:
Kabaneri of the Iron Fortress: The Battle of Unato is a Japanese animated science fantasy film directed by Hiroyuki Imaishi and produced by Wit Studio. The movie takes place in the year 1883, in a world where humans live in a walled city called New Kanegashima to protect themselves from the Kabaneri, a species of humanoid creatures infected with a deadly disease that turns them into zombie-like beings.

The story follows Ikeda, a young and skilled engineer who is part of an elite group known as the "Iron Fortress" unit. The Iron Fortress is a mobile fortress designed to fight against the Kabaneri, and Ikeda's team is tasked with defending the city from these monstrous creatures.

As the movie begins, we see Ikeda and his team preparing for battle against the Kabaneri. They are equipped with advanced steam-powered machinery and a variety of deadly weapons. The team is led by Captain Sasaki, who has a personal vendetta against the Kabaneri.

The battle against the Kabaneri is intense and brutal, with both sides suffering heavy losses. Ikeda's team fights valiantly, but they soon realize that their enemy is not just mindless monsters - it's also a complex and terrifying foe that can adapt to their tactics.

As the battle rages on, we see flashbacks of Ikeda's past, including his relationship with his sister, who was killed by the Kabaneri. This personal connection makes Ikeda even more determined to defeat the enemy.

The movie takes a dramatic turn when Ikeda discovers that the Kabaneri are not just mindless creatures - they're also being controlled by a mysterious figure known as "The Puppeteer". The Puppeteer is revealed to be a powerful and ancient being who has been manipulating the Kabaneri for centuries, using them to further its own goals.

Ikeda's team launches a final assault on the Kabaneri stronghold, determined to defeat The Puppeteer and put an end to the war. The battle is intense and chaotic, with both sides suffering heavy losses. In the end, Ikeda faces off against The Puppeteer in a one-on-one duel.

The ending of the movie is bittersweet and emotionally charged. Ikeda emerges victorious, but not without great cost. He realizes that the war has changed him forever, and that he will never be able to go back to his old life. The movie ends with Ikeda standing alone, looking out at the ruins of the city, a symbol of the devastating consequences of war.

Overall, Kabaneri of the Iron Fortress: The Battle of Unato is a gripping and emotionally charged film that explores themes of war, sacrifice, and the human condition. With its stunning animation and intense action sequences, it's a must-see for fans of science fiction and fantasy.

title: Once Upon a Deadpool
overview: A kidnapped Fred Savage is forced to endure Deadpool's PG-13 rendition of Deadpool 2 as a Princess Bride-esque story that's full of magic, wonder & zero F's.
plot:
Once Upon a Deadpool is a 2018 American superhero comedy film directed by David Leitch and written by Rhett Reese, Paul Wernick, and Ryan Reynolds. The movie is a spin-off of the X-Men film series and serves as a sequel to Logan (2017).

The story begins with Wade Wilson, aka Deadpool (Ryan Reynolds), who has been rescued from his prison cell by Cable (Josh Brolin) and brought back to the present day. However, upon arrival, Wade discovers that he is now in a reality where he never died after being shot by the villainous Ajax (Ed Skrein). In this reality, Wade is still alive and has become a successful mercenary.

Cable informs Wade that he must travel with him to find his daughter, Nebula (Zazie Beetz), who was taken from him as a child. Along the way, they are joined by Domino (Zazie Beetz) and Russell Collins (Julian Dennison), a young mutant with the ability to heal.

As they embark on their journey, Wade and Cable's relationship is put to the test as they disagree on how to handle their mission. Meanwhile, Ajax returns, seeking revenge against Wade for foiling his plans in the previous film.

Throughout their adventure, the group faces various obstacles, including a run-in with the villainous Vanisher (Bill Skarsgård) and a confrontation with the sinister organization known as the "Vanisher's" henchmen. Along the way, Wade also begins to form a bond with Russell, who becomes like a surrogate son to him.

As they near their destination, Wade and Cable's differences come to a head, leading to a dramatic showdown between the two. In the end, Wade is able to reconcile with his past and find closure with his daughter, Nebula.

The film concludes with Wade reflecting on his journey and the lessons he has learned about family, friendship, and redemption. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Wade looking forward to a brighter future for himself and those around him.

Overall, Once Upon a Deadpool is a heartwarming and action-packed adventure that explores themes of family, loyalty, and self-discovery. With its witty humor, engaging characters, and thrilling action sequences, the film is a must-see for fans of the X-Men franchise and comedy enthusiasts alike.

title: Ready or Not
tagline: In-laws will be the death of her.
overview: A bride's wedding night takes a sinister turn when her eccentric new in-laws force her to take part in a terrifying game.
plot:
Ready or Not is a 2019 American horror comedy film directed by Matt Bettinelli-Olpin and Tyler Gillett, written by Rafe Kukendat, and produced by Jason Blum, James DeMonaco, and others.

The movie follows the story of Grace Le Domas (Samara Weaving), a young woman who marries into a wealthy family, the Hesmonds, on her 21st birthday. The Hesmonds are part of an ancient tradition called "the game," where the bride must participate in a deadly game of hide and seek with the groom's family members.

The game is a twisted test of survival, where each player is eliminated until only one remains. The Hesmond family consists of Sam (Adam Brody), Paula (Andi Matichak), Jack (Mark O'Brien), Alexis (Samara Weaving's real-life sister, Mia Wasikowska was initially cast but dropped out and the role went to  Millicent Simmonds' friend), and Daniel (Henry Czerny). The family is led by Sam's father, Ben (André Holland).

As the game begins, Grace soon realizes that she must use her wits and resourcefulness to survive. However, as the night progresses, it becomes clear that the Hesmond family has a dark secret: they are all connected to an ancient curse that has been passed down through generations.

Throughout the movie, the tension builds up as Grace tries to outsmart each player, while also trying to understand the true nature of the game and the family's motivations. The film features a blend of horror, comedy, and social commentary, with a focus on class inequality and the exploitation of wealth.

As the game reaches its climax, it becomes clear that the Hesmond family is not just playing a harmless game, but are actually trying to eliminate Grace as part of their twisted tradition. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Ben has been manipulating the game all along, using his wealth and influence to ensure that only one player remains.

In the end, Grace manages to outsmart the Hesmond family and escape with her life, but not before she exacts a sense of revenge on those who have wronged her. The movie ends with a darkly comedic tone, as Grace is seen driving away from the Hesmond estate, ready to start a new life free from the curse.

Overall, Ready or Not is a tense and entertaining horror comedy that explores themes of class inequality, family dynamics, and survival. With its blend of humor, suspense, and social commentary, it has become a modern classic in the horror genre.

title: Dear Evan Hansen
tagline: An honest and original story for the outsider in all of us.
overview: Evan Hansen, a high schooler with social anxiety, unintentionally gets caught up in a lie after the family of a classmate who committed suicide mistakes one of Hansen’s letters for their son’s suicide note.
plot:
Seventeen-year-old Evan Hansen lives with social anxiety and depression. His therapist Dr. Sherman recommends that he write letters to himself detailing why "today will be a good day." Evan's mother, Heidi, suggests that he ask people to sign his cast, after Evan had fallen out of a tree and broken his arm, to try and make friends. At school, Evan writes his letter to himself, wondering whether anyone would notice if he disappeared.
Evan's classmate, Connor Murphy, offers to sign his cast, taking up a lot of space. He finds Evan's letter and becomes furious at the mention of his sister, Zoe, who he learns Evan is attracted to. Believing that Evan wrote the letter to provoke him, Connor storms out with the letter in hand. Three days later, Evan is called to the principal's office and is told by Connor's parents, Cynthia and Larry, that Connor died by suicide. Despite Evan's attempts to tell the truth, the two misinterpret the letter Connor stole as a suicide note addressed to Evan, with Connor's name on his cast solidifying their belief.
Evan is invited to the Murphys' house for dinner. Under pressure from Cynthia, he invents a friendship between himself and Connor, manufacturing a story about breaking his arm while with Connor at an orchard the Murphys visited. Evan enlists his family friend, Jared, in fabricating backdated emails between him and Connor to confirm his story. Zoe wonders why Connor included her name in his suicide note due to past experiences. Evan, still unable to tell the truth, tells Zoe all the reasons he loves her, pretending the reasons were from Connor's perspective.
Alana Beck, a classmate with social issues similar to Evan's, proposes "The Connor Project," a student group dedicated to keeping Connor's memory alive, with an upcoming assembly as the kickoff. At the assembly, Evan gives a speech about his loneliness and friendship with Connor, retelling the orchard story. A video of the speech goes viral, with Evan's words being used as hope to people dealing with mental illness. Zoe is overcome by the positive reception and thanks Evan for helping her family.
Evan and Alana launch a crowdfunding campaign through The Connor Project to reopen the orchard. Evan begins to neglect his mother, The Connor Project, and his therapy in favor of spending time with the Murphys. When Zoe comes over to Evan's house one night, she confesses her feelings for him and the two begin a romantic relationship. Meanwhile, Heidi shows up at the Murphys' for dinner, during which Cynthia and Larry offer to give Connor's college fund to Evan. Heidi declines, refusing charity from the wealthy Murphys.
When Alana begins to doubt Evan's friendship with Connor, Evan emails her his therapy letter, saying it was Connor's suicide note. Alana posts the letter on her social media in order to get The Connor Project to its funding goal.

title: The Guilty
overview: A demoted police officer assigned to a call dispatch desk is conflicted when he receives an emergency phone call from a kidnapped woman.
plot:
Troubled LAPD officer Joe Baylor works the night shift at a 911 call center while awaiting a court hearing for an incident that occurred on duty eight months prior. He answers a call from Emily Lighton, a woman who states she has been abducted. While traveling in a white van, Emily is forced to hang up before she can provide more details. Joe relays the information to the California Highway Patrol, who cannot locate the van without a license plate number.
Joe calls Emily's home phone and speaks with her six-year-old daughter Abby, who tells him that her mom left the house with her dad, Henry Fisher. After getting Henry's cell phone number from Abby, he is able to retrieve the van's plate number.
Joe also learns that Henry has a record of assault, so he calls Sergeant Miller to send a patrol unit to Emily's home to do a welfare check on Abby and her baby brother, Oliver. He also requests he send another to investigate Henry's apartment. Miller refuses to send anyone to Henry's without a warrant. Reminding Joe of his legal issues, Miller suggests he stop investigating. Afterwards, Joe calls Henry and demands to know where he is taking Emily. Henry hangs up after Joe starts asking questions in an accusatory tone. Joe then calls his former partner, Rick, who is off-duty. Joe asks him to go to Henry's house. Rick complies, but also expresses concern about Joe's upcoming hearing at which he is set to provide testimony.
Joe receives a panicked call from Abby when two officers arrive at her home; he instructs her to let them in. The officers notice blood on Abby and, upon searching the property, find Oliver in the bedroom either gravely injured or dead. Joe calls Henry and accuses him of killing his son. Henry hangs up again. On the line again with Emily, Joe tells her to try to crash the van. Emily makes an attempt, to no avail.
Meanwhile, Rick breaks into Henry's apartment and finds documents showing that Emily had recently been a patient in a psychiatric treatment facility in San Bernardino. Back on the phone with Emily, she admits she thinks she will die and does not want to be locked up again. Emily goes on to say that she believed Oliver had "snakes in his stomach" and that she "took them out." Joe realizes that Emily was the one who hurt baby Oliver, and Henry is trying to have her readmitted to the psychiatric hospital. Outside of the van, Emily hits Henry with a brick and runs away.
On the phone with Joe, Henry explains that she had been off her medication for a number of weeks, as they could not afford them. Henry feels guilty about having left Emily, believing this triggered the psychotic episode during which she hurt Oliver. Henry does not trust the police and the criminal justice system due to his own legal troubles and because of the many failed attempts by various government agencies to help his mentally ill wife. Emily does not know what she has done and Henry fears what she will do after she finds out.

title: Misbehaviour
tagline: Miss World 1970: The launch of a revolution
overview: A group of women involved in the Women's Liberation Movement hatched a plan to invade the stage and disrupt the live broadcast at the 1970 Miss World competition in London, resulting in overnight fame for the newly-formed organization. When the show resumed, the results caused an uproar and turned the Western ideal of beauty on its head.
plot:
Sally Alexander successfully applies to study history at University College London. At a conference on women's rights she meets Jo Robinson, a feminist activist. After helping Jo evade arrest for defacing a sexist billboard advertisement, Jo introduces Sally to her women's group where she is invited to collaborate on the group's messaging and media as part of a planned protest at the 1970 Miss World competition, which is due to take place in London. American comedian Bob Hope is hired to present the event over the objections of Hope's wife Dolores, who is angered by Hope's affair with the winner of the 1961 edition.
The Miss World contestants arrive in the city. Among them are Pearl Jansen (Miss "Africa South"), who the organizers have included to deflect criticisms of collaboration with the Apartheid regime, and Jennifer Hosten (Miss Grenada). Jennifer and Pearl bond over their shared experience of anti-black racism. Jennifer also befriends Marjorie Johansson (Miss Sweden), the favourite, who confesses to feeling demeaned and exploited by the competition. Frustrated by the casual sexism she experiences at university, Sally hatches a plan to disrupt the live television broadcast of the Miss World contest by infiltrating the crowd. Several members of the group volunteer and buy audience tickets. Pearl privately confesses to Jennifer that the regime warned her that if she spoke out about the treatment of black South Africans she wouldn't be allowed to return home. Sally and her mother argue about Sally's activism and the toll her mother believes it's taking on Sally's daughter and her relationship with her partner Gareth.
A car bomb, attributed to the anarchist Angry Brigade, explodes outside the theatre hosting the event. Despite Gareth's pleas for Sally to call off the protest, she and Jo resolve to proceed. The competition begins, with the contestants, audience, organizers and Hope having to cross a picket line of protestors. Hope introduces the event with a series of sexist jokes. The judging panel whittles the number of contestants down to a final seven, among them Pearl and Jennifer. Jo and Sally's group start the protest by heckling Hope and flour-bombing the stage. Jo and Sally are arrested. The broadcast is temporarily halted but resumes shortly afterwards. Pearl wins second place before it is announced that Jennifer is Miss World - the first woman of colour to win. Backstage she has a conversation with Sally, who is being taken away by police, where they disagree over the protest.
A post-script explains that Jennifer went on to study Political Science and International Relations, later becoming Grenada's High Commissioner to Canada. Sally became Professor of Modern History at the University of London. Jo gave birth five months after the competition and later trained as a midwife. Pearl returned home to South Africa and became a singer after the fall of Apartheid. The protest succeeded in widely-publicising the women's liberation movement.

title: Fractured
tagline: Finding his family means facing the truth.
overview: Driving cross-country, Ray and his wife and daughter stop at a highway rest area where his daughter falls and breaks her arm. After a frantic rush to the hospital and a clash with the check-in nurse, Ray is finally able to get her to a doctor. While the wife and daughter go downstairs for an MRI, Ray, exhausted, passes out in a chair in the lobby. Upon waking up, they have no record or knowledge of Ray's family ever being checked in.
plot:
Fractured is a 2019 American psychological thriller directed by Brad Anderson from a screenplay by Alan B. McElroy. Sam Worthington stars as Ray Monroe, a man searching for his missing wife and daughter after a head injury that may be distorting his grasp of reality, with Lily Rabe, Stephen Tobolowsky, Adjoa Andoh and Lucy Capri in supporting roles. It premiered at Fantastic Fest on September 22, 2019, and was released on Netflix on October 11, 2019.

Ray, his wife Joanne and their daughter Peri are driving home after Thanksgiving with Joanne's parents, bickering about the state of the marriage. At a gas station stop, Peri is frightened by a stray dog and backs toward an open construction pit. Ray throws a rock to scare the dog away, but Peri falls into the hole. Ray leaps in after her and strikes his head. When he comes to, Joanne is tending to Peri, whose arm appears to be broken, and the family drives to a hospital they passed a few miles back.

During admission, staff unusually ask whether they would agree to place Peri on the organ donor register. A doctor orders a CT scan, and Joanne accompanies Peri to the basement while Ray falls asleep in the waiting room. When he wakes hours later, no one has any record of his wife or daughter, and the remaining nurse insists he arrived alone and was treated only for a head wound. Increasingly frantic and convinced the hospital is involved in organ harvesting, Ray is sedated and confined but escapes and persuades two police officers to investigate. Mounting evidence suggests his family was never there, and at the gas station the officers find a large bloodstain in the pit. Ray seizes a gun, returns to the hospital and fights his way to the basement to rescue Peri and Joanne.

As he drives away, the truth is revealed: Peri died in her fall and Joanne was killed in the pit during a confrontation with Ray. Their bodies had been in the car all along, the hospital ordeal was his mind's denial of what happened, and the unconscious figure in the back seat is a seriously ill stranger he dragged from surgery.

The film was shot in Winnipeg, Manitoba. Reviews were mixed: Rotten Tomatoes gives it 56% from 27 critics, praising Worthington's arresting performance, while Metacritic gave it 36 out of 100.

tagline: There's a little magic in all of us ...almost all of us.

plot:
Encanto is a 2021 animated musical fantasy film produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie takes place in Colombia and follows the story of the Madrigal family, who live in a magical house in the mountains.

The story centers around Mirabel Madrigal (voiced by Stephanie Beatriz), the only member of the family who does not possess any special gifts or magical powers. According to Colombian folklore, each member of the family has been blessed with a unique gift that allows them to contribute to the household and its magic.

Mirabel's family is led by her mother, Julieta (voiced by Jennifer Lopez), who can heal physical wounds through cooking; her father, Agustín (voiced by Juan de Dios Botero), who can make anyone fall in love with him through music; and her older sister, Luisa (voiced by Diane Guerrero), who has superhuman strength.

As Mirabel navigates her way through adolescence, she struggles to find her place within the family. She feels like an outcast because of her lack of magical powers and is often overlooked by her family members. However, when a mysterious curse begins to affect the family's gifts, Mirabel must embark on a journey to save her family and their magical house.

Along the way, Mirabel discovers that the curse was caused by a past tragedy in the family's history and that she has a crucial role to play in breaking it. With the help of her family members, Mirabel learns to appreciate her own unique qualities and finds a way to contribute to the household in her own special way.

The movie features stunning animation, catchy music, and a heartwarming story that celebrates Colombian culture and the importance of family. The characters are well-developed and relatable, making it easy for audiences to become invested in their stories.

Overall, Encanto is a beautifully crafted film that explores themes of identity, belonging, and the power of love and acceptance. With its vibrant animation, memorable music, and inspiring story, it's no wonder why Encanto has become a modern Disney classic.

title: Weathering with You
tagline: A story about the secret of this world that only I and she know.
overview: The summer of his high school freshman year, Hodaka runs away from his remote island home to Tokyo, and quickly finds himself pushed to his financial and personal limits. The weather is unusually gloomy and rainy every day, as if taking its cue from his life. After many days of solitude, he finally finds work as a freelance writer for a mysterious occult magazine. Then, one day, Hodaka meets Hina on a busy street corner. This bright and strong-willed girl possesses a strange and wonderful ability: the power to stop the rain and clear the sky.
plot:
In June 2021, high schooler Hodaka Morishima runs away from home. When his ferry to Tokyo is hit by a torrential rainstorm, he is almost washed away, but is saved by Keisuke Suga. Suga gives the boy his business card and tells him to call if he needs a job. Hodaka struggles to find work in the city. He finds an abandoned Makarov PM handgun and keeps it even though guns are illegal. He meets Hina Amano, a McDonald's employee, who pities him and gives him free food. Suga hires him as his assistant; he and his niece Natsumi publish a small occult magazine investigating strange phenomena, including the unusually rainy weather. They hear the legend of "Sunshine Girls" who can stop rain, and bring sunshine.
Hodaka sees Hina being intimidated into working at a club and in panic, fires his gun at the club owner, barely missing him. Hina takes him to Yoyogi Kaikan, an abandoned building with a shrine on the roof, where he also throws the gun away, and amazes him by demonstrating her ability to clear the sky by praying. Hodaka learns that Hina is an orphan living alone with her younger brother Nagi. Seeing that they are also in financial trouble, Hodaka proposes they start a business having Hina clear the weather for social gatherings. Their business becomes a success, but Hina is filmed and shown on television, leading to their site getting flooded with requests. They decide to temporarily suspend business to let Hina rest. Meanwhile, Suga and Natsumi interview the old priest of a shrine who tells them the legend of "Weather Maidens" (天気の乙女, Tenki no Otome) who can control the rain, adding that they pay a heavy price for their powers.
Police are searching for Hodaka, whose family has reported him missing. They trace him using security footage of him using the gun. Officers arrive at Hina's apartment and interrogate her; Hina realizes that because they have no legal guardian, social services will separate her and Nagi. Suga, also visited by the police, fires Hodaka, explaining that police suspect him of kidnapping, and gives him severance pay in cash. Hodaka, Hina, and Nagi decide to run away together. As torrential rain, unnatural cold, and even snow continue to descend on Tokyo, a state of emergency is declared in response to the severe and abnormal weather.
Police spot Hodaka as a fugitive and restrain him, but he is saved by Hina, who unintentionally uses her powers to destroy a small box truck with lightning. They take shelter in a hotel using the cash Hodaka received from Suga. Hina reveals that her body is slowly turning transparent the more she uses her power, and says her sacrifice will allow the weather to return to normal. The next day, Hina has vanished and the rain has stopped. The police track Hodaka to the hotel and take him into custody. Nagi is sent to the children's counseling center.
Hodaka, realizing that he has fallen in love with Hina, escapes from custody with the help of Natsumi.

title: Snake Eyes: G.I. Joe Origins
overview: After saving the life of their heir apparent, tenacious loner Snake Eyes is welcomed into an ancient Japanese clan called the Arashikage where he is taught the ways of the ninja warrior. But, when secrets from his past are revealed, Snake Eyes' honor and allegiance will be tested – even if that means losing the trust of those closest to him.
plot:
Living on the run, a young boy and his father are found by their sinister pursuers. Forced to roll dice to determine his fate, the father is murdered after rolling double ones, but his son escapes.
Twenty years later, the boy has adopted the name "Snake Eyes" and is discovered by Yakuza boss Kenta Takamura, competing in an underground fighting circuit. With the promise of help finding his father's killer, he agrees to join Kenta's criminal organization, and is asked to execute a man who infiltrated the gang, but helps him escape instead.
The man is Kenta's cousin Tommy, who reveals that they were both in line to lead the Arashikage clan, an ancient ninja society. Banished after trying to have Tommy killed, Kenta still seeks control of the clan. Grateful to Snake Eyes, Tommy brings him to his family's dōjō in Tokyo to be initiated. Tommy's grandmother Sen, the clan's current leader, agrees to let Snake Eyes undergo three trials to prove his worth.
In his first test, Snake Eyes is unable to seize a bowl of water from the clan's Hard Master; realizing this is a test of humility, he succeeds by respectfully asking instead. Unbeknownst to the clan, Snake Eyes has been tasked by Kenta with betraying Tommy; their escape was staged to allow Snake Eyes to win Tommy's trust, and to steal the clan's sacred "Jewel of the Sun".
The clan's head of security, Akiko, distrusts Snake Eyes, but she accompanies he and Tommy on a raid of Kenta's gang. They learn through an ally, Major Scarlett O'Hara, that Kenta is allied with the terrorist organization Cobra. Snake Eyes confronts Kenta and his Cobra liaison, the Baroness, who warns that stealing the jewel is the only way they will lead him to his father's killer.
The clan's Blind Master administers Snake Eyes' second test, a vision of his father, and he bonds with Akiko after telling her about his father's death. For his final trial, he faces the clan's gigantic, sacred anacondas. Sensing he is not truly pure of heart, the snakes attack, but he is saved by Akiko. Snake Eyes conceals his deception, but admits to having vengeance in his heart, & his lifelong search for his father’s murderer. He is allowed to live, but is expelled from the clan. He bids farewell to Tommy as blood brothers, but breaks into the clan's temple that night, subduing Akiko and stealing the jewel.
He delivers it to Kenta, who agrees to give it to Cobra once he has used it to take over the Arashikage. Snake Eyes receives his reward — his father's killer, a former Cobra agent — and forces him to roll his own dice, but spares his life and returns to warn the Arashikage. Tommy puts aside his anger when Snake Eyes comes to his aid, as Kenta uses the jewel's fiery magical powers to lay waste to the dōjō. Scarlett arrives to fight off Kenta's men, but she and Sen are captured.
A power-hungry Kenta refuses to hand over the jewel, prompting the Baroness to agree to a temporary alliance with Scarlett and the clan.

title: Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse
tagline: Miles Morales' story and the Spider-Verse web expands.
overview: After reuniting with Gwen Stacy, Miles Morales — Brooklyn's full-time, friendly neighborhood Spider-Man — is catapulted across the Multiverse, where he encounters a team of Spider-People charged with protecting its very existence. But when the heroes clash on how to handle a new threat, Miles finds himself pitted against the other Spiders and must redefine what it means to be a hero so he can save the people he loves most.
plot:
Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse is a 2022 American animated superhero film directed by Joaquim Dos Santos, Kemp Powers, and Justin K. Thompson. The movie is produced by Sony Pictures Animation and Columbia Pictures.

The story begins with Miles Morales (voiced by Shameik Moore), a teenager who has just been bitten by a genetically engineered spider that gives him superpowers. Miles struggles to balance his new life as Spider-Man with his relationships with his family, particularly his parents, Rio (Lauren Vélez) and Jefferson (Brian Tyree Henry).

As Miles navigates his new identity, he meets Peter B. Parker (voiced by Jake Johnson), a worn-out Spider-Man from another dimension who has been traveling through the multiverse to find a way back home. The two Spiders team up to stop Kingpin (Jason Schwartzman) and his son, Otto Octavius (Riz Ahmed), who have stolen the Spider-Verse's most powerful artifact, the Web-Slinger.

The movie takes Miles on an epic journey across multiple dimensions, where he meets other Spider-People, including Spider-Gwen (Hailee Steinfeld), Spider-Man Noir (Nicolas Cage), Peni Parker (Kimiko Glenn), and Spider-Ham (John Mulaney). Together, they form the Spider-Verse's defense against Kingpin's plans to destroy the multiverse.

As Miles and his new friends navigate through different dimensions, they encounter various challenges and obstacles. They also learn about the concept of the "Multiverse" and how it works, which adds a layer of complexity to the story.

Throughout the movie, Miles struggles with his own identity as Spider-Man, feeling pressure from Peter B. Parker's mentorship and trying to prove himself as a worthy Spider-Man in his own right. He also grapples with the consequences of his actions, particularly when he is forced to make difficult choices that affect the lives of those around him.

The movie features stunning animation, vibrant colors, and an energetic soundtrack that perfectly captures the spirit of the Spider-Verse. The voice cast delivers impressive performances, bringing depth and nuance to their characters.

In the end, Miles and his friends successfully defeat Kingpin and Otto Octavius, saving the multiverse from destruction. However, the movie concludes on a bittersweet note, as Miles says goodbye to Peter B. Parker, who has found a way back home. The final scene sets up the possibility for future adventures in the Spider-Verse.

Overall, Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse is an exciting and visually stunning film that explores themes of identity, friendship, and responsibility. With its talented voice cast, engaging storyline, and impressive animation, it's a must-watch for fans of the Spider-Man franchise and superhero movies in general.

overview: The series focuses on the adventures of Arata Kasuga, a high school student, who is targeted by Lilith, a teacher at a mystical school. plot:
Trinity Seven: Heavens Library & Crimson Lord is a 2019 Japanese animated fantasy romantic comedy and the second feature film based on the Trinity Seven manga created by Kenji Saitō and Akinari Nao, following The Eternal Library and the Alchemist Girl. Hiroshi Nishikiori directed at the studio Seven Arcs from a screenplay by Saitō, with character designs by Shinpei Tomōka and music by Technoboys Pulcraft Green-fund, and the cast of the television series returned, led by Yoshitsugu Matsuoka as Arata Kasuga and Yumi Hara as Lilith Asami, with Aya Uchida, Ayane Sakura, Yōko Hikasa and Nao Tōyama, joined by Tomoaki Maeno as the demon lord Abyss Trinity and Shizuka Itō as the demonic sword Judecca.

Arata, a student mage who carries the power of a Demon Lord candidate, sets out on a routine expedition with Lilith, Akio, Lieselotte and the former enemy Lugh to a lifeless ruin that was once Akio's hometown, destroyed in an attack and closely linked to a hidden library in the sky. Soon after they arrive, a beam of light seizes the group and carries them up to the floating Heavens Library.

There they face their most dangerous opponent yet: Abyss Trinity, a powerful Demon Lord from another dimension who reveals that he is Lilith's father. He challenges Arata, who is now a Demon Lord candidate himself, and the battle goes badly; Lilith is taken captive, since her father intends to use her to restore his full power, and the rest of the group is forced into hiding. To stand a chance, Arata must grow stronger and obtain a new weapon. He seeks out Judecca, a Demon Lord weapon sealed within the library, but nearly loses control of his magic when he tries to wield it, until Lieselotte's numerology magic pulls him back from the brink and he masters a new archive of magic. With the other members of the Trinity Seven joining the fight, Arata and his companions rescue Lilith from Abyss and defeat him, and the Heavens Library is destroyed. As in the series, the action is interspersed with risqué comedy built around Arata's lecherous streak.

The film opened in Japanese cinemas on 29 March 2019 through Avex Pictures and was streamed by Crunchyroll outside Japan. Its theme song, "Against the Abyss," was performed by ZAQ. Reviewers described it as light, entertaining fan service aimed at existing fans of the series, with energetic action but little depth.

title: Trouble
tagline: From the silk sheets... to the mean streets...
overview: A pampered dog named Trouble must learn to live in the real world while trying to escape from his former owner's greedy children and must learn how to survive on the big-city streets.
plot:
Trouble, also known as Dog Gone Trouble, is a 2019 computer-animated comedy directed by Kevin Johnson and written by Rob Muir from a story by Muir and Jordan Katz. It features the voices of Big Sean as Trouble, Pamela Adlon as Rousey and Lucy Hale as Zoe Bell, with Wilmer Valderrama, Marissa Winokur, Joel McHale, Damon Wayans Jr., Olivia Holt and Betty White, in what became her final film role. The film was dedicated to the memory of executive producer Conrad Vernon's dog, Linus.

Trouble is a pampered dog who lives in luxury in a mansion with his wealthy elderly owner, Mrs. Sarah Vanderwhoozie, cared for by her loyal butler James. When Mrs. Vanderwhoozie dies of natural causes, her greedy niece and nephew, the twins Claire and Norbert, arrive to claim her fortune. While clearing out the house, they carelessly get rid of Trouble, only to learn from their aunt's lawyer that they can inherit only if they prove they can take care of the dog within a few days. Desperate, they hire Thurman Sanchez, an eccentric animal tracker, to bring him back.

Meanwhile, Trouble finds himself lost in the city with no collar, after a gang of nut-obsessed squirrels steals it in revenge for a mishap. Having never fended for himself, he must learn to survive on the streets. He meets Rousey, a tough but kind-hearted stray pit bull, and accidentally causes a chase through a restaurant that costs Zoe, a pizza delivery girl and aspiring singer, one of her deliveries. As Trouble struggles to adjust to life without his comforts, he finds friendship among other dogs, forms a bond with Zoe and begins to discover what home and family really mean, while Thurman and the twins close in on him.

The film includes cameo appearances by personalities such as dog trainer Cesar Millan and chef Ludo Lefebvre, and blends slapstick chases with a story about loyalty and belonging.

Completed in 2019, Trouble was distributed worldwide by Netflix on May 28, 2021. It received largely negative reviews; Chris Azzopardi of The New York Times wrote that while home is at the center of the story, the film itself is nothing to write home about.

title: Saving Flora
tagline: How far would you go to save a friend?
overview: Flora is a circus elephant who can no longer perform her tricks. The night before she's scheduled to be euthanized, the circus owner's 14-year old daughter, Dawn, sneaks Flora from the circus. All that stands between them and the safety of the elephant preserve is two hundred kilometers of woods, one raging river, two elephant hunters and the fear of not making it.
plot:
Saving Flora is a 2018 American family adventure drama directed by Mark Drury Taylor from a screenplay he wrote with David Moss. Produced by FJ Productions, it stars Jenna Ortega, Martin Martinez, David Arquette and Leonor Varela, with Tom Arnold and Rhea Perlman, under the tagline "How far would you go to save a friend?". The film was shot in 21 days in the Los Angeles area, including the town of Piru and the Angeles Crest. Flora is played by Tai, a veteran film elephant nearly 50 years old at the time of filming, whose earlier credits include Water for Elephants; the animal rights organisation PETA objected that the elephant had been exploited and trained under cruel conditions and asked why computer effects had not been used instead.

Flora was once the star attraction of the struggling circus run by Henry (Arquette), but because of arthritis the elephant can no longer perform her tricks. Henry and his 14-year-old daughter Dawn (Ortega) hope that an elephant preserve will take her in, but at the last minute it turns them down, demanding a large donation the circus cannot afford. With a heavy heart Henry decides to have Flora put down, and knowing it would break Dawn's heart, since Flora was trained by her late mother, he sends the girl to her aunt. Dawn discovers the plan, and the night before Flora is due to be euthanised she sneaks the elephant out of the circus and sets off on foot for the preserve. Between them and safety lie some two hundred kilometres of woods, a raging river and the mountains. They are pursued not only by Henry and Isabella (Varela), his new partner and the circus's star performer, but also by two elephant hunters, and a crook sends his protégé Sebastian (Martinez), a young pickpocket, after them. Sebastian, however, has his heart in the right place and helps Dawn and Flora on their journey. Flora finally reaches the preserve and is taken in, thanks to donations raised by Isabella, who documented the search on social media; there Flora meets her daughter. Sebastian joins the circus, where Dawn becomes a rising star.

Saving Flora premiered at the Southampton International Film Festival in October 2018, winning best feature film, and Taylor received the Indie Vision debut director award at the Twin Cities Film Fest. In Poland it grossed about 148,000 dollars. Germany's Lexikon des internationalen Films called it a likeable if hardly credible children's adventure, winning viewers over with its sincere animal-welfare message.

title: The Invisible Man
tagline: What You Can't See Can Hurt You
overview: When Cecilia's abusive ex takes his own life and leaves her his fortune, she suspects his death was a hoax. As a series of coincidences turn lethal, Cecilia works to prove that she is being hunted by someone nobody can see.
plot:
The Invisible Man is a 2020 psychological horror film directed by Leigh Whannell, based on the 1933 novel of the same name by H.G. Wells.

The story begins with Cecilia Kass (Elisabeth Moss), a young woman who escapes from an emotionally and physically abusive relationship with her boyfriend, Adrian Griffin (Oliver Jackson-Cohen). After a violent incident, Cecilia flees to Boston, where she meets a therapist named Dr. Bernard Rose (David Strathairn).

Cecilia begins to experience strange occurrences, including hearing whispers in her ear and seeing apparitions around her. She becomes convinced that Adrian is stalking her from beyond the grave, using his wealth and influence to manipulate those around him.

As Cecilia delves deeper into her past, she discovers a dark secret: Adrian was involved in a sinister experiment at his family's estate, where he used a revolutionary technology to become invisible. The experiment went horribly wrong, leaving Adrian with severe psychological trauma and a deep-seated need for control.

Cecilia becomes determined to expose the truth about Adrian's past and bring him to justice. She enlists the help of Dr. Rose, who is initially hesitant but eventually becomes her ally.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Adrian has become increasingly unstable and paranoid, using his wealth and influence to manipulate those around him. He begins to stalk Cecilia again, this time using his technology to make himself invisible.

The film's tension builds as Cecilia tries to evade Adrian's attacks and uncover the truth about his past. Along the way, she discovers a series of cryptic messages and clues that suggest Adrian's experiment has had far-reaching consequences, including the creation of an army of mindless drones who are loyal only to him.

In the film's climax, Cecilia confronts Adrian at his family's estate, where she discovers the full extent of his plan. Adrian has created a network of invisible drones who are programmed to do his bidding, and he plans to use them to take over the world.

Cecilia manages to outsmart Adrian and destroy his technology, but not before he reveals that he has been manipulating her entire life, including her relationships and her career. The film ends with Cecilia, finally free from Adrian's control, setting out on a new journey of self-discovery and empowerment.

Throughout the film, Whannell explores themes of trauma, abuse, and the dangers of unchecked power. The Invisible Man is a thought-provoking and deeply unsettling film that challenges viewers to confront their own fears and vulnerabilities.

title: Down
tagline: This Valentine's Day, fall head over heels
overview: A pair of coworkers gets trapped in an elevator over a long weekend, but what at first promises to be a romantic connection turns nefarious as each party begins to reveal who they truly are.
plot:
"Down" is an episode of the American horror anthology web series Into the Dark, the fifth installment of its first season. Directed by Daniel Stamm from a script by Kent Kubena, it premiered on Hulu on February 1, 2019, and stars Natalie Martinez as Jennifer and Matt Lauria as Guy, with Arnie Pantoja, Diane Sellers and Christina Leone. Set over a Valentine's Day holiday weekend, it is a claustrophobic thriller about two strangers trapped in an elevator.

On the evening before Valentine's Day, Jennifer and Guy, who have both worked late in a high-rise office building, step into the same elevator on different floors. The car suddenly stops, apparently because of a storm, and with no phone signal they fear being stuck until Tuesday, since Monday is Presidents' Day. At first they get along well, sharing water, wine and chocolates and sketching each other. They agree to tell their raciest stories, and Jennifer records Guy on her phone as he invents one, until his mood darkens and he stops. They have sex, after which Guy says he could fall in love with her, but Jennifer tells him it was casual and that she still has feelings for an ex.

Stung, Guy confesses that he is not an accountant but one of the building's security guards, that he has been stalking her and that he stopped the elevator with his key. When Jennifer threatens him with prison, he halts it again; in the struggle the key breaks, truly trapping them. They climb through the ceiling, and Jennifer tries to escape up a ladder, but he chases her and both fall back into the car. Jennifer ties him up and, threatening him with a cigar cutter, records his confession: his name is John Deakins, a former white-collar worker whose "invented" story was real, except that his companion died when he crashed his car; after six months in jail he could not rebuild his career and staged the elevator incident to relive his old life. Early on Monday, a guard named Eddie tries to free them, but John, having freed himself and knocked Jennifer out, kills him with the elevator, murders Eddie's girlfriend, wipes the security files and drives off with Jennifer in his trunk. When he opens it, she attacks him, rams him into a dumpster with his car and sets it ablaze with a lit cigar, killing him.

The episode received a 73% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus praised its mix of suspense, violence and romance, though Brian Tallerico of RogerEbert.com called it the series' worst episode to date.

title: Digimon Adventure: Last Evolution Kizuna
original_title: デジモンアドベンチャー LAST EVOLUTION 絆
overview: Tai is now a university student, living alone, working hard at school, and working every day, but with his future still undecided. Meanwhile, Matt and others continue to work on Digimon incidents and activities that help people with their partner Digimon. When an unprecedented phenomenon occurs, the DigiDestined discover that when they grow up, their relationship with their partner Digimon will come closer to an end.  As a countdown timer activates on the Digivice, they realize that the more they fight with their partner Digimon, the faster their bond breaks. Will they fight for others and lose their partner? The time to choose and decide is approaching fast. There is a short time before “chosen children” will become adults. This is the last adventure of Tai and Agumon.
plot:
Digimon Adventure: Last Evolution Kizuna is a Japanese animated film directed by Keisuke Furukura, produced by Toei Animation, and released in 2020. The movie serves as the final installment of the Digimon Adventure trilogy.

The story takes place one year after the events of Digimon Adventure Tri.: Reunion. The main characters, Taichi "Tai" Kamiya (also known as Tai Kamiya), Kari Kamiya, Sora Takenouchi, Mimi Tachikawa, Joe Kido, and Renamon, are now in their mid-teens. They have been reunited with their Digimon partners, Agumon, Gabumon, Biyomon, Tentomon, Palmon, Gomamon, Patamon, and Renamon.

The movie begins with the group preparing for a school festival, but they soon discover that an evil organization known as the "Digital World's" rival, the "Dark Area," has appeared. The Dark Area is led by a powerful Digimon named Zemi, who seeks to destroy the Digital World and invade the human world.

As the story unfolds, Tai and his friends learn that Zemi was once a Digimon partner of a human boy named Takato Matsuda, who had been separated from his partner, Agumon. The group soon realizes that Zemi's true intention is to take revenge on the Digital World for abandoning Takato.

The movie follows the classic Digimon Adventure formula, with Tai and his friends embarking on a perilous journey through the Digital World to stop Zemi and save their partners. Along the way, they encounter new allies, including a young girl named Yui Kanzaki, who becomes the partner of a powerful Digimon named Gatomon.

As the story progresses, Tai and his friends face numerous challenges and obstacles as they navigate the Dark Area. They also uncover the truth about Takato's past and the reason behind Zemi's desire for revenge.

In the climactic final battle, Tai and his friends confront Zemi and her minions in an epic showdown. With the help of their Digimon partners and new allies, they manage to defeat Zemi and save the Digital World from destruction.

The movie concludes with a heartwarming moment as Tai and his friends reflect on their adventures and the bonds they have formed with their Digimon partners. The film ends on a hopeful note, with the group looking forward to a bright future together.

Overall, Digimon Adventure: Last Evolution Kizuna is a thrilling and emotional conclusion to the Digimon Adventure trilogy. It features stunning animation, engaging characters, and an exciting storyline that will keep fans of the series on the edge of their seats until the very end.

title: Valhalla
overview: The Viking children Røskva and Tjalfe embark on an adventurous journey from Midgard to Valhalla with the gods Thor and Loki. Life in Valhalla, however, turns out to be threatened by the dreaded Fenrir wolf and the god's barbaric archenemies, the Jotnar. Side by side with the gods the two children must fight to save Valhalla from the end of the world - Ragnarok.
plot:
Valhalla, released in some English-speaking markets as Valhalla: The Legend of Thor, is a 2019 Danish dark fantasy adventure film directed by Fenar Ahmad. It is based on the Danish comic book series Valhalla by Peter Madsen, Hans Rancke-Madsen and Henning Kure, which had previously been adapted as a celebrated 1986 animated film. Roland Møller plays Thor and Dulfi Al-Jabouri plays Loki, with Cecilia Loffredo and Saxo Moltke-Leth as the human children Røskva and Tjalfe and Jacob Ulrik Lohmann as Týr.

Røskva and her brother Tjalfe live with their parents in a humble farmstead in Midgard. One stormy night, the gods Thor and Loki arrive and demand shelter. Thor slaughters one of the goats that pull his chariot to feed the family, warning that none of its bones must be broken so that the animal can be restored the next morning. Egged on by Loki, Tjalfe cracks a bone to eat the marrow, and when the goat rises lame, the furious Thor takes the boy as a servant to the realm of the gods. Røskva stows away in the cart, and both children end up serving in the great hall of the Aesir.

They arrive at a time of crisis. The monstrous wolf Fenrir has broken free of the chains guarded by the war god Týr, and according to prophecy his escape heralds Ragnarok, the end of the world, in which he will kill Odin. The gods are quarrelsome and divided, more concerned with keeping up appearances than with finding a solution, and they also face their ancient enemies, the giants known as the Jotnar. While the children befriend a mute and unruly young giant named Quark and set off on a dangerous journey to the stronghold of Útgarða-Loki, Røskva discovers that she possesses a special gift, a bond with wolves that allows her to approach Fenrir where the gods only seek to fight him, offering a way to restore balance between the gods and the forces of nature.

The film was shot on location in Norway, Sweden, Denmark and Iceland and was released in Denmark on 10 October 2019, exactly 33 years after the animated version. Danish reviews were mixed: B.T., Soundvenue and DR's Per Juul Carlsen each gave it four stars out of six, praising its visuals and its update of the material, while Politiken and Ekko gave it two, finding it thin and unable to match international fantasy productions. It sold around 44,000 tickets in its first weeks, far fewer than Ahmad's previous film Darkland, and was nominated for the Robert Award for Best Children's Film.

title: Time to Hunt
overview: Four young men want to leave their dystopian world behind and go to a distant paradise to execute a money robbery, a daring act that will have unexpected consequences.
plot:
Time to Hunt is a 2020 South Korean dystopian action thriller written and directed by Yoon Sung-hyun, starring Lee Je-hoon, Ahn Jae-hong, Choi Woo-shik, Park Jeong-min and Park Hae-soo. It premiered at the 70th Berlin International Film Festival in February 2020, the first South Korean film selected for the Berlinale Special section. Its planned theatrical release was postponed by the COVID-19 pandemic, and Netflix released it worldwide on April 23, 2020.

In a near-future South Korea wracked by economic collapse, where the won has become virtually worthless, Jun-seok is released from prison after serving time for a botched robbery. He proposes one last heist to his best friends Jang-ho and Ki-hoon so that they can escape their miserable lives: an illegal gambling den that keeps its money in US dollars. They recruit Sang-soo, a friend who works there, and obtain guns from Jun-seok's contact Bong-sik. Despite a chaotic execution, the robbery succeeds, and the gang escapes with a large haul of cash along with the den's surveillance hard drives. Sang-soo stays on at his job to avoid suspicion while the others lie low.

The hard drives, however, contain footage of the den owners' dealings with powerful criminals, and the owners hire Han, a former police officer turned contract killer, to retrieve them. Han murders Bong-sik after forcing him to reveal the trio's whereabouts, then kills Sang-soo and uses his phone to track them. Realising they are being hunted, the friends flee, but Han shoots Jang-ho as they leave and then toys with them, granting them a five-minute head start to prolong the chase. Han tracks them through the city's surveillance network to a hospital, from which they barely escape. Arrested by police, he is released on the orders of a police chief.

The trio hide out near a harbour, waiting to leave the country at dawn, but Ki-hoon goes back to check on his parents. Han finds the others, and in a desperate gunfight Jang-ho is killed. As Han closes in on Jun-seok, masked men led by Bong-sik's brother Bong-soo ambush him and riddle him with bullets, and he falls into the sea. Jun-seok escapes by boat to Taiwan, but learns that Han has survived and that Ki-hoon is apparently dead. Deciding that he will never be free by running, he trains, arms himself and returns home to confront Han.

Critics praised the film's technical prowess and tension, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 69% approval; The Hollywood Reporter called it a technical tour de force.

title: Pokemon the Movie: Mewtwo Strikes Back - Evolution
original_title: ミュウツーの逆襲 EVOLUTION
overview: After accepting an invitation from a mysterious trainer, Ash, Misty and Brock meet Mewtwo, an artificially created Pokémon who wants to do battle.
plot:
Pokémon: Mewtwo Strikes Back – Evolution is a 2019 Japanese computer-animated fantasy film directed by Kunihiko Yuyama and Motonori Sakakibara, the twenty-second film in the Pokémon anime series and a CGI remake of Pokémon: The First Movie (1998). It features Rica Matsumoto as the voice of Ash Ketchum. It was released in Japan on July 12, 2019, and worldwide on Netflix on February 27, 2020.

The scientist Dr. Fuji is hired by Giovanni, the leader of the criminal organization Team Rocket, to create a powerful living weapon by cloning the legendary Pokémon Mew from one of its eyelashes. The result is Mewtwo, a genetically engineered Pokémon with immense psychic powers. When Mewtwo awakens and learns that he was made merely as an experiment, he destroys the laboratory, killing the scientists. Giovanni persuades him to work for Team Rocket, but when Mewtwo realizes that he is being used as a tool, he escapes to New Island and plots revenge against humans and their Pokémon.

Mewtwo sends holographic invitations to skilled Pokémon trainers to challenge the world's greatest Pokémon master on New Island. Ash, Misty and Brock accept, but Mewtwo whips up a storm that cancels the ferries. The trainers who reach the island by riding their Pokémon across the sea, including Ash's group, are greeted by Nurse Joy, who has been under Mewtwo's control. Mewtwo reveals his plan: using his own superior clones, he defeats the trainers' Pokémon and captures them to create an army of clones. Team Rocket sneaks onto the island, unknowingly followed by Mew.

Ash pursues his captured Pikachu into the cloning laboratory and destroys the machine, freeing the Pokémon. Mew appears, and Mewtwo challenges it to prove that clones are superior to originals, setting off a brutal battle between the original Pokémon and their copies. Horrified by the senseless suffering, Ash throws himself between the psychic attacks of Mew and Mewtwo and is turned to stone. The tears of the grieving Pokémon bring him back to life. Moved by Ash's sacrifice, Mewtwo realizes that a living being's worth depends not on its origins but on its choices. He leaves with Mew and the clones, turning back time and erasing everyone's memories of the events.

The film received mixed reviews, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 44% approval from nine critics; critics such as the Los Angeles Times's Charles Solomon criticized its CGI character designs. It was the most-watched anime title on Netflix in 2020.

title: Zombie for Sale
tagline: What do you know about a zombie?
overview: When a pharmaceutical company's illegal experiments inadvertently create a zombie, the strange Park family finds it and tries to profit from it.
plot:
The Odd Family: Zombie on Sale (Korean: Gimyohan gajok), also released in English as Zombie for Sale, is a 2019 South Korean zombie comedy directed by Lee Min-jae in his feature debut. Jung Jae-young, Kim Nam-gil, Uhm Ji-won, Lee Soo-kyung, Jung Ga-ram and Park In-hwan star as members of an eccentric rural family whose lives are upended by a most unusual visitor.

The film opens as a young zombie escapes through a sewer and wanders into a sleepy village. After being chased by a dog, he bites an elderly local before suffering a string of indignities, including being hit by a car, and he is finally captured by the Park family, who run a struggling gas station. At first the family pities their strange, gentle captive, not realizing what he is. The younger son, Min-geol, researches the creature's behavior online and concludes that he is a zombie, insisting that both the zombie and their father Man-deok, who was bitten, must be killed. The family is torn over whether they could kill their own father.

To everyone's surprise, Man-deok, locked in a camper van, does not turn into a monster. Instead, after a night of sweating and writhing, he wakes up visibly stronger and younger. When news of his rejuvenation spreads among the village elders, the family sees a business opportunity and begins charging the old people of the village to be bitten by the zombie. The venture is wildly profitable, though Man-deok soon absconds with the earnings for a trip to Hawaii, leaving Min-geol in charge. The family gives the zombie the affectionate nickname "Jjongbi" and tames him by feeding him cabbage, which he eats in place of brains, and the youngest daughter, Hae-geol, played by Lee Soo-kyung, grows especially fond of him. As word spreads, even younger villagers line up to be bitten. But when the incubation period ends, the rejuvenated villagers begin turning into real zombies, and the village descends into chaos as the oddball family must defend their home and their unusual friend.

Principal photography took place from October 2017 to January 2018. The film was well received, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting an 89% approval rating from 28 critics and a consensus calling it an auspicious debut that puts a light yet surprisingly poignant spin on a familiar genre formula.

title: Rascal Does Not Dream of a Dreaming Girl

overview: In Fujisawa, Sakuta Azusagawa is in his second year of high school. Blissful days with his girlfriend and upperclassman, Mai Sakurajima, are interrupted by the appearance of his first crush, Shoko Makinohara.
plot:
Rascal Does Not Dream of a Dreaming Girl (Seishun Buta Yarō wa Yumemiru Shōjo no Yume o Minai) is a 2019 Japanese animated supernatural romantic drama produced by CloverWorks and distributed by Aniplex. Adapting the sixth and seventh volumes of Hajime Kamoshida's light novel series, illustrated by Kēji Mizoguchi, it continues the 2018 television anime Rascal Does Not Dream of Bunny Girl Senpai. Director Sōichi Masui, writer Masahiro Yokotani, character designer Satomi Tamura and composers Fox Capture Plan returned, as did the entire voice cast, led by Kaito Ishikawa, Asami Seto, Inori Minase, Yurika Kubo, Nao Toyama and Atsumi Tanezaki.

In Fujisawa, high school junior Sakuta Azusagawa is enjoying his relationship with his girlfriend, the actress and upperclassman Mai Sakurajima, when his first love, Shoko Makinohara, reappears. Sakuta realizes there are two Shokos: a middle schooler who is gravely ill and needs a heart transplant, and a grown woman who once helped him. He gradually connects the mysterious scars on his chest to the adult Shoko and learns the truth: she has come back from a future in which she survived thanks to his heart, donated after he was left brain dead by a car accident on Christmas Eve. Having fallen for him, she returned to change that fate.

Sakuta resolves to accept his death so Shoko can live, but at the decisive moment Mai pushes him out of the way and is killed instead, becoming the donor herself. Devastated, Sakuta is offered one last chance by the adult Shoko, who helps him travel back in time even though doing so will erase her. Invisible to almost everyone, he finds his classmate Tomoe Koga, who can still see him, warns his past self and saves both Mai and himself, leaving young Shoko without a donor. Unwilling to accept her death, Sakuta and Mai vow to find a way, until Shoko chooses to rewrite her own past so that she never meets them. In the new present, the couple meets a healthy Shoko on a beach, and fragments of memory let them recognize one another.

The film opened in Japan on 15 June 2019, selling over 250,000 tickets and earning about ¥377 million in its first 24 days. Aniplex of America premiered it at Anime Expo before a limited North American release that October. Anime News Network called it a tearjerker that brings the story's characters and themes full circle. A sequel film followed in 2023.

title: Seized
tagline: They kidnapped his son. Big mistake.
overview: Hiding out with his son Taylor on the Mexican coast, Nero hopes to put his violent Special Forces career behind him. But after Nero’s home is attacked and Taylor is abducted, the mysterious Mzamo orders Nero to slaughter the members of three rival crime syndicates. If he fails, Taylor will die. plot:
Seized is a 2020 American action thriller film directed by Isaac Florentine. Scott Adkins stars as a former special agent forced to wipe out a series of crime syndicates to save his kidnapped son, with Mario Van Peebles as the man pulling the strings. It was released on October 13, 2020.

Nero, a former special forces operative, lives a quiet life with his son, Taylor, in Rosarito Beach on the Baja California coast, following the death of his wife. One day he is knocked unconscious by a tranquilizer dart and wakes to find that Taylor has been abducted. A mysterious caller sends him a live video feed of the boy locked inside a truck rigged to fill with exhaust fumes, and gives him an ultimatum: to see his son again, Nero must eliminate the members of three dangerous criminal organizations. He is provided with weapons, a bulletproof SUV and a vest fitted with a body camera, through which his every move is watched.

The caller, a crime lord named Mzamo, monitors Nero's progress with his lover, Alanza, his associates and a group of corrupt intelligence agents led by Donovan. Nero storms a restaurant and kills a cartel boss and all of his men, then fights his way through a brothel run by a notorious criminal and kills him. When allowed to speak with Taylor, Nero tells his son the truth about his past: he once worked for an intelligence agency under a cover name, and his wife was kidnapped and killed after someone betrayed him. After he avenged her death, the agency relocated him and Taylor to Mexico. It emerges that Donovan was the traitor and has manipulated events so that Nero's combat skills will eliminate Mzamo's rivals.

Nero's third target, the arms dealer Omar Chavez, is ready for him and destroys his body camera, leading Mzamo and Donovan to believe Nero is dead. Chavez, learning why Nero is fighting, reveals Taylor's location, but is killed when Mzamo's men attack. Donovan wants to kill Taylor, but Mzamo, realizing the agents' treachery, has already moved the boy to safety. Nero arrives at Mzamo's estate and kills Donovan and his agents, then lets Mzamo go with a warning to stay away before riding off with his son.

Seized received mixed reviews. Rotten Tomatoes reported 40% approval from five critics, though Screen Anarchy praised Florentine's fluid camerawork and Adkins's fight choreography for creating a highly entertaining, video game-like action film.

title: An Egg Rescue
overview: Toto and his friends must rescue his egg children after they're taken away for a gourmet food event in Africa.
plot:
Little Eggs: An African Rescue, released in Mexico, Latin America and the United States as Un rescate de huevitos, is a 2021 Mexican computer-animated adventure comedy produced by Huevocartoon Producciones and directed by brothers Gabriel and Rodolfo Riva Palacio Alatriste. The fourth film in the Huevos franchise and a sequel to Un gallo con muchos huevos (2015), it brings back the Spanish voice cast alongside newcomers including Jesús Ochoa and the comedy duo Freddy and Germán Ortega. Rodolfo drew the story of an overprotective father from raising his daughter, Dione, who voices one of the chicks, and the plot from articles about rare eggs and endangered animals sold as luxury food. About 350 people worked on it, many remotely during the COVID-19 pandemic. Delayed from 2019 and 2020, it opened in Mexico on 12 August 2021, with a limited US release through Pantelion Films on 27 August.

At the Granjas el Pollón farm, the rooster Toto and his wife, Di, welcome two golden eggs, the twins Max and Uly. Their unusual color wins a ranch contest and attracts La Duquesa, a Russian egg collector, whose offer to buy them is refused. Toto, newly anxious and overprotective, tears up the twins' prize ribbons in a fit of worry and frightens them. That night Duquesa's henchmen, Panzovich and Gordimitri, send moles in mind-control helmets to steal the twins. Toto's friends Bibi and Willy free one mole, Toporocho, who helps the group board the cargo plane bound for Congo, but Toto and Di are thrown off mid-flight and saved by parachute.

The twins are taken to the African mansion of Barón Roncovich, where a Master Chef orders the captured eggs, from a peacock, an eagle, a parrot and other rare species, chilled for a gourmet auction. Max and Uly lead the others in a breakout, while Toto and Di, caught up in an animal talent show run by the lion king Leonidas I, find the courage to stand up to him and recruit an army of animals. They storm the dinner, rescue the eggs and escape a fire, and Toto apologizes to his children. When Duquesa ambushes them on the flight home, Toto trusts the twins to fight back, and a newly hatched eagle sends her out of the plane.

Bruno Bichir voices Toto and Maite Perroni voices Di. Reviews were mixed to favorable; Common Sense Media called it well made, while The Guardian gave it one star. It earned about MX$50 million in Mexico, making Huevos the country's most-watched domestic film franchise.

title: Halo Legends
tagline: Seven stories from the heart of the Halo universe.
overview: The universe of the Halo video game series is expanded in seven short animated films from Japan's greatest anime directors and studios.
plot:
Halo Legends is a 2010 adult animated military science fiction anthology film set in the universe of the Halo video game franchise and produced by 343 Industries, the Microsoft division created to oversee the Halo brand. It compiles seven animated short films, ranging from about ten to twenty minutes each, that detail the backstory of the Halo universe and offer side stories expanding it. The shorts were made by six Japanese anime houses, Bee Train, Bones, Casio Entertainment, Production I.G, Studio 4°C and Toei Animation, with directors including Mamoru Oshii, Hideki Futamura and Hiroshi Yamazaki, while Shinji Aramaki, the creator of Appleseed, served as creative adviser. The idea had its origins in the 2006 Marvel tie-in The Halo Graphic Novel; 343's creative director Frank O'Connor supplied story outlines or finished scripts, felt that the Japanese style of narrative suited the stories, and gave the studios access to Halo's story bible and art assets along with wide latitude in visual style.

The two-part Origins, set after the events of Halo 3, has the artificial intelligence Cortana recount the history of the universe to the Master Chief in cryogenic sleep, from the Forerunners' struggle against the Flood to humanity's war with the alien Covenant, while reflecting on whether war will ever end. The Duel, rendered with a filter that makes each frame resemble a watercolour painting, tells the tragic story of an Arbiter on the Elite home world who defies the Prophets. Homecoming centres on the final mission of a Spartan, Odd One Out follows the clumsy Spartan 1337, Prototype tells the story of an elite soldier called Ghost, The Babysitter depicts an infiltration mission by a squad of ODST troopers and a Spartan, and The Package follows five Spartans who must recover a "package" from a Covenant fleet.

Warner Bros. released Halo Legends on DVD and Blu-ray on 16 February 2010, a week later than planned, after a United States premiere at the AMC Metreon in San Francisco. Reception was mostly positive. IGN UK's Orlando Parfit called it a successful if uneven attempt to fuse Halo with anime, essential viewing for dedicated fans, and IGN US found the shorts surprisingly accessible to science fiction fans in general, while Game Informer felt it would appeal to fans interested in the story rather than multiplayer. It ranked second in US Blu-ray sales in its first week, and its DVD sales eventually grossed about 11 million dollars in the United States.

title: The Car: Road to Revenge
overview: In a dilapidated cyberpunk city plagued by crime and corruption, an unscrupulous District Attorney is savagely murdered and tossed out of a building onto his brand new car. Mysteriously, the District Attorney and his car come back to life as a single being with a thirst for vengeance. The eerie driver-less car embarks on a vicious rampage exacting revenge on the criminals who murdered him. The Car: Road to Revenge is the stylized sequel to the unconventional horror cult classic The Car (1977), and features an homage to the original with the return of Ronny Cox as the Mechanic.
plot:
The Car: Road to Revenge is a 2019 American science fiction action horror film directed by G.J. Echternkamp, who wrote the screenplay with Michael Tabb and Matt Yamashita. A belated sequel to the 1977 cult film The Car, it was produced by Jeffrey Beach and Phillip Roth through Roth's UFO International and released direct to video by Universal 1440 Entertainment on 8 January 2019. It stars Grant Bowler as Detective Rainer, Kathleen Munroe as Daria Morris and Jamie Bamber as District Attorney James Caddock, with Martin Hancock as Talen, Micah Balfour, Burt Grinstead, Nina Bergman and Ronny Cox, the only returning actor from the original, as the mechanic Waits. It was shot on location in Bulgaria, with music by Frederik Wiedmann, and runs 89 minutes.

In a dilapidated near-future city plagued by crime and corruption, Caddock is a fiercely ambitious and unscrupulous district attorney whose convicts are executed on the spot in the courtroom. After a bust, he takes possession of a chip containing technology belonging to The Night, a criminal gang led by Talen whose members are given cyborg enhancements. Caddock has just bought a new black luxury sedan, the Lazarus 1, and leaves the chip inside it after taking Daria, the object of his attentions, out to dinner. Members of The Night storm his office looking for the chip and throw him out of the window onto his own car. Rainer, a gruff cop who breaks the rules, investigates the killing. Soon afterwards the driverless car mysteriously comes to life, as if the dead man and his vehicle had become a single vengeful being, breaks out of impound and begins hunting down and killing the gang members responsible for the murder. Rainer, who has taken it on himself to protect Daria from the gang, joins forces with her to solve the mystery of the car, and in an homage to the original, Waits later refits the vehicle with the body of the 1977 car.

The film was poorly received. Kurt Dahlke of DVD Talk found Bowler and Munroe to have a fair amount of chemistry and praised one stunt sequence, but called the film daft, cliched and irritating, recommending it only as brain-dead entertainment if found cheaply. Moria gave it one star, criticizing Echternkamp for an action film in which the car does little but run people over, a sketchily developed future and contradictory explanations for the car, and named it the worst film of 2019.
