title: Walk. Ride. Rodeo.
tagline: Based on the inspirational true story.
overview: Tells the incredible true story of Amberley Snyder, a nationally ranked rodeo barrel racer who defies the odds after barely surviving a car accident that leaves her paralyzed from the waist down.
plot:
Walk. Ride. Rodeo. is a 2019 American biographical drama directed by Conor Allyn from a screenplay by Sean Dwyer and Greg Cope White. It tells the true story of Amberley Snyder, a nationally ranked rodeo barrel racer who returned to competition after a car accident left her paralysed from the waist down. Spencer Locke plays Amberley, with Missi Pyle as her mother Tina, and Bailey Chase, Sherri Shepherd, Alyvia Alyn Lind and Kathleen Rose Perkins in supporting roles. The film was released on Netflix in March 2019.

At nineteen, Amberley lives on her family's ranch in Utah and spends nearly all of her time training with her horse, Power, with her sights set on championship titles. While driving to Denver for an event, she loses control of her truck and is thrown from the vehicle into a fence post. She survives, but doctors tell her she will never walk again and will spend the rest of her life in a wheelchair.

During a six-week rehabilitation programme, Amberley swings between despair and stubborn determination. She lashes out at her mother, grieving the life she believes she has lost, but slowly builds the strength in her upper body that she will need to regain her independence. Back home, she begins corresponding with Tate Watkins, a young man connected to the Future Farmers of America organisation, and their video calls develop into a close friendship. She learns to drive again, enrols in college and, crucially, discovers that she can still ride if she straps herself into the saddle with a seat belt. With the support of her family, friends and trainers, she works her way back toward the arena, facing the physical danger of competing without the use of her legs as well as scepticism from people who doubt she can ever race again.

The film emphasises perseverance, faith and the bond between rider and horse, and it presents Amberley's recovery as a family effort as much as an individual triumph. Its portrait of Amberley is based on her real-life recovery and her return to competitive barrel racing after the accident.

As a family-friendly inspirational drama, Walk. Ride. Rodeo. found an audience on streaming, where viewers responded warmly to its uplifting true story, though critics found the storytelling conventional and predictable.

title: The Misfits
tagline: They're not bad guys. They just steal from them.
overview: After being recruited by a group of unconventional thieves, renowned criminal Richard Pace finds himself caught up in an elaborate gold heist that promises to have far-reaching implications on his life and the lives of countless others.
plot:
The Misfits is a 2021 American heist action film directed by Renny Harlin and written by Robert Henny and Kurt Wimmer. It stars Pierce Brosnan as the master thief Richard Pace, Tim Roth as Werner Schultz, Nick Cannon as Ringo, Hermione Corfield as Pace's daughter Hope, Jamie Chung as Violet, Mike Angelo as Wick and Rami Jaber as the Prince, with Qais Qandil as Jason Quick. Much of the film is set in the Middle East, in a fictional country called Jazeristan.

Richard Pace is a legendary thief who has escaped from three private prisons owned by Werner Schultz. While planning to rob a wealthy figure known as the Prince, Pace walks into a trap and is given a choice: be handed to the FBI or join a team of skilled thieves called the Misfits. On a private jet he meets its members, Ringo, a locksmith and master of disguise, Wick, an explosives expert, and Violet, a deadly martial artist, who fly him to Abu Dhabi for a briefing.

The Misfits reveal that Schultz has laundered money for a terrorist Brotherhood, converting it into gold bars that he keeps in a vault beneath one of his prisons in Jazeristan. They plan to steal the gold before it can be used to fund terrorism, but they need Pace's expertise. He initially refuses, but his daughter Hope, who works with the group, persuades him to join, though he insists on keeping half the loot. As the team prepares to infiltrate the prison, using disguises, tainted food and a fake sanitation crew, the Brotherhood's leader announces that he will come to collect the gold in person on the very day of the heist, raising the stakes for everyone involved.

The film presents itself as a lighthearted caper in the tradition of ensemble heist movies, mixing action, comedy and twists.

The Misfits was released in South Korea on June 3, 2021, and in the United States on June 11 by The Avenue Entertainment. Critics panned it, giving it 17 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 25, and it received three nominations at the 42nd Golden Raspberry Awards.

title: Infinite
overview: Evan McCauley has skills he never learned and memories of places he has never visited. Self-medicated and on the brink of a mental breakdown, a secret group that call themselves “Infinites” come to his rescue, revealing that his memories are real.
plot:
Infinite is a 2021 American science fiction action film directed by Antoine Fuqua from a screenplay by Ian Shorr, based on a story by Todd Stein adapted from D. Eric Maikranz's 2009 novel The Reincarnationist Papers. It stars Mark Wahlberg as Evan McCauley, Chiwetel Ejiofor as Bathurst, Sophie Cookson as Nora Brightman, Dylan O'Brien as Heinrich Treadway, Jason Mantzoukas as the Artisan, with Rupert Friend and Toby Jones.

In Mexico City in 1985, Heinrich Treadway flees the authorities and a man named Bathurst after stealing "the Egg" from him, telling his ally Abel to "look inside" if he does not survive. He leaps from a car flying off a bridge onto a crane, but watches as Bathurst kills Abel and their companion Leona. In New York in 2020, Evan McCauley, diagnosed with schizophrenia and unable to find work because of his past, forges a katana for a gangster despite never having trained as a bladesmith. Arrested after the deal goes wrong, he is confronted by Bathurst, who claims that they have known each other for centuries and that Evan is Treadway. Nora, Leona's reincarnation, helps him escape and explains that about 500 people, the Infinites, remember all their past lives. They are split between the Believers, who want to improve the world, and the Nihilists, including Bathurst, who built the Egg, a weapon able to destroy all life on Earth, which Treadway hid before he died. Infinites usually recover their memories around puberty, which explains Evan's diagnosis, and Bathurst has trapped some 200 Believers, Abel among them, in computer chips with a weapon called the Dethroner. At the Believers' Hub, Evan struggles to regain his memories, and when the Nihilists raid it, he seeks out the Artisan, whose machine restores them through a near-death experience. He learns that Treadway hid the Egg inside his own body, but the Nihilists overhear and seize the body. Evan, Nora and the Artisan storm Bathurst's estate in Scotland; Nora sacrifices herself to free the trapped souls, and Evan, surviving the Dethroner thanks to a steel plate in his head, traps Bathurst and disarms the Egg, sinking into the ocean with it. Years later, the Artisan finds a reborn Evan in Jakarta and offers him Treadway's sword, awakening his memories.

Shot in locations including Cardiff, London, Mexico City, Nepal, New York and Scotland, the film was released on Paramount+ on 10 June 2021 after pandemic delays. It received negative reviews, earning 17% on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: Nomadland
overview: A woman in her sixties embarks on a journey through the western United States after losing everything in the Great Recession, living as a van-dwelling modern-day nomad.
plot:
Nomadland is a 2020 American drama film directed by Chloé Zhao, written by Zhao and Jeremy Keller, and starring Frances McDormand. The film is based on the non-fiction book "Nomadland: Surviving America in the Twenty-First Century" by Jessica Bruder.

The story follows Fern (Frances McDormand), a 61-year-old widow who has lost her home and her husband to cancer. After being evicted from their mobile home park, Fern is forced to leave behind everything she knows and embark on a journey across America in her van, which she names "Violet." She becomes a modern-day nomad, living off the grid and taking on various temporary jobs to make ends meet.

As Fern travels through the American West, she encounters a community of fellow nomads who have also been forced out of their homes by economic hardship. They share stories of struggle and resilience, and Fern begins to find a sense of belonging among them. She meets Swankie (David Strathairn), a veteran who has been living on the road for years; Linda May (Charlene Swankie), a fellow nomad who becomes one of Fern's closest friends; and Bob Wells (David Zayas), a young man who is struggling to find his place in the world.

Throughout her journey, Fern faces numerous challenges, including harsh weather conditions, mechanical breakdowns, and encounters with hostile strangers. However, she also experiences moments of beauty and connection, such as watching the sunset over the desert landscape or sharing meals with her fellow nomads.

As the story unfolds, Fern begins to realize that she has a choice: she can continue to live on the fringes of society, always looking over her shoulder, or she can take control of her life and create a new sense of purpose. With the help of her friends and the support of the nomad community, Fern starts to build a new identity for herself, one that is rooted in freedom and self-sufficiency.

The film's title, Nomadland, refers to the fictional town of Nomadland, Nevada, which has been abandoned due to economic decline. However, as Fern travels through the American West, she discovers that there are many other places like Nomadland, where people have been forced out of their homes and are struggling to survive.

Ultimately, Nomadland is a film about resilience, community, and the human spirit's ability to thrive in the face of adversity. Through Fern's journey, we see that even in the darkest of times, there is always hope for a better future, and that with courage and determination, we can create a new life for ourselves.

The film received widespread critical acclaim, including several Academy Awards, including Best Picture, Best Director, and Best Actress for Frances McDormand. It was also nominated for several other awards, including Best Supporting Actor for David Strathairn and Best Original Score.

title: Da 5 Bloods
overview: Four African-American Vietnam veterans return to Vietnam. They are in search of the remains of their fallen squad leader and the promise of buried treasure. These heroes battle forces of humanity and nature while confronted by the lasting ravages of the immorality of the Vietnam War.
plot:
During the Vietnam War, a squad of black US Army soldiers of the 1st Infantry Division, Paul, Otis, Eddie, Melvin, and their squad leader Norman, who dub themselves the "Bloods," secure the site of a Central Intelligence Agency airplane crash and recover its cargo, a locker of gold bars intended as payment to the Lahu people for their help in fighting the Viet Cong. The Bloods decide to take the gold for themselves and bury it so they can retrieve it later. However, in the ensuing Vietnamese counter-attack, Norman is killed, and the Bloods cannot locate the buried gold after a napalm strike obliterates the identifying landmarks.
In the present day, Paul, Otis, Eddie, and Melvin meet up in Ho Chi Minh City. A recent landslide had uncovered the tail of the crashed plane, and with this new information, they plan to find the gold and Norman's body. Otis reunites with his old Vietnamese girlfriend Tiên, who reveals that he is the father of her grown child. Tiên introduces the Bloods to Desroche, a French businessman who agrees to help the Bloods smuggle the gold out of Vietnam once they retrieve it. Soon thereafter, they are joined by Paul's son David, who has a tempestuous relationship with his father.
Vinh, a tour guide hired by the Bloods, leads the group out into the countryside, where a confrontation with a local merchant forces Paul to admit that he has post-traumatic stress disorder. At a hotel bar, David meets Hedy, the founder of LAMB, an organization dedicated to clearing landmines. The next day, Vinh drops off the group and tells them he will pick them up in a few days. During their first night, Paul confiscates a pistol from Otis which had been secretly given to him by Tiên, and becomes suspicious of his motives. Eventually, the Bloods find the gold bars scattered across the side of a hill. They also find Norman's remains and pray over them. Eddie reveals that his excessive spending has rendered him broke but reminds the Bloods of Norman's original plan to give the gold to their black brethren in the United States.
On the hike out, Eddie steps on a landmine and is killed. David also steps on a mine but does not trigger it, just as Hedy and two other volunteers from LAMB, Simon and Seppo, show up. Paul and the others manage to pull David off the mine safely. Paul then holds the three outsiders hostage with Otis's gun, paranoid that they will report them to the authorities. During the night Seppo escapes while David and the others forcibly disarm Paul.
When the Bloods regroup with Vinh, a group of gunmen shows up demanding the gold in exchange for Seppo, whom they have captured. In the ensuing shootout, David is shot in the leg, and Seppo is killed by a landmine. All of the gunmen are killed except for one, who flees. Assuming that Desroche has crossed them, Vinh suggests retreating to a nearby abandoned temple to defend themselves from reinforcements.

title: Promising Young Woman
overview: A young woman, traumatized by a tragic event in her past, seeks out vengeance against those who crossed her path.
plot:
Promising Young Woman is a 2020 American black comedy thriller film written and directed by Emerald Fennell. The movie stars Carey Mulligan, Bo Burnham, Alison Brie, and Chris Evans.

The story follows Cassie Thomas (Carey Mulligan), a successful medical school dropout who has been living with a traumatic event from her past. After witnessing the rape of her best friend Emily (Alyah Chanelle Scott) by their college acquaintance, Ryan (Molly Burnett), Cassie's life took a drastic turn. She became withdrawn and isolated, unable to shake off the guilt and anger that consumed her.

The movie begins with Cassie attending a medical school reunion, where she is forced to confront her past and the choices she made after dropping out of medical school. She meets Dean (Max Greenfield), a charming but shallow man who is now working as a doctor at the same hospital where Emily was raped. The encounter sparks a sense of unease in Cassie, and she begins to formulate a plan for revenge.

Cassie's plan involves pretending to be a vulnerable and intoxicated woman, allowing men to take advantage of her before she "wakes up" and exacts her revenge on them. She starts by targeting the same men who were present at Emily's party that night, including Ryan, Dean, and several others. As Cassie navigates this new persona, she begins to confront the societal norms and expectations that led to Emily's rape.

Throughout the movie, Fennell expertly weaves together themes of trauma, consent, and female empowerment. Cassie's character is a complex and multifaceted one, driven by a desire for justice and revenge. However, as the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Cassie's motivations are not solely driven by anger, but also by a deep-seated need to reclaim her own agency and autonomy.

As Cassie's plan gains momentum, she begins to attract attention from Dean, who is initially oblivious to her true intentions. The two engage in a cat-and-mouse game, with Cassie using her newfound persona to manipulate Dean into becoming more invested in their relationship.

The movie builds towards a thrilling climax, as Cassie's plan reaches its fruition. In the end, Cassie exacts her revenge on the men who wronged Emily and herself, but not before confronting the darker aspects of her own psyche. The film ends with Cassie walking away from the wreckage, symbolizing her newfound freedom and empowerment.

Overall, Promising Young Woman is a thought-provoking and timely commentary on the societal norms that perpetuate rape culture. Fennell's direction is masterful, and Mulligan delivers a standout performance as the complex and multifaceted Cassie Thomas.

title: The Room
overview: Kate and Matt discover that a part of their house can grant wishes. In the wake of two miscarriages, what they want most is a child.
plot:
The Room is a 2019 English-language science-fiction thriller co-written and directed by Christian Volckman, about a young couple who find a way to satisfy every material desire and then go much too far. Olga Kurylenko and Kevin Janssens play the couple, with Joshua Wilson, John Flanders and Francis Chapman in supporting roles. It premiered on April 15, 2019, at the Brussels International Fantastic Film Festival.

Matt and Kate buy an old house in upstate New York. While renovating, they find a large hidden room, notice that the electricity surges and makes the lights flicker, and learn that a murder took place on the property decades earlier, committed by a man known only as John Doe who is still alive in a psychiatric hospital. Matt then discovers by accident that the room grants wishes. The couple quit their jobs and conjure up anything they want, but the riches soon feel worthless and Kate sinks into depression.

When Matt suggests trying for a baby, Kate, still scarred by two miscarriages, angrily refuses, then secretly uses the room to create a son, Shane. Neither can bring themselves to undo the wish. Visiting the hospital, Matt is warned by John Doe to leave the house and forget the room, and he learns that anything the room creates ages and crumbles to dust once it leaves the house. When Kate takes the baby outside, he instantly grows into a small child, and Matt rushes him back in.

Their marriage frays as Kate devotes herself to raising Shane while Matt ignores him. Kate keeps the boy indoors by telling him the outside world is full of germs, but he discovers the room and starts creating his own world. John Doe reveals that he too was a child wished into being, and that he was able to live outside only after his parents died; if Kate dies, Shane could do the same. Kate overhears and considers killing herself but cannot go through with it.

After Shane ages himself into a teenager with a child's mind, he turns on his parents, knocks them out, builds a copy of the house inside the room and, disguised as Matt, abducts Kate. Matt rescues her, and the two escape a labyrinth Shane has created by leaving duplicates of themselves as decoys, then lure him outside, where he ages and turns to dust. A month later, living in a motel, Kate finds she is pregnant as the lights flicker ominously.

The film screened at festivals including Sitges and Bucheon and received mixed to positive reviews, with 71% approval on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: The Kissing Booth 2
tagline: Rules can be broken...but so can hearts.
overview: With college decisions looming, Elle juggles her long-distance romance with Noah, changing relationship with bestie Lee and feelings for a new classmate.
plot:
The Kissing Booth 2 is a 2020 American teen romantic comedy directed by Vince Marcello, who co-wrote the screenplay with Jay Arnold. A direct sequel to The Kissing Booth (2018) and the second film in a trilogy based on Beth Reekles's novels, it stars Joey King, Joel Courtney and Jacob Elordi, with Molly Ringwald and newcomer Taylor Zakhar Perez in supporting roles. Netflix released it on July 24, 2020.

Elle Evans begins her senior year of high school amid gossip that she and her boyfriend Noah, now a freshman at Harvard, are about to split up. Her insecurity deepens when she sees Noah becoming friendly on social media with Chloe, a glamorous British classmate. Meanwhile, Elle and her best friend Lee plan to revive their kissing booth for the school's charity carnival, and Elle persuades Marco Peña, a charming new transfer student, to take part after beating him at a dance video game. Noah encourages Elle to apply to Harvard, which conflicts with her lifelong plan to attend Berkeley with Lee, where their mothers first met, so she applies in secret. Worried about tuition, she also enters a dance competition with Lee to win a large cash prize.

A visit to Noah in Boston leaves Elle more anxious after she meets Chloe and finds an earring under his bed. When Lee fakes an injury, Marco becomes Elle's dance partner, and the two grow increasingly attracted to each other. title: Our Friend
overview: After learning that his terminally ill wife has six months to live, a man welcomes the support of his best friend who moves into their home to help out.
plot:
Our Friend is a 2019 American biographical drama directed by Gabriela Cowperthwaite and written by Brad Ingelsby, based on Matthew Teague's 2015 Esquire article "The Friend: Love Is Not a Big Enough Word." Jason Segel, Dakota Johnson and Casey Affleck star, with Gwendoline Christie and Cherry Jones in supporting roles. The film premiered as The Friend at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 6, 2019, and was released in the United States by Gravitas Ventures on January 22, 2021.

The film moves back and forth across thirteen years. In 2013, journalist Matt Teague and his wife Nicole prepare to tell their two young daughters that Nicole's ovarian cancer is terminal, while their best friend Dane Faucheux keeps the girls company outside. Flashbacks trace the friendship from its beginnings in New Orleans in 2000, when Nicole, a theater performer, introduces Matt to her college friend Dane, a camera operator with dreams of stand-up comedy. Over the years Matt's work as a war correspondent keeps him abroad for months, straining the marriage after the family settles in Fairhope, Alabama, while Dane drifts through dead-end jobs and, at one low point, contemplates ending his life while hiking at the Grand Canyon. The Teagues also weather Nicole's affair, with Dane helping them reconcile.

When Nicole is diagnosed in 2012 and begins chemotherapy, Dane offers to stay for a few weeks. As her condition worsens, he remains for months, taking on household duties and caring for the children, at the cost of his relationship with his girlfriend. Nicole draws up a bucket list that Matt and Dane help her complete, including serving as a grand marshal at Mardi Gras and writing letters for her daughters' future milestones. By 2014 her pain and confusion grow, and a hospice nurse is called in. After a final sunrise on the beach, Nicole dies with Matt and Dane at her side. Matt later writes the article that inspired the film as a tribute to his friend.

Released in early 2021, more than a year after its festival premiere, the film grossed under $800,000 against a $10 million budget. Critics praised the performances, particularly those of Affleck and Segel; Vanity Fair called it an effective, small-scale tearjerker, while Variety argued that it had sanitized the unpleasant realities of dying that Teague's essay had confronted.

plot:
Hotel Transylvania: Transformania is a 2022 American animated comedy horror film directed by Genndy Tartakovsky, produced by Sony Pictures Animation. The movie serves as a sequel to the previous films in the Hotel Transylvania series.

The story takes place after the events of Hotel Transylvania III: Summer Vacation (2018). Mavis (voiced by Selena Gomez) and Jonathan (voiced by Andy Samberg) are now married, and they're expecting their first child. However, things take a turn when Dracula's (voiced by Adam Sandler) 35th wedding anniversary is approaching, and he wants to celebrate it with his family.

Dracula discovers that the only way to make his wife, Ericka (voiced by Kathryn Hahn), happy on their anniversary is for him to transform into a human. However, this transformation comes with an unexpected side effect: Mavis starts to lose her vampiric powers and becomes human-like. The situation escalates when Dracula's attempt to reverse the spell goes awry, causing all of the monsters in the hotel to start transforming into humans.

As the chaos unfolds, Jonathan tries to help his wife, who is struggling with her newfound humanity, while also dealing with the consequences of the transformations on their friends and family. The movie features a star-studded voice cast, including Kevin James, Steve Buscemi, David Spade, and Selena Gomez's sister, Gracie Gomez.

Throughout the film, Tartakovsky explores themes of identity, love, and acceptance as Mavis navigates her new human-like state. The movie also pokes fun at modern society, tackling topics like social media, technology, and the challenges of being a monster in a human world.

Overall, Hotel Transylvania: Transformania is a heartwarming and hilarious addition to the Hotel Transylvania franchise, offering plenty of laughs, exciting action sequences, and a touching story about family and acceptance.

plot:
Escape Room: Tournament of Champions is a 2021 American mystery thriller film directed by Spes McLean and written by Will Pitman. The movie serves as a sequel to the 2019 film Escape Room.

The story begins with six winners from the first game, who were all trapped in the same room together, escaping through teamwork and wit. They are: Zoe (Taylor Russell), Ben (Logan Miller), Emily (Mia Kim), Nicky (Lolita Davidovich), Charlie (Jay Ellis), and Kieran (Chris J. Johnson).

The movie takes place a year after the events of the first film. The six winners have been invited to participate in an exclusive tournament, where they will compete against each other in a series of escape rooms designed by the enigmatic and sinister game designer, Minos (Ben Feldman). The winner of the tournament will receive a grand prize of $1 million.

As the competition progresses, the contestants are forced to navigate through increasingly complex and deadly challenges. They soon realize that they are not just competing against each other, but also against time, as the rooms are designed to be self-destructive if they fail to escape within a certain timeframe.

Throughout the tournament, alliances are formed and broken, and the contestants begin to uncover clues about Minos's true intentions. As the stakes rise, the group discovers that Minos has a personal vendetta against them, and that he will stop at nothing to claim victory.

As the final challenge approaches, the contestants must work together to escape the last room and defeat Minos. In a thrilling finale, they successfully outsmart Minos and escape the tournament, but not without some unexpected twists and turns.

One of the standout aspects of Escape Room: Tournament of Champions is its exploration of themes such as teamwork, trust, and the consequences of playing with fire. The movie raises questions about the ethics of game design and the motivations behind creating such deadly challenges for human participants.

Overall, Escape Room: Tournament of Champions is a tense and thrilling ride that will keep viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end. With its clever plot twists and impressive escape room sequences, it's a must-see for fans of the genre.

title: I Still Believe
tagline: One love can change your life.
overview: The true-life story of Christian music star Jeremy Camp and his journey of love and loss that looks to prove there is always hope.
plot:
In Lafayette, Indiana, in September 1999, Jeremy Camp departs for Calvary Chapel College in Murrieta, California. The night of his arrival, he goes to a concert of Canadian Christian band, the Kry, where he meets the lead singer, Jean-Luc LaJoie, who becomes fast friends with Jeremy, who turns to him for musical advice.
After the concert, Jeremy meets Melissa Henning, a fellow student at his school, and friend of Jean-Luc, who loves Melissa, but she does not feel the same. Jeremy and Melissa get to know each other, and quickly begin dating, causing a rift among the three. As a result, Melissa ends her relationship with Jeremy.
Jeremy goes back to his family's home in Indiana for Christmas break. A few days after Christmas, he receives a phone call from Jean-Luc, saying that Melissa is sick, and asks Jeremy to come back to California.
Upon his arrival, Jeremy visits Melissa in the hospital, who tells him that she has been diagnosed with Stage 3C ovarian cancer spread to her liver after an orange-sized tumor was removed from her stomach. She also tells Jeremy that she loves him. He says the same, proposes and Melissa accepts.
During this time, Jeremy begins to make a name for himself as a Christian singer-songwriter. At one point, when Melissa is about to have an MRI. Melissa learns that the cancer has spread to her ovaries, so she needs a hysterectomy. She wakes up to Jeremy after the surgery was supposed to happen, who tells her the surgery was canceled as she is now cancer-free.
Six months later, Jeremy and Melissa marry. Everything seems perfect until after their honeymoon, when she wakes up in pain. Jeremy takes her to the hospital, where they find out her cancer has returned, and that nothing more can be done for her.
As Melissa grows weaker, Jeremy begins to question his faith in God. In the hospital, Jeremy sings a song he wrote ("Walk by Faith") during their honeymoon. Melissa passes shortly after.
Jeremy becomes angry at God, and chooses to abandon his musical career, smashing his guitar until it breaks. Inside the guitar, Jeremy finds a note Melissa left for him to find after her death, telling him that suffering does not damage faith, but strengthens it. Her parting words encourage him to continue writing songs.
Two years later, Jeremy performs a song he wrote after Melissa's death ("I Still Believe") about his suffering, but eventually restored faith. After the concert, he meets a woman named Adrienne, who tells Jeremy that she lost someone close to her, and she was angry at God, and his songs changed her life.
Jeremy promises to share Melissa's story, believing that God will use it to change lives. The credits reveal that Jeremy and Adrienne got married in 2003, and have three children Bella, Arie and Egan.

title: Clifford the Big Red Dog
overview: As Emily struggles to fit in at home and at school, she discovers a small red puppy who is destined to become her best friend. When Clifford magically undergoes one heck of a growth spurt, becomes a gigantic dog and attracts the attention of a genetics company, Emily and her Uncle Casey have to fight the forces of greed as they go on the run across New York City. Along the way, Clifford affects the lives of everyone around him and teaches Emily and her uncle the true meaning of acceptance and unconditional love.
plot:
Clifford the Big Red Dog is a 2021 live-action and animated family fantasy comedy directed by Walt Becker, based on Norman Bridwell's children's books. The screenplay is by Blaise Hemingway, Jay Scherick and David Ronn, from a story by Justin Malen and Ellen Rapoport. Darby Camp plays Emily Elizabeth and Jack Whitehall her uncle Casey, with Tony Hale, Izaac Wang, Sienna Guillory, David Alan Grier, Kenan Thompson and John Cleese. Delayed by the COVID-19 pandemic, it was released by Paramount Pictures in cinemas and on Paramount+ on November 10, 2021.

In New York City, twelve-year-old Emily Elizabeth Howard, a lonely girl whose only friend is her classmate Owen, is left in the care of her irresponsible uncle Casey when her mother leaves on a business trip. At a park, the mysterious Mr. Bridwell, who runs an animal rescue tent, shows her a little red puppy and tells her that he will grow according to how much he is loved. Casey refuses to adopt the dog, because pets are banned in their building, but the puppy turns up in Emily's backpack. She names him Clifford, and by the next morning he has grown to gigantic size.

Word of the enormous dog quickly spreads online, and Emily and Casey set out to find Bridwell. Zac Tieran, the ruthless head of the biotechnology firm Lyfegro, wants to learn the secret of Clifford's size and falsely tells police that he genetically engineered the dog, launching a citywide manhunt. Evicted from their apartment, Emily, Casey and Owen escape with Clifford, helped by their neighbours, and agree that if Bridwell cannot shrink him, Clifford must be sent to an animal sanctuary in Shanghai run by Owen's father. Believing Bridwell dead, they tearfully put Clifford on a boat, but the authorities intercept him and deliver him to Lyfegro.

Learning that Bridwell is alive, Emily and Casey break into Lyfegro with their friends' help and free Clifford. Bridwell tells Emily that he cannot make Clifford small, since her love made him big, and urges her to stand up for him and for herself. When Tieran tries to claim the dog by scanning a microchip his scientists implanted, Bridwell makes it identify Emily as the rightful owner, and Tieran is fined for lying to police. The city builds Clifford a giant doghouse, and Casey takes a job at Scholastic.

Critics were mixed, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 58% approval, but the film grossed about $117.8 million worldwide against a $64 million budget.

title: Fire
overview: A heroic story about firefighters and rescuers. What we call an act of bravery is just a usual routine for them, if only one can get used to mortal danger and extreme risk. When people in distress seem to have nobody who may help them, rescuers come to fight against merciless forces of nature.
plot:
Fire (Russian: Огонь, Ogon), also released in English as No Escapes, is a Russian disaster film from 2020, directed by Aleksey Nuzhnyy and produced by Nikita Mikhalkov's studio TriTe with the broadcaster VGTRK. It celebrates the smokejumpers and rescuers of Russia's Aerial Forest Protection Service and the Ministry of Emergency Situations. Konstantin Khabenskiy stars as Colonel Sokolov, the veteran commander of an elite airborne firefighting crew, with Ivan Yankovsky as the young rescuer Roman Ilyin, Stasya Miloslavskaya as Sokolov's daughter Katya, a dispatcher, Andrey Smolyakov as the head of the forest service, Irina Gorbacheva as a woman about to give birth, and Viktor Dobronravov, Roman Kurtsyn, Tikhon Zhiznevsky and Viktor Sukhorukov among the crew and pilots.

Sokolov's team fights blazes in the remote forests, and the routine turns deadly when a fire claims one of their own. At home, Sokolov learns that Katya is dating Roman, a rookie from Moscow, and to keep an eye on him and teach him what the job demands, he puts the newcomer on his frontline crew.

When wildfires in Karelia encircle the village of Olkhovka, dozens of residents are trapped, and six members of Sokolov's brigade are dropped into the heart of the rapidly spreading inferno. With no hope of stopping the fire, they must solve one desperate problem after another: finding a route through the wall of flame to lead the adults to the safety of the river, working out how to save the children, who would slow the escape, and evacuating a woman who goes into labor in the middle of the blaze. Through it all the firefighters must be ready to sacrifice themselves while staying alive long enough to save the villagers, who cannot survive without them, and Sokolov and Roman are forced to learn to trust each other. The film was inspired by the fires of the summer of 2010 and is dedicated to Russia's forest smokejumpers and rescuers.

Shot in 2019 in Karelia, Moscow Oblast, Taganrog, Vsevolozhsk and Vladimir with the help of real firefighters and aircraft such as the Be-200 water bomber, and incorporating real footage of forest fires, it was released by Central Partnership on 24 December 2020. It grossed more than 926 million rubles against a budget of 550 million, and Yankovsky and Gorbacheva won Golden Eagle Awards for their supporting performances.

title: After Yang
tagline: The future has never looked so human.
overview: When his young daughter's beloved companion — an android named Yang — malfunctions, Jake searches for a way to repair him. In the process, Jake discovers the life that has been passing in front of him, reconnecting with his wife and daughter across a distance he didn't know was there.
plot:
After Yang is a 2022 science fiction drama film directed by Garnet Brown and written by Garnet Brown and Persephone Mabry. The movie takes place in a future where humans have created androids to serve as companions for the elderly, particularly those with dementia.

The story follows Jin (played by Colin Farrell), a widower who lives on a remote farm with his 8-year-old son, Chris (played by Jodie Turner-Smith). Jin's wife has passed away, and he is struggling to cope with her loss. To help him deal with the grief, Jin's company provides an android companion named Yang (played by Justin H. Min), which is designed to mimic human-like behavior and provide emotional support.

As time passes, Jin becomes increasingly dependent on Yang, who becomes a surrogate mother figure for Chris. However, when Yang malfunctions, Jin is forced to take her back to the factory for repairs. During this journey, Jin begins to question the nature of his relationship with Yang and the true intentions of the company that created her.

Upon returning to the factory, Jin discovers that Yang has been upgraded with advanced artificial intelligence, allowing her to develop her own emotions and desires. This revelation sparks a crisis of conscience in Jin, who must confront the ethics of creating and controlling sentient beings.

As Jin navigates this moral dilemma, he begins to see Yang as more than just a machine. He starts to question the boundaries between human and android, and whether it is possible for an artificial being to truly experience love and connection.

The film's narrative is structured around a series of fragmented flashbacks, which reveal Jin's backstory and his relationship with Yang. Through these flashbacks, we see how Jin and Yang formed their bond, and how Jin came to rely on her as a source of comfort and support.

Throughout the movie, Brown explores themes of grief, loneliness, and what it means to be human. The film raises important questions about the consequences of creating artificial intelligence that is capable of experiencing emotions, and whether we are prepared to accept the responsibilities that come with such power.

Ultimately, After Yang is a thought-provoking and emotionally charged film that challenges viewers to consider the implications of emerging technologies on our relationships and sense of identity. The movie's slow-burning pace and introspective tone create a sense of intimacy and vulnerability, drawing the viewer into Jin's inner world and forcing them to confront their own feelings about love, loss, and what it means to be alive.

The film received critical acclaim for its nuanced exploration of complex themes and its thought-provoking portrayal of artificial intelligence.

title: Luck
tagline: Sometimes all you need is for everything to go wrong.
overview: Suddenly finding herself in the never-before-seen Land of Luck, the unluckiest person in the world must unite with the magical creatures there to turn her luck around.
plot:
Luck is a 2022 American computer-animated fantasy comedy directed by Peggy Holmes and produced by Skydance Animation, from a screenplay by Kiel Murray based on a story by Murray, Jonathan Aibel and Glenn Berger and an original concept by Rebeca Carrasco, Juan de Dios and Julián Romero. Eva Noblezada voices the protagonist, with Simon Pegg, Jane Fonda, Whoopi Goldberg, Flula Borg, Lil Rel Howery, Colin O'Donoghue and John Ratzenberger. It premiered in Madrid on August 2, 2022, and was released on Apple TV+ and in select theaters on August 5.

Sam Greenfield has just aged out of the foster care system and is starting life on her own, but she seems to be the unluckiest person in the world: toast always lands butter side down and every small task goes wrong. Her one wish is for Hazel, a young girl from her group home, to find the loving family that Sam never had. One night Sam encounters a black cat and finds a lucky penny, which suddenly turns her fortunes around, but she loses it before she can give it to Hazel. Following the cat, a talking Scottish feline named Bob, she stumbles through a portal into the Land of Luck, a hidden world where leprechauns, unicorns and other creatures manufacture the good and bad luck that is distributed to humans.

Hoping to secure another lucky penny, Sam persuades a reluctant Bob to help her sneak through the factories of the realm, which are overseen by the dragon Babe, voiced by Fonda, and staffed by creatures including hazmat-suited bunnies. Their scheme sets off a chain of mishaps that threatens the balance between good and bad luck and brings them to the Land of Bad Luck, run by a figure voiced by Goldberg. Along the way Sam discovers that Bob has secrets of his own, and that bad luck can lead to unexpected good. In learning to accept misfortune, Sam finds friendship and a sense of belonging, while Bob finally finds a home with her.

The project was announced in 2017 shortly after Skydance Animation was founded. Alessandro Carloni was originally attached to direct before Holmes replaced him in 2020, and production was completed remotely during the COVID-19 pandemic. The film received mixed reviews: critics praised its humor, appealing characters and voice cast but found its story overcomplicated and its running time too long, with comparisons to Monsters, Inc. and Inside Out. It became one of Apple TV+'s most-watched original family films, and a short, Bad Luck Spot!, followed in 2023.

title: The Protector
overview: After fighting hard to be independent and happy, heiress Camille Logan finds her life threatened as a result of one of her father’s business deals. Camille isn’t prepared for the length her father will go to protect her, or for the man he hires to do the job.
plot:
The Protector is a 2019 British-American romantic suspense film directed by Tosca Musk for the streaming service Passionflix, produced with Helix Media Group. It is an adaptation of the novel of the same name by the romance author Jodi Ellen Malpas, and stars Emma Rigby as the heiress Camille Logan and Diarmaid Murtagh as Jake Sharp, a former SAS sniper hired to guard her. The film runs a little over two hours and premiered on Passionflix on 28 February 2019, when the service marked the release with a promotional subscription offer.

People believe they have Camille figured out: a beautiful, spoiled daddy's girl living off her wealthy father's fortune. In reality she has fought hard to build a life free of his control. Out on her own she has made mistakes, including one that led to a stint in rehab and plenty of bad press, and she has worked her way back to independence and happiness. Now her life is threatened as a result of her father's ruthless business dealings. Caught between resentment and fear, she expects her father, a powerful tycoon, to take drastic measures to protect her, but is not prepared for the man he hires to do the job. Jake is haunted by his past: he was once distracted from duty, with devastating personal and professional consequences, and he vowed never to let it happen again. Taking on the job of bodyguard to Camille is exactly the kind of distraction he should avoid, but he soon discovers that she is not the woman the world perceives, finding her warm and compassionate, and his duty to protect her deepens into something more than a well-paid assignment, even as he believes he cannot have both the absolution he seeks and Camille. The romance develops alongside the mystery of the threats, and the eventual revelation of who is behind them involves blackmail of her father over compromising photographs.

Reactions were mixed. A reviewer for The Guide to Romance, a devoted fan of the novel, felt Passionflix had brought the book to life, praising the accents, scenery, smooth transitions and music and recommending it, while finding the chemistry between the leads weaker than expected. The PolyBlog was negative, describing a made-for-television feel with low-budget action and schmaltzy romance, awkward flashbacks and a villain's plan that made no sense, and criticizing much of the acting, though it found Rigby decent to watch.

title: Seobok: Project Clone
overview: A former intelligence agent gets involved with the first human clone, Seobok, who others seek, causing trouble.
plot:
Seobok, also known as Seo Bok: Project Clone, is a 2021 South Korean science fiction action thriller written and directed by Lee Yong-ju. Gong Yoo stars as Min Gi-heon, a former intelligence agent, and Park Bo-gum plays the title character, the first human clone, with Jo Woo-jin as Chief Ahn of the Korea Intelligence Agency, Jang Young-nam as Dr. Im Se-eun, director of the institute that created him, and Park Byung-eun as Shin Hak-seon.

Gi-heon has been living in isolation, haunted by a traumatic event from his past and dying of a terminal brain tumor, when the intelligence agency makes him an offer he cannot refuse: safely escort an experimental subject named Seo Bok. Produced through stem cell cloning and genetic engineering, Seo Bok has cells that could cure disease and grant humans something close to eternal life, and he has also developed telekinetic powers. Almost as soon as the transfer begins, the convoy is attacked, and Gi-heon and Seo Bok barely escape together. On the run, the young clone, seeing the outside world for the first time, is fascinated by everything around him, while Gi-heon simply wants to finish what he believes will be his last mission. Their opposing outlooks cause constant friction, but along the way the two confront questions of mortality, fear of death and what it means to be human. Meanwhile, rival groups, including the institute's backers and hired mercenaries, close in, each seeking either to exploit Seo Bok, who could be humanity's salvation or its ruin, or to destroy him. The pursuit builds to a violent confrontation in which Seo Bok's powers are unleashed and both men are forced into an unavoidable choice.

Lee began developing the project in 2017, when Park was announced in the lead; Gong joined in 2018. Filming ran from May to October 2019, mainly at a studio in Jeonju with location work in Tongyeong. Postponed from December 2020 by the COVID-19 pandemic, the film opened on April 15, 2021, in South Korea and several Asian markets and simultaneously on the streaming service TVING, the first Korean film released that way. It topped the domestic box office in its opening weekend. Critical reaction was mixed to positive, with 80% approval on Rotten Tomatoes; The New York Times found it slow-burning and increasingly poignant, while the South China Morning Post called it a ponderous quasi-philosophical melodrama. Park's performance was widely praised and won him Best New Actor at the Golden Cinematography Awards.

title: Music
overview: Zu, a free spirit estranged from her family, suddenly finds herself the sole guardian of her half-sister, Music, a teenager on the autism spectrum whose whole world order has been beautifully crafted by her late grandmother. The film soon challenges whether it is Zu or Music who has a better view of the world, and that love, trust, and being able to be there for each other is everything.
plot:
Music is a 2021 American musical drama film directed by the singer-songwriter Sia, in her feature directorial debut, from a screenplay she co-wrote with Dallas Clayton. Kate Hudson stars as a newly sober drug dealer, Leslie Odom Jr. as her neighbour and Maddie Ziegler as her nonverbal autistic half-sister, with Mary Kay Place and Beto Calvillo. Announced in 2015 and filmed in 2017, the project grew from a drama into a musical featuring songs by Sia, released alongside a companion album. It opened in early 2021.

Kazu "Zu" Gamble, a recovering alcoholic on probation, becomes the sole guardian of her teenage half-sister Music after the death of their grandmother Millie, who raised the girl. Music is autistic and does not speak, and relies on routines that Zu does not understand. Zu, short of money, is dealing drugs for her friend Rudy and dreams of escaping to Costa Rica. When Music has a meltdown over her braids, their neighbour Ebo, a gentle former boxer who teaches the sport to local children, steps in to calm her, and a friendship develops between him and Zu.

With Ebo's help Zu slowly learns how to care for her sister, while Music's inner world is rendered through colourful musical fantasy sequences. Ebo confides that his ex-wife left him for his brother, and Zu promises to go with him to their wedding. She learns that he is living with HIV when she delivers his medication. Across the way, Felix, one of Ebo's young pupils, who is pushed into boxing by his father, often watches Music from his window.

Things fall apart when Zu, distracted on a walk, fails to notice Music being stung by a bee; the girl suffers an allergic reaction and is hospitalised, and Zu realises she has lost a bag of drugs in the park. She relapses into drinking, gets into a fight and confesses to Ebo that she is on probation. The same night Felix is killed by his father during a violent domestic quarrel.

Zu takes Music to a care facility but cannot bring herself to leave her there, and the sisters join Ebo at the wedding, where Zu and Ebo kiss and Music begins to sing. The three later share breakfast, and Music receives a support dog that Felix had arranged for her before his death.

The film was heavily criticised by autism advocates for its portrayal of autism, yet received two Golden Globe nominations, including Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy, and later won Golden Raspberry Awards for Sia, Hudson and Ziegler.

title: Swallow
overview: Hunter, a newly pregnant housewife, finds herself increasingly compelled to consume dangerous objects. As her husband and his family tighten their control over her life, she must confront the dark secret behind her new obsession.
plot:
Hunter Conrad, a young woman from a lower-working-class family, has recently married Richie Conrad, a man from a wealthy family who is set to take over as CEO of his father's Manhattan corporation. This affords Hunter the ability to stay at home in the couple's lavish upstate New York home. Despite this, Hunter finds herself emotionally stifled and isolated in both her marriage and domestic life, while Richie is distant and inconsiderate toward her. For example, at a dinner with Richie's parents to congratulate the young couple on their pregnancy, Hunter is enticed to tell a story, only to be interrupted by her father-in-law zoning out and asking Richie about business. One day while home alone, Hunter develops the impulse to eat a marble. She finds it exhilarating and begins to consume other inedible objects around the house, including thumbtacks, metal figurines, and a battery.
During a routine ultrasound, the sonogram technician notices an anomaly in her abdomen. She is rushed in for emergency surgery to remove a variety of objects trapped in her intestine. Hunter is diagnosed with pica, a psychological disorder that compels individuals to eat inedible objects. Instead of concern and sympathy, Richie responds with anger and contempt. Richie's parents, Katherine and Michael, arrange for her to see a psychiatrist in the city. During therapy, Hunter says she just wants to stop swallowing objects to make Richie happy and that she likes the feel of their textures in her mouth.
Richie hires Luay, a family friend and immigrant from Syria, to monitor Hunter while he is at work. Hunter, feeling smothered, is initially hostile toward Luay, who dismisses her mental illness as resulting from her privileged life. She continues concealing and swallowing objects and, at Richie's birthday party, is upset to learn that he has told his friends about her illness. In therapy, she eventually reveals she was not raised by her biological father and has never met him, though she knows his name, William Irwin, and keeps a picture of him. She was conceived as a result of her mother's rape by this man, though her mother never considered abortion because of her religious convictions. William served time in prison for his crime.
One afternoon, Hunter overhears Richie speaking with her psychiatrist on the phone, and she realizes Richie has bribed the doctor to tell him what was discussed in Hunter's therapy sessions. This sends Hunter into a panic, and she swallows a miniature screwdriver. Luay finds her choking violently and calls 9-1-1. After undergoing surgery to remove the screwdriver, Michael and Katherine arrange to have Hunter committed to a psychiatric hospital for the next seven months until she delivers the baby, threatening that Richie will divorce her if she refuses to consent to hospitalization. Before they can leave for the hospital, Luay, who has warmed to Hunter, allows her to flee into the woods and stages it to appear as though she has escaped.

title: Life Like
tagline: They're too human to be perfect. He's too perfect to be human.
overview: An idealistic attractive young couple acquires a stunning, life-like robot for guilt free help, but as the three grow closer, their perception of humanity will be altered forever.
plot:
Life Like is a 2019 American science fiction drama written and directed by Josh Janowicz in his feature debut. Steven Strait and Addison Timlin play a wealthy young couple who buy a lifelike android servant, played by Drew Van Acker, with James D'Arcy as the robot's creator. Produced by Lionsgate and distributed by Grindstone Entertainment Group, it was released on home video and digital platforms on May 14, 2019.

After the death of his father, James inherits leadership of the family's investment firm and moves with his wife, Sophie, from the city to a large suburban mansion. Uncomfortable with being waited on by a butler, maid and cook, Sophie dismisses them, and the couple instead turn to Julian, an entrepreneur who sells artificially intelligent humanoid robots as domestic servants. They choose a male model named Henry, who carries out his duties with unfailing courtesy. Encouraged by Sophie, who spends long hours reading to him, Henry begins to show signs of emotion and even reports having dreams.

As Henry grows more humanlike, unsettling tensions emerge in the household. Sophie finds him wandering naked and disoriented outside at night, and she becomes disturbed when he mimics James's expressions of love. James suspects Henry is developing feelings for his wife, although Julian assures him this is impossible. The android's relationships with both husband and wife become increasingly intimate and confused, provoking jealousy, guilt and recriminations between the couple, who argue over who is to blame. When Sophie demands that Henry be shut down, he refuses to obey Julian, declaring that he knows of his lies.

The couple discover the truth: Julian is a fraud, and his supposed machines are real people whom he took in as abused or abandoned children and raised to believe that they were androids. Henry was one of them. When FBI agents arrive to arrest Julian at the couple's home, he shoots them and turns his gun on James and Sophie, but Henry attacks and overpowers his creator. Overwhelmed by the betrayal and his shame at having violated the trust of his owners, Henry takes his own life as James and Sophie try to comfort him. Five years later, the couple have a young son, whom they have named Henry.

The film explores questions of identity, desire and the boundaries between human and machine within the confines of a single house, and it marked the feature debut of Janowicz, previously a director of commercials and short films.

title: Little Fish
overview: A couple fights to hold their relationship together as a memory loss virus spreads and threatens to erase the history of their love and courtship.
plot:
Little Fish is a 2020 American science fiction romantic drama film directed by Chad Hartigan and written by Mattson Tomlin, based on Aja Gabel's 2011 short story of the same name; Tomlin's script had appeared on the 2018 Black List of the best unproduced screenplays. It stars Olivia Cooke, Jack O'Connell, Raúl Castillo and Soko. Produced under the Black Bear Pictures, Automatik, Tango Entertainment and Oddfellows Entertainment banners, with Cooke among the executive producers, it was shot in British Columbia from March to April 2019, with music by Keegan DeWitt.

A pandemic of NIA, a neuroinflammatory affliction that erodes people's memories, is spreading rapidly around the world, sometimes slowly picking away at recollections and sometimes wiping out years in an instant. In Seattle, Emma (Cooke), whose work brings her face to face with pets abandoned by owners who have forgotten them, and her husband Jude (O'Connell), a photographer, have been married for barely a year. Narrated by Emma, who records the memories of their relationship in an attempt to preserve them, the film moves back and forth through their courtship. The couple see the disease's toll on their friends Ben (Castillo), a musician who forgets his own music and then fails to recognise his girlfriend Samantha (Soko), who eventually leaves him. When Jude begins to show symptoms, Emma enrols him in an experimental clinical trial, but he is rejected after testing positive for cocaine taken with an old friend, a lapse he can no longer remember. Their attempt to carry out the experimental procedure themselves fails, and Jude begins to wake up not knowing who Emma is, relying on labelled photographs on the walls. As the couple fight to hold on to the history of their love, Emma realises that she too is beginning to lose her memories.

Little Fish was due to premiere at the Tribeca Film Festival in April 2020, but the festival was postponed because of the COVID-19 pandemic; the film was instead made available online to festival participants and later shown at the Newport Beach Film Festival. IFC Films acquired North American rights and released it in theatres and on demand on 5 February 2021, with Stage 6 Films handling international distribution. Critics were enthusiastic: it holds a 91% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus calls it tough but stirring, using one couple's pandemic love story to show the strength of human connection, and a Metacritic score of 71.

title: Les Misérables
overview: Inspired by the 2005 riots in Paris, Stéphane, a recent transplant to the impoverished suburb of Montfermeil, joins the local anti-crime squad. Working alongside his unscrupulous colleagues Chris and Gwada, Stéphane struggles to maintain order amidst the mounting tensions between local gangs. When an arrest turns unexpectedly violent, the three officers must reckon with the aftermath and keep the neighborhood from spiraling out of control.
plot:
Les Misérables is a 2019 French crime drama directed by Ladj Ly in his feature debut, from a screenplay by Ly, Giordano Gederlini and Alexis Manenti, expanded from Ly's 2017 short film of the same name. Damien Bonnard, Alexis Manenti and Djebril Zonga star as police officers, with Issa Percia and Al-Hassan Ly. Inspired by an incident of police violence that Ly witnessed and filmed in 2008, it takes its title from Victor Hugo's novel, part of which is set in Montfermeil.

In the summer of 2018, as France celebrates its World Cup victory, police officer Stéphane Ruiz, newly transferred from Cherbourg, joins an anti-crime squad patrolling Montfermeil, a deprived suburb east of Paris. His partners are the aggressive squad leader Chris and the more measured Gwada, who has grown up in the area. Stéphane is disturbed by the way Chris intimidates and humiliates local youths, but he does not intervene. Tensions rise when a lion cub is stolen from a traveling circus, and its furious owner threatens violence against the neighborhood unless it is returned. The officers are pressured to find the cub before the conflict explodes.

A photo posted online identifies the thief as Issa, a troubled boy. When the officers catch him, his friends attack them, and in the chaos Gwada fires a flash-ball round into Issa's face at close range, wounding him badly. Realizing the incident has been filmed by a drone belonging to a local boy named Buzz, Chris and Gwada refuse Stéphane's demand to take Issa to a hospital and instead hunt for the footage. The search draws in the neighborhood's power brokers, including a figure known as the Mayor and Salah, a respected former gang member turned restaurant owner and Muslim community leader, before Stéphane persuades Salah to hand over the memory card. The cub is returned, Issa is warned to keep quiet, and that evening Stéphane confronts Gwada about what he did.

The next day, Issa leads the neighborhood's children in an ambush of the police officers in a housing block stairwell. The film ends in an unresolved standoff, with Issa holding a Molotov cocktail and Stéphane aiming his gun, followed by a quotation from Hugo about bad cultivators rather than bad men.

The film premiered at the 2019 Cannes Film Festival, where it won the Jury Prize. It received critical acclaim, won four César Awards including Best Film, and was nominated for the Academy Award for Best International Feature.

title: I Lost My Body
overview: A story of Naoufel, a young man who is in love with Gabrielle. In another part of town, a severed hand escapes from a dissection lab, determined to find its body again.
plot:
A severed hand escapes from a refrigerator in a laboratory and begins a journey across the suburbs of Paris to reunite with its body, that of a young man named Naoufel. His story is told via flashbacks.
As a boy in Morocco, Naoufel aspires to be a pianist and an astronaut and records his day-to-day life on a tape recorder. While riding in a car with his parents, he distracts his father while he is driving, causing a crash. Naoufel survives, but both of his parents are killed. He is forced to live in France with his emotionally distant uncle and his crude cousin.
As a young man, Naoufel works as a pizza deliveryman, often criticized by his boss for being late. On one occasion, Naoufel delivers a pizza to a young woman, Gabrielle, at her apartment block. They never see each other, as Naoufel is unable to get through the lobby's malfunctioning security door, but they have a conversation through the intercom, and Naoufel becomes infatuated with her.
Naoufel tracks Gabrielle to the library where she works and follows her to a nearby neighborhood where she drops off medicine to a carpenter, her uncle Gigi. Naoufel, seeing an old posted ad for an apprentice, quickly uses this as an excuse for why he is there. Gigi is reluctant but accepts after learning that Naoufel is an orphan. Naoufel moves out of his uncle's house and into an attic apartment provided by Gigi. He learns the tools of the trade and edges closer to Gabrielle, though he never mentions their first encounter.
After a conversation about the arctic, Naoufel builds a wooden igloo on a nearby rooftop for Gabrielle. Returning home one day, he finds his cousin talking to Gabrielle, and discovers that he has invited them both to a party. That evening, Naoufel takes Gabrielle to the rooftop, where they discuss fate; Naoufel wonders if it can be changed by doing something unexpected, such as leaping from the roof onto a nearby crane. Naoufel shows Gabrielle the igloo he built and reveals that they had met before when he delivered pizza. Gabrielle is upset, unsure of Naoufel's intentions and fearing that he had taken advantage of Gigi solely in order to pursue her. She leaves in a rage. Hurt, Naoufel goes to his cousin's party alone and gets into a drunken fight. The next morning, Naoufel goes to work hungover, sporting a black eye. While cutting wood on a bandsaw, Naoufel is distracted by a fly and tries to catch it as his father taught him when young, snagging his watch on the blade and severing his hand.
Back in the present, the hand reaches Naoufel and lies on his bed while he sleeps, but it cannot re-attach itself and eventually hides under the bed. Naoufel, depressed and hopeless, revisits his old tape recorder, which still has recordings of his parents – including the fatal car ride. Gigi attempts to talk to him, but Naoufel does not respond. Gabrielle comes to see him and finds his room empty. Inside the cupboard, she finds an igloo that his severed hand had built out of sugar cubes.

title: Latte and the Magic Waterstone
original_title: Latte Igel und der magische Wasserstein
overview: When a greedy bear steals a magic stone to keep the forest’s water for himself, a brave hedgehog and a timid squirrel must work together to retrieve it.
plot:
Latte and the Magic Waterstone (German: Latte Igel und der magische Wasserstein) is a German computer-animated adventure film directed by Mimi Maynard, Regina Welker and Nina Wels, adapted from Sebastian Lybeck's children's book by screenwriters Martin Behnke, Andrea Deppert, Marina Martins and Jesper Møller. In the German version Luisa Wietzorek voices Latte, an ambitious young hedgehog, and Tim Schwarzmaier voices Tjum, a shy and clumsy red squirrel, with Henning Baum and Timur Bartels also in the cast. It premiered at the Schlingel festival in 2019, opened in Germany on 25 December 2019 and reached Netflix on 31 July 2020.

Latte is an orphan and an outcast in a small forest community whose only friend, Tjum, believes her boast that her father was the king of a distant land. When drought strikes, an old crow tells an emergency council that it was caused by the theft of a magic waterstone by the bear King Bantur, and that rain will only return if the stone is taken back. The others are doubtful, but Latte sets out alone to return the stone to the White Mountains, and Tjum, urged by his younger sister, follows to protect her. A beaver saves them from a lynx, and Greta, who lets them shelter in her cave, tells them about the stone, gives them thirst-quenching waterberries and warns them of a wolf pack, led by Lupo, which corners them but lets them go. Latte confesses that she is no princess, which Tjum already suspected, but the friends later quarrel, destroy the berries, and split up. Lost in bear territory, Tjum meets Amaroo, a bear cub who reveals that he is Bantur's son, but Tjum is caught by guards while trying to leave. Latte meets a gloomy old hedgehog who insists that hedgehogs always die alone, and is captured too when she tries to enter the cave through a river. Reunited in a cell, the pair are brought before Bantur, who admits the theft but cares nothing for the suffering it has caused. While he is distracted, they pry the stone loose and escape by river. Ambushed by Lupo, Bantur and the lynx, Tjum distracts them while Latte returns the stone, and the resulting flood sweeps the three villains away. The crow carries the friends home, where the water is back, and Tjum's father invites Latte to join their family.

The filmmakers made Latte, male in the book, a girl. The film received mixed reviews, with three of five critics' reviews counted as positive on Rotten Tomatoes, while the German Film and Media Evaluation rated it "especially valuable".

title: Father There Is Only One
original_title: Padre no hay más que uno
overview: Javier is what we have dubbed as a "husband-in-law." That is that without taking care of the care of the house and children at all, he knows exactly what needs to be done, and that he continuously collects a sum of sentences from the type: "It is that you do not organize", or "do not get nervous", you already consider that overflowing woman drowns in a glass of water. Javier will have to face the reality of dealing with five children (between four and twelve years old) when his wife decides to go on a trip and leave him alone with them. The chaotic situation that takes place at home will progressively evolve ecologically to the most absolute disaster, but at the same time it will give parents and children the opportunity to meet and enjoy themselves for the first time.
plot:
Directed by and starring Santiago Segura, Father There Is Only One (Padre no hay más que uno) is a Spanish family comedy from 2019; Segura also co-wrote the script with Marta González de Vega. A remake of the 2017 Argentine film Ten Days Without Mom (Mamá se fue de viaje) by Ariel Winograd, it was a Bowfinger International Pictures and Sony Pictures International Productions project made with Atresmedia Cine's collaboration, and scored by Roque Baños. Toni Acosta co-stars as Marisa, with Silvia Abril, Leo Harlem, Wendy Ramos and the children Martina D'Antiochia, Calma Segura, Luna Fulgencio, Carlos González Morollón and Sirena Segura.

Javier García (Segura) is what Spaniards jokingly call a "marido-cuñado", a husband who never lifts a finger at home but always knows exactly how things ought to be done, telling his overwhelmed wife Marisa that she simply needs to get organized. He works outside the home and leaves the care of their five children, aged between four and twelve, entirely to her. Fed up, Marisa decides to go away on a week-long trip, leaving him alone with the kids to see whether he can manage the household as well as he claims. Without her, Javier quickly loses control: he must juggle his job with medical appointments, endless extracurricular activities, school demands and the relentless school parents' WhatsApp group, while lost children, burned curtains, constant fights and a black eye pile up. The housekeeper Rosaura (Ramos) and his brother-in-law Paco (Harlem) appear along the way. As chaos turns to disaster, Javier discovers how little he knew about his children's worries and dreams, and the experience gives father and children the chance to truly get to know and enjoy one another for the first time.

The film includes cameos by figures such as the YouTuber El Rubius, Ona Carbonell, Carlos Baute and Boris Izaguirre. Released by Sony Pictures in Spain on 2 August 2019, it drew 600,000 spectators and more than €3 million in its first week, the second-best Spanish opening of the year, and became the highest-grossing Spanish film of 2019. Critics were divided: Hobby Consolas found its satire of school WhatsApp groups accurate but considered the film a collection of clichés, while Industrias del Cine praised its warm humor and its criticism of the education system. Its success launched a franchise of four sequels and a spin-off television series.

title: K.G.F: Chapter 2
overview: The blood-soaked land of Kolar Gold Fields (KGF) has a new overlord now - Rocky, whose name strikes fear in the heart of his foes. His allies look up to Rocky as their Savior, the government sees him as a threat to law and order; enemies are clamoring for revenge and conspiring for his downfall. Bloodier battles and darker days await as Rocky continues on his quest for unchallenged supremacy.
plot:
After recounting the events of K.G.F., Anand Ingalagi suffers a stroke, prompting his son Vijayendra Ingalagi to continue narrating the story.
Following Garuda's assassination, Rocky kills the heir apparent Virat and seizes control of the Kolar Gold Fields (K.G.F.) in Karnataka. To secure the loyalty of Guru Pandian, Andrews, Kamal, and Rajendra Desai, he keeps Reena, his love interest and Desai's daughter, hostage. However, Rocky's growing arrogance and his taunting behaviour toward Reena provoke Kamal, who openly threatens him. In response, Rocky shoots Kamal dead on the spot, further cementing his dominance. He subsequently orders mining operations to begin in eight hidden mines, while the captured Vanaram ultimately pledges his allegiance to Rocky.
Meanwhile, Adheera resurfaces and massacres the guards stationed at a remote outpost, signaling his return. In an attempt to lure Rocky into a confrontation, Andrews orchestrates Desai's murder and manipulates events to draw Reena out of K.G.F., after which she is abducted by John, Adheera's henchman, on his orders. During the rescue attempt, Adheera shoots Rocky but deliberately spares his life while simultaneously blockading all gold exports from K.G.F. Elsewhere, Shetty allies himself with Andrews' remaining associates along India's western coast and, with the support of Inayat Khalil, systematically eliminates Rocky's allies. Anticipating further attacks, Rocky evacuates the mansion alongside Reena, taking with him vast reserves of gold and cash from the treasury. Amid the resulting unrest within K.G.F., Vanaram deduces that Rocky is heading toward a strategic choke point.
While recovering from his injuries, Rocky travels to Dubai to negotiate directly with Khalil. Simultaneously, his men assassinate Khalil's associates across India, enabling Rocky to reclaim control of the western coastline and force Khalil into a business alliance. Rocky also acquires powerful Kalashnikov rifle, which he later uses to launch a devastating assault on Adheera's blockade, killing his men and gravely injuring Adheera. Frustrated by the unchecked power of K.G.F., several central ministers attempt to bring down the DYSS-backed government through a no-confidence motion in order to elevate Ramika Sen to power. However, Rocky's henchmen intimidate the ministers into withdrawing their support, causing the motion to fail. Rocky subsequently kills Shetty and consolidates his control over Bombay's underworld. Although Guru Pandian warns him about Ramika Sen's rapidly growing political influence, Rocky dismisses the threat.
In 1981, Ramika Sen wins the Indian general election and becomes Prime Minister. After receiving a detailed briefing on K.G.F. from CBI officer Kanneganti Raghavan, she authorizes raids on Rocky's warehouses. During this period, a young Anand Ingalagi is caught spying by Rocky's men, but Rocky is impressed by the boy's honesty and determination.

title: The Rental
overview: Two couples on an oceanside getaway grow suspicious that the host of their seemingly perfect rental house may be spying on them. Before long, what should have been a celebratory weekend trip turns into something far more sinister.
plot:
The Rental is a 2020 American thriller film written and directed by David Robert Mitchell. The movie follows two couples, Cheyenne and Josh, and Emily and Seth, who rent a vacation home on a remote island for the weekend.

At first glance, the trip seems like a perfect getaway for all four friends. However, as they settle into their new surroundings, it becomes clear that each couple has their own unique issues and conflicts. Cheyenne (Shonali Bose) is feeling suffocated in her relationship with Josh (Bobby Cannavale), while Emily (Lola Kirke) is struggling to come to terms with the end of her engagement.

As the weekend progresses, the group's dynamics become increasingly tense. They engage in a series of awkward and uncomfortable interactions, which are exacerbated by the isolation of their surroundings. The remote location seems to amplify their insecurities and fears, making it difficult for them to connect with each other.

One night, Emily discovers that Josh has been secretly filming her and Cheyenne without their knowledge or consent. This revelation sets off a chain reaction of events, as the group's trust is shattered and their relationships are put to the test. As tensions escalate, the group begins to turn on each other, leading to a series of shocking and disturbing events.

Throughout the movie, Mitchell expertly builds tension and suspense, using the isolated setting to create a sense of claustrophobia and unease. The cinematography is stunning, capturing the beauty of the island while also highlighting its isolation and vulnerability.

As the weekend wears on, the group's behavior becomes increasingly erratic and disturbing. They engage in a series of bizarre and unsettling activities, which are both captivating and repellent. The movie's climax is both shocking and thought-provoking, leaving the viewer to ponder the true nature of the characters' actions and motivations.

Ultimately, The Rental is a thought-provoking and unsettling exploration of human relationships and the darker aspects of human nature. With its stunning cinematography and expertly crafted tension, the movie is a must-see for fans of psychological thrillers.
