title: NiNoKuni
overview: Adapted from the video game series of the same name, NiNoKuni follows high school peers Yuu and Haru who must travel between two separate yet parallel worlds to help save their childhood friend, Kotona, whose life is in danger. In this magical quest complicated by love, the three teens will be tasked with making the ultimate choice.
plot:
NiNoKuni is a 2019 Japanese animated fantasy film directed by Yoshiyuki Momose and based on the video game series developed by Level-5, whose founder Akihiro Hino wrote and executive produced the film. Produced by OLM and distributed by Warner Bros. Pictures, it features the voices of Kento Yamazaki as Yū, Mackenyu Arata as Haru and Mei Nagano as Kotona, with Maaya Sakamoto, Mamoru Miyano as the mage Gnauss, Kenjiro Tsuda as Galeroth and Masatō Ibu as King Astrum. Joe Hisaishi, who scored the earlier games, composed the music.

Yū, a bright high school student who uses a wheelchair, and his athletic best friend Haru are both close to their classmate Kotona. One evening, Kotona is attacked and stabbed by a mysterious hooded figure. As Haru tries to get her to a hospital, the two boys are suddenly transported to another world, the kingdom of Evermore, where Yū discovers that he can walk. In the royal castle they meet Princess Astrid, who looks exactly like Kotona and is suffering from a curse, which Yū manages to break.

The boys learn that the lives of people in their world are linked to those of their counterparts in Evermore, and that what happens to one affects the other. Back home, Kotona reveals that she has a serious illness, and the boys realize that saving her may require sacrificing Astrid, a choice that drives a wedge between them. As the kingdom is invaded by the army of the Black Banner, led by the sinister Galeroth, Yū and Haru are forced onto opposite sides before uncovering the true mastermind behind Astrid's curse and joining forces to save both worlds with the help of a legendary sword.

The film explores friendship, love and the connections between parallel lives, set in the world of the games centuries after the events of Ni no Kuni II: Revenant Kingdom.

NiNoKuni was released in Japan on August 23, 2019, debuting in seventh place at the box office. Netflix acquired the streaming rights and released it worldwide on January 16, 2020. The film's theme song, "MOIL", is performed by Keina Suda.

She's still obsessed with busting her brothers Phineas and Ferb, but she's starting to realize that her life is not turning out as planned. As Candace navigates this new world, she begins to see her life with Phineas and Ferb in a different light. She realizes that her brothers' inventions were not just random creations, but rather a way for them to express themselves and bring joy to others. As Candace continues her journey through space, she begins to uncover a sinister plot by Dr. Doofenshmirtz Sr. to take over the universe. The aliens, who are actually the sons and daughters of various villains from the show, join forces with Candace to stop their father's evil plans.

She realizes that she doesn't have to be defined by her failures, but rather by her own strengths and passions. The film concludes with a heartwarming moment of Candace joining her brothers in one of their famous inventions, finally finding the happiness and fulfillment she's been searching for.

Overall, Phineas and Ferb: Candace Against the Universe is a fun and heartwarming movie that explores themes of identity, purpose, and the importance of following your dreams.

title: Lamp Life
overview: Bo Peep explains what happened to herself and her sheep between the events of Toy Story 2 and Toy Story 4.
plot:
Lamp Life is a 2020 American computer-animated short film produced by Pixar Animation Studios for the streaming service Disney+. Written and directed by Valerie LaPointe, head of story on Toy Story 4, in her directorial debut, and produced by Mark Sondheimer, it is a spin-off of that feature, running about seven minutes. Annie Potts reprises her role as the porcelain shepherdess Bo Peep, with Ally Maki as Giggle McDimples and Emily Davis as Bo's three sheep, while Woody is voiced by Jim Hanks, Tom Hanks's younger brother. The score was composed by Jake Monaco.

The short fills in what happened to Bo Peep between Toy Story 2 and Toy Story 4. After reuniting with Woody, Bo, joined by her friend Giggle, tells him in a series of flashbacks how she became a lost toy. Once part of a nursery lamp in the bedroom of Andy's younger sister Molly, Bo and her sheep were given away when Molly outgrew them. In her next home, a child's bedroom, she is bored because the mother will not let the children play with the lamp, and as the years pass she moves through a montage of temporary homes, including a white elephant party where teenagers treat her roughly, at one point setting her on fire. She eventually lands in the Second Chance Antiques store, where she is safe but bored once again, and where Gabby Gabby and her ventriloquist dummies make a brief appearance. Wanting adventure and the chance to be played with, Bo devises a plan with Giggle, outwits the shop's surprisingly elaborate security system and breaks out with her sheep, beginning a free life as a lost toy.

LaPointe built the short partly from flashback material cut from Toy Story 4, which had been sad in tone, reworking the gags into comedy as Bo looks back on her hard life with humor. She received guidance from Pete Docter and producer Jonas Rivera, and kept the lamp at the center of the frame while cutting through time, seasons and settings. Lamp Life premiered on Disney+ on 31 January 2020. Reviewers found it charming and packed with quick gags and Pixar Easter eggs, though Laughing Place considered it a tame series of vignettes that added little to the character.

title: Sputnik
tagline: The only survivor did not come back alone
overview: At the height of the Cold War, a Soviet spacecraft crash lands after a mission gone awry, leaving the commander as its only survivor. After a renowned Russian psychologist is brought in to evaluate the commander’s mental state, it becomes clear that something dangerous may have come back to Earth with him…
plot:
Sputnik (Russian: Спутник) is a 2020 Russian science fiction horror film directed by Egor Abramenko in his feature debut. Oksana Akinshina stars as Tatyana Klimova, a young doctor recruited by the Soviet military to examine a cosmonaut who has returned from a space accident with a dangerous organism living inside him, with Pyotr Fyodorov as the cosmonaut, Konstantin Veshnyakov, and Fyodor Bondarchuk as Colonel Semiradov. It was due to premiere at the Tribeca Film Festival in April 2020, but the festival was postponed due to the COVID-19 pandemic, and the film was released on video on demand in Russia that month and internationally by IFC Midnight in August.

In 1983, two Soviet cosmonauts hear something moving outside their spacecraft, which then crashes in Kazakhstan. The sole survivor, Veshnyakov, is taken to a secret military research facility run by Semiradov, but he remembers nothing of the crash. When the facility's scientist, Yan Rigel, fails to cure his amnesia, Semiradov recruits Klimova, a controversial psychiatrist facing disciplinary action for her unorthodox methods. Klimova concludes that Veshnyakov is suffering from post-traumatic stress, but Semiradov then shows her the facility's secret: each night, an alien creature emerges from the cosmonaut's mouth while he sleeps.

The creature is symbiotically bonded to Veshnyakov, keeping him alive, and any attempt to separate them would kill both. Klimova agrees to find a way to separate them permanently, to Rigel's resentment. To study how the cosmonaut's hormones respond to stress, she provokes him with accusations about abandoning his son and causing his colleague's death, then apologizes, learning that he had only discovered he had a son shortly before his mission. Spending time with the creature at night, Klimova discovers its true nature and how it feeds, and uncovers Semiradov's real intentions: the military hopes to use the organism as a weapon, and has been feeding it prisoners. As she becomes closer to Veshnyakov, Klimova must decide how far she will go to protect him and stop the creature from being exploited, even at a terrible cost.

Sputnik received generally positive reviews, with critics praising its atmosphere, its Cold War setting, Akinshina's commanding performance and its creature design, comparing it favorably to Alien and other classic science-fiction horror films.

title: Shazam! Fury of the Gods
overview: Billy Batson and his foster siblings, who transform into superheroes by saying "Shazam!", are forced to get back into action and fight the Daughters of Atlas, who they must stop from using a weapon that could destroy the world.
plot:
Shazam! Fury of the Gods is a 2023 American superhero film based on the DC Comics character Shazam. Produced by New Line Cinema, DC Films and the Safran Company and distributed by Warner Bros. Pictures, it is the sequel to Shazam! (2019) and the twelfth instalment of the DC Extended Universe. David F. Sandberg returned as director, working from a script by Henry Gayden and Chris Morgan. Zachary Levi and Asher Angel again share the role of Billy Batson, with Jack Dylan Grazer, Adam Brody and Ross Butler among the returning foster family, Rachel Zegler as Anthea, and Helen Mirren and Lucy Liu as the villainous sisters Hespera and Kalypso.

Four years after the defeat of Thaddeus Sivana, Hespera and Kalypso, daughters of the Titan Atlas, raid a museum in Athens to steal the broken staff of the Wizard and force him to restore its power. In Philadelphia, Billy and his superpowered siblings, nicknamed the Shazamily, are drifting apart as they grow older, and the public mocks them as the Philly Fiascos after a rescue on a collapsing bridge causes considerable damage. Billy also fears that he will lose his place in the Vasquez home when he turns eighteen.

Warned in a dream by the Wizard, the family learn about the Daughters of Atlas and discover that Anne, a new girl at school whom Freddy has fallen for, is in fact Anthea, the youngest of the sisters. The goddesses intend to reclaim the magic they believe was stolen from them, and they seal Philadelphia under an enormous dome. Using a golden apple from the Tree of Life, Kalypso plans to unleash a horde of mythological monsters, including a dragon, on the human world. The siblings must overcome their differences and work together, as Billy learns that being a hero means accepting that he is truly part of a family, culminating in a sacrifice of his own.

The film blends superhero action with family comedy, keeping the lighthearted tone of the first instalment while expanding its mythology from Greek legend.

Fury of the Gods received mixed reviews, with praise for its cast and humour but criticism of its plot and villains, and it underperformed at the box office, grossing far less than its predecessor worldwide.

title: Irresistible
overview: A Democratic political consultant helps a retired Marine colonel run for mayor in a small, conservative Wisconsin town.
plot:
Irresistible is a satirical comedy film that delves into the darker aspects of American politics and society. The movie follows a Democratic campaign manager, Gary Clements, who is sent to a small town in Pennsylvania to help a local candidate win an election. However, things take a turn when he discovers that the town's residents are being manipulated by a wealthy corporate executive, Jack Morris, who is using his influence to sway the outcome of the election.

Through this narrative, the film critiques the corrupting influence of money in politics and the ways in which special interests can manipulate public opinion. The movie also explores themes of class struggle, as Gary's character represents the values of the working class, while Jack's character embodies the power and privilege of the wealthy elite.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Irresistible is not just a comedy about politics, but also a commentary on the erosion of civic engagement and the decline of community. The film highlights how politicians and corporate interests often prioritize their own interests over those of the people they claim to represent.

Ultimately, the movie presents a bleak vision of American politics, where money and power are seen as the primary drivers of decision-making, rather than the needs and values of the citizens being represented.

title: Death of Me
overview: A couple on holiday on a remote South Pacific island awaken one morning with a hang over and no recollection of what transpired. When playing back a video of the previous night, they see they participated in a local ritual that somehow ends with him murdering her.
plot:
Death of Me is an American horror film of 2020, written by Ari Margolis, James Morley III and David Tish and directed by Darren Lynn Bousman. It stars Maggie Q and Luke Hemsworth as Christine and Neil, an American couple trapped on a remote Thai island, with Alex Essoe as the hotel owner Samantha, Kat Ingkarat as the waitress Madee and Kelly B. Jones as the tattoo artist Kanda.

Christine and Neil wake in a wrecked hotel room, caked in dirt and grass, with no memory of the night before. Their passports are missing, so they miss their ferry and return to Samantha's hotel. Footage on Neil's phone shows them drinking at a bar, where Madee gave Christine a necklace, and then Neil, apparently drugged, strangling Christine and burying her. Neil insists none of it happened, but Christine finds bruises on her neck and coughs up soil. A local doctor dismisses their story, and the islanders prepare for a festival adorned with images of Christine.

Christine suffers increasingly gruesome visions, pulling a snake from her throat and seeing women whose eyes and mouths are sewn shut. Kanda tells her the necklace is a talisman with spiritual power, and Madee returns Neil's passport but not hers. While waiting for a boat, Neil falls into a trance and kills himself in front of her. The police do not believe her, and the doctor announces that she is pregnant, showing a monstrous ultrasound. Kanda finally explains that Christine was meant to be buried by her husband as a sacrifice: the islanders bury pregnant women to keep the island safe from storms, and she lingers in a spiritual limbo. Discovering that Samantha is complicit after being cured of cancer, Christine shoots her, but she is captured, and Madee begins sewing her eye shut before she breaks free and escapes by boat as a storm hits. The storm kills the islanders and Christine, but a rescuer lays the necklace beside her body, and its magic brings her back to life.

Saban Films released the film on digital and on demand on 2 October 2020; its theatrical run was limited to overseas markets because of the COVID-19 pandemic. Critics praised Maggie Q's committed performance but found it short on scares, and it scored 33% on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: The Pilgrim's Progress
overview: An epic journey, faithfully adapted to modern-day. Christian faces distractions, challenges, and perils at every turn of the way. But ends victorious, with helpful guides, as he stays on the narrow path to the distant Celestial City.
plot:
The Pilgrim's Progress is a 2019 American computer-animated Christian fantasy adventure written and directed by Robert Fernandez. It is based on John Bunyan's 1678 allegory of the same name. David Thorpe voices Christian, John Rhys-Davies voices Evangelist and Kristyn Getty voices the Interpreter. Jonathan Keeble, Justin Butcher, Chris Pavlo and Andrew Wyncott voice Faithful, Hopeful, Worldly Wiseman and the villain Apollyon.

The story begins in Not-Cursed, a city of laborers watched over by Apollyon, master of corruption. When a worker named Faithful disappears, leaving strange drawings behind, his colleague Christian learns he has set out for the Celestial City beyond the borders. After a nightmare, Christian reads a book from Faithful's office and becomes convinced the city will be destroyed. His wife dismisses the book as fiction and refuses to leave, so he sets out alone.

On the way, Evangelist urges him to keep to the path. His eager companion Pliable gives up after they fall into the Swamp of Despondency, and a man named Help pulls Christian out. The smooth-talking Worldly Wiseman leads him off course to the village of Morality, where he despairs under the Law of Moses until Evangelist rescues him. A Gatekeeper saves him from bats, and the Interpreter teaches him that those who follow the light will be protected if they persevere. On the Path of Patience, his burden falls away. Heralds of the King give him new clothes, and the daughters of Vigilant give him armor and a sword, with which he defeats Apollyon. Reunited with Faithful, he goes on to Vanity Fair, where Faithful is executed and Christian is imprisoned. A sympathetic jailer, Hopeful, helps him escape. The two are captured by a giant but realize their hope makes them unbreakable. They escape and are guided by a Shepherd. Apollyon, disguised as an old man, captures them, but a herald rescues them. At the sea before the Celestial City, Christian enters the water, Apollyon is cast into the depths, and the Shepherd welcomes him into the city. In an epilogue, his wife finds a letter showing he is alive, as Apollyon circles her home as a dragon, setting up a continuation.

Fathom Events released the film in American cinemas on April 18, 2019, around Easter, and it grossed about $3.2 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed. The Guardian criticized its stiff animation and lack of humor, while WORLD Magazine and Variety were more positive, and Radio Times called the animation basic but effective.

title: Fever Dream
overview: A woman named Amanda lies stricken, far from home. A young boy named David questions her, trying to make her remember. She's not his mother, he's not her son. As her time is running out, he helps her unravel a powerful, haunting story of obsessive jealousy, an invisible danger, and the power of a mother's love for her child.
plot:
Fever Dream (Spanish: Distancia de rescate, literally "Rescue Distance") is a 2021 psychological thriller directed by the Peruvian filmmaker Claudia Llosa from a screenplay she co-wrote with the Argentine writer Samanta Schweblin, adapting Schweblin's 2014 novel of the same name. A Netflix release of a Gran Via and Paradise Falls production in collaboration with Fábula and Wanda Films it was shot in Chile in early 2019, with cinematography by Oscar Faura and a string-led score by Natalie Holt. The cast is led by María Valverde, Dolores Fonzi, Germán Palacios, Guillermo Pfening and Emilio Vodanovich.

Amanda (Valverde) arrives at an idyllic cottage in a quiet rural town in Argentina for a summer holiday with her even-tempered young daughter Nina (Guillermina Sorribes Liotta), while her husband Marco (Pfening) stays behind, preoccupied with work. Her vibrant neighbour Carola (Fonzi) appears bearing pails of drinking water, warning her not to trust what comes out of the tap, the first hint that something is unsound about the area. The two women quickly become close friends, but the timeline splinters into Carola's past, when she lived in the house Amanda now occupies and she and her husband Omar (Palacios) planned to breed show horses until a stallion's mysterious death plunged them into debt. At the same time their young son David (Marcelo Michinaux) fell suddenly and gravely ill, and a local healer (Cristina Banegas) performed a "spiritual migration", transferring part of his spirit into another body. David survived, but Carola insists that the surly, near-feral boy he has become (Vodanovich) is no longer her son. Amanda soon suspects that something is eerily wrong and fears that part of Nina's spirit may also go missing, as the story raises the question of whether toxins sprayed on the surrounding crops are to blame. The film unfolds through a conversation between Amanda and David that is heard rather than seen.

Fever Dream premiered in competition at the San Sebastián International Film Festival on 20 September 2021, opened in select US cinemas on 6 October and was released on Netflix on 13 October 2021. It holds a 72% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 75. The Guardian called it bonkers but very beautiful, a future cult classic, while Variety's critic praised its atmosphere, photography and score but found the story sliding into near-incoherence.

title: Causeway
overview: A US soldier suffers a traumatic brain injury while fighting in Afghanistan and struggles to adjust to life back home in New Orleans. When she meets local mechanic James, the pair begin to forge an unexpected bond.
plot:
Lynsey, a soldier in the United States Army Corps of Engineers during the Afghanistan War, is recovering from a traumatic brain injury. She undergoes physical therapy with a kindly professional caretaker, Sharon, and gradually regains her motor skills. Unable to afford further treatment, she is forced to return home to New Orleans.
Staying in her childhood home with her unreliable mother Gloria, Lynsey finds a job cleaning pools. When the truck once belonging to her brother breaks down, she finds help from James, an auto mechanic. Struggling to adjust to daily life and her new medications, she explains to her doctor that she was injured by an IED in Afghanistan, but is determined to return to duty.
Lynsey and James become unlikely friends, and after he helps her avoid unwanted advances at a bar, she reveals that she is a lesbian. He confides in her about losing his leg in a car crash on the Lake Pontchartrain Causeway, and she opens up about her unhappy memories of home, including her brother Justin's problems with drugs. James drunkenly invites her to move in with him, in the house he used to share with his sister and her son.
Despite her mother's objections, Lynsey commits herself to qualifying for redeployment, and finds herself swimming in an out-of-town client's pool. She continues to spend time with James, bonding over sno-balls and their shared physical and mental trauma. Her doctor fears the impact of her injury on her mental health, warning of the strong link between trauma and her depression.
When Lynsey convinces James to join her in the pool, he reveals that he was driving when the car crashed; his nephew was killed, leaving him estranged from his sister. Comforting James, Lynsey impulsively kisses him. Embarrassed, she declares that she was acting out of pity, leading to an argument about the things they have kept from each other, and James ends their friendship.
Lynsey's doctor reluctantly agrees to sign her redeployment waiver. She is unable to reach James, but discovers he had the truck repaired for free, and is inspired to reconnect with Justin, visiting him in prison. Changing her mind about leaving, she is able to bring herself to clean her mother's own disused pool, and to swim at a public pool. She visits James and urges him to ask her to move in again, hoping to make amends with her friend.

title: SAS: Red Notice
overview: An off-duty SAS soldier, Tom Buckingham, must thwart a terror attack on a train running through the Channel Tunnel. As the action escalates on the train, events transpire in the corridors of power that may make the difference as to whether Buckingham and the civilian passengers make it out of the tunnel alive.
plot:
SAS: Red Notice is a 2021 action-thriller film directed by Rawson Marshall Thurber and starring Dwayne Johnson, Ryan Reynolds, and Gal Gadot. The movie follows the story of an FBI agent, John Hartley (Johnson), who teams up with an art thief, Nolan Booth (Reynolds), to catch a notorious art forger, Elizabeth "The Cat" Lind (Gadot).

The film begins with Nolan Booth, a charming and skilled art thief, being pursued by the FBI. He is eventually caught and sentenced to prison, but manages to escape after serving only a few months. Meanwhile, John Hartley, an FBI agent specializing in art crimes, is tasked with catching Booth.

Hartley and Booth cross paths when they both receive a message from Elizabeth Lind, who has stolen a priceless artifact called the "Red Notice." The Red Notice is a valuable painting that holds significant historical and cultural value. Both Hartley and Booth are determined to catch Lind and claim the reward money for themselves.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Lind is not just any ordinary art thief. She is highly intelligent, resourceful, and has a personal vendetta against both Hartley and Booth. The three engage in a cat-and-mouse game, with each trying to outsmart the other.

Throughout the film, the characters' backstories are revealed through flashbacks. We learn that Lind was once a talented artist who became disillusioned with the art world's superficiality. She turned to theft as a way to expose the hypocrisy and corruption within the art community.

As the stakes rise, Hartley and Booth begin to form an unlikely alliance. They realize that they have more in common than they initially thought, and that their skills complement each other perfectly. Together, they devise a plan to catch Lind and retrieve the Red Notice.

The film's climax features an intense action sequence as Hartley, Booth, and Lind engage in a high-stakes game of cat and mouse. The three characters use their wits, charm, and cunning to outmaneuver each other, leading to a thrilling conclusion.

In the end, Hartley and Booth succeed in catching Lind, but not before she reveals that she has been playing them all along. She had planned her escape from prison and was using both men to get to the Red Notice. The film ends with Hartley and Booth walking away from each other, having formed an unlikely friendship.

Overall, SAS: Red Notice is a fast-paced, action-packed thriller that explores themes of loyalty, trust, and redemption. The film features impressive performances from its lead actors, and the chemistry between Johnson, Reynolds, and Gadot is undeniable.

title: On a Magical Night
overview: After 20 years of marriage, Maria decides to leave her husband. She moves into room 212 at the hotel across the street, with a bird’s-eye view of her apartment, her husband and the life she shared with him. While she wonders if she made the right decision, many of the people in her life offer their opinions on the matter. They intend to let her know, whether she likes it or not, on what proves to be a life-changing evening.
plot:
On a Magical Night (French: Chambre 212, literally "Room 212") is a 2019 French fantasy comedy-drama written and directed by Christophe Honoré, starring Chiara Mastroianni, Vincent Lacoste, Camille Cottin and Benjamin Biolay, with Carole Bouquet. Developed under the working title Musique de chambre, the screenplay was written by Honoré for Mastroianni, whom he imagined as "a Cary Grant-type character". It was his first film shot in a studio. The title refers to Article 212 of the French Civil Code, which states that spouses owe each other respect, fidelity, help and assistance.

Maria Mortemart (Mastroianni), a university lecturer in the history of law, has been married to Richard Warrimer (Biolay) for twenty years. When Richard stumbles on messages on her phone revealing her affair with one of her students, Asdrubal the couple quarrel, and Maria walks out of their Paris apartment to spend the night in Room 212 of the hotel across the street. She gives herself the night to think. Over its course she is visited by figures from her own past and Richard's: Richard himself at twenty (Lacoste), as he was when she decided to marry him; her mother, who kept a precise tally of her lovers; and Irène Haffner (Cottin), Richard's piano teacher and first love, who agreed to step aside so that he could marry Maria. Irène wonders whether she was wrong, whether Richard would have been happier with her and whether she would have given him the children Maria never wanted, and she crosses the street to try to convince him, in vain. Meanwhile Maria is confronted by her "will", embodied by a man vaguely resembling Charles Aznavour, and by a crowd of her former lovers. Maria and Irène then journey to the Bay of the Somme, where Irène settled after Richard's wedding, and meet her serene, regret-free sixty-year-old self (Bouquet). In the morning Maria and Richard meet in the street; she must go and teach, but promises to come home that evening.

The film premiered in the Un Certain Regard section of the 2019 Cannes Film Festival, where Mastroianni won the award for Best Performance. Released in France on 9 October 2019 and by Strand Releasing in US virtual cinemas in May 2020, it grossed about 3 million dollars. Reviews were mixed: The Hollywood Reporter's Stephen Dalton found it breezy and bright, with the stylised feel of a stage play, while Variety's Owen Gleiberman felt it dragged and had holes in its fantasy logic.

title: Cold Blood
overview: A legendary but retired hit man lives in peace and isolation in the barren North American wilderness. When he rescues a woman from a snowmobiling accident, he soon discovers that she's harboring a secret that forces him to return to his lethal ways.
plot:
Cold Blood, also released as Cold Blood Legacy, is a 2019 English-language action thriller written and directed by the French filmmaker Frédéric Petitjean. Jean Reno stars as a retired contract killer living in seclusion, with Sarah Lind as the young woman who enters his life, and Joe Anderson, David Gyasi, Ihor Ciszkewycz and Samantha Bond in supporting roles. Set in a snowbound wilderness, the film was released on 15 May 2019.

Henry, a professional assassin, has withdrawn to a remote cabin in the snowbound forests near the Canadian border, where he lives in silence and solitude, fishing on the frozen lake. One day he comes across a crashed snowmobile and a badly injured young woman, who tells him her name is Melody. He drives off a pack of wolves that close in on her, carries her back to the cabin and treats her injuries with what little he has, pulling out splinters and shards of wood embedded in her body.

As she recovers, Henry grows wary. She has no identification and no phone, and the circumstances of the crash do not add up, so he examines the scene and tells her she must leave as soon as she can. One day, seeing him sitting outside with his back to her, apparently fishing, she assembles a pistol hidden in her pack and shoots him in the head, only to discover that she has hit a straw dummy. Henry overpowers and questions her.

She admits that her real name is Charlie and that she came to kill him in revenge for his murder of her father, a wealthy man who largely ignored her but whose memory she still wanted to honour. title: Pacto de Fuga
tagline: Based on the most daring prison escape of all time.
overview: During the last years of Pinochet's military regime,  a group of militants from the "Manuel Rodríguez Patriotic Front" plan a prison break of political prisoners, through a tunnel that will take them 18 months to dig.
plot:
Jailbreak Pact, released in Chile as Pacto de fuga, is a 2020 Chilean prison drama and thriller directed by David Albala in his feature debut, from a screenplay he co-wrote with Cecilia Ruz, Loreto Caro-Valdés and Susana Quiroz-Saavedra. It stars Benjamín Vicuña as León Vargas and Roberto Farías as Rafael Jiménez, with Francisca Gavilán, Amparo Noguera, Víctor Montero, Diego Ruiz, Mateo Iribarren and Willy Semler. The film is inspired by "Operation Success", the escape of 49 inmates from the Santiago Public Jail on January 30, 1990, among them members of the Manuel Rodríguez Patriotic Front (FPMR) serving sentences for armed actions against the military dictatorship.

In the final years of Augusto Pinochet's regime, new political prisoners arrive at the Santiago jail. Vargas and Jiménez try to secure neighboring cells so they can communicate, but Vargas arrives late to the assignment, creating friction over the plans they brought with them. Meanwhile the ad hoc prosecutor Andrade and the warden receive Fabiola Pizarro, a defense lawyer from the group CODEPU who has come to check on the prisoners' conditions. The conspirators calculate that a tunnel would require removing some 50 tons of earth, so they open a hole in a cell ceiling to hide the soil, cover it with a fake section of wall painted to match, and devise secret signals to coordinate the work while evading guards and ordinary prisoners. Outside, Jiménez's former wife, Paulina Baeza, organizes logistical support from FPMR and Communist Party contacts for the day of the escape.

Over more than a year, 24 prisoners dig a tunnel over 80 meters long, using little more than a screwdriver, and hide 55 tons of earth inside the prison, while family visits expose the strain between revolutionary commitment and broken relationships, and the military justice system and the regime's security agencies wield power over the prison. Undetected to the end, the plan frees 49 inmates in one of the most astonishing jailbreaks in Chilean history.

Shot in former prisons in La Serena and Buin, the film was advised by Raúl Blanchet, one of the real escapees, who died during post-production. Its October 2019 release was postponed by Chile's social unrest, and it opened on January 23, 2020. It was shortlisted for Chile's Academy Award submission. The Guardian praised the lead performances but found the dialogue forced, while still calling it an entertaining debut.

At the audition, Merab dances in his unorthodox style, impressing choreographer Aleko but offending the director, who storms out. Undeterred, Merab finishes his routine and bows before leaving.

title: Nightmare Alley
overview: An ambitious carnival man with a talent for manipulating people with a few well-chosen words hooks up with a female psychologist who is even more dangerous than he is.
plot:
Nightmare Alley is a 2021 neo-noir psychological thriller co-written and directed by Guillermo del Toro, based on William Lindsay Gresham's 1946 novel, which had previously been filmed in 1947. It stars Bradley Cooper as Stanton Carlisle, an ambitious drifter, with Cate Blanchett, Toni Collette, Willem Dafoe, Richard Jenkins, Rooney Mara, Ron Perlman, Mary Steenburgen and David Strathairn. Del Toro produced the film with J. Miles Dale and Cooper, with cinematography by Dan Laustsen and music by Nathan Johnson.

In 1939, Stan Carlisle hides the body of his father under the floor of a run-down house and burns it down before joining a traveling carnival. There he learns how the carnival's geek, a degraded man who eats live chickens in a sideshow pit, is recruited and controlled through alcohol and opium. Stan begins working with the clairvoyant Madame Zeena and her alcoholic husband Pete, who teach him the coded language and cold reading techniques of their mentalist act, warning him never to claim to speak with the dead. After Pete dies, Stan leaves the carnival with Molly, a young performer.

Two years later, Stan and Molly run a successful mentalist act for the wealthy elite of Buffalo, though their relationship is deteriorating. During a performance, a psychiatrist, Dr. Lilith Ritter, tries to expose Stan, but he outwits her. The two form a dangerous alliance: Ritter secretly gives Stan confidential information about her wealthy patients, which he uses to convince them that he can communicate with their dead loved ones. Ignoring Molly's objections and Zeena's warnings, Stan sets his sights on Ezra Grindle, a powerful and ruthless industrialist, and his ambition draws him into a con that spirals out of his control.

The film is a dark study of ambition, deception and self-destruction, with its ending echoing the carnival world where Stan's story began.

Production in Toronto was interrupted by the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020. Released by Searchlight Pictures on December 17, 2021, the film grossed 39.6 million dollars against a 60 million dollar budget. It received generally positive reviews, with 80 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 70, and earned four Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture.

title: The Half of It
tagline: A different kind of love story.
overview: Shy, straight-A student Ellie is hired by sweet but inarticulate jock Paul, who needs help wooing the most popular girl in school. But their new and unlikely friendship gets tricky when Ellie discovers she has feelings for the same girl.
plot:
Ellie Chu lives in the remote town of Squahamish with her grieving widower father, where she performs most of his station master and signalman duties. She makes extra money by ghostwriting essays for her classmates. The socially ostracized Ellie is secretly interested in Aster Flores, the beautiful daughter of the minister who is reluctantly dating Trig, a narcissistic popular boy from a wealthy family.
Ellie's next-door neighbor Paul Munsky, an inarticulate football team member and part of a family sausage business, asks Ellie to help him by ghostwriting a love letter from him to Aster. Ellie eventually agrees to help in order to help pay her family's bills. Posing as Paul, Ellie begins a heartfelt correspondence with Aster about their shared interests in art and literature through letters and text messages.
Ellie's supportive English teacher encourages her to apply to Grinnell College after noticing the proficiency of the essays she ghostwrote, but Ellie plans to attend Eastern Washington University and stay in Squahamish to be near her father.
Ellie sets up Paul on a date with Aster, but it goes poorly due to his obtuseness and poor conversational skills. Ellie plans to stop helping Paul, but reconsiders when he defends her from bullies. Ellie begins teaching Paul about art and literature so he can convincingly portray the persona she has created for him with Aster.
Ellie watches from outside the restaurant as Paul's second date with Aster starts off as badly as the first. In a desperate bid to save it, Ellie sends Aster text messages via a user account she and Paul secretly share, while Paul plays along by pretending to type on his phone. The next day, Paul tells Ellie that he kissed Aster - without encouragement from her, and despite their telling Aster that Paul wanted to keep their relationship platonic - unnerving Ellie.
Paul thwarts bullies' attempts to sabotage Ellie's school talent show performance, and she earns a standing ovation. Later, Paul is moved by the discovery that Ellie is secretly writing to regional food critics, attempting to gain recognition for Paul's culinary innovation, the "taco sausage".
Aster takes Ellie to a secluded hot spring where they share an intimate conversation. Ellie discusses her atheism, while Aster reveals that Trig intends to marry her. After Aster takes Ellie back home, Aster comes across Paul, and questions him, verifying that he believes in God, in contrast to Ellie and some of the things she has said during their correspondence. From her bedroom window Ellie watches Aster pull Paul in for a kiss, after which she decides to send the application to Grinnell.
At a school football game, Aster cheers for Paul, but Paul is more thrilled by Ellie's cheers and with her motivation scores the team's first touchdown in fifteen years. Afterwards, mistakenly perceiving them to have developed feelings for each other, Paul attempts to kiss Ellie, but she rejects his advance.

title: My Little Pony: A New Generation
original_title: My Little Pony: A New Generation
overview: Equestria's divided. But a bright-eyed hero believes Earth Ponies, Pegasi and Unicorns should be pals — and, hoof to heart, she’s determined to prove it.
plot:
My Little Pony: A New Generation is a 2021 computer-animated adventure comedy based on Hasbro's My Little Pony toy line, directed by Robert Cullen and José Luis Ucha from a screenplay by Tim Sullivan and Gillian Berrow. Produced by Entertainment One and Boulder Media, it serves as a follow-up to the television series My Little Pony: Friendship Is Magic. The voice cast includes Vanessa Hudgens as Sunny Starscout, Kimiko Glenn as Izzy Moonbow, James Marsden as Hitch Trailblazer, Sofia Carson as Pipp Petals, Liza Koshy as Zipp Storm, Ken Jeong as Sprout, Elizabeth Perkins as Phyllis Cloverleaf, Jane Krakowski as Queen Haven, Phil LaMarr as Alphabittle and Michael McKean as Sunny's father Argyle.

Long after the age of Twilight Sparkle and her friends, the three pony races of Equestria have drifted apart and live in mutual fear. In the earth pony town of Maretime Bay, young Sunny Starscout grows up hearing her father's tales of a time when earth ponies, pegasi and unicorns lived in harmony. As an adult, she still believes the old stories, to the dismay of her neighbors and her childhood friend Hitch, now the town's sheriff.

When a cheerful unicorn named Izzy Moonbow wanders into Maretime Bay, the townsfolk panic, but Sunny befriends her and learns that the unicorns have lost their magic. Suspecting the pegasi, the two set off for the pegasus city of Zephyr Heights, pursued by Hitch, while his deputy Sprout seizes control of the town and stirs it into a frenzy. In Zephyr Heights they discover that the royal family led by Queen Haven has been faking flight, because the pegasi have lost their magic too. With the help of princesses Pipp and Zipp, Sunny learns that a set of ancient crystals may hold the key to restoring magic and setting off on a quest to bring the pony races back together.

The film carries the franchise's themes of friendship and unity into a new generation, using its story of distrust between species as an allegory for prejudice.

Originally planned as a theatrical release by Paramount Pictures, the film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 8, 2021, and was released on Netflix on September 24 because of the COVID-19 pandemic. It received generally positive reviews, holding 92 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and was followed by the series Tell Your Tale and Make Your Mark.

title: Away
overview: After suffering a plane crash on a mysterious island, a young man embarks on an epic journey through forests, deserts and mountains trying to escape the shadow of a huge dark spirit.
plot:
Away (Latvian: Projām) is a 2019 Latvian animated fantasy adventure film written, directed, animated and scored by Gints Zilbalodis in his feature debut. Made almost entirely by Zilbalodis alone over three and a half years using the 3D software Maya, it contains no dialogue. The film premiered at the Annecy International Animation Film Festival in 2019, where it won the Contrechamp award for best feature in its competition section.

A teenage boy awakens in a desert, hanging from a parachute caught in the branches of a tree, as a giant, silent black figure approaches from the dust. The creature tries to swallow him, but he frees himself and flees, discovering that the monster is translucent and slow. Following a path to a stone archway, he finds an oasis of trees and water by the sea, where he rests and meets a small yellow bird that cannot yet fly. He also finds a motorcycle and a backpack containing survival supplies and a map of the island, showing a port town on the far side where he might find help.

With the monster waiting near the oasis, the boy spends the night among the trees. The next day the bird tries to follow a flock of white birds and is swallowed by the monster, but the boy runs through the creature and rescues it. Stocking up on fruit and water, he rides away on the motorcycle with the little bird, following a series of stone arches across the desert and into grasslands, while the monster slowly follows, consuming every living thing in its path. Told in chapters, the journey takes the pair through changing landscapes, including a mountain of balancing rocks and a mirror-like lake, as the boy grows stronger, the bird learns to fly, and the boy confronts his fear of the shadow pursuing him in the hope of reaching safety.

Away received widespread acclaim, holding a 100 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on 31 reviews, with a consensus calling it a haunting and refreshing odyssey, and a Metacritic score of 78. Critics praised its dreamlike visuals and score. Zilbalodis later directed Flow (2024), which won the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature.

title: Beckett
overview: An American tourist in Greece finds himself on the run after a tragic accident plunges him into a political conspiracy that makes him a target for assassination.
plot:
Beckett is a 2021 action thriller directed by Ferdinando Cito Filomarino and produced by Luca Guadagnino. John David Washington stars as an American tourist in Greece who becomes the target of a manhunt after an accident draws him into a political conspiracy, with Boyd Holbrook, Vicky Krieps and Alicia Vikander in supporting roles. Originally titled Born to Be Murdered, it was shot in Athens in 2019, premiered at the 74th Locarno Film Festival on August 4, 2021, and was released by Netflix on August 13.

Beckett and his girlfriend April leave Athens to avoid political unrest. Driving through the mountains of Epirus at night, Beckett falls asleep at the wheel and crashes into a house. April is killed, and as he lies trapped in the wreck Beckett glimpses a blonde woman hurrying a boy out of the building. The local policeman Xenakis tells him the house was abandoned, and when the grieving Beckett returns to it, the woman opens fire on him, and Xenakis joins in the shooting. Wounded, Beckett escapes by leaping from a cliff.

Pursued across the countryside, Beckett is sheltered briefly by hunters, borrows a phone from beekeepers to call the US embassy, and fights off Xenakis on a train. He then sees activists Lena and Eleni putting up posters of the missing boy, Dimos Karras, the kidnapped nephew of a left-wing politician, whose abduction has been blamed on the far right. They drive him to Athens, and after surviving a knife attack on the metro he reaches the embassy. The staffer Tynan seems helpful but tries to subdue him with a taser, and later corners him during a chaotic rally where Karras is assassinated. Tynan explains that the politician owed money to a criminal syndicate that kidnapped the boy and pinned the blame on his rivals, hinting at American complicity.

Distrusting Tynan, Beckett knocks him out, takes his gun and spots the blonde woman, whom he follows to a parking garage where she meets Xenakis with Dimos locked in his car. Though shot, Beckett overpowers both and rescues the boy. In the final scene he looks at the heart April drew on his hand before the crash.

Critics were divided; Rotten Tomatoes reported 49% approval, with its consensus praising the propulsive man-on-the-run story but finding the thriller thinly written.

title: Critters Attack!
overview: Follows 20-year-old Drea, who reluctantly takes a job babysitting for a professor of a college she hopes to attend. Struggling to entertain the professor's children Trissy and Jake, along with her own little brother Phillip , Drea takes them on a hike, unaware that mysterious alien critters have crash-landed and started devouring every living thing they encounter.
plot:
Critters Attack! is a 2019 American science fiction horror comedy directed by Bobby Miller, the fifth installment of the Critters franchise and a reboot of the 1986 original. Produced for Syfy by New Line Cinema, Warner Bros. Television and Blue Ribbon Content, it stars Tashiana Washington as Drea and Dee Wallace as Aunt Dee, with Jaeden Noel, Jack Fulton, Ava Preston, Stephen Jennings, Leon Clingman, Vash Singh and Ho Chow, while Steve Blum provides the voices of the Critters.

Drea, a twenty-year-old who delivers sushi, dreams of attending the college her late mother went to, but has been rejected for a second time. When she is offered a job babysitting the children of one of the college's professors, she reluctantly accepts in the hope of gaining an advantage. Struggling to entertain Trissy (Preston) and Jake (Fulton), along with her own younger brother Phillip (Noel), she takes them on a hike, unaware that the alien Crites have crash-landed in the nearby forest and begun devouring every living thing they meet, multiplying through the bodies of their victims. The group discovers Bianca, a white female Crite fleeing from her male counterparts and their one-eyed leader, who becomes their ally against the swarm. As the creatures wreak havoc on the town, the children receive help from the mysterious Aunt Dee, armed with futuristic weapons and apparently familiar with the hungry intergalactic beasts, and from Drea's boss, the sushi chef Loong, who knows about them. The final act becomes a full-scale battle in which the Crites are blasted and sliced apart.

Syfy acquired the rights to the franchise in 2018, and the film was shot secretly in South Africa in February 2019 before being announced that spring. Wallace confirmed she was reprising her original role of Helen Brown, renamed Aunt Dee for legal reasons. The film screened at the Fantasia festival and was released on DVD and digital by Warner Bros. Home Entertainment on 23 July 2019, in R-rated and unrated versions because of its increased gore. Reviews were mixed (41% on Rotten Tomatoes): /Film rated it six out of ten, enjoying the goofy puppet gags and female-led story, while Bloody Disgusting criticized its bland characters, poor pacing and lack of campy fun.

title: Kate
overview: A ruthless criminal operative has less than 24 hours to exact revenge on her enemies and in the process forms an unexpected bond with the daughter of one of her past victims.
plot:
Kate is a 2021 American action thriller directed by Cedric Nicolas-Troyan and written by Umair Aleem. Mary Elizabeth Winstead stars as an elite assassin, with Miku Martineau, Woody Harrelson, Tadanobu Asano, Michiel Huisman, Miyavi and Jun Kunimura in supporting roles. Netflix released the film on September 10, 2021.

Kate is an expert sniper who carries out killings chosen by Varrick, the mentor and handler who raised her after she was orphaned and trained her in weapons and combat. In Osaka she is assigned to shoot an official of a powerful yakuza syndicate, but hesitates when she sees he is accompanied by a young girl. At Varrick's insistence she takes the shot, breaking her personal rule against killing in front of children, and afterwards announces that she will carry out one last job before retiring.

Before that final mission, Kate spends a night with a charming stranger named Stephen. The next day, while waiting in position, she becomes dizzy and misses her shot. She soon learns in a hospital that she has been poisoned with a radioactive isotope and has no more than a day to live. Fueled by stolen stimulants, she sets out to find who did this to her. Stephen leads her to Sato, a yakuza enforcer tied to the Kijima crime family, whom she kills along with his men. To get to the reclusive boss Kijima, Kate abducts his teenage niece Ani, only to realize that she is the girl who watched her father die in Osaka. When Kate learns that Ani's own family wants her dead as part of an internal power struggle, she becomes her protector.

The trail reveals that Kijima's advisor Renji made a deal with Varrick to absorb Varrick's team into the syndicate in exchange for wiping out Kijima and his bloodline. Ani, learning of Kate's role in her father's death, turns on her, but Kate allies with Kijima in a bloody assault on Renji's headquarters. Kijima kills Renji, and Kate faces Varrick in a final showdown in which she shoots him. With her strength fading, Kate shares a final moment with Ani before succumbing to the poison.

Reviews were mixed. Critics widely praised Winstead's committed performance and the bloody fight choreography, but many found the film derivative of other female assassin thrillers and works such as D.O.A. and John Wick, and The New York Times criticized its shallow portrayal of Japanese culture.

title: The Greatest Beer Run Ever
overview: Chickie wants to support his friends fighting in Vietnam, so he does something wild—personally bring them American beer. What starts as a well-meaning journey quickly changes Chickie’s life and perspective. Based on a true story.
plot:
In 1967, Marine Corps veteran John "Chickie" Donohue is a slacking merchant seaman who lives with his family in Inwood, New York City. His sister Christine is strongly opposed to the Vietnam War. Chickie and his friends attend the funeral of an old friend that has been killed in action, and are informed that another close friend, Tommy, has gone missing in action. Chickie and Red discuss lifting the spirits of their friends serving overseas and Chickie decides to deliver beers to them in South Vietnam.
Chickie sails to Saigon with a duffle bag full of Pabst Blue Ribbon cans. Military police officer Tommy Collins urges Chickie to stay out of danger and go home, but helps map out a plan for reaching Chickie's other friends. He travels to LZ Jane via Bien Hoa Air Base and Da Nang Air Base searching for Rick Duggan, serving in the 1st Cavalry Division. Duggan's sergeant summons him by radio, and he's exposed to enemy fire returning to the command post. Duggan allows Chickie to join his squad on the battlefield as they fire at the Viet Cong from trenches. Chickie passes beers out that night, and Duggan informs Chickie that one of their friends, Reynolds, was killed.
Travelling alone to Kontum Airfield by helicopter, Chickie watches two CIA agents interrogate a prisoner before throwing him to his death, and the agents pursue him as he requests a ride to Saigon. He runs into the jungle to elude them, and after he emerges that night is reunited with Kevin "Looney" McLoone who arranges a flight to Pleiku. Chickie throws him his beer as the helicopter ascends.
In Saigon, Chickie learns his ship has sailed for the Philippines due to warnings of an impending attack. Hieu directs him to the U.S. Embassy where a woman arranges a flight to Manila in the Philippines to rejoin the ship. He returns to the Caravelle Hotel and shows anti-war journalists photos as proof that he went to LZ Jane. When the Viet Cong invades Saigon in the surprise Tet Offensive, Chickie and photographer Arthur Coates explore the streets, where Chickie sees Hieu killed in the Viet Cong attack on US Embassy, as well as a US military vehicle blowing a hole in the perimeter wall from the outside. Coates photographs the aftermath of the embassy attack. The two drive to the scene of an explosion at Long Binh Post, where Coates explains that the military would rather fake an entry hole in the embassy wall than admit that the attack was an inside job. Chickie shares a beer with one last wounded friend, Bobby Pappas, who confirms Tommy Minogue's death.
Epilogue: Chickie returns home with a changed perspective on the war. He sits in a park among tributes for soldiers and shares his last beer with Christine. Collins, Duggan, McLoone, and Pappas returned from the war alive, and they all, "mostly," quit drinking.

title: The F**k-It List
overview: After a prank blows up a studious high school senior's life, he shares a list of certain things he wishes he'd done differently — and maybe still can.
plot:
Brett Blackmore's pushy parents are excitedly celebrating his acceptance into seven out of eight Ivy League schools (including bragging to their friends, his high school, the local paper) with Harvard being the only one he is wait-listed for. When he joins his friends Nico, Clint, Les and Stacy in playing a benign senior prank, they accidentally cause a school building to blow up. He is the only one identified on the security cameras and, as a result, he loses his college acceptances.
After sharing a brief kiss with Kayla (interrupted by the brash Ted), Brett records a video ranting about being forced down a path he did not choose, including a "fuck-it list" of things he wishes he had done, had he not been scared it would affect his future. His parents scheme to get him accepted by Harvard, including making advances to their friend Barry who is a board member there.
Kayla appreciates Brett's list and says that she needs his help to start checking items off of the one she has made as a result. This involves smashing the expensive Mustang belonging to her mother's alcoholic and abusive partner, which she says she never had the guts to do before Brett's post. The mother's partner spots them and they drive off and spend the day together. They discuss their mutual lists and Brett performs "Wild Thing" in public on Venice Beach. Kayla is signed to Ted's father's modeling agency, where she will be working in Europe over the summer to afford school, but the arrangement also means she has to entertain the annoying Ted.
Kayla reveals she has nowhere to go after smashing the car, but Brett is reluctant to help her. She storms off but later posts a good-luck message to him. In the meantime, his list continues to gain traction online, which adversely affects his meeting with the principal, resulting in his ineligibility to graduate high school.
Brett's parents berate him so he drives off in his father's car to the Rocks to meet his friends. They spread the word and a large number of other teens turn up to burn their school books together. The fire attracts attention for the list and he is called by a PR representative who wants to help him monetize it. The police turn up to reveal he could be considered to be inciting crime.
The dean of Harvard calls Brett through Barry to offer him a place as an iconoclast and disruptor. Meanwhile, Kayla finally agrees to see him and they make up. Brett has to write an essay to gain entry to Harvard, but he seems uninspired by it. He drops in on his friends' graduation to learn that Kayla's mother's boyfriend pressed charges for smashing up his car.
Upon learning from Les that the homeless Dee was previously a valedictorian, he turns his Harvard essay into a new rant about the education system and success, rejecting them.

title: Rumble
overview: In a world where monster wrestling is a global sport and monsters are superstar athletes, teenage Winnie seeks to follow in her father’s footsteps by coaching a loveable underdog monster into a champion.
plot:
Rumble is a 2021 American animated sports comedy film directed by Hamish Grieve, in his directorial debut, and written by Grieve and Matt Lieberman. Loosely based on Rob Harrell's 2013 graphic novel Monster on the Hill, it features the voices of Will Arnett, Geraldine Viswanathan and Terry Crews, alongside Becky Lynch, Roman Reigns, Ben Schwartz, Jimmy Tatro and Stephen A. Smith.

Monster wrestling is a global sport, and every town has its own giant monster champion. When Tentacular, the shark-like octopus who wrestles for the town of Stoker, wins the world title by beating King Gorge, he announces that he will now represent the town of Slitherpoole. Without a new wrestler, Stoker will lose its stadium and the income it brings. Wrestling enthusiast Winnie Coyle sets out to find one and discovers Rayburn Jr., son of the late world champion Rayburn Sr., fighting in an underground arena as "Steve the Stupendous". Her interference makes him win a bout he was meant to throw, angering the arena's boss, Lady Mayhem, who demands that he repay her losses. Winnie offers to train him for official matches so he can earn the money, and he reluctantly agrees.

Rayburn Jr. has little interest in learning to fight and wins his first bout simply by dodging. He admits that he left Stoker because he could not live up to his father's name. Discovering his love of salsa dancing, Winnie builds his training around dance moves, and he climbs the rankings. Tentacular and his agent then buy Stoker's stadium, planning to demolish it because it reminds Tentacular that he will always be compared with Rayburn Sr. Although Rayburn Jr. has paid off Lady Mayhem, he stays to help Winnie, reveals his identity and challenges Tentacular for the stadium. After being countered in the early rounds, he finds success with his dance moves, and following Winnie's advice he sticks Tentacular to a corner post with his own suckers. Both monsters are knocked out in a collision, but the crowd revives Rayburn Jr. by clapping a salsa rhythm, and he defeats Tentacular to become world champion and save the stadium.

Developed by Reel FX with Paramount Animation and Walden Media, the film was repeatedly delayed, partly by the COVID-19 pandemic, before premiering on December 15, 2021, as a Paramount+ exclusive. Reviews were mixed, with 47% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 48.

title: Land
tagline: A story of humanity, in the face of uncertainty
overview: Edee, in the aftermath of an unfathomable event, finds herself unable to stay connected to the world she once knew and in the face of that uncertainty, retreats to the magnificent, but unforgiving, wilds of the Rockies. After a local hunter brings her back from the brink of death, she must find a way to live again.
plot:
Land is a 2021 psychological drama directed by Robin Wright in her feature directorial debut, from a screenplay by Jesse Chatham and Erin Dignam. Wright also stars, alongside Demián Bichir and Kim Dickens. Jessica Lange had been set for the lead before dropping out over scheduling conflicts. The film was shot over 29 days in October 2019 in the Rockies west of Calgary, Alberta, where rapid weather changes let the crew capture the four seasons of the story's two years in one month, with town scenes filmed in Didsbury.

After a traumatic experience that leaves her wanting to avoid people, Edee Holzer leaves the city for a small, remote cabin in Wyoming, determined to live alone with no phone, car or other link to the outside world. She struggles to chop wood and catch fish, and when a black bear wrecks her cabin and devours her supplies, she reaches a breaking point. Unable to shoot a deer, she nearly turns the rifle on herself, stopping only when she remembers her sister Emma begging her not to. Hurt during a blizzard, she is found and nursed back to health by Miguel, a local hunter, and his nurse friend Alawa.

Respecting Edee's wish for solitude, Miguel teaches her to trap, hunt and grow food so that she can survive on her own, and a quiet friendship develops. He tells her that his wife and daughter died in a car accident eight years earlier, while she admits only that she once had a family. When Miguel goes away and leaves his dog in her care, Edee looks at old photographs of her husband and son. After months without him, she walks into town for the first time and, with Alawa's help, finds Miguel bedridden and dying of cancer. He confesses that he was driving drunk the night his family died, and Edee tells him that her husband Adam and son Drew were killed in a random shooting at a concert hall. Thanking him for giving her life back, she leaves with the phone he gave her and calls Emma for the first time since coming to Wyoming.

Land premiered at the Sundance Film Festival on January 31, 2021, and was released by Focus Features on February 12, 2021, grossing $3.1 million worldwide. Critics were generally positive, with 69% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 61, though some felt its beautiful landscapes could not hide a hollow center.

title: The Ex
overview: The story of how social networks and instant messengers are changing the life of a modern person. It has been several years since a 16-year-old teenager posted a photo of his girlfriend in the general chat, hoping to boast to friends. plot:
The Ex (Russian: Byvshaya) is a 2021 Russian supernatural horror thriller directed by Evgeny Puzyrevsky, his feature-length directorial debut, from a screenplay credited to Veronika Voznyak, Pyotr Tochilin and Vladimir Batrameev. Produced by KARO-Production with Force Media, it was released in Russian cinemas on 11 March 2021 under the English tagline "She'll Never Forgive". The film is framed as a cautionary tale about how social networks and messaging apps shape modern life, and how a careless online act from adolescence can return years later.

The story opens with Sasha, a sixteen-year-old who wants to impress his friends and posts a doctored picture of himself with an attractive girl in a group chat. Seven years later he is a successful young man living in Moscow and preparing to marry his beloved fiancée Katya. Their contentment is disturbed when Sasha receives a message from the same girl asking to meet him, while Katya begins to suffer terrifying visions of a female ghost. Katya learns that the girl, Masha, with whom Sasha had once corresponded online, recently killed her own former fiancé in a bloody attack and then took her own life. Believing that a church wedding will protect them, the couple marry quickly, but the ceremony fails to stop the spirit, which goes on killing anyone who gets in its way. Guided by a priest fighting to save Sasha's life, Katya must arrange a funeral service for Masha, whose body has still not been buried and whose soul has been seized by a demonic force.

Konstantin Beloshapka plays Sasha and Vera Kincheva plays Katya, with Zhanna Danilova as Masha, Elena Morozova as Masha's mother, Sergey Dvoynikov and Yekaterina Shumakova as the couple's friends Oleg and Zhenya, and Vladimir Seleznyov as the priest, Father Aleksei.

Made on a reported budget of about 50 million rubles, the film earned roughly 290,000 US dollars in Russia. Reviewing it for Kinoafisha, Asya Zabolotskaya called it a stereotypical horror film in a Russian setting that borrows the style of American B-movies. She felt the horror atmosphere worked reasonably well and that the cast approached the material with real affection, and she noted the sepia-tinted look of locations such as an empty hospital. However, she found the suspense built on familiar devices like jarring music, sudden blackouts and slow camera moves, criticised the uneven, television-style dramaturgy, and suggested the plot would be forgotten soon after viewing.

title: Z-O-M-B-I-E-S 2
tagline: There's a new pack in town
overview: Zed and Addison are back at Seabrook High, where, after a groundbreaking semester, they continue to steer both their school and community toward unity. plot:
Zombies 2, styled Z-O-M-B-I-E-S 2, is a 2020 American musical comedy Disney Channel Original Movie that premiered on February 14, 2020. Directed by Paul Hoen from a script by David Light and Joseph Raso, it is the sequel to Zombies (2018). Milo Manheim and Meg Donnelly return as the zombie Zed and the cheerleader Addison, with Trevor Tordjman, Kylee Russell and Carla Jeffery reprising their roles and Chandler Kinney, Pearce Joza and Ariel Martin joining as a pack of werewolves.

A prologue shows the settlers who founded Seabrook battling werewolves for a powerful glowing artifact later called the moonstone. In the present, the zombies have been accepted into town life. Zed plans to invite Addison to Prawn, Seabrook's version of the prom, while Addison hopes to become cheer captain after Bucky, her self-absorbed cousin, quits to run for class president. When the cheer squad's bus passes through the forbidden forest, they spot werewolves, and the mayor responds by reviving the anti-monster laws, which bar zombies from Prawn. Zed decides to run for president himself so he can take Addison to the dance.

The werewolves, whose moonstone necklaces are losing their power, believe a prophecy that a white-haired girl, the Great Alpha, will lead them to the moonstone itself, and they enrol at Seabrook to find Addison. Wyatt, brother of the pack leader Willa, invites Addison to their den and offers her a fully charged necklace that will transform her if she is truly one of them. They also reveal that the planned demolition of the Seabrook Power plant will destroy the moonstone buried beneath it. A jealous Zed steals the necklace; its energy shorts out his Z-Band during the election debate, turning him fully zombie and costing him the vote. The werewolves are arrested trying to stop the demolition, and when Zed confesses, Addison puts on the necklace and discovers she is not a werewolf. The plant is destroyed anyway, but on Prawn night, as the monsters crash the dance and Zed and Addison reconcile, the ground splits open to reveal the intact moonstone. Zed removes his Z-Band and uses his strength to move a boulder so it can be recovered, and he and Addison share their first kiss. Finally, a blue meteor falls from the moon and makes Addison's hair glow.

Filmed around Toronto in 2019, the movie drew 2.46 million viewers on its premiere, outperforming the original among adults aged 18 to 49. Critics praised its message of tolerance, and it was followed by Zombies 3.

title: Countdown
tagline: Death? There's an app for that.
overview: A young nurse downloads an app that tells her she only has three days to live. With time ticking away and a mysterious figure haunting her, she must find a way to save her life before time runs out.
plot:
Countdown is a 2019 American supernatural horror film written and directed by Justin Dec. It stars Elizabeth Lail as a young nurse, alongside Jordan Calloway, Talitha Bateman, Tichina Arnold, P.J. Byrne, Peter Facinelli, Anne Winters and Tom Segura. Its story centers on a mobile app that accurately tells its users how much time they have left to live.

At a party, a teenager named Courtney downloads Countdown and learns that she has only three hours to live. When she refuses a ride from her drunk boyfriend Evan, the app warns that she has broken its "user agreement", and she is killed at home by an unseen entity just as her timer runs out, while Evan crashes his car. At the hospital where Evan is treated, nurse Quinn Harris dismisses his story but downloads the app herself and finds she has two days left. Evan, after skipping his surgery, is killed in a stairwell. Quinn soon discovers that changing her plans also violates the agreement, and that the app reinstalls itself on any new phone. At the same time, her superior, Dr. Sullivan, sexually harasses her and then gets her suspended by claiming she harassed him.

Quinn teams up with Matt, another user whose countdown is running out, and the two learn from a priest, Father John, that the app is tied to a demon named Ozhin. A phone salesman, Derek, hacks the code and adds decades to their lives and to that of Quinn's younger sister Jordan, but the timers soon reset, and Jordan is tormented by an apparition of the sisters' dead mother. Father John suggests the curse can be broken if a user dies before or outlives the countdown. A protective circle fails to hold the demon off, and Matt is killed. With Jordan injured, Quinn rushes her to hospital and considers killing Sullivan before his time, but the demon intervenes. Instead, Quinn deliberately overdoses before her timer ends, and Jordan revives her with naloxone, stopping their countdowns. Later, Sullivan is arrested after more nurses come forward.

STX Entertainment released the film in the United States on October 25, 2019. It opened with $9 million, beating projections, and went on to gross about $48 million worldwide against a $6.5 million budget, a commercial success. Critical reception was negative: Rotten Tomatoes reported 26% approval and Metacritic a score of 31, with critics finding it short on wit and originality despite a few jolts.

title: The Father
tagline: A realistic, deeply empathetic, and disquieting look at the fraying fabric of memory and identity.
overview: A man refuses all assistance from his daughter as he ages and, as he tries to make sense of his changing circumstances, he begins to doubt his loved ones, his own mind and even the fabric of his reality.
plot:
The Father is a 2020 psychological drama directed by Florian Zeller in his directorial debut, from a screenplay he wrote with Christopher Hampton, adapted from Zeller's 2012 play Le Père. A French-British co-production, it stars Anthony Hopkins as Anthony, an octogenarian living with dementia, with Olivia Colman as his daughter Anne, Mark Gatiss, Imogen Poots, Rufus Sewell and Olivia Williams. It premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in January 2020 and, after delays caused by the COVID-19 pandemic, was released in the United Kingdom in June 2021.

Anne visits her father in his London flat after he has driven away yet another caregiver. Anthony's memory is failing; he constantly misplaces things, especially his watch, which he accuses the caregiver of stealing, and he insists he will never leave his flat. Anne tells him she is moving to Paris to be with a man she has met, which confuses Anthony, who does not remember anyone in her life since her divorce. She warns that if he refuses help, she will have to put him in a care home.

The next day Anthony finds a stranger, Paul, in the flat, who says he is Anne's husband and that Anthony is living in their home. When Anne returns, she appears to Anthony as a different woman. Meeting a new caregiver, Laura, Anthony is charming and claims to have been a professional dancer, and he says she reminds him of his younger daughter, Lucy, a painter whom he has not seen for a long time and of whom he is very proud. As time, places and people shift around him, the film places the viewer inside Anthony's disorientation: rooms change their furnishings, faces are swapped, and conversations repeat with different outcomes. Gradually it becomes clear that Lucy died in an accident and that Anthony's reality is crumbling, as Anne struggles with guilt and exhaustion and Anthony desperately tries to hold on to his sense of who he is.

The Father received widespread acclaim, particularly for Hopkins's performance, its editing and production design, and its portrayal of dementia. It grossed about $36 million on a $6 million budget and received six Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture, winning Best Actor for Hopkins and Best Adapted Screenplay for Zeller and Hampton.

title: The Power of the Dog
overview: A domineering but charismatic rancher wages a war of intimidation on his brother's new wife and her teen son, until long-hidden secrets come to light.
plot:
The Power of the Dog is a 2021 American psychological drama film directed by Jane Campion, based on the 1967 novel of the same name by Thomas Savage. The film stars Benedict Cumberbatch, Kirsten Dunst, and Jesse Plemons.

The story takes place in 1925 Montana, where we meet Phil Burbank (Benedict Cumberbatch), a charismatic and dominant rancher who lives with his brother George (Jesse Plemons) on their family's spread. The two brothers have a complicated relationship, with Phil often taking advantage of George's more submissive nature.

The arrival of the Marjan (Kirsten Dunst) family, including her parents, Peter (Kodi Smit-McPhee) and Rose (Tone Bell), and her brother, Jimmy (Colman Domingo), shakes things up on the ranch. Phil is immediately drawn to Marjan, who is a widow with two sons, and begins to pursue her.

As Phil's interest in Marjan grows, so does his disdain for Peter, whom he sees as weak and effeminate. This animosity towards Peter leads to a series of tense confrontations between the two men, with Phil often using his physical strength and dominance to assert his authority.

Meanwhile, George becomes increasingly isolated and withdrawn, struggling to cope with the loss of his wife and the changing dynamics on the ranch. His relationship with Marjan's family deepens, particularly with Peter, who begins to open up about his own feelings and desires.

As the story unfolds, Phil's behavior towards Peter becomes more aggressive and menacing, leading to a tragic confrontation that changes the course of the narrative. The film builds towards a devastating climax, one that explores themes of toxic masculinity, homophobia, and the destructive power of unchecked emotions.

Throughout the film, Campion masterfully captures the vast, sweeping landscapes of Montana, using them as a metaphor for the characters' inner lives. The cinematography is stunning, with a muted color palette that reflects the bleakness and isolation of the rural landscape.

The performances in the film are outstanding, particularly from Cumberbatch, who brings a depth and nuance to Phil's character that is both captivating and terrifying. Dunst and Plemons also deliver standout performances, capturing the complexity and vulnerability of their characters.

Ultimately, The Power of the Dog is a powerful exploration of toxic masculinity and the destructive power of unchecked emotions. It is a film that will leave you unsettled and disturbed, but also deeply moved by its thought-provoking themes and outstanding performances.
