title: The Eyes of Tammy Faye
tagline: Sometimes in life, you have to take your lashes.
overview: From the 1960's to the 1980's, evangelist Jim Baker and his ambitious wife, Tammy Faye, rose from humble beginnings to to build an empire based on big-time evangelical Christianity--only for the couple to fall from grace because of some all-too-human sins.
plot:
As her mother is a divorcee, young Tammy Faye LaValley is deemed a reminder of her mother's sins and subsequently denied entrance to the rural, charismatic fundamentalist church where her mother plays piano, until Tammy sneaks in one day, receives communion wine and begins speaking in tongues at the altar and collapses. This is deemed a miracle by the pastor.
Years later, Tammy is chastised by her Bible college professors for wearing makeup. She is enamored with fellow student Jim Bakker's charismatic preaching while studying at North Central Bible College in Minneapolis, Minnesota. Jim had wanted to be a rock and roll DJ, until a tragic car accident one night almost killed his female passenger.
The two marry despite disapproval from Tammy's mother Rachel, and against NCB college policy, then leave school and move in with Tammy's parents.
Their charismatic preaching, singing and children's puppet show, earns the attention of Pat Robertson's Christian Broadcasting Network, who hires them as hosts of children's show Jim and Tammy. Jim later becomes the first host of CBN's The 700 Club, as the two welcome daughter Tammy Sue.
Tammy and Jim meet conservative, Baptist patriarch, Rev. Jerry Falwell at Robertson's lush estate, with Jerry expressing interest in working with CBN to reach his Christian followers.
Some years later, following an argument with Falwell in which Tammy dismisses the politicization of faith, she encourages Jim to create their own television network. The two leave CBN and establish the PTL Satellite Network, with their flagship show The PTL Club becoming immensely popular, reaching over 20 million people worldwide daily.
Tammy invites Rachel and stepfather Fred to move in with them at their Tega Cay, South Carolina compound, but Rachel expresses her disapproval of how PTL monetizes the religious faith of its viewers.
As the press and Democrats become critical of the PTL Network's tax exempt status, Tammy develops an addiction to pills. While recording an album of Christian songs, a lonely Tammy becomes flirtatious with famed Nashville music producer Gary S. Paxton, whom Jim fires following the birth of their son Jay.
In the mid 1980s, Jim focuses his attention on building a Christian theme park, while Falwell's influence over PTL grows. When Falwell decries the "gay cancer", Tammy deliberately interviews AIDS patient and Christian pastor Steve Pieters on The PTL Club.
After collapsing during a PTL taping, Tammy must go to rehab. Tammy argues with Jim over their strained relationship and his subservience to Falwell.
Falwell subsequently usurps control of PTL following news scandals about PTL's financial debt and Jim's extramarital affairs, including speculations about homosexual relationships. Jim is ultimately imprisoned for embezzling and financial fraud, and with no one left to protect her, Tammy is left jobless and forced to sell her home and possessions.

title: I Care a Lot
overview: A court-appointed legal guardian defrauds her older clients and traps them under her care. But her latest mark comes with some unexpected baggage.
plot:
Con artist Marla Grayson makes a living by convincing the justice system to grant her guardianship over elders who she pretends cannot take care of themselves. She places them in an assisted living facility, where they are sedated and lose contact with the outside world. She then sells off their homes and assets, pocketing the proceeds. She and the court deny a man, Mr. Feldstrom, access to his mother after he attempts to force his way into the facility. He later threatens her outside the courthouse, saying that he hopes she is raped and murdered.
Dr. Karen Amos informs Marla about a potential case, a wealthy retiree named Jennifer Peterson with no apparent husband or close family. A judge appoints Marla guardian after she and Dr. Amos falsely testify that Jennifer has dementia, confusion, and loss of mobility. Marla moves Jennifer into assisted living and gets to work selling Jennifer's furniture, car, and home. While rooting through Jennifer's possessions, Marla discovers the key to a safe deposit box. It contains a watch, gold bars, bank notes, and hidden, loose diamonds, which she takes and stashes away.
As Marla's girlfriend and business partner, Fran, oversees the renovation of the house, a cab arrives driven by Alexi Ignatyev, who says he is there to pick up Jennifer. Fran says that Jennifer has moved. Alexi returns to his employer, Roman Lunyov, distressed. Roman, a crime lord, is revealed to be Jennifer's son. He threatens Alexi and orders him to find his mother and report back. Mafia lawyer Dean Ericson offers to pay Marla $150,000 in cash to release Jennifer but she refuses, willing to do it only if she is paid $5 million. He threatens Marla and takes her to court. The judge dismisses the case as Ericson cannot prove Jennifer hired him.
Fran discovers "Jennifer Peterson" is an identity stolen from an infant who died of polio. When Jennifer refuses to tell Marla her real identity, Marla teams up with property manager Sam Rice and withdraws filling many of Jennifer's basic needs. Finding his mother's safe deposit box rifled, Roman sends three thugs to Jennifer's facility to take her. This effort fails, and Marla helps police apprehend Alexi, who is one of the men. Fran's police contact tells them that Alexi is the sibling of two other mafia bosses who supposedly died in a fire. Having failed to rescue his mother, Roman has Dr. Amos killed at her office. After hearing this news, Marla and Fran move into an unsold property of a previous victim. Jennifer is baited into attacking Marla when she visits the facility and is moved to a psychiatric ward.
Marla is tranquilized and kidnapped while Fran is attacked in their home. Marla is taken to Roman and demands $10 million to arrange Jennifer's release. He refuses, and his associates knock her out with chloroform and send her in a car into a lake. She escapes and returns home to find Fran beaten unconscious as gas fills the house. They escape an explosion and flee to another unsold property.

title: Alienoid
tagline: For Ages, Aliens have locked up their prisoners in humans bodies.
overview: Gurus in the late Goryeo dynasty try to obtain a fabled, holy sword, and humans in 2022 hunt down an alien prisoner that is locked in a human's body. The two parties cross paths when a time-traveling portal opens up.
plot:
Alienoid (Korean: Oegye+in 1bu) is a 2022 South Korean science fiction action film written and directed by Choi Dong-hoon, the first part of a two-part story. Its ensemble cast includes Ryu Jun-yeol as the Taoist swordsman Mureuk, Kim Woo-bin as the robots Guard and Thunder, Kim Tae-ri as Lee Ahn, So Ji-sub as the detective Moon Do-seok, and Yum Jung-ah, Jo Woo-jin, Kim Eui-sung, Lee Hanee and Shin Jung-geun. The story unfolds across two eras, late Goryeo and the present day, linked by a portal through time. CJ E&M released the film in South Korea on 20 July 2022.

In a prologue set in 1380, warrior monks fail to defeat an alien hidden inside a human host. Guard and Thunder, humanoid robots responsible for supervising alien prisoners, arrive from the future and extract the creature. Before dying, the host asks Guard to look after her baby daughter, and although Guard insists that they cannot interfere in human affairs, Thunder secretly takes the infant back with them to the present.

Guard raises the girl, Lee Ahn, while Thunder disguises himself as the family car. Guard explains the system the aliens use: their prisoners are locked inside the minds of human hosts who do not know they are carrying them, and they can be awakened by haava, the atmosphere of their home planet. When an alien ship arrives to free the prisoners and release haava that would poison humanity, Guard, Thunder and the now grown-up Lee Ahn fight back, eventually luring the surviving aliens into the past through time travel. In 1391, the carefree Taoist bounty hunter Mureuk sets out to claim a reward for a mystical object called the Divine Blade, which is in fact Guard's power source. His search brings him into contact with Lee Ahn, who now wields thunder-shooting weapons, and with rival sorcerers and the aliens' agents, as the two timelines converge around the blade and the fate of the Earth.

The film mixes martial arts fantasy, alien invasion science fiction and comedy, with its two timelines interwoven rather than told in strict order. Its sequel, completing the story, followed in 2024.

Alienoid opened at the top of the South Korean box office and passed one million admissions in a week, but it ended with about 1.5 million admissions, far short of the roughly seven million needed to break even on its high production cost. Critics praised the performances of Ryu Jun-yeol, Kim Woo-bin and Kim Tae-ri.

title: Becky
tagline: There once was a little girl...
overview: A teenager's weekend at a lake house with her father takes a turn for the worse when a group of convicts wreaks havoc on their lives.
plot:
Thirteen-year-old Becky Hooper is questioned about a recent incident at her family's lakehouse two weeks earlier. She gives vague answers and claims to remember only minor details. The story unfolds through her flashbacks.
Becky's mother died from cancer a year earlier, and she has a strained relationship with her father, Jeff. In an attempt to reconnect with her, they go on a trip to the family's old lakefront home. Meanwhile, prisoners Dominick Lewis, a Neo-Nazi, and his men Wallace "Apex" Landham, Sonny Cole, and Roman Hammond are transferred in a prison van. The group kills an inmate to get the van to pull over, kills the guards and escapes. They stop a car and steal it, killing the occupants in the process, a father and his two young children.
Jeff's girlfriend, Kayla, and her young son, Ty, arrive at the house, upsetting Becky. Jeff announces his engagement to Kayla. Becky storms out of the house, upset, followed by her Cane Corso dog, Diego. At her small fort in the woods, she knocks over a box of possessions, including a key whose bow is formed in the shape of a valknut. Dominick and his men show up at the family house, take everyone hostage, and demand the key. Kayla and Ty try to escape but are intercepted by Apex, who has grown tired of killing, and urges them to escape. Cole kills Dora, the family's other dog. Jeff lies about Becky's presence to protect her, but Dominick shoots Kayla to get the truth out of them.
Becky becomes aware of the assailants' presence and talks over a walkie-talkie, pretending to call the police in an attempt to scare them away. Dominick calls her bluff and tortures Jeff to lure her out. Dominick allows Jeff to talk to Becky, but Jeff tells her to run. Jeff breaks free and finds Becky, telling her he loves her, before Dominick shoots him dead. Dominick demands the key, but Becky gouges out his left eye with it then flees with Diego.
Dominick goes back into the house and sends Cole and Hammond to retrieve the key. Cole chases Becky back to her fort and tries to negotiate, but she ambushes and kills him with colored pencils and a sharpened ruler.
Apex shows Kayla and Ty compassion, and Dominick tries to have Apex reaffirm his loyalty to him. After finding Cole's corpse, Hammond chases Becky down to the lake, where she lures him into a trap, impaling his stomach. Hammond then falls into the lake, and Becky kills him with the propeller of an outboard motor. Apex finds Becky and her dog, incapacitates the latter, but does not want to hurt Becky, and urges her to flee.
Becky makes her presence known to Kayla and Ty; Kayla tries to distract Dominick by asking him about the key's purpose. Becky sets off the car alarm to lure Dominick out, while Kayla frees herself. Apex fends off Dominick long enough for Becky to run a lawnmover over Dominick's head, and then shoots the apologetic Apex dead. Kayla and Ty join Diego and Becky to wait for the police.

title: Rurouni Kenshin: The Final
original_title: るろうに剣心 最終章 The Final
overview: In 1879, Kenshin and his allies face their strongest enemy yet: his former brother-in-law Enishi Yukishiro and his minions, who've vowed their revenge.
plot:
Rurouni Kenshin: The Final is a 2021 Japanese jidaigeki action film written and directed by Keishi Ōtomo, based on Nobuhiro Watsuki's manga Rurouni Kenshin. The fourth installment of the live-action film series, following Rurouni Kenshin: The Legend Ends (2014), it adapts the manga's final arc with some changes. Takeru Satoh returns as Himura Kenshin, with Emi Takei as Kamiya Kaoru, Mackenyu as Yukishiro Enishi, Kasumi Arimura as Yukishiro Tomoe, Munetaka Aoki as Sagara Sanosuke and Yū Aoi as Takani Megumi.

Yukishiro Enishi, head of the Shanghai mafia, arrives in Tokyo seeking revenge on Kenshin, a former government assassin. He and allies who all hold grudges against Kenshin launch attacks across the city, firing a cannon into the Akabeko restaurant and targeting the Maekawa Dojo and the home of the police chief, leaving behind notes reading jinchū, or "human judgment". Confronting Kenshin, Enishi declares that he wants him to suffer as he did when Kenshin killed his sister. Kenshin then tells his friends of his past: fifteen years earlier, while serving the Imperialists, he fell in love with and married Tomoe, a Shogunate spy who had originally meant to avenge her fiancé, whom Kenshin had killed. When assassins ambushed him, Tomoe stepped between them and was accidentally killed by Kenshin, leaving him the second scar that forms the cross on his cheek.

Allies including Shinomori Aoshi and Makimachi Misao arrive with Tomoe's diary, while Saitō Hajime and his troops are lured into a trap by Sawagejō Chō, who is revealed to be working with the mafia. As bombings spread through Tokyo, Enishi beats Sanosuke and kidnaps Kaoru but cannot bring himself to kill her because she reminds him of his sister. Aided by Misao, Saitō and the police, and by his former enemy Seta Sōjirō, Kenshin storms Enishi's mansion. In their duel he lets Enishi stab him and apologizes. When Woo Heishin fires at Kenshin, Enishi shields Kaoru and takes a bullet. Arrested, Enishi reads Tomoe's diary and understands that she gave her life to stop Kenshin from killing; Kenshin bids farewell to Tomoe at her grave.

Released in Japan by Warner Bros. Pictures Japan on April 23, 2021, and later internationally on Netflix, the film had the year's biggest opening weekend for a live-action film despite pandemic closures and grossed about 4.34 billion yen. Reviews were positive, praising its fight sequences and its conclusion to Kenshin's story.

title: Inheritance
overview: The patriarch of a wealthy and powerful family suddenly passes away, leaving his wife and daughter with a shocking secret inheritance that threatens to unravel and destroy their lives.
plot:
Inheritance is a 2020 American thriller film directed by Vaughn Stein and written by Matthew Kennedy. It stars Lily Collins, Simon Pegg, Connie Nielsen, Chace Crawford and Patrick Warburton, and centers on the dark secret left behind when the patriarch of a wealthy and powerful family dies suddenly. Collins joined the cast in early 2019, replacing Kate Mara, and filming took place in Birmingham, Alabama.

After the sudden death of Archer Monroe, the patriarch of a powerful political family, his estate is divided among his wife, Catherine; his son, William, a politician running for reelection; and his daughter, Lauren, the Manhattan District Attorney. The family lawyer, Harold Thewlis, gives Lauren a private message from her father revealing a secret and directing her to an underground bunker on the family estate. Inside, she finds a man chained to the wall who calls himself Morgan Warner.

Morgan tells Lauren that he was Archer's friend and business partner, and that years ago the two of them, driving drunk, killed a pedestrian. To protect his career, Archer imprisoned Morgan rather than risk exposure, and over the years he used his captive as a confessor. Morgan's information leads Lauren to the victim's body, to Archer's longtime mistress and illegitimate son, and to evidence that Archer paid bribes to help his children win public office. Convinced, Lauren frees Morgan and has Harold arrange an offshore account and a private jet so he can disappear. But when his fingerprints are identified, Catherine recognizes the man in the photographs as Carson, calling him evil. Lauren discovers that his flight never left and that Harold has been murdered. At the house, Carson has taken Catherine to the bunker. He overpowers Lauren and reveals that 30 years earlier he drugged and raped Catherine; Archer had been taking him away to kill him when they struck the pedestrian, and imprisoned him instead. Archer died from the poison he had meant for Carson. As they fight, Carson claims to be Lauren's father, before Catherine shoots him dead. The women set the bunker on fire and leave.

Planned to premiere at the Tribeca Film Festival before its postponement due to COVID-19, the film was released on DirecTV Cinema on April 23, 2020, and by Vertical Entertainment on May 22. It received negative reviews, with 25% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 31.

title: The Forever Purge
overview: All the rules are broken as a sect of lawless marauders decides that the annual Purge does not stop at daybreak and instead should never end as they chase a group of immigrants who they want to punish because of their harsh historical past.
plot:
In 2048, eight years after Charlie Roan's presidential election, the New Founding Fathers of America (NFFA) party has been re-elected and have re-instituted the annual Purge with its original rules. White supremacists and nativism have surged nationwide following their re-election, and many outside the ruling party are concerned that the upcoming Purge will inflict more damage on the country than the NFFA realizes. Mexican couple Juan and Adela illegally cross the border into Texas to build a new life near Austin, with Juan working as a farmhand on the Tucker family ranch while Adela works in town.
Ten months later, on the eve of the 2049 Purge, Juan and Adela join a migrant community behind a walled sanctuary with armed security to protect them. As the Purge begins, Adela witnesses a nationalist Purger group, who declare themselves to be the Purge Purification Force (PPF), intent on killing those people that they consider non-American. The migrant community survives the Purge with no incidents. Come morning, Juan and Adela return to their jobs, but both notice that many of their co-workers did not report to work. Adela is attacked by two self-proclaimed Forever Purgers, but she is rescued by her boss, Darius, before the police arrests both for killing their attackers.
Juan and fellow migrant co-worker T.T. discover that the Tucker family has been taken hostage by their white farmhands, Forever Purgers, intending to take the ranch for themselves. Patriarch Caleb Tucker sacrifices himself and distracts the Purgers long enough for Juan and T.T. to rescue his son Dylan, Dylan's pregnant wife Cassie, and Dylan's sister Harper. As they drive off to search for Adela, the news confirms that civilians nationwide, connecting via social media, have declared a Forever Purge, opposing NFFA orders to stand down.
The group rescues Adela and Darius from Purgers. Darius stays behind to search for his family while the others escape from a burning Austin. At a gas station, they hear news reports that, to protect non-Purger civilians, Canada and Mexico have opened their borders for the next six hours. Following that, the borders will close and entry will be denied. The group decides to escape across the Mexican border at El Paso.
By the time the group arrives in a chaotic El Paso, the NFFA has invoked martial law across the United States to contain the violence. Fighting through El Paso, Adela and Cassie are split from the group by military forces. At the same time, Juan, T.T., Dylan, and Harper are captured by the PPF, with their Alpha Leader offering Dylan and Harper a chance to live if they kill T.T. and Juan. When they refuse, the Purgers murder T.T. just before the military intervenes, allowing the group to escape. However, the military is forced to withdraw from El Paso when more Purgers destroy their base.

title: Harry & Meghan: Becoming Royal
overview: The continuing love story of newlyweds Prince Harry and American actress Meghan Markle during their first year of marriage.
plot:
Harry & Meghan: Becoming Royal is a 2019 American biographical romance television film that dramatizes the royal wedding of Prince Harry and Meghan Markle and the couple's first year of marriage. Directed by Menhaj Huda from a screenplay by Scarlett Lacey and executive produced by Merideth Finn and Michele Weiss, it was made for Lifetime as a sequel to Harry & Meghan: A Royal Romance (2018), whose leads were recast. Charlie Field plays Prince Harry and Tiffany Smith, in her first leading role, plays Meghan, with Charles Shaughnessy as Prince Charles, Deborah Ramsay as Camilla, Jordan Whalen as Prince William, Bonnie Soper as Diana, Clare Filipow as Stella, Marlie Collins as Annabella and James Dreyfus as Sir Leonard Briggs.

The film opens as Meghan shoots her final wedding scene on the legal drama Suits before moving to London, where Harry welcomes her to Kensington Palace with a homemade banner and champagne. As the wedding approaches, she struggles with royal protocol and a hostile press, embodied by a fictional morning show, Good Day UK, and its racist co-host. She attends her first royal Christmas, plans the guest list, supports victims of the Grenfell Tower fire and argues with palace staff over her white gown and tiara. When her father, Thomas Markle, is exposed for staging paparazzi photographs and then withdraws from the ceremony, Charles and Camilla reassure her, and Charles offers to escort her for part of the walk down the aisle. After the wedding the duchess promotes a charity cookbook created with women from a community kitchen formed after the fire, realizes she is pregnant as Harry gives her a puppy, and decides she will no longer suppress her own style, discarding the pantyhose palace aides expect her to wear. The film ends with a real photograph of the couple holding their newborn baby.

Lifetime announced the project in February 2019, and the film premiered on Memorial Day, 27 May 2019. It was followed by Harry & Meghan: Escaping the Palace. Reception was divided. title: The Little Things
tagline: Some things never let us go.
overview: Deputy Sheriff Joe "Deke" Deacon joins forces with Sgt. Jim Baxter to search for a serial killer who's terrorizing Los Angeles. As they track the culprit, Baxter is unaware that the investigation is dredging up echoes of Deke's past, uncovering disturbing secrets that could threaten more than his case.
plot:
One night in 1990, a teenaged girl drives on a deserted highway, stalked by a motorist. After pulling into a gas station, she finds it closed. A terrifying pursuit on foot begins. She manages to catch the attention of a passing truck driver and escapes her stalker.
Some time later in Bakersfield, Kern County Sheriff's Office Deputy Sheriff Joe "Deke" Deacon is sent to the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department to collect evidence pertaining to a recent murder. A former LASD detective, Deacon accompanies newly appointed lead detective Jimmy Baxter to the scene of a new murder in L.A. Deacon notices similarities between the M.O. of the killing and the M.O. of an old serial murder case he was unable to solve.
That night, a woman named Ronda Rathbun is followed by a car while jogging and is reported missing the following morning. Baxter learns from Captain Farris that Deacon had gotten divorced and suffered a heart attack due to his obsession with the unsolved case. So, he is advised not to involve him any further, but Deacon takes vacation leave from his station to assist in solving Baxter's case.
The next night, the police discover the body of another victim washed up beneath a bridge. Baxter learns the M.O. is consistent with the earlier murder and others: the victims were all prostitutes who were stabbed to death. Deacon begins investigating Albert Sparma, a suspect working at a repair shop in proximity to the murders. He tails him but is thwarted, so he takes him in for questioning. While under interrogation, Sparma taunts the detectives and is released after provoking Deacon into an angry outburst. The young woman pursued in the desert is interviewed but has seen Sparma in handcuffs at the police station, which compromises her eligibility as an objective witness to identify him as a suspect.
The FBI will take charge of the investigation within the week, giving Deacon and Baxter less time to resolve it. Farris informs Baxter that eight years prior, Sparma confessed to a murder which he could not possibly have committed and is thus an unlikely suspect. Baxter and Deacon nonetheless continue investigating. Sparma's fingerprint is similar to the killer's but not a definitive match. Their next move is an illegal search at Sparma's apartment. With Baxter standing guard outside, Deacon unsuccessfully searches the apartment for incriminating evidence, only finding newspaper clippings related to the cases. Suddenly Sparma's police scanner goes off and Deacon hears an "officer down" alert for this very address. As police converge on the building, Deacon narrowly escapes over the roof, with Sparma watching his ordeal and casually waving his hand at Baxter.
While surveilling Sparma, Baxter corners the suspect alone and demands to know Rathbun's location. Sparma offers to drive him to where he supposedly hid Rathbun's body. Baxter cautiously agrees while Deacon secretly follows.

title: Horizon Line
overview: A couple flying on a small plane to attend a tropical island wedding must fight for their lives after their pilot suffers a heart attack.
plot:
Horizon Line is a 2020 English-language Swedish adventure thriller film directed by Mikael Marcimain. Allison Williams stars as Sara Johnson and Alexander Dreymon as her former boyfriend Jackson Davisen, who must fight to survive aboard a small GippsAero GA8 Airvan over the Indian Ocean after their pilot, Freddy Wyman, played by Keith David, dies of a heart attack. Pearl Mackie appears as Pascale and Jumayn Hunter as the air traffic controller Samuel. With a budget of 200 million Swedish kronor, about US$22 million, it was among the most expensive Swedish films at the time, and it was shot in Mauritius, Dublin and at Pinewood Studios.

A year after slipping away from Jackson at an island bar without saying goodbye, Sara travels from London to Mauritius for a friend's wedding. There she spends the night with Jackson, misses the last boat to the wedding venue on Rodrigues and catches a ride on a small plane flown by her friend Freddy, only to discover that Jackson has booked the same flight. While Jackson sleeps, Freddy lets Sara take the co-pilot's seat, but he suffers a fatal heart attack and the plane plunges. The two regain control, yet with the autopilot damaged, Sara, who has learned a few basics from Freddy, must fly the aircraft. Reaching Samuel by radio, they try to follow his guidance but must first pass through a storm, which damages their compass, and the plane starts losing fuel rapidly. Jackson climbs outside to patch a fuel line, succeeding but badly breaking his arm. To save fuel they jettison weight, including Freddy's body, and Sara climbs out of the window to pour bottles of rum into the tank as makeshift fuel. When the radio falls silent and the fuel runs out, they glide toward a small island, but the plane crashes into the sea and flips over, and Sara frees the trapped Jackson before both swim ashore. The island proves to be a sandbar that soon vanishes beneath the rising tide. As they tread water, Jackson offers Sara his life vest, but she refuses, saying they are a team, and he declares his love for her just as a fishing boat that heard their radio calls arrives to rescue them.

SF Studios released Horizon Line in Swedish cinemas on 6 November 2020, and STXfilms released it on video on demand in the United States on 12 January 2021. It grossed about $916,000 internationally. It holds a 40% Rotten Tomatoes rating from a handful of reviews, with critics praising its pacing but finding it preposterous.

title: Spiral: From the Book of Saw

overview: Working in the shadow of an esteemed police veteran, brash Detective Ezekiel “Zeke” Banks and his rookie partner take charge of a grisly investigation into murders that are eerily reminiscent of the city’s gruesome past.  Unwittingly entrapped in a deepening mystery, Zeke finds himself at the center of the killer’s morbid game.
plot:
Spiral: From the Book of Saw is a 2021 American supernatural thriller film directed by Darren Lynn Bousman, written by Josh Stolberg and Peter Goldfinger, and produced by Lionsgate. The film serves as a sequel to the Saw franchise.

The story begins with Detective Ezekiel "Zeke" Banks (Chris Rock), a tough and seasoned detective from New York City, who is investigating a series of gruesome murders that seem to be connected to an old case from his past. As Zeke delves deeper into the investigation, he discovers that the murders are linked to Jigsaw's (Tobin Bell) legacy.

Zeke soon finds himself in the midst of a deadly game, where he must navigate through a series of puzzles and traps set by Jigsaw's successor, a mysterious figure known as "The Conductor" (Max Hogan). The Conductor is revealed to be a former apprentice of Jigsaw who has taken up his mantle and continues his twisted games.

As Zeke navigates the deadly game, he meets Amanda Young (Samantha Sloyan), a young woman with a troubled past who was once an apprentice of Jigsaw. Amanda becomes a key player in the game, as she is forced to confront her own dark past and the consequences of her actions.

Throughout the film, Zeke must use his wits and resourcefulness to survive the deadly traps and puzzles set by The Conductor. Along the way, he uncovers clues that suggest Jigsaw's legacy lives on through Amanda, who has become a complex and conflicted character in her own right.

As the game reaches its climax, Zeke discovers that The Conductor is actually a former cop who was obsessed with Jigsaw's philosophy and saw him as a twisted genius. The Conductor believes that by continuing Jigsaw's games, he can bring about a new era of enlightenment and self-discovery for humanity.

In the end, Zeke manages to outsmart The Conductor and escape the deadly game, but not before Amanda is forced to confront her own demons and make a choice between redemption and further descent into darkness. The film ends with a sense of closure for Zeke, but also raises questions about the legacy of Jigsaw's twisted games and whether they can ever be truly escaped.

Overall, Spiral: From the Book of Saw is a tense and thrilling ride that explores the darker themes of the Saw franchise while introducing new characters and plot twists. The film's use of puzzles and traps is clever and inventive, making for a fun and suspenseful viewing experience.

title: The Silencing
tagline: It takes a hunter to catch a killer.
overview: A reformed hunter becomes involved in a deadly game of cat and mouse when he and the local sheriff set out to track a vicious killer who may have kidnapped his daughter years ago.
plot:
The Silencing is a 2020 action thriller directed by Robin Pront from a screenplay by Micah Ranum. It stars Nikolaj Coster-Waldau and Annabelle Wallis, with Hero Fiennes Tiffin, Zahn McClarnon and Melanie Scrofano in supporting roles. Saban Films released it through DirecTV Cinema in July 2020, followed by a theatrical and video-on-demand release in August 2020.

Coster-Waldau plays Rayburn Swanson, a former hunter and recovering alcoholic who now runs a wildlife sanctuary in the forests of northern Minnesota. He named it after his daughter Gwen, who disapproved of his trapping and who vanished five years earlier from his car while he stepped into a store to buy whiskey. The sanctuary is his form of penance, and he patrols it with surveillance cameras to keep hunters away. Wallis plays Alice Gustafson, the local sheriff, who also has to deal with her volatile younger brother Brooks.

When the body of a young girl is found near a lake, Alice notices a distinctive scar on the victim's throat and recovers the head of a spear from a nearby tree, a projectile launched with an atlatl, an ancient throwing device. Rayburn rushes to view the body, fearing it is Gwen, but it is not. Soon afterwards he spots a figure in a ghillie suit moving through the woods and is wounded by a thrown spear when he tries to intervene. Reviewing his camera footage, he discovers that the masked hunter has been using the sanctuary to stalk and kill abducted girls. He rescues one survivor, Molly, who has been left mute by the same throat injury, and the case draws him and Alice together as the investigation points closer to people they know.

The story becomes a cat-and-mouse thriller in the wilderness, in which Rayburn's tracking skills are pitted against a killer who knows the terrain just as well, while Alice wrestles with suspicions that touch her own family. The film combines a serial-killer mystery with a portrait of a grieving father who refuses to give up on finding his child.

Reviews were largely negative. On Rotten Tomatoes the film holds an approval rating of about 20 percent, with the consensus arguing that it mistakes mood for character development and delivers an undercooked mystery, although some critics praised Coster-Waldau's committed lead performance and the bleak, wintry atmosphere.

title: Stars at Noon
tagline: A sumptuous tale of romance and espionage.
overview: In present-day Nicaragua, a headstrong American journalist and a mysterious English businessman strike up a romance as they become embroiled in a dangerous labyrinth of lies and conspiracies and are forced to try and escape the country.
plot:
Trish is a young American journalist stranded in Nicaragua during the COVID-19 pandemic and amid a period of severe governmental instability. She is a travel writer whose coverage of brutal extrajudicial killings has alienated both her superiors and the ruling party; her passport has been confiscated and she is living in a flophouse paid for by a sympathetic cabinet minister. Trish assumes that she will be executed for her anti-government activities when the minister can no longer protect her. She has sex with government officials for money and basic necessities (largely unavailable due to the political crisis) while searching desperately for a way out of the country.
One day, Trish solicits a British man named Daniel for sex in a hotel reserved for wealthy foreigners. Daniel introduces himself as a petrochemicals consultant, but Trish assumes that he is really an intelligence agent. They have passionate, tender sex, and Trish follows him the day after. She observes him meeting with a man she identifies as a Costa Rican police officer. When questioned about the meeting, Daniel is surprised to hear of the man's true identity, eventually realizing his hostile intentions after the officer chases the two through a market.
Trish lets Daniel hide out in the flophouse. The Costa Rican officer quickly finds them, but he is unwilling to attack Daniel in a building protected by a governmental official. Trish and Daniel fall in love. The climax of their emotional bond occurs in a deserted nightclub, where they dance romantically as he speaks about his wife.
Eventually, Trish is informed that the government can no longer protect her; she runs out of money and Daniel is cut off by his employer. Realizing that they will be killed by the Costa Rican once they leave the hotel, the two steal a car and drive towards a border. Along the way, they meet a man who Trish quickly realizes is a CIA agent. The man offers Trish safe passage to the U.S. in exchange for Daniel, but Trish refuses. At the border, the agent offers her the same deal, and questions how they will cross the border without Trish's passport. It becomes clear that the agent and the Costa Rican are colluding with the authoritarian government, while Daniel is in some way trying to destabilize it.
Trish and Daniel trade the car to smugglers in exchange for a boat ride across the border. At the end of the journey, the smugglers are shot dead by unseen soldiers and Daniel is wounded. They make their way to an abandoned church and fall asleep. When they wake up, the agent and the Costa Rican, along with armed troops, have surrounded them. Daniel convinces Trish to abandon him, and the soldiers take him away. A Nicaraguan police officer and former client of Trish's returns her passport, allowing her to legally fly home. The agent pays her and leaves.

title: The Hating Game
tagline: He's the one she loves to hate.
overview: Resolving to achieve professional success without compromising her ethics, Lucy embarks on a ruthless game of one-upmanship against cold and efficient nemesis Joshua, a rivalry that is complicated by her growing attraction to him.
plot:
The Hating Game is a 2021 American romantic comedy directed by Peter Hutchings and adapted from Sally Thorne's 2016 novel. Lucy Hale and Austin Stowell star as two rival executive assistants at a publishing company, with Yasha Jackson, Sakina Jaffrey and Corbin Bernsen in supporting roles. Vertical Entertainment released it in limited cinemas and on video on demand on December 10, 2021.

After two publishing houses merge, Lucy Hutton and Joshua Templeman share an office as assistants to the company's two co-CEOs. They are opposites in every way. Lucy, who studied literature, is warm and accommodating, while Josh, a Harvard MBA, is cold, methodical and responsible for cutting a large share of the staff. Each loathes the other, and they wage a constant war of petty games, with Lucy disturbing the precise order of Josh's desk and Josh mocking her as a pushover. When a new senior position opens up, both apply and agree that whoever loses will resign.

Their rivalry reveals how closely they watch each other. After a vivid dream about Josh, Lucy wears a revealing dress to the office, and when he teases her about a supposed hot date, she invents one with the friendly colleague Danny. Leaving work, their bickering turns into a passionate kiss in the lift. Josh later sends flowers, which Lucy mistakes for Danny's. When she falls ill with a fever at a paintball team-building day, Josh takes her home and brings his doctor brother Patrick to treat her, and she offers to be his date at Patrick's wedding.

Their relationship deepens as Josh speaks of his strained ties with his parents, both doctors, who never forgave him for leaving medical school. At the wedding, held at an overbooked inn where they must share a room, they sleep together, and Lucy learns that the bride, Mindy, once left Josh for his brother. She defends Josh when his father belittles his career. Back home, Josh tells her he loves her and wants a real relationship. But Lucy overhears part of a conversation and wrongly concludes that he has used her to win the job. She throws herself into the final presentation and wins the promotion, only to discover that Josh has already accepted a better job elsewhere, and the two finally get together.

Reviews were generally positive, with 68% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, critics praising the chemistry between Hale and Stowell.

title: John Wick: Chapter 4
tagline: No way back, one way out.
overview: With the price on his head ever increasing, John Wick uncovers a path to defeating The High Table. But before he can earn his freedom, Wick must face off against a new enemy with powerful alliances across the globe and forces that turn old friends into foes.
plot:
John Wick: Chapter 4 is a 2023 American neo-noir action thriller directed by Chad Stahelski and written by Shay Hatten and Michael Finch, the fourth installment in the John Wick series and the sequel to Chapter 3 – Parabellum. Keanu Reeves returns as the legendary assassin John Wick, joined by Donnie Yen as Caine, Bill Skarsgård as the Marquis Vincent Bisset de Gramont, Laurence Fishburne as the Bowery King, Hiroyuki Sanada as Shimazu Koji, Shamier Anderson as Mr. Nobody, Rina Sawayama as Akira, Scott Adkins as Killa, Clancy Brown as the Harbinger, Lance Reddick as Charon and Ian McShane as Winston.

Recovering underground with the Bowery King after being shot off the roof of the Continental by Winston, John strikes back at the High Table by traveling to Morocco and killing the Elder, the one who sits above the Table. In response, the High Table gives the Marquis de Gramont unlimited resources to eliminate him. The Marquis strips Winston of his position, destroys the New York Continental, and coerces John's old friend Caine, a blind, retired assassin, into hunting him by threatening Caine's daughter.

John seeks shelter at the Osaka Continental run by his friend Koji, but the hotel is overrun by High Table enforcers, and a massive battle ensues in which Koji is killed by Caine, while a mercenary tracker known as Mr. Nobody waits for the bounty to rise. Back in New York, Winston suggests a way out: under an old High Table tradition, John can challenge the Marquis to a duel, which would free him from all obligations if he wins. To do so, John must first be readmitted to the Ruska Roma crime family in Berlin, a task that requires killing the brutal High Table member Killa. The duel is set for sunrise at the Sacré-Cœur in Paris, and as the Marquis puts a huge bounty on him, John must battle his way across the city to arrive on time.

The film is known for its elaborate set pieces, including a chaotic chase and shootout in the traffic around the Arc de Triomphe, and for its themes of loyalty, friendship and the cost of freedom.

John Wick: Chapter 4 premiered in London on March 6, 2023, and was released in the United States on March 24, shortly after Reddick's death. It grossed 447 million dollars worldwide, the highest of the series, and received critical acclaim, with 94 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 78.

title: Super Me
overview: Sang Yu is so exhausted from trying to stay awake. Every time he closes his eyes, a demon chases and kills him in his dreams. One night Sang realizes he has a special power: he can bring treasures from his dreams into reality. Almost overnight, he becomes a rich man. But his wealth also attracts the attention of a ruthless gangster.
plot:
Super Me (Chinese: 超级的我) is a 2019 Chinese fantasy film that mixes action, comedy, romance and drama, written and directed by Zhang Chong as his second feature after The Fourth Wall. It was released in Chinese cinemas in April 2021 and picked up by Netflix, which began streaming it internationally on 8 May 2021. The project was originally to be produced by Anthony and Joe Russo through their Chinese venture Anthem Pictures, but the brothers withdrew and the film was ultimately made by the Shanghai companies Hehe Pictures and Black Ant Entertainment.

Taiwanese actor Darren Wang plays Sang Yu, a struggling, impoverished screenwriter whose scripts have never been filmed. Crippled by writer's block and months of insomnia, he cannot deliver the screenplay demanded by his producer San Ge (Cao Bingkun), and every time he does fall asleep a demonic blue creature hunts him down and kills him in his dreams. After losing his apartment and ending up on the streets, Sang reaches the point of attempting suicide, but a street pancake vendor stops him and advises him to remind himself, during his next nightmare, that he is only dreaming so that he can wake up before dying. Following this advice, Sang wakes to find himself holding the golden sword that had just wounded him in the dream. The priceless object fetches a fortune, and by repeating the trick night after night he collects valuable artefacts from the dream world and becomes rich almost overnight. San Ge now becomes his subordinate, and Sang finally finds the courage to court Hua Er (Song Jia), the café owner he has long admired from afar. His wealth carries a cost, however: injuries from the dream world keep following him into reality, and his money draws the attention of a ruthless gangster boss, Qiang (Wu Gang). King Shih-chieh and Kevin Lee also appear.

Critical responses varied. Writing for Yahoo News Singapore, Teng Yong Ping gave it three out of five stars, reading it as a fable warning against unearned wealth; he found its effects decent but below Hollywood level and faulted Wang's broad acting, the vague rules of the dream world and an anti-climactic ending. M.N. Miller of Ready Steady Cut was far more enthusiastic, calling it great fun and interpreting the dream demon as a metaphor for a writer's inner struggles. AsianMovieWeb judged it surprisingly entertaining as a fantasy comedy with a subtle romance and neat effects, though it felt the script grew too convoluted towards the end.

title: Vanguard
overview: Covert security company Vanguard is the last hope of survival for an accountant after he is targeted by the world's deadliest mercenary organization.
plot:
Vanguard (Chinese: 急先鋒) is a 2020 Chinese action comedy written and directed by Stanley Tong, marking his sixth collaboration with Jackie Chan. Chan stars as Tang Huanting, head of an elite private security company, with Yang Yang, Miya Muqi, Allen Ai Lun and Jackson Liu. Originally set for release in January 2020, the film was postponed because of the COVID-19 pandemic and opened in China on 30 September 2020, followed by releases in the United States in November and India in December.

Qin Guoli, a Chinese accountant based in Britain, was coerced into managing the finances of Maasym, the leader of a terrorist group called the Brothers of Vengeance. After Qin tipped off Scotland Yard, Maasym was killed in an American military operation, but his son Omar survived and is determined to recover his father's fortune, whose location only Qin knows. Omar hires a mercenary gang known as the Arctic Wolves, who abduct Qin and his new wife during Chinese New Year festivities in London's Chinatown.

Vanguard, the international security firm charged with Qin's protection, sends its agents Zhang Kaixuan, Lei Zhenyu and Mi Ya to rescue him. After the successful operation, Qin asks Tang to protect his daughter, Fareeda, who is working in Africa, before Omar can use her as leverage. Tang, Lei and Mi Ya travel to Africa, where they find Fareeda but must fight off both the Arctic Wolves and a gang of poachers hired as extra muscle. In the chaos, Lei and Fareeda are separated from the group and hide in the jungle, while Tang and Mi Ya track them with satellite support from Vanguard's headquarters. The reunited team escapes in a furious river chase with an amphibious vehicle, and the pursuit eventually leads to the Middle East and to Dubai, where the agents must stop Omar's plans for a devastating terrorist attack, in a series of elaborate action set pieces involving vehicles, explosions and animals.

Vanguard received mixed reviews. Critics praised Chan's performance, the action sequences and the music but criticized the screenplay, editing and length. The film was released during China's National Day holiday period, one of the first major Chinese releases after cinemas reopened following pandemic closures.

title: Skyfire
overview: Tianhuo Island is a beautiful paradise. It almost makes people forget that it is located in the "Ring of Fire", the world-famous Pacific Rim volcanic belt. Young geologist Li Xiaomeng brings her team here to develop the first volcanic monitoring system, the Suzaku. Li Xiaomeng's father, Li Wentao, a volcanic expert who has retired for many years, rushes to the crater after learning about it, trying to persuade her to leave. plot:
Skyfire (Chinese: 天·火) is a 2019 Chinese disaster action film directed by Simon West and written by Wei Bu and Sidney King. It stars Wang Xueqi as volcanologist Wentao Li, Hannah Quinlivan as his daughter Meng Li, Shawn Dou as Zhengnan Xiao and Jason Isaacs as the resort developer Jack Harris. Billed as China's first big-budget disaster film, it depicts a catastrophic eruption at a luxury resort on a tropical island.

When Meng Li is a child, her mother is killed when a volcano suddenly erupts on Ting-Hao, a Southeast Asian island. Years later, Meng has become a scientist herself and returns to the island to set up an advanced monitoring system designed to predict eruptions. In the meantime, the businessman Jack Harris has built an extravagant theme park resort at the foot of the volcano, confidently assuring investors and guests that it will not erupt for another century and a half and believing that tourists enjoy living on the edge.

Meng's father, Wentao, comes to the island to warn his daughter that a new eruption is imminent. As the volcano awakens, Meng and Wentao are forced to work together to rescue a group of tourists stranded on an observation platform inside the crater. When the eruption intensifies, burning rocks rain down on the resort and rivers of lava threaten the island's villages, and the survivors must race across the devastated landscape to reach a control center, where they hope to release a reservoir and divert the lava, while Harris's reckless decisions endanger everyone.

The film follows the conventions of Hollywood disaster cinema, combining spectacular visual effects with a story of reconciliation between a father and daughter.

Skyfire was released in China in December 2019 and was intended as the first film of a trilogy. Western critics were largely dismissive, criticizing its thin characters and formulaic action and comparing it to films such as When Time Ran Out and Jurassic Park, although it holds a rating of 57 percent on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: Project Power
tagline: What would you risk for five minutes of pure power?
overview: An ex-soldier, a teen and a cop collide in New Orleans as they hunt for the source behind a dangerous new pill that grants users temporary superpowers.
plot:
Project Power is a 2020 American science fiction action film directed by Henry Joost and Ariel Schulman and written by Mattson Tomlin. It stars Jamie Foxx as Art, a former soldier, Joseph Gordon-Levitt as New Orleans police officer Frank Shaver and Dominique Fishback as Robin Reilly, a teenage dealer, with Colson Baker, Rodrigo Santoro, Amy Landecker and Allen Maldonado. The story centers on a pill that gives its user a unique superpower for five minutes.

In near-future New Orleans, a mysterious supplier begins distributing a pill called Power for free to local drug dealers. Each user gains a random superpower for five minutes, based on abilities found in the animal kingdom, but the effects are unpredictable and sometimes fatal. Robin, a bright teenager who deals the drug to pay for her mother's medical care, is friends with Frank Shaver, a police officer who secretly uses Power himself, which makes him bulletproof, to keep up with the criminals. Frank's superiors tell him that powerful figures want the investigation into the drug shut down and give him the photograph of a suspect: Art.

Art, in fact, is not the source of the drug but a former U.S. Army major who was one of its first test subjects. He is searching for his daughter Tracy, who was born with powers as a result of his treatment and was kidnapped by Teleios, the shadowy defense contractor behind Power, which is using New Orleans as a testing ground for its product. Art forces Robin to help him find the distributor, and the two form an unlikely bond. With Frank on their trail and Teleios preparing to sell the drug to a potential buyer, the three must join forces to expose the conspiracy and rescue Tracy.

The film uses its premise to comment on pharmaceutical exploitation and on the treatment of poor communities as test subjects, and it was praised for Fishback's breakout performance.

Project Power was released on Netflix on August 14, 2020. It received mixed to positive reviews, with 61 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus highlighted a star-making turn from Fishback, and a Metacritic score of 51.

title: The Influence
overview: After moving back to her family home to care for her dying mother, a nurse haunted by her childhood memories must struggle with an evil force in the house.
plot:
The Influence (Spanish: La influencia) is a 2019 Spanish supernatural horror film directed by Denis Rovira van Boekholt in his feature debut. It adapts the 1988 novel of the same name by the English horror writer Ramsey Campbell, relocating the story to Spain, from a screenplay by Rovira, Daniel Rissech and the Goya-winning writer Michel Gaztambide. Manuela Vellés stars as Alicia, with Maggie Civantos as her sister Sara, Alain Hernández as her husband Mikel, Claudia Placer as her young daughter Nora and Emma Suárez as her mother Victoria.

Alicia, a nurse, returns after a long estrangement to the family home she fled as a child, a gloomy, isolated mansion in the woods that is crammed with hunting trophies, stuffed animals and dusty curiosities. Her sister Sara has spent years caring for their possessive mother, Victoria, who now lies in a deep coma on the top floor, barely kept alive by a respirator, and Alicia moves in with Mikel, an electrician, and Nora to share the burden. She insists that Victoria will never wake up, but flashbacks gradually reveal the cruelty the old woman inflicted on her daughters in the past, and a room beside her bed is filled with jars, spell books marked with pentagrams, skulls and other occult objects revealing her lifelong devotion to witchcraft.

Nora is drawn to her grandmother and to the forbidden room, where she takes a spider-shaped locket. At her new school she is bullied, and she begins spending time with Luna, a strange, grubby girl who watches her from outside. When the remaining relatives gather for the reading of the will, they learn that Nora is the sole heir. The girl grows sullen and violent, beating her tormentor bloodily, while unexplained events multiply around the house, and Alicia must confront the past she had tried to forget as she realizes that even in her coma Victoria is able to shape what happens around her.

Sony Pictures released The Influence in Spanish cinemas on 21 June 2019, and Netflix began streaming it internationally on 11 October 2019. Reviews were mostly negative. Critics compared it with Hereditary and gothic Spanish horror such as The Others, and some praised its atmosphere, elaborate production design and Civantos's performance, but HobbyConsolas found its incoherent script, overloaded clichés and ridiculous dialogue turned it into unintended comedy, and Decider called it a slow, self-serious tale with underwhelming reveals and a nonsensical ending.

title: The Wretched
tagline: What is forgotten will never be found.
overview: A rebellious teenage boy, struggling with his parent's imminent divorce, encounters a terrifying evil after his next-door neighbor becomes possessed by an ancient witch that feasts on children.
plot:
In 1985, Megan arrives at the home of the Gambels to babysit their daughter Ashley. In the basement, she finds a creature feeding off little Ashley. Terrified, she tries to escape, but Mr. Gambel purposely shuts the door on her. Megan is presumed killed. A strange sign is shown on the door.
In the present, Ben Shaw comes to be with his father Liam as his parents are in the middle of a divorce. Ben lands a job working at the marina, where he befriends Mallory. He also notices Liam getting close with Sara, a co-worker. In the woods, Dillon, the son of Liam's neighbor Abbie, finds a tree with the same symbol seen at the Gambel house. He hears what sounds like Abbie's voice coming from the tree, calling to him before the real Abbie appears. They bring a buck home that they hit and that night, something crawls out of the buck's corpse.
Ben befriends Dillon. That night, Abbie goes to check on Sam in his crib. In his room, she hears a crunching sound and sees the window left open. In the crib she sees finds sticks wrapped inside a blanket and is then attacked. Ben later notices Abbie going into the forest with a child. At work, he learns that Dillon never showed up for sailing lessons. When he goes to Dillon's house, the father Ty denies having a son. Later, Abbie whispers something demonic in Ty's ear that makes him bleed. She then takes a shower and her body starts to decay.
Ben is suspicious and reads about a witch that is known for possessing people and taking children. He goes into Abbie's cellar and finds a picture of the family, along with a picture of Mallory and her sister Lily, making him realize that the witch is after Lily next. He rushes to save Lily, but is too late, as the witch has pulled her into her tree, leading to Mallory forgetting Lily. While Ben is with Sara, he notices flowers decaying, and realizes she is possessed by the witch. When she tries to attack, he slashes her arm, but the witch makes it look like he attacked Sara for no reason. He is taken into custody. The officer driving Ben to the station instead attempts to drown him at the beach until a dog attacks. The officer shoots the dog and then himself as he realizes that something is controlling him to kill Ben. Meanwhile, Liam finds the dead bodies of Ty and Abbie at their house. Sara sneaks up to stab Liam but Ben arrives and shoots her. The witch crawls out of Sara's corpse and goes after Ben, but he takes Liam to safety as their house burns down. Ben then remembers that he has a little brother, Nathan. All this time, the witch had made him forget about Nathan.
Ben and Mallory go to the tree to rescue their siblings. As Ben rescues Nathan and Lily, Liam arrives and rams his car into the witch. Later, Ben and Mallory kiss goodbye, and she puts a flower in his hair before leaving to give sailing lessons. Ben notices the flower is fake, revealing that the witch is alive and is now possessing Mallory, who is alone with three children.

title: A Cinderella Story: Christmas Wish
tagline: Happily ever after begins with a dream.
overview: Kat is an aspiring singer-songwriter who dreams of making it big. However, her dreams are stalled by her reality: a conniving and cruel stepfamily  and a demoralizing job working as a singing elf at billionaire Terrence Wintergarden’s Santa Land.
plot:
A Cinderella Story: Christmas Wish is a 2019 American musical teen romantic comedy written and directed by Michelle Johnston, and the fifth instalment of the A Cinderella Story film series. Laura Marano stars as an aspiring singer-songwriter and Gregg Sulkin as the wealthy young man who falls for her, with Isabella Gomez, Johannah Newmarch, Lillian Doucet-Roche, Chanelle Peloso, Maddie Phillips and Barclay Hope. It was released digitally on October 15, 2019, followed by a DVD release later that month.

Seventeen-year-old Kat Decker dreams of a music career, but since her father Jason's death she has lived under the control of her cold stepmother Deirdre and spoiled stepsisters Joy and Grace. They treat her as a servant, keep her inheritance and take much of her pay, supposedly for the care of her disabled dog Bruno. Saving to escape, Kat sings at Santa Land, a Christmas theme park, with her best friend Isla, a talented seamstress. There she meets the park's new young Santa, who is secretly Nick Wintergarden, son of the billionaire Terrence Wintergarden and a quiet manager of bands, and he is captivated by her voice.

Deirdre discovers that Terrence was Jason's best friend and schemes to attend his Christmas charity gala as the grieving widow. When his reply invites both Deirdre and Katherine, she plans to have Joy pose as Kat. As Nick and Kat grow closer, he invites her to the gala and reveals who he is, while Kat keeps her own family situation to herself. Isla sews her a copy of an expensive green dress, but her stepfamily steal it and Deirdre burns her invitation. A visit to Nick's home goes badly when his friends, especially his girlfriend Skyler, snub her, and her father's cherished snow globe is broken during a fight with her stepsisters.

When Bruno uncovers Terrence's letter, Kat realises her identity is being stolen and resolves to stop the plan. Isla smuggles her into the gala disguised as one of the elf performers, but she is pushed on stage, stumbles through the routine and ends up filling in as the Snow Queen. Nick, who has broken up with Skyler, finds her and encourages her to pursue her dream for her father's sake, and she wins over the audience with a new original song. Introduced to Terrence, Kat explains her situation; he sends Deirdre and her daughters away, offers to support her in memory of his friend, and Kat and Nick finally share a dance.

title: Archive
overview: Archive is a 2020 science fiction thriller directed by Gavin Rothery. Set in 2038, it follows George Almore, a scientist working in a remote facility on developing a true human-equivalent artificial intelligence. George’s goal is deeply personal: to recreate his deceased wife through advanced AI and robotics technology.George has created several prototypes of androids designed to house his wife’s consciousness. He is in the final stages of perfecting the latest model, which is almost indistinguishable from a real human. Throughout the film, George struggles with the ethical and emotional challenges of his project, as well as the risks involved in pushing the boundaries of technology.As George interacts with the android, named J3, it becomes clear that the line between human and machine is blurring. J3 shows moments of self-awareness and emotional responses, raising questions about consciousness and identity.Meanwhile, George is hiding his true motive—his desperate desire to reunite with his wife, who passed away years earlier. His work is secretive, and the risks of his experiment extend beyond technical difficulties to psychological and moral dilemmas.The film explores themes such as grief, love, loss, the nature of consciousness, and the ethical implications of artificial intelligence. It probes the question of whether recreating a loved one digitally can truly replace the original person or if it’s a haunting illusion.
plot:
Archive is a 2020 British science fiction film written and directed by Gavin Rothery in his directorial debut. Set in 2038, it stars Theo James as George Almore, a robotics engineer, with Stacy Martin, Rhona Mitra, Peter Ferdinando, Lia Williams and Toby Jones. Its planned premiere at South by Southwest in March 2020 was canceled because of the COVID-19 pandemic, and it was instead released digitally and in limited theaters in the United States on 10 July 2020.

George's wife, Jules, has been killed in a car accident, but her consciousness has been preserved by a company called Archive, whose technology lets George speak with her by video for a limited total of about 200 hours. Working alone at a remote, snowbound research facility in Japan on a project for his employer, George secretly pursues a personal goal: building a robot body capable of holding Jules's consciousness permanently. He has already made two prototypes. J1 is a crude, childlike machine, while J2 has the mind of a teenager and grows jealous of George's work on the third, nearly complete model, J3, increasingly behaving unpredictably.

Representatives from Archive come to inspect the device storing Jules's mind, notice that it has been tampered with and suspect that George is stealing their intellectual property. George finishes the J3 robot, which is strikingly humanlike. Confronted with the realization that she will never become anything more than she is, J2 destroys herself by walking into a lake, and Archive retrieves the robot and threatens to sue George's employer. When his boss discovers his secret project, she fires him. In a final call with Jules, George ends by saying he will see her soon, and J3, overhearing, realizes that he intends to overwrite her consciousness with Jules's. As George races to complete the transfer before he loses access to the facility, the film builds toward a revelation that reframes everything he believes about his situation and his wife's death.

Archive received generally favorable reviews. It holds a 78 percent approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus says it executes its fairly basic program efficiently while offering an engaging meditation on love and human nature, and a Metacritic score of 67. Critics particularly praised its production design and atmosphere on a modest budget.

title: Yaksha: Ruthless Operations
overview: Nicknamed after a human-devouring spirit, the ruthless leader of an overseas black ops team takes up a dangerous mission in a city riddled with spies.
plot:
Yaksha: Ruthless Operations is a South Korean action thriller film released on December 22, 2022, by Showbox. The movie follows the story of Jang Do-jin (played by Lee Jung-jae), a former special forces operative who becomes embroiled in a conspiracy involving a mysterious organization known as "Yaksha."

The film begins with Jang Do-jin, now living a quiet life as a detective, investigating a series of gruesome murders. As he delves deeper into the case, he discovers that the victims all have one thing in common: they were involved in a top-secret government project codenamed "Yaksha." Intrigued, Do-jin decides to dig deeper and soon finds himself entangled in a web of corruption and deceit.

As Do-jin digs deeper, he encounters a mysterious woman named Yoon (played by Kim Ji-won), who seems to be connected to the Yaksha organization. The two form an uneasy alliance as they navigate the treacherous landscape of government conspiracies and corporate espionage.

The plot thickens as Do-jin uncovers evidence of a massive cover-up involving corrupt government officials, corporate executives, and even some members of his own special forces unit. He soon realizes that Yaksha is not just a project, but a complex network of operatives and agents working to manipulate world events from behind the scenes.

As the stakes escalate, Do-jin finds himself in a cat-and-mouse game with the masterminds behind Yaksha. The action unfolds at breakneck speed, with intense hand-to-hand combat sequences and high-stakes chases through the streets of Seoul.

Throughout the film, Lee Jung-jae delivers a nuanced performance as Jang Do-jin, bringing depth and complexity to his character's struggles against overwhelming odds. Kim Ji-won also shines in her supporting role, adding an air of mystery and intrigue to the plot.

The climax of the film sees Do-jin facing off against the leader of Yaksha, a ruthless and cunning adversary who will stop at nothing to achieve their goals. The final confrontation is intense and suspenseful, with both characters engaging in a battle of wits and physical prowess.

Ultimately, Do-jin emerges victorious, but not without scars. As he reflects on the events that transpired, he realizes that the true enemy was not Yaksha itself, but the corrupt system that enabled its existence. The film concludes on a somber note, with Do-jin vowing to continue fighting against injustice and corruption.

Overall, Yaksha: Ruthless Operations is a gripping action thriller that explores themes of power, corruption, and the blurred lines between right and wrong. With its breakneck pace, intricate plot, and strong performances from its leads, this film is sure to keep viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end.

title: Follow Me
overview: A social media personality travels with his friends to Moscow to capture new content for his successful VLOG. Always pushing the limits and catering to a growing audience, they enter a cold world of mystery, excess, and danger. When the lines between real life and social media are blurred, the group must fight to escape, and survive.
plot:
No Escape, released internationally as Follow Me, is a 2020 American horror thriller written and directed by Will Wernick. Keegan Allen stars as a social media celebrity whose overseas birthday adventure turns into a nightmare, with Holland Roden, Denzel Whitaker, Ronen Rubinstein, Pasha D. Lychnikoff, George Janko and Siya. It was released in theaters and on demand and digital platforms on September 18, 2020.

Cole Turner is an image-obsessed internet star whose channel, "Escape From Reality", has millions of followers who watch him livestream his thrill-seeking adventures. To celebrate the channel's tenth anniversary, Cole, his girlfriend Erin and his friends Dash, Sam and Thomas travel to Moscow for an extreme escape room arranged by Dash with the help of Alexei Koslov, a wealthy Russian fan. After a night out at a seedy club, where they are threatened by a pair of local gangsters, the group returns to Alexei's mansion.

On the day of the game, Alexei hooks Cole's phone up to the surveillance cameras so that his followers can watch live, and warns the friends that the experience will be extreme and unpredictable. Blindfolded, they are led to separate rooms. Cole wakes beside the body of a dead soldier and must cut it open to retrieve a key. He then finds his friends trapped in realistic, deadly contraptions and frees them one by one, solving puzzles to save Thomas and Dash and then Sam, and finally smashing open a tank in which Erin is drowning.

Convinced that the game is truly dangerous, they flee, but are captured by Andrei, one of the gangsters from the club, who kills Alexei's girlfriend Viktoria and knocks Cole out. Cole wakes alone in a cell and watches on screens as his friends are apparently tortured and murdered for the entertainment of Andrei's own audience. He learns that Alexei is working with the gangsters and watches helplessly as Erin is shot.

Escaping through a duct, Cole finds Alexei waiting for him in a dark room, filming him on his phone, and in a rage beats him to death. The lights come on to reveal Erin and all his friends alive: the entire ordeal was an elaborate, staged surprise for his anniversary. They stare in horror at Alexei's body as Cole's livestream audience floods the chat with shocked messages, and Cole realises that he has killed a man for nothing.

The film received mixed to negative reviews, with 38% approval on Rotten Tomatoes from a small sample of critics, and JoBlo.com rated it four out of ten.

title: The High Note
tagline: You've got to start at the bottom before you take it from the top.
overview: Set in the dazzling world of the LA music scene comes the story of Grace Davis, a superstar whose talent, and ego, have reached unbelievable heights. Maggie is Grace’s overworked personal assistant who’s stuck running errands, but still aspires to her childhood dream of becoming a music producer. When Grace’s manager presents her with a choice that could alter the course of her career, Maggie and Grace come up with a plan that could change their lives forever.
plot:
Maggie Sherwoode is the longtime personal assistant to legendary R&B singer Grace Davis, who still has a successful touring career despite not releasing new material for a decade. Also an aspiring music producer, Maggie remixes Grace's songs in her free time. Grace's egocentric manager, Jack Robertson, believes that her time has passed and she should accept a Las Vegas residency and release live albums rather than record new material.
At a grocery store, Maggie meets aspiring musician David Cliff, watching him perform outdoors. He invites her to a party at his house, where to her surprise she learns that despite slumming it as a musician he is quite wealthy. Impressed by his voice, Maggie lies about being a professional producer and offers to work with him on an album. David accepts and they begin work together with Maggie coaching him through his nerves.
Grace is displeased when a famous music producer modernizes one of her songs, remixing it with excessive synths and pop elements. Appalled, Maggie shows her own version of the song, and she releases Maggie's version, without payment or credit. While pleased to be producing for her, Jack pulls her aside to reveal how her tactlessness ruined potential future deals.
When Grace later expresses her interest in recording a new album to her record label, they discourage her, pushing her towards the Vegas residency. When Maggie encourages Grace to disregard the label and create new material, Grace lectures her on how women of her age ("over 40") and race rarely succeed in releasing new material after successful earlier careers.
Maggie and David begin a romance as recording for his demo comes to a close. At the same time, she learns that Ariana Grande has backed out of opening for Grace's album launch. She initially books Dan Deakins to open for Grace before realizing it would be the perfect place for David to perform his songs. She enlists Dan's assistant to help but is surprised when Dan himself, after listening to David's songs, decides to step away to allow him to perform.
On the night of the party, Maggie tells Jack and Grace that Dan has backed out and promises to fix it. She then asks David, who believed they were going on a date, to sing. Hearing that the party is for Grace Davis, David leaves in a huff, refusing to perform. Maggie tells Jack and Grace she was unable to deliver a backup performer and Grace berates her, mocking her ambitions to become a producer when she cannot even succeed as an assistant before firing her.
Maggie moves back home with her father Max, a radio DJ, and starts planning her future. After encouragement from him, she reaches out to David to continue work on their album and to Grace to thank her for her time working for her. At the same time, Grace realizes that she misses Maggie, who was a faithful assistant who never used her.
Grace arrives at Maggie's home and offers a roundabout apology.

title: Togo
overview: The untold true story set in the winter of 1925 that takes you across the treacherous terrain of the Alaskan tundra for an exhilarating and uplifting adventure that will test the strength, courage and determination of one man, Leonhard Seppala, and his lead sled dog, Togo.
plot:
Togo is a 2019 American biographical drama film directed by Ross Katz and produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The film is based on the true story of Leonhard Seppala, a Finnish-Swedish sled dog breeder who played a crucial role in saving the life of a young boy during a diphtheria outbreak in Nome, Alaska.

The film begins with Leonhard Seppala (played by Willem Dafoe), a struggling sled dog breeder living on his farm in Nome. He is married to Rose (played by Anne Hathaway), and they have two children together. The story takes a dramatic turn when the town of Nome is hit by a diphtheria outbreak, which claims the lives of many residents.

The situation becomes dire as the town's medical supplies are running low, and the only way to transport medicine from Bluff, Alaska (about 674 miles away) is through sled dogs. The US Army sends a team led by Captain Balto (played by Paul Giamatti), who is tasked with delivering the diphtheria serum to Nome.

Leonhard Seppala, determined to save his community, decides to take on the challenge of leading the sled dog team himself. He chooses his most experienced and strongest dogs, including Togo (played by a combination of two dogs: Buck and Tundra), to make the perilous journey.

As the team sets out, they face numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, harsh weather conditions, and the risk of losing their dogs in the process. Despite these obstacles, Seppala's determination and expertise as a sled dog breeder keep the team moving forward.

Meanwhile, Captain Balto is struggling with his own doubts about leading the mission. He is haunted by a past failure to deliver supplies during a previous expedition, which led to the death of several people in Nome.

As the journey progresses, Seppala's team faces numerous setbacks, including a near-fatal accident that leaves Togo injured. However, Seppala refuses to give up and continues to push his dogs forward, driven by his love for his community and his determination to save lives.

In the end, Seppala's team successfully delivers the diphtheria serum to Nome, saving countless lives in the process. The film ends with a poignant moment of reflection, as Seppala looks back on the journey and realizes that it was not just about delivering supplies but also about the bond between humans and animals.

Throughout the film, Willem Dafoe delivers a powerful performance as Leonhard Seppala, capturing the complexity and depth of his character. The chemistry between him and Anne Hathaway is undeniable, adding an emotional layer to the story. Paul Giamatti's portrayal of Captain Balto is equally impressive, conveying the weight of responsibility and the personal stakes involved in leading the mission.

Overall, Togo is a heartwarming and inspiring film that celebrates the human spirit and the unbreakable bond between humans and animals.
