title: The Survivor
tagline: Some fight to win. He fought to live.
overview: Harry Haft is a boxer who fought fellow prisoners in the concentration camps to survive. Haunted by the memories and his guilt, he attempts to use high-profile fights against boxing legends like Rocky Marciano as a way to find his first love again.
plot:
The Survivor is a 2021 biographical drama directed by Barry Levinson from a screenplay by Justine Juel Gillmer, based on Alan Scott Haft's book about his father, the boxer Harry Haft. Ben Foster stars as Haft, with Vicky Krieps, Billy Magnussen, Peter Sarsgaard, John Leguizamo, Danny DeVito and Dar Zuzovsky. It was produced by New Mandate Films, Bron Studios and Creative Wealth Media, with a score by Hans Zimmer.

The story moves between the Holocaust and its aftermath. At Auschwitz, the young Polish Jew Harry survives because the SS officer Dietrich Schneider (Magnussen), after seeing him strike another officer, decides to turn him into a fighter, staging bouts against fellow prisoners for the entertainment and wagers of the camp's officers; winning means food, losing means death. In 1949, Harry is a struggling heavyweight in the United States, still haunted by guilt and obsessed with finding Leah (Zuzovsky), the love he lost before the war. He hopes that a high-profile fight against the rising star Rocky Marciano will make him famous enough for her to find him. He confides his wartime story to the reporter Emory Anderson (Sarsgaard), but when the article is published, members of the Jewish community condemn him as a traitor. Marciano's trainer Charlie Goldman (DeVito) offers him a few days of training at a camp upstate, alongside his trainer Pepe (Leguizamo), so that he will not be destroyed in the ring. Miriam Wofsoniker (Krieps), who works for an agency helping survivors find lost relatives, assists in his search and gradually becomes part of his new life, while memories of the camp, triggered by everyday moments such as fireworks, keep intruding. Harry ultimately loses to Marciano but begins to come to terms with the past.

To play the emaciated prisoner, Foster lost 62 pounds, after which production paused for five weeks so he could regain weight for the postwar scenes. Filming began in February 2019, with locations in Hungary as well as New York and Savannah. The film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on 13 September 2021 and debuted on HBO and HBO Max on 27 April 2022. Reviews were positive, with an 86% Rotten Tomatoes rating and a Metacritic score of 71; critics singled out Foster's performance, and RogerEbert.com praised the film's layered characters and humor. It was nominated for the Emmy Award for Outstanding Television Movie.

title: Fatherhood
overview: A widowed new dad copes with doubts, fears, heartache and dirty diapers as he sets out to raise his daughter on his own. Inspired by a true story.
plot:
Fatherhood is a 2021 American comedy-drama film directed by Paul Weitz, who wrote the screenplay with Dana Stevens, based on Matthew Logelin's 2011 memoir Two Kisses for Maddy: A Memoir of Loss and Love. Kevin Hart stars as a young widower raising his daughter alone, with Alfre Woodard, Frankie Faison, Lil Rel Howery, DeWanda Wise, Anthony Carrigan, Melody Hurd and Paul Reiser. Originally intended for theatrical release by Sony Pictures, it was sold to Netflix during the COVID-19 pandemic and released on June 18, 2021.

Matt Logelin and his wife, Liz, childhood sweethearts, eagerly prepare for the birth of their first child. Just after their daughter, Maddy, is born, Liz suffers a pulmonary embolism and dies. Devastated, Matt resolves to raise Maddy on his own, despite the doubts of friends and family. Liz's mother, Marion, with whom he has a strained relationship, is the most concerned. When Matt turns down her offer to stay for months to help, and refuses to move back to Minnesota where both families live, she warns him that Maddy will need family and female role models.

Matt struggles at first to balance his grief, a demanding full-time job and the endless demands of an infant, while facing condescension from people who assume a father cannot be the primary parent. With help from friends and other parents, he finds his footing. Years later, Maddy is a confident, tomboyish schoolgirl. Matt is set up with a woman, played by Wise, whose name echoes his late wife's, and they begin dating. Maddy soon grows fond of her, but when Maddy is hurt at school and Matt misses the calls because he is with her, he blames himself and ends the relationship, upsetting his daughter.

On a trip to Minnesota for Marion's birthday, Maddy delights in staying in her mother's childhood room and learning about Liz, and asks to remain with her grandparents. Convinced that he has failed to understand what she needs, Matt reluctantly leaves her there. Back at work, on the verge of a promotion and about to leave on a business trip abroad, he is overwhelmed by thoughts of his daughter and returns to Minnesota. He reconciles with Maddy and, with Marion's blessing, brings her home, where he also rekindles his romance.

Fatherhood received mixed reviews. Rotten Tomatoes reported 67% approval, its consensus crediting the strong cast with giving the fact-based story real emotional resonance, and Metacritic gave it a score of 53.

title: Aquaslash
overview: To celebrate their graduation, the teenagers from Valley Hills High School have organized an ’80s-themed party at the old Wet Valley water park. Things turn gruesome when it's revealed that a mysterious maniac has inserted giant razor blades into one of the water slides. The water park thus becomes the backdrop for a bloodbath (literally), and everyone is a suspect...
plot:
Aquaslash is a 2019 Canadian slasher film directed by Renaud Gauthier, who co-wrote it with Philip Kalin. Nicolas Fontaine, Brittany Drisdelle, Madeline Harvey, Lanisa Dawn, Paul Zinno, Nick Walker and Chip Chuipka star in a deliberately retro horror comedy set at a water park, where a killer targets a group of recent high school graduates competing for a cash prize in a water slide race.

The film opens one night at the Wet Valley Water Park, where two teenagers are murdered by a machete-wielding attacker. Some time later, the class of 2018 from Valley Hills High arrives for a weekend-long graduation celebration at the park, which is owned by the sleazy Paul Wilkinson. The large cast of characters includes Josh, a member of a band called the Blades, and his bandmates; Paul's wife Priscilla, rumored to choose one graduate to sleep with every year; Alice, a graduate with whom Paul is having an affair; park employee Tommy; an elderly pool cleaner named Conrad; and Kimberly, Tommy's girlfriend and Josh's former girlfriend. When Josh and Kimberly have sex in the showers, another student secretly films them and the video is sent to their classmates during the Blades' performance, leading Tommy to punch Josh and lose his job.

Tensions grow as Josh's father, a real estate developer, negotiates to buy the park and is later shot dead by an unseen attacker. Meanwhile, a mysterious figure secretly installs a pair of large, crossed metal blades inside one of the park's water slides. The next day the park's annual competition begins, in which teams of three race down three slides into the pool below for a cash prize. Tommy warns that one of the slides is unsafe, but nobody listens. When the first teams launch, those who take the sabotaged slide are cut to pieces, and the pool fills with blood as panic spreads and the survivors struggle to stop the race and identify the killer before more victims are sent down the chute.

Reception was predominantly negative, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting that only 14% of seven critics' reviews were positive. Some genre critics enjoyed its gleefully gory set piece: Arrow in the Head said the extended slide sequence earns the film a recommendation, and Dread Central called it an irreverent retro slasher throwback. Film School Rejects dismissed it as a barely watchable misfire with occasional unintentional laughs.

title: Nine Days
overview: A reclusive man conducts a series of interviews with human souls for a chance to be born.
plot:
Will is an arbiter who judges souls before they inhabit bodies in the living. He lives in an isolated house in the middle of a desert landscape, interviewing candidate souls for the opportunity to be born. If they are not selected, Will gives them an experience of their choosing to enact before their existence is erased. His only company is Kyo, who acts as a sort of supervisor, making sure Will selects the best candidate and assisting him with the process. Unlike Will, who spent a previous lifetime as a living being, Kyo was never alive. Will spends his days watching and taking notes on a multitude of television screens, each displaying the life of a different individual that Will has previously selected. His favorite is Amanda, a 28-year-old violin prodigy. While observing Amanda drive to a major concert, Will sees her suddenly speed on the highway. Amanda crashes into an overpass and dies.
As Will grapples with Amanda's death, candidates begin arriving to interview for the vacancy Amanda left behind, a process that will take nine days. He asks the candidates simple questions about life and has them take notes on what they like or dislike about the lives of others who were chosen. Will is particularly intrigued by Emma, who displays heightened empathy and curiosity despite showing little interest in the selection process. Over the course of the nine days, most of the candidates are dismissed for various reasons, such as self-consciousness and lack of respect for suffering. Will does his best to recreate life events for the failed candidates, such as walking on the beach or bike-riding through a city, before the candidates disappear forever.
Kyo invites another nearby interviewer to meet with Will, as she had previously selected Amanda's cousin for birth. She shows Will a tape shortly after Amanda's death, which reveals that Amanda left behind a suicide note before her crash. Kyo attempts to help Will get over her death, but Will continues to watch tapes from her life, unable to understand why she did it. Will has told Emma that he cannot tell her anything about his previous life, but in response to her showing concern for him, he now indicates that in his previous life, he once gave a theater performance that made him feel alive but never pursued his passion after that. He reacts angrily when another candidate, Alex, points out Will's hypocrisy for judging people's lives when he never did anything meaningful with his own life.
The candidates are narrowed down to two: Emma and Kane. While Emma is carefree and sees the best in people, Kane is more pessimistic, recognizing the evil in the world and showing resolve to fight back against it. Despite Kyo recommending that Will pick Emma, he chooses Kane to be born. When Will offers Emma a last experience, she writes something down that Will says he cannot do. Emma then declines a last experience and opts to walk across the desert until she disappears.

title: Escape from Mogadishu
tagline: A city in revolt, we must escape.
overview: Diplomats from the North and South Korean embassies in Somalia attempt a daring joint escape from Mogadishu when the outbreak of civil war leaves them stranded.
plot:
Escape from Mogadishu (Korean: Mogadisyu) is a 2021 South Korean political action thriller directed by Ryoo Seung-wan, based on real events during the Somali Civil War. It stars Kim Yoon-seok as South Korean ambassador Han Sin-seong, Zo In-sung as the embassy counselor and intelligence officer Kang Dae-jin, Huh Joon-ho as North Korean ambassador Rim Yong-su and Koo Kyo-hwan as North Korean counselor Tae Jun-ki, with Kim So-jin and Jung Man-sik. The film was shot entirely in Morocco in the second half of 2019.

In 1990, both North and South Korea are lobbying for admission to the United Nations and competing to win the support of Somalia's government under President Siad Barre. The rival embassies in Mogadishu sabotage each other at every turn, while the country slides into civil war between the government and rebels led by Mohamed Farrah Aidid. When the rebels enter the capital, fighting erupts across the city, and both delegations realize they must flee immediately.

Their attempts to reach the airport fail for lack of papers, and the North Koreans, after their embassy is ransacked and the Chinese embassy is found abandoned, make their way through the chaos to the South Korean compound, where Han lets them in despite deep mutual suspicion. Living under one roof, the two groups must set aside ideological hostility and propaganda games to survive. When the Italian embassy offers places on a Red Cross evacuation flight to Kenya, which the North Koreans are not eligible for, Han claims they are defecting. The diplomats and their families then armor their cars with bags of dirt and books, tie white flags to them and set out on a dangerous drive across the war-torn city, trying to reach the Italian embassy before gunfire cuts them down.

The film explores how shared danger can bridge the divide between the two Koreas, combining tense action with a humane portrait of the people caught in a foreign war.

Released in South Korea on July 28, 2021, Escape from Mogadishu topped the local box office and became the highest-grossing Korean film of 2021, with about 3.6 million admissions and 29 million dollars worldwide. It was selected as South Korea's entry for the Academy Award for Best International Feature Film. Critics responded positively, with 95 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 71.

title: Seven Days War
overview: In the town of Saima, when summer is about to begin, a group of six high school students intend to live a secret adventure by spending seven carefree days in a ruined mining facility.
plot:
Seven Days War (Japanese: Bokura no Nanoka-kan Sensō) is a 2019 Japanese animated coming-of-age action drama directed by Yūta Murano from a screenplay by Ichirō Ōkouchi, produced by the studio Ajiadō and distributed in Japan by Gaga and Kadokawa. It is a new adaptation of Osamu Sōda's 1985 novel, the first of his long-running Bokura series, previously filmed in live action in 1988. Updating the story some thirty years to 2020, the film changes the kanji numeral in the title to an Arabic "7"; Sōda approved the remake on condition that it keep the series' themes of challenging adults and humorous battles. The setting moved to a former coal-mining town in Hokkaido. The voice cast is led by Takumi Kitamura and Kyōko Yoshine, with Rie Miyazawa in a special appearance.

In 2020, Mamoru Suzuhara (Kitamura) is a bookish, solitary high-school second-year in the old mining town of Satomiya, steeped in military history. Shortly before the summer holidays he learns that his childhood friend and neighbour Aya Chiyono (Yoshine), whom he has long loved, is about to move to Tokyo, because her father, a local politician, plans to run for a Tokyo seat. Aya, who wanted at least to spend her birthday a week later in her hometown, accepts Mamoru's proposal to run away, and dressing it up as a "camp", she invites classmates until six of them are living in a disused mine on a hill. There they find Malet, a Thai child hiding from immigration officers after being separated from her parents. When officials arrive and lock the teenagers in, Mamoru shields Malet and the six are drawn into a seven-day "war" against the adults. Following Mamoru's tactics, they thwart a search, and post videos of their stand online to draw onlookers. Aya's father, his secretary and a construction company run by the father of Aya's best friend Kaori try to break in, and when the secretary exposes the group's old secrets on social media, tensions erupt. Eventually each confesses the feelings they had kept hidden, including Aya, who reveals that she is gay, and the reunited friends launch a final plan to save Malet.

The film opened in Japan on 13 December 2019 and was selected for the feature competition at the 2020 Annecy festival. It won the award for best animated feature at the Sitges Film Festival, and in France, where Eurozoom released it as 7 Jours in 2021, Télérama called it a successful adaptation of a classic of Japanese youth literature, while Le Monde found its themes too numerous.

title: In Full Bloom
overview: Set shortly after the end of World War II, a philosophical boxing drama of two fighters from opposite worlds (USA and Japan) who are pulled together for a questionable fight arranged by their unscrupulous managers and the Yakuza.
plot:
In Full Bloom is a 2019 American period sports drama written and directed by Adam VillaSeñor and Reza Ghassemi in their feature debut; the pair also shot and edited it. Set in Japan shortly after World War II, it stars Tyler Wood as the American boxer Clint Sullivan and Yusuke Ogasawara as the Japanese champion Masahiro, with Hiroyuki Watanabe as the former champion Tetsuro Tokugawa, S. Scott McCracken as Clint's manager Silas, Timothy V. Murphy as Roane, Hazuki Kato as the courtesan Asami, and Stefanie Estes and Navid Negahban. The score is by Andrew Kawczynski.

With resentment of the American occupation still widespread, a light-heavyweight title fight between the washed-up Clint and the undefeated Masahiro takes on a weight far beyond sport, charged by bitter references to Pearl Harbor and Hiroshima. Clint, who fought in the war and is haunted by what he saw there, learns that Silas, his smooth-talking and unscrupulous manager, has made a deal with a murderous yakuza betting syndicate for him to throw the fight. Too proud to go along, Clint clings to his last shreds of self-respect, even if refusing could cost him his life.

Masahiro, meanwhile, prepares for the bout by seeking out Tetsuro, a reclusive former champion living in a remote, snowbound retreat. The old man is reluctant to become a teacher but soon tests his pupil with unconventional training: catching fish by hand in an icy stream, hunting blindfolded in the woods and resisting the seductions of Asami, while offering Zen-like counsel such as the warning that the only enemy is ego. The film moves back and forth in time, revealing both fighters' histories in flashbacks and letting each speak his innermost thoughts in whispered voice-over, before their parallel journeys meet in the ring.

In Full Bloom premiered at the Oldenburg International Film Festival in September 2019, where it won the festival's top prize, the German Independence Award, and it later received the Grand Jury Award for a feature at the 2020 Mammoth Film Festival before reaching American audiences in 2020 and 2021, with the mixed martial artist Henry Cejudo joining as an executive producer. Critics compared its lyrical style to Terrence Malick's. The Hollywood Reporter called it an impressively polished, ambitious debut despite muddled plotting, portentous dialogue and uneven acting, singling out the climactic match, and Film Threat praised it as a visually striking, soulful meditation on combat.

title: The Cleansing Hour
tagline: The perfect internet hoax just went to hell
overview: Two millennial entrepreneurs stage elaborate fake exorcisms on social media until one of their girlfriends becomes possessed by a demon.
plot:
The Cleansing Hour is a 2019 American horror film directed by Damien LeVeck, a feature-length adaptation of his 2016 short film of the same name about a staged televised exorcism that goes horribly wrong. It stars Ryan Guzman as Max, Kyle Gallner as Drew and Alix Angelis as Lane.

Childhood friends Max and Drew run The Cleansing Hour, a popular livestream on which "Father Max" exorcises a different possessed person in every episode. Every possession is fake, carefully scripted and staged to win followers and sell merchandise, and Max is obsessed with growing the audience. When the actress hired for the latest episode fails to show up, Drew's fiancée Lane, unhappy but supportive, agrees to play the possessed woman. Once the stream begins, however, it becomes clear that Lane has truly been possessed. The demon kills the crew one by one until only Max and Drew remain, and forces them to confess their secrets before the growing audience. Max admits that the show is a fraud, then reveals that as a boy at their Catholic school he killed a sadistic nun who beat them, to save Drew. He also confesses that he had once been a priest but left after witnessing abuses within the priesthood go unpunished, starting the show in the belief that it would harm no one. Drew cuts the feed, believing the demon wants to humiliate the Church, then restores it after using clues from its speech and a database to identify it as Aamon. The demon forces a final revelation, that Max slept with Lane before she met Drew, which nearly derails them, but they go on to perform the rite and drive it out of Lane, leaving the friendship in ruins. The demon then reappears and reveals that it was never Aamon but Lucifer himself, who used Lane to reach the stream and its more than 17 million viewers, whom it now possesses. The possessed viewers attack those around them, including the President of the United States, who is attacked by his own son, and the closing credits show chaos spreading around the world.

The film screened at the Strasbourg European Fantastic Film Festival on 18 September 2019 before its world premiere at Fantastic Fest, and was released on Shudder on 8 October 2020. It received generally positive reviews, holding 73% on Rotten Tomatoes; critics praised its cinematography and practical effects, though some found it too similar to earlier possession films such as The Exorcist.

title: The Heist of the Century
tagline: The Story Of The Theft That Made History
overview: In 2006, a group of thieves performed what is considered one of the most famous and smart bank heists in the history of Argentina. How they robbed the Rio bank is as surprising as what happened afterwards. This is their story.
plot:
The Heist of the Century (Spanish: El robo del siglo) is a 2020 Argentine heist comedy thriller film directed by Ariel Winograd, based on the real robbery of the Banco Río branch in Acassuso, Buenos Aires Province, on 13 January 2006, when six thieves carrying replica weapons took 23 hostages and emptied 147 safe deposit boxes. Diego Peretti stars as the mastermind Fernando Araujo and Guillermo Francella as Mario Vitette Sellanes, "the man in the gray suit", with Pablo Rago, Rafael Ferro, Mariano Argento and Luis Luque as the police negotiator Miguel Sileo.

Fernando Araujo, a painter and Brazilian jiu-jitsu expert, tells his psychoanalyst about another of his passions: robbing banks. Sheltering from the rain one day, he notices the Banco Río across the street, and a plan he and his acquaintance Sebastián had abandoned is revived when they discover a storm drain running near the bank. Araujo recruits three more criminals, the gang leader "the Doc", the street thief Beto and, through the Doc, the Uruguayan Vitette, while "the Paisa" is hired to drive their getaway vehicle. After studying the sewers, they strike at midday: Araujo, in a blond wig, and Beto enter the bank, Vitette, calling himself "Walter", and the Doc take the staff and customers hostage, and the rest fill bags with cash while Sebastián waits in a tunnel he has dug. As hundreds of police officers and sharpshooters surround the building, Vitette stalls negotiations with Sileo for hours, releasing a few hostages and ordering pizzas, until the gang slips away through the drain. When the police finally storm in, they find the vault emptied, the replica guns and a sign mocking the "rich neighborhood" and declaring that it was only money. The thieves split the loot and go their separate ways, but months later Beto's wife, embittered after he leaves her for another woman, informs on them. One by one they are arrested: Beto, the Paisa, Sebastián, Vitette, who surrenders, and finally Araujo, caught by gendarmes during a spiritual retreat in the mountains of San Juan. Later, Araujo walks out of prison to find Vitette waiting for him in a red car.

The script was co-written by producer Alex Zito and the real Araujo, and filming took place in Buenos Aires and Mendoza in 2019. Released by Warner Bros. on 16 January 2020, the film had the second-biggest opening day for an Argentine film, sold about two million tickets and received positive reviews.

title: The Marvels
overview: Carol Danvers, Monica Rambeau, and Kamala Khan trade places with each other every time they use their powers and must team up to fix their problem.
plot:
The Marvels is a Marvel Studios superhero film from 2023, based on Marvel Comics. The sequel to Captain Marvel (2019) and a continuation of the miniseries Ms. Marvel (2022), it is the 33rd film in the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Nia DaCosta directed and co-wrote it with Megan McDonnell and Elissa Karasik. Brie Larson stars as Carol Danvers, with Teyonah Parris as Monica Rambeau, Iman Vellani as Kamala Khan, Zawe Ashton as Dar-Benn and Samuel L. Jackson as Nick Fury.

After Danvers destroyed the Supreme Intelligence, the artificial intelligence ruling the Kree, the resulting civil war left their home world, Hala, stripped of air, water and sunlight over thirty years, and the Kree came to call her "the Annihilator". Their new leader, Dar-Benn, finds one of a pair of legendary Quantum Bands and uses it to tear open a new jump point in the network used for travel across space, disrupting the whole system. When Danvers and Captain Monica Rambeau touch two affected jump points, they swap places with each other and with Kamala Khan, the teenage hero on Earth who wears the other Band, and the three fight Kree attackers, wrecking Kamala's home. Rambeau concludes that their light-based powers are entangled, swapping them whenever all use them at once.

The trio reunite at a Skrull refugee colony on the planet Tarnax, which Danvers helped found, where peace talks with the Kree collapse and Dar-Benn opens a jump point that drains Tarnax's atmosphere to replenish Hala. Calling themselves "the Marvels", the heroes realise that Dar-Benn is targeting worlds dear to Danvers and that her ruptures threaten the entire universe. On the water world Aladna, where people communicate in song, they warn Prince Yan, Danvers's husband by diplomatic arrangement, but Dar-Benn steals the planet's water. On Fury's space station, Danvers's Flerken Goose gives birth to kittens that swallow the crew to carry them to safety. Dar-Benn seizes Kamala's Band and is destroyed by using both at once, opening a rift between realities. Rambeau seals it but is trapped on the other side, while Danvers rekindles Hala's sun. Kamala begins recruiting young heroes, starting with Kate Bishop, and a mid-credits scene finds Rambeau in a parallel universe.

The film premiered in November 2023. Reviews were mixed, with 63% on Rotten Tomatoes, and it became the lowest-grossing film in the franchise, earning $206.1 million worldwide; Deadline Hollywood estimated its losses at $237 million.

title: Paranormal Activity: Next of Kin
overview: Margot, a documentary filmmaker, heads to a secluded Amish community in the hopes of learning about her long-lost mother and extended family. Following a string of strange occurrences and discoveries, she comes to realize this community may not be what it seems.
plot:
Paranormal Activity: Next of Kin is a 2021 American supernatural horror film directed by William Eubank and written by Christopher Landon, produced by Jason Blum and series creator Oren Peli. A reboot and the seventh installment in the Paranormal Activity series, it stars Emily Bader as Margot, a documentary filmmaker, with Roland Buck III as her cameraman Chris, Dan Lippert as sound recordist Dale, Henry Ayres-Brown as Samuel and Tom Nowicki as Jacob. Like the earlier films, it is presented as found footage.

Margot, who was abandoned as a baby outside a hospital by her mother, Sarah, sets out with her friend Chris to make a documentary about her origins. Through a genetics website she connects with Samuel, a young relative from an Amish community, who leads Margot, Chris and Dale to the remote farm where her mother grew up. Jacob, the community's patriarch and Margot's grandfather, welcomes them, explaining that Sarah left after becoming pregnant and is presumed dead.

During their stay, strange events multiply: a little girl speaks cryptically about Sarah, Margot sees a spirit in her mother's old room, and the crew secretly witnesses a nocturnal ritual in which a two-headed goat is sacrificed. Breaking into the community's forbidden church, Margot and Chris discover paintings of the demon Asmodeus and a deep pit. They soon learn that the settlement is not truly Amish and that its members descend from a Norwegian village that trapped a demon inside a woman's body, passing it from mother to daughter through the generations. Margot realizes that she was lured to the farm because she is the next in line, and her friends must try to save her as the community prepares to complete the ritual.

The film moves the franchise away from its suburban home setting toward folk horror, with more polished visuals than earlier entries.

Originally planned for theatrical release, the film was delayed by the COVID-19 pandemic and premiered on Paramount+ on October 29, 2021. It received generally negative reviews, with 32 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 37.

title: Dragon Ball Super: Super Hero
original_title: ドラゴンボール超 スーパーヒーロー
tagline: A super awakening and calamity is born.
overview: The Red Ribbon Army, an evil organization that was once destroyed by Goku in the past, has been reformed by a group of people who have created new and mightier Androids, Gamma 1 and Gamma 2, and seek vengeance against Goku and his family.
plot:
Dragon Ball Super: Super Hero is a 2022 Japanese animated martial arts fantasy adventure film and the sequel to Dragon Ball Super: Broly (2018). The twenty-first animated feature in the Dragon Ball franchise, it was the first to be produced mainly in CGI and the last Dragon Ball film made under the supervision of creator Akira Toriyama before his death in March 2024; Toriyama supplied the concept and character designs. Its Japanese voice cast includes Masako Nozawa, Toshio Furukawa, Yuko Minaguchi, Hiroshi Kamiya and Mamoru Miyano.

Commander Magenta, head of Red Pharmaceuticals, plans to revive the Red Ribbon Army, once led by his late father, Commander Red, before Goku destroyed it more than three decades earlier. With his assistant Carmine, he recruits Dr. Hedo, the superhero-obsessed grandson of Dr. Gero, a convicted grave robber, by convincing him that Bulma's Capsule Corporation is an evil organization bent on world domination. While Goku, Vegeta and Broly train on Beerus's planet, Piccolo, frustrated that Gohan is neglecting his potential, is attacked by the android Gamma 2 and follows him back to the Red Ribbon base. He learns that Hedo has built the androids Gamma 1 and Gamma 2 to defeat Capsule Corporation and has reluctantly used his grandfather's designs to create an improved Cell, known as Cell Max. Unable to reach Goku and Vegeta, Piccolo has the dragon Shenron unlock his full potential. Learning that Magenta plans to kidnap Gohan's daughter Pan to lure him into a trap, Piccolo volunteers to carry out the abduction himself and has Pan play along. Enraged, Gohan storms the base and overpowers Gamma 1 in his "Ultimate" form, while Piccolo unleashes a powerful new transformation against Gamma 2 and convinces him that Magenta has lied about Capsule Corporation. Turning against the Red Ribbon Army, the Gammas side with the heroes, but Magenta unleashes Cell Max, a giant, rampaging monster. Reinforced by Goten, Trunks, Android 18 and Krillin, the heroes fight back; Gamma 2 sacrifices himself in a failed attempt to destroy it, and after Piccolo is beaten, Gohan awakens a new "Beast" form and kills Cell Max with a Special Beam Cannon. Bulma then offers a repentant Hedo and Gamma 1 jobs at Capsule Corporation.

Delayed by a cyberattack at Toei Animation, the film was released in Japan on June 11, 2022, and internationally that August. It received positive reviews and grossed about US$102.5 million worldwide, the second-highest for a Dragon Ball film.

title: Halloween Kills
overview: The nightmare isn't over as unstoppable killer Michael Myers escapes from Laurie Strode's trap to continue his ritual bloodbath. Injured and taken to the hospital, Laurie fights through the pain as she inspires residents of Haddonfield, to rise up against Myers. Taking matters into their own hands, the Strode women and other survivors form a vigilante mob to hunt down Michael and end his reign of terror once and for all.
plot:
Halloween Kills is a 2021 American slasher film from director David Gordon Green, who wrote it with Danny McBride and Scott Teems. It is the sequel to Halloween (2018) and the twelfth entry in the Halloween franchise. Jamie Lee Curtis returns as Laurie Strode alongside Judy Greer as her daughter Karen, Andi Matichak as granddaughter Allyson, Will Patton as Frank Hawkins and Anthony Michael Hall as Tommy Doyle, with James Jude Courtney and Nick Castle sharing the role of Michael Myers.

The story resumes on Halloween night 2018, moments after the previous film. Deputy Hawkins, stabbed and left for dead, is rescued and vows to finish Michael off; a flashback to 1978 shows a young Hawkins accidentally killing his own partner and stopping Dr. Loomis from shooting the captured Michael. While Laurie is rushed into surgery at Haddonfield Memorial Hospital, Michael escapes her burning house, slaughters the firefighters sent to put out the blaze and murders more locals as he heads back into town. At a bar, Tommy and fellow survivors of 1978, Marion Chambers, Lindsey Wallace and Lonnie Elam, are marking the anniversary of his capture when they learn of the killings. Tommy whips up a mob of vengeful townspeople to hunt Michael down, and Allyson joins them with her ex-boyfriend Cameron to avenge her father.

The mob realises Michael is heading for his childhood home, where he kills the current owners. At the hospital, the hysteria turns lethal when the crowd mistakes Lance Tivoli, an escaped mental patient, for Michael and chases him until he leaps to his death, despite Karen's efforts to stop them. Lonnie and Cameron are killed in the Myers house, but Karen stabs Michael with a pitchfork, takes his mask and lures him into the waiting mob, which appears to kill him. Michael rises and massacres them all, including Tommy and former sheriff Leigh Brackett, then kills Karen in his old house as Laurie watches from her hospital window.

Delayed a year by the COVID-19 pandemic, the film premiered at the Venice Film Festival in September 2021 and was released in October simultaneously in theatres and on Peacock. It grossed $133.4 million worldwide, but reviews were mixed, with 38% on Rotten Tomatoes and 42 on Metacritic. It was followed by Halloween Ends.

title: See You Soon
overview: A U.S. soccer star suffers a career-threatening injury in the run-up to the World Cup, and during his recovery, embarks on an epic romance with a Russian single mom.
plot:
See You Soon (Russian: До скорой встречи) is a 2019 American-Russian romantic drama directed by David Mahmoudieh from a screenplay by Jenia Tanaeva and Mike Cestari. Tanaeva, who also produced, makes her screen debut as Lana Kalinina, a Russian single mother, opposite Liam McIntyre as the American soccer star Ryan Hawkes, with Harvey Keitel as Ryan's demanding agent, Poppy Drayton as his fiancée Elise, Oleg Taktarov as Lana's husband Ruslan and Larisa Malevannaya as her grandmother. Mark Isham composed the score, and Tanaeva has said the story was inspired by An Affair to Remember.

Ryan's World Cup hopes collapse when he suffers a potentially career-ending leg injury in a drunk-driving crash. Escaping the media frenzy and leaving behind his materialistic fiancée, he boards a luxury cruise ship to drink away his troubles. Lana, trapped in an unhappy marriage to the abusive, hard-drinking Ruslan, has left her young son Danny in the care of her loving grandmother and taken a temporary job as a bartender on the same ship.

Ryan flirts with her at the bar, and despite their very different lives the two are soon drawn together. After they spend an innocent night on a beach, Lana returns to the ship late and is fired, and the couple head off to a tropical resort, where their romance blossoms. Ryan wants to take the relationship further, but Lana proposes a test: if he still feels the same in two months, he should come and find her in a square in St. Petersburg at the start of the city's White Nights.

Back home, Lana leaves her husband, but a series of misfortunes conspires to keep the lovers apart. Danny suffers a life-threatening head injury, and Ryan is asked by the Make-A-Wish Foundation to visit sick children in a hospital. Through it all, Lana's young son may hold the key to bringing the couple together, and the story builds to Ryan's daring leap across a drawbridge and a triumphant return to the soccer field.

The film premiered on Russian television early in 2019 before Vertical Entertainment gave it a limited theatrical release in the United States on 26 July 2019. Critics were largely dismissive of its contrived plot and computer-generated backdrops: The Hollywood Reporter said it made Cinderella seem grittily realistic, and Variety described it as the best kind of bad movie, while several reviewers were puzzled by Keitel's presence.

title: Violet Evergarden: Eternity and the Auto Memory Doll
original_title: ヴァイオレット・エヴァーガーデン 外伝 - 永遠と自動手記人形 -
overview: Isabella, the daughter of the noble York family, is enrolled in an all-girls academy to be groomed into a dame worthy of nobility. However, she has given up on her future, seeing the prestigious school as nothing more than a prison from the outside world. Her family notices her struggling in her lessons and decides to hire Violet Evergarden to personally tutor her under the guise of a handmaiden.  At first, Isabella treats Violet coldly. Violet seems to be able to do everything perfectly, leading Isabella to assume that she was born with a silver spoon. After some time, Isabella begins to realize that Violet has had her own struggles and starts to open up to her. Isabella soon reveals that she has lost contact with her beloved younger sister, whom she yearns to see again.  Having experienced the power of words through her past clientele, Violet asks if Isabella wishes to write a letter to Taylor. Will Violet be able to help Isabella convey her feelings to her long-lost sister?
plot:
Violet Evergarden: Eternity and the Auto Memory Doll is a 2019 Japanese animated film based on Kana Akatsuki's light novel series Violet Evergarden. Produced by Kyoto Animation and distributed by Shochiku, it was directed by Haruka Fujita from a script by Takaaki Suzuki and Tatsuhiko Urahata. Yui Ishikawa voices Violet, with Minako Kotobuki, Aoi Yūki, Takehito Koyasu, Kouki Uchiyama and Aya Endo in the cast. The film was completed only a day before the arson attack on Kyoto Animation's studio in July 2019, and it was released in Japanese cinemas that September. Netflix began streaming it internationally in April 2020.

Set after the events of the anime series, the film follows Violet, a former child soldier who now works as an Auto Memory Doll, a professional writer of letters for those who cannot express their feelings. She is sent to a prestigious boarding school for girls at the request of a noble family to tutor Isabella York, who is being trained as a debutante before her presentation to society. Isabella is unhappy at the school, struggles to fit in and has no interest in the refined skills she is expected to master, and she suffers from periodic coughing fits.

Initially suspicious of Violet, Isabella warms to her when she realises that Violet has no interest in her aristocratic status. She eventually confides that she was born Amy Bartlett, the illegitimate child of the York family, and grew up in poverty, caring for an orphan named Taylor whom she raised as a younger sister. When the York family tracked her down and demanded that she join them, she accepted in exchange for a promise that Taylor would be given a better life. Before leaving the school, Violet helps Isabella write a letter to Taylor. Three years later, Taylor runs away from her orphanage and arrives at the CH Postal Company in Leiden, determined to become a postman like Benedict Blue, who once delivered her sister's letter. Violet teaches the girl to read, and together with Benedict they set out to find Isabella and deliver a letter of their own.

The film is structured in two parts, centred on the sisters Isabella and Taylor, and explores the bonds between family members separated by circumstance, as well as Violet's own growth in understanding human emotions. It was noted for the detailed, painterly animation characteristic of Kyoto Animation.

It was followed in 2020 by Violet Evergarden: The Movie, which concluded the story.

title: The Knight Before Christmas
tagline: A modern day romance with a medieval twist
overview: A medieval English knight is magically transported to present day where he ends up falling for a high school science teacher.
plot:
The Knight Before Christmas is a 2019 Christmas fantasy romantic comedy directed by Monika Mitchell and written by Cara J. Russell. Vanessa Hudgens stars as a small-town science teacher and Josh Whitehouse as a medieval knight transported to the present day, with Emmanuelle Chriqui, Harry Jarvis and Ella Kenion in supporting roles. It was filmed in Ontario, with Charleville Castle in Ireland standing in for the knight's home, and released on Netflix on November 21, 2019.

In 1334, near Norwich, England, the knight Sir Cole Lyons takes part in a Christmas hawking contest with his brother, Geoffrey. In the woods, Cole meets an old woman and kindly offers to escort her to shelter. Revealing herself to be a sorceress, she gives him a glowing medallion and announces that she will send him on a quest to a distant land of "flying steel dragons" and "magic boxes," warning that unless he completes it by midnight on Christmas Eve he will never become a true knight. She does not tell him what the quest is.

In present-day Bracebridge, Brooke Winters, a science teacher disillusioned with love after being left by her boyfriend, takes her niece Claire to the opening of a Christmas castle attraction, the very spot where Cole appears. Bewildered by the modern world, he is struck by Brooke's car. When doctors and a police officer assume he has amnesia, since he has no identification and insists that he is a medieval knight, Brooke lets him stay in her guest house while he recovers.

Cole gradually adapts to modern life, marveling at television, diners and voice assistants, and charms Brooke's family and friends with his chivalry. Brooke opens up about her late parents and her past heartbreak, while Cole searches for his quest, rescuing children from a frozen lake and stopping a pickpocket, yet still feeling unfulfilled. On Christmas Eve he helps Brooke host a festive dinner, and when they kiss under the mistletoe, his medallion glows: his quest is complete. They part tearfully at the castle, and Cole returns to the 14th century in time for his knighting ceremony. Seeing his unhappiness, Geoffrey urges him to go back, and the sorceress returns him to 2019, where on Christmas Day he rides up on horseback to declare his love for Brooke.

Rotten Tomatoes reports a 71% approval rating, its consensus calling the film endearing and charming despite a plot that borders on the absurd.

title: Initiation
tagline: He pledges to hunt you down.
overview: During a Whiton University's pledge week, the carefree partying turns deadly when brutal murders start befalling the students, sending Ellery into a race against time to uncover the truth behind the school's dark secrets and the horrifying meaning of a recurring symbol: a single exclamation mark.
plot:
Initiation, stylised as Init!ation, is a 2020 American slasher film directed, co-produced and co-written by John Berardo, developed from his earlier short film Dembanger. Set at a university, it centres on a cruel social media game that spirals out of control as a masked killer begins murdering students. The cast includes Lindsay LaVanchy, Isabella Gomez, Froy Gutierrez, Gattlin Griffith, Shireen Lai and Jon Huertas. The film combines the conventions of the campus slasher with commentary on sexual assault, consent and the culture of silence that can surround privileged fraternity members.

The story begins at a homecoming party, where a sorority member named Kylie is found unconscious and alone in a room with three members of the Sigma Nu Pi fraternity: Beau, Dylan and Wes. The next morning she wakes to find herself the target of cruel jokes on social media, and she cannot remember what happened. Kylie turns to her sorority sister Shayleen, who seeks help from Ellery, another member of the sorority. Ellery agrees to look into the incident, all the more because Wes is her own brother and has previously been accused of sexual assault.

Before long, Wes is killed by an unknown assailant, and Dylan and Beau discover his body. The university's chancellor, Van Horn, publicly honours Wes as a promising swimmer cut down in his prime, while Detective Sandra Fitzgerald and Officer Rico Martinez, played by Huertas, investigate the killing. Martinez learns that the earlier assault accusation against Wes was covered up by the chancellor himself. As the masked killer continues to target those connected to the fraternity and the cover-up, Ellery is warned to stop digging, but she presses on toward the truth about what happened at the party and who is taking revenge, leading to a series of violent confrontations and a final reveal of the killer's identity and motive.

Berardo uses smartphones, livestreams and social media posts as recurring storytelling devices, reflecting how rumours and humiliation spread instantly on campus. Its kills are graphic, and the film pairs its horror with a deliberate focus on survivors' experiences.

Initiation received mixed reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes it holds an approval rating of about 59 percent; the consensus notes that it struggles to balance its gorier ambitions with its social commentary, but that this added maturity makes it a worthwhile slasher.

title: Work It
overview: A brilliant but clumsy high school senior vows to get into her late father's alma mater by transforming herself and a misfit squad into dance champions.
plot:
Work It is a 2020 American dance comedy film directed by Laura Terruso and written by Alison Peck, and produced by Alicia Keys among others. It follows a group of high school students of different backgrounds as they try to win the Work It dance competition of the title. Sabrina Carpenter stars as Quinn Ackerman, with Liza Koshy as her best friend Jasmine Hale, Keiynan Lonsdale as Julliard Pembroke, Michelle Buteau as the admissions counselor Veronica Ramirez and Jordan Fisher as Jake Taylor.

Quinn, a high school senior, is technical director for the Thunderbirds, her school's elite dance team and reigning Work It champions, until she accidentally starts a fire and is fired by the team's ruthless leader, Julliard. Hoping to attend Duke University, her late father's alma mater, she is told by Ramirez that her application will not stand out, and on impulse she claims to dance for the Thunderbirds. Ramirez vows to watch her perform at Work It. Committing to the lie, Quinn has Jasmine, a Thunderbirds dancer, teach her for the team's open auditions, but Julliard rejects her anyway and sarcastically suggests the two start their own team, so they do. They track down Jake, a former champion sidelined by a knee injury, but he refuses to coach them, insisting that dance comes from passion rather than thinking. The girls recruit a group of unknown dancers with different styles, and after seeing their potential Jake agrees to choreograph if they can qualify on their own, which they do on a technicality as "TBD". During a freestyle session she and Jake kiss. When Julliard reports the team for practising at the studio without paying, Jake loses his job; Quinn's grades fall and she learns that Ramirez has left Duke. Confessing to her mother, Quinn quits the team, angering Jasmine, who returns to the Thunderbirds, and ends things with Jake. Rediscovering her love of dance, she reconciles with Jake and Jasmine, and the team reunites, blending everyone's styles. On competition day Quinn tells her mother that Duke and medicine were her parents' dream, not hers, and arrives mid-performance. title: Undercover Wedding Crashers
overview: Geeky-looking Sebas is a surprisingly good classical musician. He’s also a complete unknown in the criminal underworld, and as a new newbie on the police force, that makes him the perfect man for a dangerous mission: to go undercover as a keyboard player for “Los Lolos”, a cheesy flamenco-trap band, who have been hired to play at the wedding of a local mafia boss’ daughter that a major drug trafficker will be attending.  Sebas is keen to take on the mission, blissfully unaware that he will turn out to be even cheesier than Lolo, the band’s lead singer, and fall in love with his sister, Luci. Now Sebas will face a tough choice: remain loyal to his new friends or complete his police mission.
plot:
Undercover Wedding Crashers (Spanish: Operación Camarón) is a 2021 Spanish action comedy directed by Carlos Therón and an adaptation of the 2013 Italian film Song'e Napule by the Manetti Bros. Julián López stars as Sebas, a novice police officer, with Natalia de Molina, Carlos Librado "Nene", Miren Ibarguren, Canco Rodríguez and Julián Villagrán. The film, set in Cádiz, was released in Spanish cinemas in June 2021 and later reached international audiences through streaming.

Sebas is a classically trained pianist who has ended up in the police almost by accident, and whose awkward, timid manner makes him an unlikely candidate for dangerous work. When the anti-drug unit led by the hot-tempered Pepa needs someone to infiltrate the entourage of a powerful drug lord in Cádiz, Sebas's musical talent makes him the ideal choice. The plan is for him to join Los Lolos, a rising flamenco-trap band hired to perform at the wedding of the narco's daughter, giving the police a chance to identify the elusive trafficker and catch him in the act.

Pepa's assistant Mula takes charge of transforming the refined pianist into a convincing street-smart "cani," complete with new clothes, hairstyle and attitude, while her trigger-happy colleague Blas provides backup. Sebas manages to replace the band's keyboard player, but he struggles to fit in with its members, especially the arrogant lead singer, El Lolo, who takes an instant dislike to him, as well as guitarist Ortiguilla and percussionist Fotoshó. He finds an ally in Luci, El Lolo's sister and the band's manager, who constantly argues with her brother, and the two begin to fall for each other. As the wedding approaches and the band's popularity unexpectedly takes off, Sebas must keep his cover, learn to play a style of music completely foreign to him, and survive the narcos' world, while the operation repeatedly threatens to fall apart because of the police team's blunders.

The film received generally positive reviews in Spain. Raquel Hernández Luján of HobbyConsolas praised its well-executed humor and the cast's sensational comic talent but found the ending too sentimental, while Beatriz Martínez of El Periódico gave it four stars for its good script, cast and jokes. Juan Pando of Fotogramas also awarded it four stars.

title: The Legacy of the Bones
overview: Inspector Amaia Salazar must return to the Baztan valley in order to solve a series of suicides that seem to follow a similar pattern.
plot:
The Legacy of the Bones (Spanish: Legado en los huesos) is a 2019 Spanish supernatural crime thriller directed by Fernando González Molina, the second part of the Baztán Trilogy based on the novels by Dolores Redondo. A sequel to The Invisible Guardian (2017), it stars Marta Etura as police inspector Amaia Salazar, with Leonardo Sbaraglia, Susi Sánchez, Imanol Arias and Elvira Mínguez. It premiered at the Sitges Film Festival in October 2019 and was released in Spain on 5 December 2019, followed by a Netflix release in April 2020.

About a year after the events of the first film, a heavily pregnant Amaia and her team await the trial of Jason Medina, accused of raping and murdering his stepdaughter, but he kills himself in the courthouse before proceedings begin, leaving a note bearing a single word: "Tartalo." The shock sends Amaia into labor, and she gives birth to a son, Ibai, with her American husband, James. When she returns to duty months later, she is asked to investigate the desecration of a church in the Baztán Valley, where a baby's arm has been left on the altar, and a prisoner who killed his wife takes his own life after leaving the same word. Amaia links the word to the Tartalo, a child-eating giant of legend.

Amaia moves with her family to Elizondo, where her aunt Engrasi's tarot cards warn of evil, while the demands of the case strain her marriage. She seeks advice from her mentor, the FBI agent Aloisius Dupree, as the investigating judge, Javier Markina, follows her work closely. The case takes a disturbing turn when DNA from the severed arm reveals that it belonged to Amaia's own twin sister, of whose existence she was unaware. Memories resurface of the night her mother, Rosario, tried to kill both infant daughters, and only Amaia was saved.

Rosario, confined to a psychiatric hospital, attacks a nurse and leaves the word "Tartalo" written in blood. Amaia uncovers her mother's links to a sect that practiced human sacrifice, and that the psychiatrist treating Rosario is involved. Realizing that her mother intends to sacrifice Ibai, she races through the flooded valley, and finds Rosario and the doctor preparing to kill the baby. Amaia intervenes in time to save her son, but Rosario escapes into the night, and Amaia lays her sister's remains to rest, knowing her mother is still at large.

The film received mixed reviews. It was followed by Offering to the Storm (2020).

title: After We Collided
overview: Tessa finds herself struggling with her complicated relationship with Hardin; she faces a dilemma that could change their lives forever.
plot:
While reflecting upon his breakup with Tessa Young, Hardin Scott meets a homeless man, whom he rebuffs after the man tries to ask him a question. On her first day as an intern at Vance Publishing, Tessa shares an awkward encounter with coworker Trevor Matthews. Impressed with her work, Vance's owner Christian Vance takes Tessa, Trevor, and his secretary and girlfriend Kimberly to a Seattle-area work event.
At a nightclub, Tessa and Trevor network with and impress a businessman considering an investment in Vance. Tessa drunk-dials Hardin, compelling him to track her down. He arrives at her hotel room to find a half-dressed Trevor (whose clothes were drying after Tessa accidentally spilt wine on them). Hardin kicks him out of the room, and she fights with him before they have sex.
The next morning, Hardin and Tessa fight again before she and Trevor leave with Vance. He informs his interns that he has secured financing from the businessman. Tessa and Hardin each come to regret ending their relationship.
When Tessa returns to the apartment she shared with Hardin to retrieve some belongings, he steps in with his mother Trish, who believes they are still dating. Tessa plays along and finds that she enjoys spending time with both of them. Trish reveals to her the source of Hardin's issues: he was traumatized after watching her get violently raped by men to whom his father Ken owed money when he was a boy.
On the following day, her birthday, Tessa visits her mother Carol's and encounters her ex-boyfriend Noah. The two accidentally reveal that Tessa's long-lost father had come looking for her, but her mother had turned him away. Feeling betrayed, Tessa returns to Hardin's apartment and resumes their relationship.
On Christmas Day, Hardin, Tessa, and Trish attend a holiday party at Hardin's dad Ken's. Furious at Ken's apparent willingness to forgive himself for his past misdeeds, Hardin gets drunk and assaults him. Tessa recounts the incident to Trevor, who warns her that her relationship with Hardin will not end well. Vance contacts Tessa to inform her that his company is expanding and moving to Seattle, so offers her a job there.
On New Year's Eve, Tessa and Hardin attend a party hosted at a university frat house, where they reconnect with a number of their former college friends. Each misinterprets a conversation held by the other: Tessa assumes Hardin is cheating on her when she sees him asking for the forgiveness of another girl with whom he had previously been involved, and Hardin accidentally learns of Vance's offer and concludes that Tessa will leave him for Trevor.
The couple fight, and she storms off. Hardin only sees apologetic texts sent by Tessa the next day after charging his phone. He calls her, but she reaches for her phone while driving and is injured in a car accident.
Devastated by his indirect responsibility for the accident, Hardin decides to end his relationship with Tessa, but Trish talks him out of it.

title: Cousins
overview: Lucas is a young man who lives with his religious aunt Lourdes in a quiet country town. He helps his aunt by holding religious meetings with the ladies of the area, in the living room, playing biblical songs on the keyboard. This quiet life will end as soon as the charitable aunt communicates the arrival of another nephew, Mario, just out of jail. The clash of reality between the cousins ends up causing unusual situations, and an unexpected attraction among the boys.
plot:
Cousins (Portuguese: Primos) is a 2019 Brazilian romantic comedy-drama written by Thiago Cazado and co-directed by Cazado and Mauro Carvalho. It was Cazado's second feature after About Us, and he also plays one of the two leads, Mario Hantz, opposite Paulo Sousa as Lucas Hantz. The cast also includes Juliana Zancanaro as Aunt Lourdes, Duda Esteves as Julia and Denis Camargo as Emilio. The film was produced by MACA Entretenimento and runs 83 minutes.

Lucas is a reserved young man who lives with his charitable, deeply religious Aunt Lourdes in a quiet country town. He helps her by playing hymns on his keyboard at the religious meetings she holds in the living room with the local ladies, and he gives music lessons to an eccentric young woman whose increasingly inappropriate advances he has to fend off. His tranquil routine is upended when Lourdes announces the arrival of another nephew he barely knows, Mario, a distant cousin who has just spent a couple of weeks in jail over a mix-up and cannot return home because his abusive father has rejected him. Shortly before Mario arrives for what is meant to be a brief stay, Lourdes leaves on a trip, so the two young men are left alone and Lucas must share his bedroom with the newcomer. The contrast between the uninhibited, scrappy ex-prisoner and his repressed, closeted cousin produces comic situations, while playful flirting gradually builds into sexual tension and then a passionate romance. The story also mocks the hypocrisy of the town's devout churchgoers and homophobes, and the aunt turns out to have a few surprises of her own.

Cazado said he wanted to make a love story that defied moral standards but in a light way, something fun with a happy ending that would encourage audiences to believe they could love whom they want and be accepted by their families. The film was released in Brazil in 2019 and distributed on home video and on demand in the United Kingdom by TLA Releasing from December 2019. English-language reviewers were generally warm. Culture Fix praised the charming central performances, the uplifting tone and a satire of judgmental religion it likened to John Waters, while Derek Winnert gave it four stars, calling it sweet and good-natured and highlighting the chemistry between Cazado and Sousa as well as Zancanaro's performance as the drinking, smoking, swearing aunt. Some Brazilian critics, including Cinema com Rapadura, were harsher, describing it as a weak fable about overcoming prejudice.

title: Bliss
overview: A mind-bending love story following Greg who, after recently being divorced and then fired, meets the mysterious Isabel, a woman living on the streets and convinced that the polluted, broken world around them is just a computer simulation. Doubtful at first, Greg eventually discovers there may be some truth to Isabel’s wild conspiracy.
plot:
Bliss is a 2021 American drama written and directed by Mike Cahill. Owen Wilson stars as Greg Wittle, a recently divorced, estranged man who suffers a breakdown after losing his job, and Salma Hayek as Isabel, a homeless woman who befriends him and draws him into what seems to be drug addiction as he struggles to tell reality from fantasy.

Greg spends his days at work daydreaming and sketching, and cannot refill his medication without a new prescription. Called into his boss's office and fired, he accidentally kills his boss, hides the body and goes to the bar across the street, where Isabel seems to know what he has done. She claims to have created this world, with unintended consequences, and uses telekinesis to make the death look like a suicide in exchange for a favor. She brings him to a tent encampment, gives him yellow crystals and teaches him to bend the world with his mind. After the two trip a bully at a roller rink, Greg watches the man's arrest only to find himself in the police car. His daughter, Emily, finds him on the street and gives him her number, but when he calls her, Isabel is furious, insisting that Emily is not real.

To prove it, Isabel has them snort blue crystals, and they awaken hooked to a giant computer. Greg is told he has been living in a simulation inside a Brain Box that Isabel designed to study alternate realities and their effect on the brain. In this utopian world, she and Greg are a couple, and his sketches turn out to depict it. Greg cannot remember any of it, and at a gala celebrating the Brain Box, he sees a ghostly Emily begging him to return. When pieces of the simulation start to leak into Isabel's view too, she concludes that they must go back and take more blue crystals to leave for good. Inside the simulation, she commits a murder while getting crystals, and the police give chase. With enough for only one of them, Greg, hearing Emily, who has tracked him down, tells Isabel to go alone. She distracts the police so Greg can escape to a rehab clinic, where he admits he believes his daughter is real, and he later reconnects with her.

Cahill cast Wilson and Hayek from a short pitch before they had read the script, and filming took place in Los Angeles and Croatia in 2019. Amazon Prime Video released the film on February 5, 2021. Reviews were mostly negative, with many critics drawing unfavorable comparisons to The Matrix; it scored 27% on Rotten Tomatoes and 40 on Metacritic.

To All the Boys: Always and Forever is a romantic comedy film released on February 12, 2021, directed by Susan Johnson and produced by Awesomeness Films. The movie serves as the third installment in the To All the Boys I've Loved Before trilogy.

The story begins with Lara Jean Covey (Lana Condor), who has just graduated from high school and is preparing to attend college. She's excited about this new chapter, but also a bit nervous about leaving her family and friends behind. Lara Jean's life takes an unexpected turn when she receives news that the University of California, Berkeley, has accepted her early decision.

As Lara Jean navigates her senior year, she must balance her relationships with her family, particularly her sister Margot (Anna Cathcart), who is dealing with her own college acceptance and subsequent anxiety. The sisters' bond is put to the test as they face new challenges together.

Meanwhile, Lara Jean's on-again, off-again relationship with Peter Kavinsky (Noah Centineo) continues to blossom. However, their love story takes an unexpected turn when Peter reveals that he has been accepted into a prestigious university in New York City. The couple must decide whether to pursue their individual dreams or stay together.

Throughout the movie, Lara Jean also explores her passion for writing and journalism, which becomes a significant part of her identity. She starts working on a school newspaper project, where she meets a charming and talented writer named Josh (Jordan Fisher). As they work together, Lara Jean finds herself drawn to Josh's creative energy and kind heart.

As the story unfolds, Lara Jean must confront her feelings about love, family, and growing up. She learns valuable lessons about embracing change, taking risks, and being true to oneself. Ultimately, Lara Jean makes a decision that will impact her future and the people she loves.

The movie concludes with Lara Jean embarking on a new journey, one that is filled with uncertainty but also full of promise. The film ends on a hopeful note, leaving audiences feeling uplifted and inspired by Lara Jean's resilience and determination.

Overall, To All the Boys: Always and Forever is a heartwarming and engaging romantic comedy that explores themes of love, family, and self-discovery. With its talented cast, witty dialogue, and relatable characters, this movie is sure to delight fans of the trilogy and newcomers alike.

title: Insidious: Fear the Dark
tagline: It ends where it all began.
overview: Ten years after he first ventured into the Further, Josh Lambert heads east to drop his son Dalton off at an idyllic, ivy-covered university. However, Dalton's college dream becomes a nightmare when the repressed demons of his past suddenly resurface.
plot:
Insidious: The Red Door is a 2023 American supernatural horror film directed by Patrick Wilson in his directorial debut, from a screenplay by Scott Teems based on a story by Leigh Whannell and Teems. The fifth Insidious film and a direct sequel to Insidious: Chapter 2 (2013), it reunites Wilson, Ty Simpkins, Rose Byrne and Lin Shaye, with Sinclair Daniel and Hiam Abbass joining the cast.

Nine years after the Lambert family's ordeal, Josh and his son Dalton have had their memories of the Further, the realm of the dead visited through astral projection, suppressed through hypnosis. Josh and Renai have since divorced, and Josh, struggling with lapses of memory, has grown distant from his children. After the funeral of Josh's mother, Josh drives Dalton to college, where the young man is studying art, but their relationship remains strained. Dalton befriends his roommate, Chris, and in an art class he is encouraged to delve into his subconscious, producing a painting of a red door that awakens buried memories and his dormant abilities.

Experimenting with astral projection, Dalton is confronted by the red-faced demon that tormented him as a child, which also attacks Chris. His brother Foster recalls a recurring nightmare in which their possessed father tried to kill them, and Dalton completes his painting, depicting Josh in front of the red door. Pulled back into the Further, Dalton relives Josh's possession and becomes trapped in the demon's lair. Meanwhile, Josh investigates his own father, who died in a psychiatric hospital, and learns from Renai the truth about their family's past and that his father also had the gift of astral projection but believed his visions were madness.

With Renai's help, Josh re-enters the Further to rescue his son as the demon takes control of Dalton's body and tries to kill Chris. Josh frees Dalton and holds the red door shut against the demon so that his son can escape, and Dalton seals the door by painting over his canvas in black. Guided home by the spirit of his own father, Josh returns to the living, reconciles with his family and visits Dalton, who shows him a painting of Josh carrying his young son out of the Further.

Released in the United States by Sony Pictures Releasing on July 7, 2023, the film received mixed reviews; Rotten Tomatoes' consensus called it a disappointing conclusion to a once-frightening franchise, and Metacritic gave it 45 out of 100. It grossed over $189 million, the highest of the series.

title: #Alive
overview: As a grisly virus rampages a city, a lone man stays locked inside his apartment, digitally cut off from seeking help and desperate to find a way out.
plot:
#Alive (Korean: #saraitda) is a 2020 South Korean action horror film directed by Cho Il-hyung, starring Yoo Ah-in as Oh Joon-woo and Park Shin-hye as Kim Yoo-bin, with Jeon Bae-soo as a mysterious survivor. It is based on Alone, a 2019 screenplay by American writer Matt Naylor, who adapted it with Cho; Naylor's script also became a separate film. The film follows a young video game streamer trying to stay alive alone in his Seoul apartment as a zombie outbreak engulfs the city.

Joon-woo wakes up alone in his family's apartment as people outside begin attacking and infecting each other. After a neighbor bursts in and turns into a zombie, Joon-woo barricades the door with the refrigerator, posts a call for help online and receives a message from his parents saying they are safe. Using a drone, he discovers that the entire neighborhood is overrun. Gradually he loses phone service, the internet and running water, and his food supplies run out.

Isolated, hungry and tormented by a final voicemail suggesting his family's refuge has fallen, Joon-woo sinks into despair and is on the verge of taking his own life when he notices a laser pointer from the building opposite. It belongs to Kim Yoo-bin, another survivor, who has been defending her apartment with a hand axe and booby traps. Using a rope line and walkie-talkies, the two begin to share supplies and support one another. When the noise attracts the infected, they decide to rappel down from their balconies and fight their way through the complex in search of help. Their hopes are tested when a seemingly kind stranger offers them food and water, and they must keep each other alive long enough to be rescued.

The film reflects the loneliness and isolation of the COVID-19 era, and centers on how technology, social media and human connection become means of survival.

#Alive was released in South Korea on June 24, 2020, achieving the strongest first-day admissions of any film there since the pandemic began, and globally on Netflix on September 8, 2020. It received generally positive reviews, with 88 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it well acted, genuinely unsettling and occasionally even funny.

title: King Richard
tagline: Venus, Serena and a plan for greatness.
overview: The story of how Richard Williams served as a coach to his daughters Venus and Serena, who will soon become two of the most legendary tennis players in history.
plot:
King Richard is a biographical sports drama film directed by Reinaldo Marcus Green and written by Zach Baylin. The movie stars Will Smith as Richard Williams, a former tennis player who trains his daughters Venus and Serena Williams to become professional tennis players.

The film begins with Richard (Will Smith) living in Compton, California, with his wife, Oracene (Aunjanue Ellis), and their two young daughters, Venus (Saniyya Sidney) and Serena (Demi Singleton). The family is struggling financially, but Richard has a vision for his daughters' futures. He believes that with hard work and dedication, they can become professional tennis players.

Richard's unorthodox training methods, which include hitting the ball against walls and using makeshift rackets, are met with skepticism by Oracene and the girls at first. However, as they begin to see progress, they start to believe in Richard's vision. The family moves to Florida, where Richard sets up a tennis academy for his daughters.

As Venus and Serena grow older, they face numerous challenges on and off the court. They encounter racism and sexism from their opponents, coaches, and even some of their own family members. Despite these obstacles, the sisters persevere and begin to make a name for themselves in the tennis world.

The film's plot development is marked by several pivotal moments, including a dramatic match between Venus and her opponent, Zina Garrison (Nia Long), which showcases the sisters' growing skills and confidence. Richard's relationship with his daughters also deepens, as he becomes more than just a coach but a mentor and a father figure.

As Serena begins to rise through the ranks of professional tennis, she faces increasing pressure from her family and coaches to perform. The film culminates in a dramatic match between Serena and Martina Navratilova (played by actress Kate Winslet), which marks a turning point in Serena's career.

The movie ends with Richard watching his daughters achieve their dreams on the court, while also acknowledging the sacrifices he made for them along the way. Will Smith delivers a powerful performance as Richard Williams, capturing the complexity and nuance of this remarkable man. The film is a testament to the power of family, perseverance, and determination in overcoming adversity.

Overall, King Richard is a heartwarming and inspiring film that celebrates the achievements of two tennis legends. With outstanding performances from its cast, including Will Smith, Saniyya Sidney, and Demi Singleton, the movie is a must-see for sports fans and anyone interested in underdog stories.

title: Elvis
tagline: The Man. The Legend. The King of Rock & Roll.
overview: The life story of Elvis Presley as seen through the complicated relationship with his enigmatic manager, Colonel Tom Parker.
plot:
Elvis is a 2022 musical epic biographical drama film directed and co-produced by Baz Luhrmann, who wrote the screenplay with Sam Bromell, Craig Pearce and Jeremy Doner. It chronicles the life of the American singer and actor Elvis Presley through his long association with his manager, Colonel Tom Parker. Austin Butler stars as Presley and Tom Hanks as Parker, with Olivia DeJonge, Helen Thomson, Richard Roxburgh, David Wenham, Kodi Smit-McPhee and Luke Bracey in supporting roles. Announced in 2014, the project stalled in development until Hanks joined in 2019, and filming wrapped in March 2021.

Raised largely by his devoted mother Gladys, the young Elvis grows up poor in Tupelo, Mississippi, and after the family moves to Memphis he is drawn to the African-American music of Beale Street. Parker, a former carnival huckster managing country singer Hank Snow, hears "That's All Right" and recognizes Elvis's crossover appeal, then witnesses the frenzy his performance provokes at the Louisiana Hayride and persuades him to hand over control of his career. Elvis rises meteorically, moving to RCA Records and lifting his family out of poverty, but his suggestive dancing alarms segregationist politicians, and Parker steers him into the Army to avoid legal trouble. Elvis is devastated by his mother's death, meets the young Priscilla Beaulieu while serving in West Germany and, after his discharge, turns to films and marries her. Shaken by the assassinations of Martin Luther King Jr. and Robert F. Kennedy in 1968, he defies Parker's plans for a wholesome Christmas special and, working with director Steve Binder, delivers a triumphant comeback ending with "If I Can Dream". Elvis then conquers Las Vegas, but Parker, burdened by gambling debts, blocks his wish for a world tour and traps him in a long casino residency. As exhaustion and prescription drug addiction take their toll and Priscilla leaves with their daughter Lisa Marie, Elvis learns the truth about Parker's stateless past, yet remains bound to his manager until his death in 1977.

Elvis premiered at the Cannes Film Festival on 25 May 2022 and was released by Warner Bros. Pictures in June. It grossed $288.7 million worldwide against an $85 million budget, received generally positive reviews, with Rotten Tomatoes' consensus praising Luhrmann's dazzling style and Butler's outstanding performance, and earned eight Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture and Best Actor.
