title: Bros
tagline: A romantic comedy that gives you all the feels.
overview: Two men with commitment problems attempt a relationship.
plot:
In New York City, Bobby Lieber, host of the podcast and radio show The Eleventh Brick at Stonewall who prides himself on being single, attends an awards ceremony for the LGBTQ community, where he wins an award for "Best White Cis Gay Man". He announces that he has accepted a position as a curator for the upcoming national LGBTQ+ history museum in Manhattan.
Bobby joins his friend Henry at a nightclub where a new gay dating app is being launched, and spots Aaron Shepard, whom Henry describes as hot but "boring". Aaron and Bobby flirt, but Aaron does not seem interested in Bobby. A few days later, the two start spending time together, but their connection is not strong. While on a date at the movies, Aaron runs into a former high school hockey teammate, Josh, and his fiancée. Bobby and Aaron are unsure what to make of their time together; Bobby feels Aaron acts too straight and Aaron thinks Bobby is too intense and that his clout in the gay community is intimidating. Aaron later discovers that Josh called off his engagement and has come out as gay.
After some time apart, Aaron confides to Bobby that his original dream was to be a chocolatier, but had thought that it was unachievable and never pursued it. Bobby invites Aaron to a trip to Provincetown, where he solicits an eccentric millionaire for a donation to the struggling museum. The millionaire is unimpressed by Bobby at first, but Aaron helps him to adjust his pitch, and they secure a $5 million donation. Bobby is impressed by Aaron and the two grow closer romantically, and Bobby opens up about having to tone down his flamboyant behavior to make others comfortable.
Bobby and Aaron date for several months and Aaron integrates into Bobby's group of friends. At a Christmas party, Josh arrives and Aaron asks Bobby if they can have a threesome. Bobby agrees, but later recants on his wishes after seeing the connection Aaron and Josh have. When Aaron's family comes to the city for a visit, Bobby's excessive, outspoken behavior ends up causing a rift between the two men. Aaron hooks up with Josh again and they break up. People are threatening to boycott the museum and pull donations over an exhibit Bobby created that suggests that Abraham Lincoln was gay.
Sometime later, Bobby returns to work and reconciles with his coworkers over his outburst over the exhibit. The others all admit they have their own issues as well over matters such as their sexual identities, and agree to compromise on the exhibits that will be presented. Meanwhile, Aaron quits his job and fulfills his dream of making chocolates, telling Bobby that all proceeds will go to the museum.
On the opening night of the museum, a large crowd turns out. Bobby misses Aaron, and after talking to his friend Tina, decides to text him. Aaron receives the text and is encouraged by his brother to go after the person he loves, arriving just as Bobby begins his speech.

title: The Witch: Part 2. The Other One
overview: A girl wakes up in a huge secret laboratory, then accidentally meets another girl who is trying to protect her house from a gang. The mystery girl overthrows the gang with her unexpected powers, and laboratory staff set out to find her.
plot:
The Witch: Part 2. The Other One is a South Korean science fiction action horror film of 2022 written and directed by Park Hoon-jung, a sequel to his The Witch: Part 1. The Subversion (2018) with a largely new cast. Shin Si-ah stars as Ark 1, a girl who escapes from a secret laboratory, with Park Eun-bin as Kyung-hee, Sung Yoo-bin as her younger brother Dae-gil, Seo Eun-soo as the agent Jo-hyeon, Jin Goo as the gangster Yong-du, Jo Min-su as Dr Baek, Lee Jong-suk as the institute chief Jang and Kim Da-mi as Goo Ja-yoon, the witch of the first film.

Years earlier, a teenage girl riding a bus with a friend is gassed and abducted in a staged accident; Dr Baek and her twin tell her that the fraternal twins she is carrying will be of great importance. In the present, a girl known as Ark 1 slaughters every soldier and scientist at a hidden facility and flees into the forest, where she is snatched by henchmen of Yong-du, who are also holding Kyung-hee for refusing to sign over her house. Kyung-hee takes her in, has her uncle remove the experimental devices from her skin, and brings her home to live with Dae-gil. Jang, head of the institute, discusses the escape from its coastal base on Jeju Island with Dr Baek and sends a tactical team.

When Yong-du's gang threatens Kyung-hee for the deed to her late father's land, revealing that Yong-du murdered him, the girl overpowers them with brute strength and he flees. Baek gives the agent Jo-hyeon and her partner Tom a device to track Ark 1, and Jo-hyeon shows Kyung-hee footage of the massacre, asking for her help. Yong-du trades the girl's location to Jang's squad in return for a dose of their power. As the gang and the squad descend on the house, Kyung-hee is shot dead while buying time for the others, and Dae-gil is killed by Yong-du. The girl survives a rocket strike, breaks Yong-du's feet, and destroys one of the squad with telekinesis before Ja-yoon arrives, kills the last survivor and reveals that they are sisters. Needing the girl's stronger psychic bond to find their mother, she sedates her and drives away. Baek senses the danger the two now pose, and their mother is shown suspended in a vast tank, opening her eyes. A post-credits scene shows that Jo-hyeon and Tom survived and are joined by more witches to hunt the sisters.

Delayed by the COVID-19 pandemic, the film was released in June 2022 and drew over 2.8 million admissions, grossing about $23.4 million to rank seventh among Korean films that year.

title: Spiderhead
tagline: How far would you go to fix human nature?
overview: A prisoner in a state-of-the-art penitentiary begins to question the purpose of the emotion-controlling drugs he's testing for a pharmaceutical genius.
plot:
Spiderhead is a 2022 American science fiction psychological thriller directed by Joseph Kosinski and written by Rhett Reese and Paul Wernick, adapted from George Saunders's 2010 short story "Escape from Spiderhead". Chris Hemsworth plays the charismatic scientist Steve Abnesti, Miles Teller the inmate Jeff and Jurnee Smollett his fellow inmate Lizzy, with Mark Paguio and Tess Haubrich. Shot in Australia in 2020, it premiered in Sydney on June 11, 2022, before its Netflix release on June 17.

Spiderhead is a high-tech island prison where inmates volunteer as test subjects for experimental drugs in exchange for reduced sentences. Instead of guards and cells they have comfortable rooms and freedom of movement, under the friendly supervision of Abnesti and his assistant Mark. Each prisoner wears a surgically implanted device, the MobiPak, that delivers drugs which manipulate emotion and perception. Jeff, haunted by a drunk-driving crash that killed his friend, is dosed with an aphrodisiac and then asked which of two women should receive Darkenfloxx, a drug that causes unbearable terror and anguish. When he refuses to choose, Abnesti claims superiors have ordered it anyway, and the young inmate Heather, given the drug, takes her own life.

Shaken, Mark begins to doubt the project. Jeff, finding Abnesti's desk unlocked, learns that there are no superiors and the facility belongs to Abnesti's own pharmaceutical company. Jeff confides in Lizzy that the crash also killed his girlfriend, and the two fall in love. When Abnesti orders him to give Lizzy Darkenfloxx, Jeff, with Mark's help, turns the tables and forces the scientist to admit the real purpose: testing an obedience drug, B-6, which had been secretly used to obtain the inmates' consent. Jeff also learns his sentence ended months earlier and that Lizzy's appeal has succeeded.

Abnesti floods Lizzy's device with Darkenfloxx, and in the ensuing struggle Jeff overpowers him and removes the vials from her. The pair fight their way out past drugged inmates and flee by boat, while Abnesti, high from his own damaged MobiPak, crashes his floatplane into a mountain. Jeff reflects that forgiveness cannot come from a drug and must be chosen.

Critics were lukewarm, giving it a 39% Rotten Tomatoes approval rating.

title: Minari

plot:
Minari is a 2020 American drama film written and directed by Lee Isaac Chung, produced by Plan B Entertainment, and released in 2021. The movie tells the story of the Park family, who move from California to rural Arkansas in search of a better life.

The film begins with David Park (Steven Yeun), a successful Korean-American businessman, and his wife Monica (Youn Yuh-jung), a Korean immigrant who grew up in an orphanage. They are expecting their first child, but the pregnancy is complicated due to Monica's age and health issues. The couple decides to move to rural Arkansas, where David's father-in-law, Jacob (Will Patton), has offered them a plot of land to build a new home.

Upon arrival, the family faces numerous challenges, including cultural differences, language barriers, and the harsh realities of rural life. David struggles to adjust to his new role as a husband and father, while Monica tries to balance her desire for independence with her responsibilities as a wife and mother-to-be. The couple's relationship is put to the test as they navigate their differences and confront their own insecurities.

As the family settles into their new home, they face various obstacles, including a failing farm, a distant father-in-law, and a community that is wary of outsiders. David's father-in-law, Jacob, is a complex character who is both loving and demanding. He expects David to take over the family farm and restore it to its former glory.

Throughout the film, Lee Isaac Chung explores themes of identity, culture, and belonging. The Park family must navigate their Korean heritage in a predominantly white American community, where they are often met with suspicion and misunderstanding. Monica's experiences as an orphan and her struggles to find her place in the world serve as a powerful metaphor for the immigrant experience.

As the story unfolds, David and Monica face numerous challenges, including a miscarriage, a failed farm, and a strained relationship with their father-in-law. However, through it all, they hold onto each other and their values, ultimately finding a way to build a new life together.

The film's title, Minari, is the Korean word for "barley," which serves as a symbol of hope and resilience. The Park family's struggles are reminiscent of the hardships faced by Korean immigrants who came to America in search of a better life. Through their story, Chung offers a powerful exploration of the immigrant experience and the complexities of identity, culture, and belonging.

Ultimately, Minari is a film about the power of love, family, and community. The Park family's struggles serve as a reminder that even in the face of adversity, we can find strength and resilience in each other. The film's ending is both hopeful and bittersweet, leaving the audience with a sense of wonder and awe at the complexities of human experience.

plot:
Meg 2: The Trench is a 2023 science fiction action film directed by Ben Wheatley and a sequel to The Meg (2018), based on Steve Alten's 1999 novel The Trench. Jason Statham reprises his role as Jonas Taylor, with Wu Jing as Jiuming Zhang, Sophia Cai as Meiying, Cliff Curtis as Mac, Page Kennedy as DJ, Sergio Peris-Mencheta as Montes, Skyler Samuels as Jess and Sienna Guillory as Hillary Driscoll.

Five years after the first film, Jonas fights environmental crime and helps the research station Mana One explore the Mariana Trench. Widowed, he helps raise his stepdaughter Meiying with her uncle Jiuming, whose company is backed by the investor Driscoll. Jiuming has raised a female megalodon named Haiqi from a pup in a reserve on Hainan. On a dive into the Trench, Haiqi, who escaped the night before, pursues the subs, and below the thermocline two larger Megs mate with her. Deeper still, they discover an illegal mining operation run by the mercenary Montes, who holds a grudge against Jonas for having had him jailed. The corrupt Driscoll has hired Montes to exploit Mana One's access to the Trench and extract valuable rare-earth minerals.

Montes blows up his own crew to hide the operation, rupturing the Trench. With their rescue pod sabotaged, they cross the sea floor in exosuits, and only four survive. They escape a murder attempt by Jess, a traitor. At the surface, they find that the rupture has released the three Megs, lizard-like predators called Snappers and a giant octopus. Jess is eaten, and at the resort Fun Island, Driscoll and Montes come to finish them off. Driscoll is eaten by Snappers. Jonas kills the beta male and knocks Montes into the jaws of the alpha, which he finally kills by impaling it on a helicopter rotor, while Haiqi kills the octopus. Jiuming uses his training signals to turn Haiqi away, and the survivors realize she may be pregnant.

Development began in 2018 after the first film's success, and Wheatley was announced as director in October 2020. Filming took place in 2022. The film premiered at the Shanghai International Film Festival on June 9, 2023, and Warner Bros. released it in the United States on August 4. It grossed $397.8 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed: Rotten Tomatoes reported 27% approval and criticized its disjointed story, and RogerEbert.com called it one of the year's dullest films until its chaotic finale. It received Golden Raspberry nominations for Worst Picture, Worst Actor and Worst Director.

title: Awake
tagline: Disorientation. Hallucinations. Hysteria. Sleep is survival.
overview: After a sudden global event wipes out all electronics and takes away humankind’s ability to sleep, chaos quickly begins to consume the world. Only Jill, an ex-soldier with a troubled past, may hold the key to a cure in the form of her own daughter. The question is, can Jill safely deliver her daughter and save the world before she herself loses her mind.
plot:
Awake is a 2021 American apocalyptic science fiction thriller directed by Mark Raso from a screenplay he wrote with Joseph Raso. Gina Rodriguez stars as Jill Adams, a former army medic, with Ariana Greenblatt as her daughter Matilda, Lucius Hoyos as her son Noah, Jennifer Jason Leigh, Barry Pepper, Finn Jones, Shamier Anderson, Frances Fisher and Gil Bellows. Netflix released the film on 9 June 2021.

Jill, a recovering addict who works as a security guard at a college, steals drugs from a research lab to sell. Separated from her children, Noah and Matilda, who live with their grandmother, she is driving them home when a mysterious global event knocks out all electronic devices. Their car loses power and is struck by another vehicle, plunging into a lake. Matilda drowns but is revived by a police officer. At the hospital they learn that coma patients have suddenly awakened, and that night the family finds that they cannot sleep. Jill soon learns that the whole population has lost the ability to sleep. A psychiatrist she once worked with, Dr. Murphy, explains that without sleep people will rapidly deteriorate and die within days, and that scientists are studying an elderly woman who can still sleep at a military facility called the Hub in the hope of finding a cure.

Jill realizes that Matilda slept the night before and may hold the key to humanity's survival. As society begins to collapse, desperate people learn of Matilda's ability; at a church, a group of churchgoers tries to sacrifice the girl, and Jill escapes with her children amid gunfire. With Noah urging his mother to take Matilda to the Hub, they set out across a land descending into madness, encountering escaped prisoners who steal their car with Matilda inside, and other increasingly unhinged survivors. As Jill's own mind begins to fail from sleep deprivation, she races against time to protect her children and get Matilda to the scientists, who may not have her best interests at heart.

Awake received generally negative reviews, with a 24 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it a scattered and shallow disaster film, and a Metacritic score of 35. Critics found the plot derivative and lacking in tension, although Rodriguez's committed performance received some praise.

Workaholic Sloane Benson hates the holidays due to familial judgement she receives for being single. Having recently broken up with her boyfriend, her mother Elaine is constantly trying to set her up with a new man, much to Sloane's annoyance.
At Sloane's family's Christmas dinner, her younger brother York gets engaged to Liz, his girlfriend of three months, so Sloane is now the only single adult left in the family. Meanwhile, Jackson, an Australian golfer, is stuck spending the holidays with Carly, a woman he has no interest in, and her parents. His date becomes angry with him for not getting her a Christmas present although they had agreed not to exchange gifts, so he leaves in frustration.
After Christmas, Sloane and Jackson have a chance encounter at the mall when both are returning presents they received. Jackson suggests to avoid crazy and clingy dates, they should make a pact to be Holidates (dates only for Holidays). Though initially reluctant, she decides to take him up on his offer and they end up spending New Year's Eve together, but have no further contact.
However, on Valentine's Day, both have another chance encounter where Jackson pretends to be her boyfriend in front of her ex and his young and beautiful girlfriend. They slowly become friends after spending various holidays together.
After Sloane and Jackson become closer when he loses a finger on July 4th, he fears he is not good enough for her, so he tries to set her up with a better date. This leads to a fight at her brother's wedding on Labor Day, where her date, Faarooq, and his date, Sloane’s aunt Susan, hook up.
While at a Halloween party together, Sloane becomes unwell after unknowingly taking laxatives. Jackson takes care of her until they end up falling asleep together. They then have sex the morning after, until Sloane's married sister, Abby, arrives panicking about kissing Jackson’s friend, Neil, the night before at the party. Sloane uses it as an excuse to shove Jackson out, much to his dismay.
At Thanksgiving, they fight after Jackson opens up to Sloane and tells her how he feels about them. In the store when Sloane says "Ryan Gosling would never do his own shopping" there is a blurred customer in the background who looks like the actor. Both break off contact afterwards. Abby’s husband, Peter, finds out about her kissing Neil at Halloween. Susan’s holidate, Wally, has a heart attack, and the doctor treating him is Faarooq, who Susan had a brief but intense romance with over Halloween, before breaking it off. Susan confesses to Faarooq that she made a mistake in ending things and asks him for another chance. They kiss and reconcile.
In the days leading to Christmas, Sloane visits Jackson's place but loses her nerve, still unable to speak to him. When shopping at the mall, they have another chance encounter. In front of hundreds of people, she finally confesses her love for Jackson and the two embrace.
The end credits reveal that all of the couples are still together.

title: A Boy Called Christmas
overview: An ordinary young boy called Nikolas sets out on an extraordinary adventure into the snowy north in search of his father who is on a quest to discover the fabled village of the elves, Elfhelm. Taking with him a headstrong reindeer called Blitzen and a loyal pet mouse, Nikolas soon meets his destiny in this magical and endearing story that proves nothing is impossible…
plot:
A Boy Called Christmas is a 2021 British fantasy adventure film directed by George Miller and written by Sarah Smith. The movie stars Lee Cormie, Debra Wilson, and Nonso Anozie.

The story begins on the eve of Christmas Eve in the year 1492, where we meet an orphan boy named Eric (Lee Cormie), who lives with his cruel and abusive stepmother, Queen Elizabeth I's advisor, Lord Thomas (Nonso Anozie). Despite being mistreated by his stepmother, Eric is a kind-hearted and adventurous young man.

One day, while out on a walk, Eric stumbles upon an old map that supposedly leads to the North Pole. Intrigued by the prospect of finding Santa Claus, Eric sets out on a journey to find the mythical land. He meets a talking reindeer named Jingle (voiced by Debra Wilson), who becomes his companion and guide.

As they travel through treacherous landscapes and encounter various obstacles, Eric and Jingle develop an unlikely friendship. Along the way, Eric learns valuable lessons about courage, kindness, and believing in oneself.

Upon arriving at the North Pole, Eric discovers that Santa Claus (played by Nonso Anozie) is not as jolly as he seems. In reality, Santa is a kind-hearted man who has been forced to live in hiding due to his association with the mythical figure of Santa Claus. The real Santa is being held captive by Lord Thomas, who seeks to exploit the legend for his own gain.

Eric and Jingle join forces with Santa's elves to rescue their leader and bring him back to the North Pole. In the process, Eric learns about the true meaning of Christmas and the importance of kindness, generosity, and believing in oneself.

As they face numerous challenges and dangers, Eric and his companions ultimately succeed in rescuing Santa Claus. With the help of Jingle's magical powers, they defeat Lord Thomas and shatter the illusion that has kept Santa captive for so long.

In the end, Eric returns home to a hero's welcome, where he is celebrated for his bravery and kindness. The movie concludes with Eric reflecting on the lessons he learned during his journey, realizing that the true magic of Christmas lies not in the gifts or the presents, but in the love, kindness, and generosity that we share with one another.

Overall, A Boy Called Christmas is a heartwarming and visually stunning film that celebrates the spirit of adventure, friendship, and believing in oneself. The movie features impressive visual effects, engaging characters, and a story that will leave audiences of all ages feeling merry and bright.

title: We Can Be Heroes
overview: When alien invaders capture Earth's superheroes, their kids must learn to work together to save their parents - and the planet.
plot:
We Can Be Heroes is a 2020 American superhero film directed by Robert Rodriguez and written by Carlos Gallardo. The movie takes place after the events of Avengers: Endgame and follows a group of young superheroes as they try to save the world from an alien invasion.

The story begins with a flashback of Nick Fury (Samuel L. Jackson) explaining that aliens have been monitoring Earth's children for years, looking for one who can be their savior. The chosen child is Alex Owens (Yara Shahidi), a 12-year-old girl who possesses unique abilities. However, she is not the only one; other kids around the world also possess special powers.

The movie then shifts to the present day, where we meet our main characters: Alex's friends and fellow superheroes, including Marcus (Jacob Vargas), Ella (Viola Davis), and Sam (Gael García Bernal). They are all brought together by a mysterious figure known as "The Director" (Rami Malek) who claims to be the leader of an organization called "The Department of Youth."

As The Director explains, the aliens have returned, and their spaceship is heading straight for Earth. However, they need human help to defeat the alien threat. The kids are tasked with stopping the aliens' ship from reaching its destination.

The plot thickens as we learn that each child has a unique power that can be used against the aliens. Alex's power allows her to create force fields, Marcus can turn invisible, Ella can control plants, and Sam can manipulate technology. However, they soon realize that their powers are not enough to defeat the aliens alone.

The kids embark on a journey across the globe, visiting different countries and meeting new allies along the way. They also discover that The Director's true intentions may not be entirely pure, and that he has his own agenda for the children.

As the stakes rise, the kids face numerous challenges and obstacles as they try to stop the alien invasion. Along the way, they learn valuable lessons about teamwork, trust, and believing in themselves.

The movie culminates in an epic battle between the kids and the aliens. Using their combined powers, they manage to defeat the aliens and save the world. However, not without some sacrifices and unexpected twists along the way.

In the end, The Director's true identity is revealed, and it turns out that he was once a superhero himself who had been thought to be dead. He has been searching for a new generation of heroes to carry on his legacy.

The movie concludes with Alex and her friends being hailed as heroes, but also realizing that their journey is far from over. They have saved the world, but there are still many challenges ahead, and they must continue to work together to protect it.

Overall, We Can Be Heroes is a heartwarming and action-packed film that celebrates the power of teamwork, friendship, and believing in oneself.

title: Thunder Force
overview: In a world where supervillains are commonplace, two estranged childhood best friends reunite after one devises a treatment that gives them powers to protect their city.
plot:
In 1983, Earth was subjected to cosmic rays that gave sociopaths superpowers, resulting in a rise of supervillains known as Miscreants. With no one able to stop the Miscreants, normal people are usually left living in fear of them. After a Miscreant kills her geneticist parents on their way home from work, Emily Stanton becomes determined to find a way to stop Miscreants.
By 1988, Emily has sacrificed much of her social life in favor of researching ways to fight back against Miscreants. While this results in her being bullied, Lydia Berman stands up for her and becomes her best and only friend. Lydia supports Emily's dream of giving superpowers to normal people, though she tries to make sure that Emily does not overwork herself. When Lydia convinces Emily to take a half-hour nap from studying, Emily accidentally oversleeps and wakes up late for an AP exam, straining their relationship and causing them to drift apart.
In 2024, Emily and Lydia have gone their separate ways, with Emily becoming a successful scientist and researcher for her own company and Lydia becoming a longshoreman. Lydia tries to reconnect with Emily when their high school reunion comes around. When she fails to show up on the night of the reunion, Lydia concludes that Emily is still uncomfortable attending parties by herself and goes to pick her up. Emily tells her that while she would have liked to go to the reunion, she had forgotten when the reunion was and had a project she had to work on that night, which Emily wants to show to Lydia. Unfortunately, Lydia accidentally injects herself with a serum Emily had been working on.
Having been injected with the serum, Lydia learns from Emily that the serum was designed to give a normal person superhuman strength and that she would have to undergo special training and treatment so the serum does not kill her. Emily also joins Lydia in the treatment, although a less painful one since Emily took the serum in a pill form to earn the other superpower concocted, invisibility. Lydia discovers that in the years since their high school graduation, Emily had a daughter, Tracy, with one of the researchers, who could not handle the responsibility and left them.
Once they finish their training and treatment, Emily and Lydia foil a liquor store robbery run by a Miscreant with crab arms known as the Crab, who falls in love with an equally smitten Lydia, much to Emily's concern. Emily and Lydia, now known as the superhero team Thunder Force, are praised for their heroics. This brings Thunder Force to the attention of mayoral candidate William Stevens, whose campaign is built on the idea that only he can end the Miscreants' crimes.
With the help of Laser, a Miscreant who can generate and control whip-like energy beams, Stevens tries to get Thunder Force to work for him, leaving Chicago at the mercy of the Miscreants unless he wins the mayoral election.

title: Scooby-Doo! Return to Zombie Island
overview: Scooby-Doo and his pals win an all-expense paid vacation and embark on a trip of a lifetime to a tropical paradise. Their destination however, turns out to be Zombie Island. As soon as they arrive, they realize the place looks strangely familiar and is reminiscent of a trip they took years ago, in which they became wrapped up in a mystery involving zombies. The gang soon learns that their trip to paradise comes with a price when the zombies re-emerge and attack their hotel. Will Scooby-Doo and the Mystery Inc. gang finally solve the mystery behind Zombie Island?
plot:
Scooby-Doo! Return to Zombie Island is a 2019 American animated direct-to-video mystery film produced by Warner Bros. Animation, the thirty-third entry in the direct-to-video Scooby-Doo series and a standalone sequel to Scooby-Doo on Zombie Island (1998), the franchise's first such film. The voice cast features Frank Welker as Scooby-Doo and Fred, Grey DeLisle as Daphne, Matthew Lillard as Shaggy, Kate Micucci as Velma, John Michael Higgins as Alan Smithee, Travis Willingham as Seaver and Cassandra Peterson as Elvira.

After Fred dreams of catching a string of villains who all turn out to be members of the Withers family, he wakes to the reality that the gang has been forced into retirement by the local sheriff and that he has sold the Mystery Machine. When Fred wants to return to sleuthing, Shaggy and Scooby, tired of being taken for granted, make the others promise never to solve another mystery. Then Elvira announces on television that Shaggy has won a tropical vacation. On the island, greeters warn the gang to get out, a clawed figure blocks their road with a fallen palm tree, and at the Moonstar Island Resort they meet manager Alan and a staff who resemble the people they met on Moonscar Island. Chased by zombies, Shaggy and Scooby find a secret passage to a cavern full of cat statues and release their friends from the promise. A trap, a fire and the sprinklers reveal the zombies as the staff in make-up: the resort is really Moonscar Island, and Alan is the film director Alan Smithee, who rigged Shaggy's prize to shoot a horror movie inspired by Velma's blog, though he knows nothing of the black were-cat they saw. Agreeing to help finish the film, the gang meets Fred's stunt double, Seaver, and his monster-truck Mystery Machine. Soon feral cats and three were-cats attack, and the cat creatures seize Alan's medallion, once Simone's pendant, using it in the harvest moonlight to find a chest of gold coins that proves to be foil-wrapped Scooby Snacks. Disguised as zombies, the gang scares and unmasks them as the greeters and the ferry captain, treasure hunters who controlled the cats with whistles, while a fourth were-cat appears to be real. The tamed cats then help dig up the real treasure, Alan retires a rich man and the sheriff lets Mystery Inc. return.

The film premiered at San Diego Comic-Con on 21 July 2019 and was released on digital platforms and home media on 3 September 2019.

title: Babylon
overview: A tale of outsized ambition and outrageous excess, tracing the rise and fall of multiple characters in an era of unbridled decadence and depravity during Hollywood's transition from silent films and to sound films in the late 1920s.
plot:
Babylon is a 2022 American epic drama film written and directed by Damien Chazelle. The film is set in Hollywood during the Golden Age of cinema, specifically between 1926 and 1930.

The story follows Jack Conrad (played by Brad Pitt), a struggling actor who becomes embroiled in the tumultuous world of Hollywood's silent era. Jack is a former soldier who returns to Los Angeles after World War I, seeking fame and fortune on the silver screen. He meets Nellie LaRoy (played by Margot Robbie), a young actress with a troubled past, and together they navigate the cutthroat world of Hollywood.

As the film progresses, we are introduced to Maxine "Max" Fairman (played by Lily Gladstone), a talented but ambitious young actress who becomes embroiled in Jack's life. The three characters become entangled in a complex web of relationships, rivalries, and power struggles within the Hollywood elite.

The story is also intertwined with that of Neil (played by Diego Calva), a Mexican-American actor who becomes a key player in the film industry. Neil's rise to fame is marked by his involvement with the infamous silent film director, George Valentin (played by Jared Leto).

As the narrative unfolds, we see the characters navigate the changing landscape of Hollywood during this period. The film explores themes of ambition, identity, and the corrupting influence of power. Through a series of dramatic events, including a tragic accident involving Max, Jack's world begins to unravel.

The film's climax features a pivotal confrontation between Jack and George Valentin, which ultimately leads to a devastating conclusion for all involved. The ending is both poignant and haunting, leaving the audience with a lasting impression of the characters' struggles and sacrifices.

Throughout the film, Chazelle pays homage to the era's iconic figures, including Charlie Chaplin, Mary Pickford, and Douglas Fairbanks. The cinematography is stunning, capturing the glamour and excess of 1920s Hollywood in vivid detail.

Overall, Babylon is a sweeping epic that explores the darker side of Hollywood's Golden Age. With its talented ensemble cast, intricate plot, and stunning visuals, the film is a must-see for fans of cinema history and drama enthusiasts alike.

title: Marry Me
overview: Music superstars Kat Valdez and Bastian are getting married before a global audience of fans. But when Kat learns, seconds before her vows, that Bastian has been unfaithful, she decides to marry Charlie, a stranger in the crowd, instead.
plot:
Marry Me is a 2022 American romantic comedy film directed by John M. Chu and written by Cassandra Peterson. The movie stars Jennifer Lopez, Owen Wilson, and Michael Caine.

The story begins with Alice (Jennifer Lopez), a successful music journalist who has lost touch with her passion for music after the death of her fiancé in a tragic accident. On the eve of her 40th birthday, she meets Charlie (Owen Wilson), a charming and charismatic musician who is about to get married to his girlfriend, Kate (played by Vanessa Hudgens).

During their conversation, Alice accidentally drinks a glass of champagne that Charlie had been saving for his wedding night, which contains a surprise twist - it's laced with a sedative that will make the drinker fall in love with the person they're with. Unbeknownst to Alice, this is a prank by Charlie, who wants to test whether he still has feelings for Kate.

As the night progresses, Alice finds herself falling deeply in love with Charlie, and she starts to question her own feelings about marriage and relationships. Meanwhile, Charlie's relationship with Kate begins to unravel as he realizes that his true feelings are for Alice.

The plot takes a turn when Alice discovers the truth behind the sedative and confronts Charlie about it. However, instead of being angry, she's touched by his vulnerability and willingness to take risks in love. The two start to develop real feelings for each other, but their relationship is put to the test as they navigate their past heartaches and fears.

As Alice and Charlie spend more time together, they realize that they have a deep connection and share similar values. They also discover that they both have unfinished business with Kate, who has been struggling to move on from her failed engagement.

In the end, Alice and Charlie must decide whether to follow their hearts or play it safe. In a heartwarming climax, they confess their love for each other and choose to take a chance on a new beginning together.

Throughout the movie, Jennifer Lopez shines as the lead character, bringing depth and nuance to Alice's emotional journey. Owen Wilson provides comedic relief and charm as Charlie, while Michael Caine adds a touch of sophistication and wit as Kate's father.

Overall, Marry Me is a delightful romantic comedy that explores themes of love, vulnerability, and taking risks. With its witty dialogue, engaging characters, and heartfelt performances, it's a must-watch for fans of the genre.

title: Armageddon Time
tagline: The end of an era. The beginning of everything.
overview: In 1980, Queens, New York, a young Jewish boy befriends a rebellious African-American classmate to the disapproval of his privileged family and begins to reckon with growing up in a world of inequality and prejudice.
plot:
In 1980 Queens, New York City, on his first day in sixth grade, Jewish-American Paul Graff becomes friends with a rebellious African-American classmate, Johnny Davis. Johnny was held back by a year and gets harsher treatment from their teacher when they both joke around in class. Paul often disengages from his schoolwork and draws pictures instead.
Paul lives with his financially stable family. He is close with his maternal grandfather, Aaron Rabinowitz, who encourages him to pursue his aspiration to become an artist. His well-meaning but strict parents, Esther and Irving, are less convinced of Paul's career prospects as an artist. At night, Aaron tells Paul the story of how Aaron's mother escaped antisemitic persecution in Ukraine, fleeing to London before eventually emigrating to the U.S. with Aaron and her British husband.
One day, Paul and Johnny are caught smoking a joint in the restrooms, unaware that it's an illegal drug. Furious, Esther allows Irving to beat Paul as punishment. In the hope that he becomes more disciplined, Paul is sent to the Forest Manor Prep private school by his parents, where his older brother Ted is studying. Meanwhile, Johnny stops going to school after being relegated to special education.
Forest Manor is financially supported by famous businessman Fred Trump, who also supports Ronald Reagan in the upcoming presidential election. Many of the students are also Reagan supporters. On Paul's first day, Fred's daughter Maryanne, one of the school's famous alumni, gives a speech to the students about working to earn their success. Paul sees the school's advantages over his previous school but doesn't feel welcome. He is also unnerved by other students' racist comments when Johnny meets with him during recess. Johnny begins living in secret at Paul's clubhouse, having nowhere to go other than living with his sick grandmother, where foster system workers searching for Johnny have begun to visit regularly.
While playing at the park on the weekend, Paul tells Aaron of his struggles at school and how he did nothing when he witnessed racism. Aaron encourages Paul to stand up against prejudice when he sees it, reminding him that while antisemitism still covertly persists, he and his family still have the privilege of being white. Shortly after, Aaron dies of bone cancer, with the family mourning his loss.
Tired of living under high expectations from family and school, as well as the unfair treatment of Johnny, Paul convinces Johnny to steal a computer from school and sell it so they can run away together. After stealing the computer, they are arrested for trying to pawn it. While being interrogated, Paul confesses that it was all his plan. But knowing that he has no options in life, Johnny takes the blame to let Paul go, much to Paul's dismay. Paul and Johnny bid farewell, as Irving arrives to take him home with no consequences because Irving once did the interrogating officer a favor.

title: The Broken Hearts Gallery
tagline: There's an art to letting go.
overview: Lucy is a young gallery assistant who collects mementos from her relationships. She discovers that she must let go of her past to move forward, and comes up with a lovely, artistic way to help herself and others who have suffered heartbreak.
plot:
Lucy is a young assistant at the Woolf Gallery in New York City. Idolizing her boss, Eva Woolf, she readily provides info about her to her boyfriend and colleague, Max. Her friends and roommates, law student Amanda and model Nadine, hear her talking non-stop about him. At the gallery opening, instead of Max asking her to move in, she is both dumped for his ex Amelia and fired.
Drunk and despondent, Lucy climbs into Nick's car, believing it is her Lyft. The kind Nick takes her home while she describes the gallery fiasco. For weeks, she wallows in her room, with her roommates' support. Finally, they urge her to clear out her cave of memorabilia from past relationships. Unable to sell her mementos, Lucy follows Max and Amelia into a restaurant. Nick sees her and steers her outside before she can cause a scene.
Lucy and Nick end up at the Chloe hotel, an old YMCA. Renovating his dream boutique hotel for five years, he is out of money and needs help to keep the project going. He encourages her to hang Max's tie on an old nail. Inspired, she writes a caption, and they jointly come up with the concept of a Broken Heart Gallery.
Nick shows up at Lucy's, inviting her to see something added to the wall. Excited, she envisions a chance for New Yorkers to connect over shared loss and humanity. Meeting and bonding with Marcos, Nick's friend on the building project, they convince Nick to give her gallery space in exchange for work.
Lucy shares photos with their stories on social media #BROKENHEARTGALLERY, then posts short videos of people parting with their memorabilia. She sees first-hand how freeing it is for people to give up their baggage.
Seeking furniture and decorations for the gallery-hotel, they pound the streets, reclaiming pieces as they go. On the way, they chat about themselves. The money to start the hotel came from his grandmother's inheritance. Lucy's mother sees art everywhere. Browsing in a secondhand-book shop, Lucy sees Max, follows him to a café, and meets Amelia. Nick rescues her again, saying they are off to a meeting about their hot new gallery. They leave, Max looking intrigued.
While Lucy is alone one day in the hotel-gallery, a cold, blonde woman arrives looking for Nick, and declines to leave a message. Shortly thereafter, the three roommates invite Nick, Marco and his wife to a karaoke night birthday bash. Lucy shows Nick New York magazine mentioning their project, and she tells him about her idea for a ball opening. They sing a "Don't Go Breaking My Heart" duet. Marco (like her roommates) suggests Nick ask her out.
Arriving home at 3 am, they find Max out front. After railing on him in Lucy's defense, Amanda and Nadine head up. Max is telling her he wants her back when Nick shows up with birthday cake and the men butt heads. She and Max stay out, talking, and she agrees to a lunch.
As Nick's loan falls through, he tells her to rehome her exhibit, so Lucy approaches every gallery she knows.

title: Breaking Surface
overview: Two Swedish/Norwegian half sisters go on a winter diving trip in Northern Norway, when they get trapped after a rockslide.
plot:
Breaking Surface is a 2020 survival thriller drama written and directed by Joachim Hedén, produced as a co-production between Sweden, Norway and Belgium. Moa Gammel and Madeleine Martin star as two half-sisters whose diving trip turns into a desperate fight for survival, with Lena Hope, Trine Wiggen and Maja Söderström in supporting roles.

Ida and her half-sister Tuva are experienced scuba divers whose relationship carries old tensions. For a winter diving trip they travel to the remote, snow-covered coastline of northern Norway, where they head out to dive in an isolated fjord. Not long after they descend into the icy water, a rockslide crashes down from the cliffs above, pinning Tuva beneath a heavy boulder on the seabed at a depth from which she cannot free herself.

With no other people nearby, no phone signal and the winter daylight quickly fading, Ida must keep her trapped sister alive as Tuva's air supply steadily runs out. Ida repeatedly races back and forth between the seabed, the shore and their car in search of fresh tanks, tools and help, battling exhaustion, the freezing temperatures and the physical dangers of repeated ascents and descents. Every decision carries a risk to both women, and old resentments surface as the sisters confront their shared history under extreme pressure. The film builds suspense through the claustrophobic underwater sequences and the stark beauty and isolation of the Arctic landscape, while exploring themes of sisterhood, endurance and survival against the indifferent power of nature.

The film was shot in Belgium, in Strömstad and Gothenburg in Sweden, and in the Lofoten islands of Norway. It premiered internationally at the virtual Nightstream Film Festival in October 2020 after its Swedish release earlier that year. Critical response was very positive, with a 100% rating on Rotten Tomatoes from seven reviews. Peter Martin of ScreenAnarchy wrote that it consistently surprises as it develops into a gripping story of survival, Bloody Disgusting awarded it four skulls out of five, and Film Threat rated it seven out of ten. The film was remade in English in 2023 as The Dive, starring Sophie Lowe and Louisa Krause.

title: Halloween Ends
overview: Four years after the events of Halloween in 2018, Laurie has decided to liberate herself from fear and rage and embrace life. But when a young man is accused of killing a boy he was babysitting, it ignites a cascade of violence and terror that will force Laurie to finally confront the evil she can’t control, once and for all.
plot:
Halloween Ends is a 2022 American slasher film directed by David Gordon Green, who co-wrote it with Danny McBride, Paul Brad Logan and Chris Bernier. The thirteenth Halloween film and the sequel to Halloween Kills (2021), it concludes the trilogy that began with the 2018 film, a direct follow-up to the 1978 original. Green conceived it as a love story. After pandemic delays, it was filmed in Georgia from January to March 2022. It premiered at Beyond Fest in Los Angeles on October 11, 2022, and Universal Pictures released it on October 14, simultaneously streaming on Peacock.

On Halloween night in 2019, Corey Cunningham, 21, is babysitting a boy named Jeremy, who locks him in the attic as a prank; when Corey kicks the door open, Jeremy tumbles over the railing to his death. Cleared in court, Corey is still shunned by Haddonfield. Three years later, Michael Myers has vanished, and Laurie Strode is writing a memoir and living with her granddaughter, Allyson. After Laurie helps Corey when he is hurt escaping bullies, he and Allyson begin dating. Thrown off a bridge by the bullies, Corey is dragged into the sewers by Michael, who chokes him but lets him live. Soon afterward Corey kills a homeless man in a struggle, then lures Allyson's ex-boyfriend, a police officer, to Michael, and kills the doctor who passed Allyson over for a promotion while Michael kills the nurse involved. Laurie senses Michael's evil in Corey, straining her bond with Allyson.

When Laurie tells Corey to leave Allyson alone, he vows that no one else will have her, overpowers Michael, takes his mask and goes on a rampage, killing the bullies, his mother and a radio DJ. Laurie fakes a suicide attempt to lure him to her house; after she shoots him, Corey stabs himself to frame her in front of Allyson, and Michael arrives and breaks his neck. Laurie fights Michael, unmasks him and cuts his throat, and Allyson returns to help her finish him. With the town following in procession, they feed his body into an industrial shredder. Allyson leaves Haddonfield, and Laurie completes her memoir, reunites romantically with Deputy Frank Hawkins and keeps Michael's mask.

Jamie Lee Curtis plays Laurie, with Andi Matichak as Allyson, Rohan Campbell as Corey, Will Patton as Hawkins and James Jude Courtney as Michael. Reviews were mixed, with 40% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, though Curtis and Campbell were praised. It grossed $105 million on a $33 million budget.

title: Theatre: A Love Story
overview: Nagata works as a writer and director for theater company Oroka. His work has not received positive responses and ticket sales has not increased. Making things worse, his relationship with the theatrical troupe is not good. Nagata feels lonely. One day, he sees a woman named Saki  on the street. She is wearing the same sneakers as he is. Nagata talks to her. Saki is a university student and she dreams of becoming an actress. Nagata and Saki fall in love.
plot:
Theatre: A Love Story (Japanese: Gekijō) is a 2020 Japanese romantic drama directed by Isao Yukisada from a screenplay by Ryūta Hōrai, adapted from the novel by comedian and author Naoki Matayoshi. The book, Matayoshi's first love story, was serialised in the literary magazine Shinchō in April 2017 and published by Shinchosha the following month; like his earlier Spark, it follows a young artist chasing success in Tokyo. The film's score was composed by Keiichi Sokabe.

Kento Yamazaki plays Nagata, a struggling playwright and director who co-founded the small theatre company Oroka with his school friend Nohara (Kanichiro Sato). His avant-garde productions draw poor reviews and few ticket sales, and his relations with the troupe are deteriorating. Wandering the streets in a daze, he stops at a gallery window and notices a young woman, Saki (Mayu Matsuoka), who is wearing the same sneakers as him. Saki has come to Tokyo from Aomori to study at a fashion college and dreams of becoming an actress, and the two fall in love. Nagata soon moves into her apartment, contributing nothing towards the rent while she works several jobs. Over the years his insecurity, jealousy of other people's success and possessive, dismissive treatment of her gradually wear Saki down, leaving her depressed and drinking heavily as she nears thirty. A former troupe member, Aoyama (Sairi Ito), and Nohara confront him about his behaviour, and Nagata ultimately turns their story into a stage play. Satoru Iguchi of the band King Gnu appears as Komine, a rival playwright of the same age, with Shusaku Kamikawa, Ritsu Otomo and Kodai Asaka in supporting roles.

The film, made by The Fool and distributed by Shochiku and Aniplex, was due to open on 17 April 2020, but the release was postponed indefinitely as COVID-19 spread in Japan. In June, Yoshimoto Kogyo took over distribution, and the film opened in cinemas on 17 July 2020 while also streaming worldwide on Amazon Prime Video the same day, reportedly the first time a Japanese live-action feature had done so.

Sairi Ito won the Blue Ribbon Award for Best Supporting Actress. Reviews were divided over the central character. The Japan Times headlined its review as a tortured romance with no sparks, while Windows on Worlds read the film as a portrait of toxic narcissism and abusive behaviour, seen only through Nagata's eyes, that ends with him rediscovering his love of theatre and accepting that a chapter of life has closed.

title: The Last Duel
tagline: The true story of a woman who defied a nation and made history.
overview: King Charles VI declares that Knight Jean de Carrouges settle his dispute with his squire, Jacques Le Gris, by challenging him to a duel.
plot:
While the plot of the film is portrayed in three separate chapters, each telling the same story from the perspective of the three main characters, the following description summarizes all three presentations into a single narrative:
After serving in the Caroline War, French squire Jean de Carrouges and his comrade Jacques le Gris swear allegiance to Count Pierre d'Alençon, who has been named Jean's overlord by King Charles VI. To improve his finances, Jean marries Marguerite de Thibouville on the promise of a large dowry from her father Robert that includes the rights to many valuable estates. Pierre, however, seizes the prized estate of Aunou-le-Faucon to settle Robert's back taxes and gifts it to Jacques, who has become one of Pierre's favorites. Jean appeals to King Charles, but the king upholds Pierre's decision, and the count exacts revenge by depriving Jean of a prominent captaincy previously held by his late father and gifting it to Jacques, making him superior to Jean in rank.
Jean's marriage becomes strained due to the couple's failure to conceive. He and Jacques reconcile at a celebration, where Jacques becomes smitten with Marguerite after she befriends him in an attempt to win favor. Jacques misinterprets this as a reciprocation of his affections, coming to believe she actually does not love Jean.
Following his participation in a failed military campaign in Scotland that sees him knighted but still bankrupt, Jean sets off for Paris to collect his promised rewards. Marguerite demonstrates a talent for managing the estate in his absence; while collecting taxes from her peasants, she also learns Jean regularly defers the poorest from their obligation. One day, when Marguerite is left alone at the chateau, Jacques visits and tricks his way in, haughtily proclaiming his love. Marguerite rejects his advances and attempts to flee, but he chases her to her room and rapes her before ordering her not to tell her husband. Upon Jean's return, Marguerite tells him of the assault; after questioning whether she is telling the truth, Jean becomes convinced that Jacques raped Marguerite to insult him specifically. Jean insists that Marguerite immediately have sex with him so that Jacques will not be "the last man that knew her."
Pierre informs Jacques that Jean is accusing him of raping Marguerite, which he denies. Despite the count's attempt to exert his authority, Jean appeals his case directly to King Charles and requests a duel to the death. Jacques accepts, having decided not to seek a favorable forum of a Catholic ecclesiastical court. Marguerite's friends abandon her, believing her to be lying to cover up an affair, while Jean's mother, who was also raped as a youth but never revealed the truth, insists Marguerite drop her accusations. At Jacques' trial six months later, a now-pregnant Marguerite remains resolute that she is telling the truth, while the court implies that Jacques is the father of her child.

title: The Other Lamb
overview: For her entire life, the cult she was born into has been all that teenage Selah has known. Along with a band of similarly cloistered young women she lives seemingly unstuck in time, cut off from modern society in a remote forest commune presided over by a man called Shepherd, a controlling, messiah-like figure with a frightening dark side. But when her insular world is rocked by a series of nightmarish visions and disturbing revelations, Selah begins to question everything about her existence—including her allegiance to the increasingly dangerous Shepherd.
plot:
The Other Lamb is a 2019 horror film directed by Małgorzata Szumowska and written by Catherine Smyth-McMullen, based on her short story "The Other-faced Lamb". Raffey Cassidy stars as Selah, a teenage girl raised in a cult, with Michiel Huisman as its leader, the Shepherd, and Denise Gough as Sarah, one of his first wives.

Selah lives in a remote forest compound run by a polygamist cult whose messianic leader, the Shepherd, is its only man. The women are divided into the younger Sisters, dressed in blue, and the older Wives, dressed in red, and the group raises sheep for food and sacrifice. As she grows up, Selah draws more of the Shepherd's attention and seems attracted to him, while wondering about her mother, who she was told died giving birth to her. Sent with leftovers to the dark hut where "unclean" menstruating women are kept, she meets Sarah, a scarred and banished Wife, who warns her about the Shepherd's violence. When a police officer orders the group to move on, the Shepherd leads the women on a long trek toward a new home. After Selah begins to menstruate she is forced to walk at the back with Sarah, who reveals that she and Selah's mother were the first two wives and that her mother died of an infection because the Shepherd refused to take her to hospital. On the journey a pregnant Wife dies in childbirth, the Shepherd treats her grieving daughter harshly, and Sarah leaves with the newborn, whom he wanted to abandon because "there can only be one ram in a flock". When he beats a Sister named Tamar, Selah's doubts deepen. At a lakeside valley he proclaims their new Eden, but Selah is haunted by visions of him drowning her and, after he chooses her for sex and chokes her, dreams of the women devouring him. The next morning the Wives have vanished, and the Shepherd tells the Sisters that they have ascended and must take their place. Selah defies him, declaring that he is not their shepherd. Later, police find the Wives' bodies washed up on the shore and the Shepherd's corpse strung between two trees with ram's horns on his head, while the Sisters, led by Selah, gather at a waterfall near their old compound.

Shot in County Wicklow, Ireland, the film premiered at the 2019 Toronto International Film Festival. IFC Midnight released it in the United States on 3 April 2020, largely on video on demand because of pandemic closures. Reviews were generally favourable, with a 75% Rotten Tomatoes rating.

title: The Harder They Fall
overview: Gunning for revenge, outlaw Nat Love saddles up with his gang to take down enemy Rufus Buck, a ruthless crime boss who just got sprung from prison.
plot:
Eleven-year-old Nat Love is eating dinner with his parents when Rufus Buck and his associate Cortez arrive. Nat's father begs Buck to spare his wife and son and asks Buck for forgiveness, but Buck shoots and kills both of Nat's parents and then carves a cross into his forehead.
Twenty years later, Love finds and kills Cortez. Meanwhile, his partners, sharpshooter Bill Pickett and quick draw Jim Beckwourth, ambush the Crimson Hood gang and steal their haul from a recent bank robbery. The lone survivor tells them the $25,000 they have stolen belongs to Buck. Love travels to meet his former lover Mary Fields, who runs a chain of saloons. Pickett brings news of the heist to Love.
Buck's gang, led by Trudy Smith and Cherokee Bill, forcefully free Buck from a train leaving from Yuma Territorial Prison. They reveal Buck has been pardoned, and they have been paid to kill the corrupt U.S. Army soldiers guarding the prison car. After slaughtering the soldiers, Buck and his gang arrive in their former stronghold of Redwood City, now run by Buck's associate, Sheriff Wiley Escoe. Learning that Escoe has used the position to profit at the expense of the town, Buck brutally pistol whips him and orders him to leave town. Buck gathers the townspeople and after killing a naysayer, demands that they raise $50,000 to save Redwood, threatening to kill and burn the property of any who resist.
U.S. Marshal Bass Reeves arrests Love after a standoff in a saloon. However, Reeves reveals to Love that Buck has been released, and he offers him a chance for revenge. Love's gang, accompanied by Fields and her friend and enforcer, Cuffee, arrive and insist on joining. They encounter Escoe, who tells them Buck has returned to Redwood. Fields volunteers to scout Redwood under the cover of offering to buy Smith's saloon. Love proposes marriage to Fields, but she turns him down.
When Fields arrives in Redwood, Smith takes her prisoner and beats her. Love's gang arrives, and Love joins Fields in captivity to save her life. Smith has Love beaten, and he in turn asks Buck to release Fields. Buck demands Love return the money he stole plus $10,000 as 'interest', requiring him to rob a bank in a white town. Love and Cuffee rob the bank without killing anyone and escape. However, the group recognizes that Buck is unlikely to release Fields willingly, so they devise a plan to rig a decoy wagon with dynamite.
They enter Redwood and the decoy wagon is destroyed, killing some of Buck's gang. Love prepares to hand over the money, but is interrupted by Cherokee Bill preparing to shoot him in the back. Beckwourth intervenes, challenging Bill to a quick draw showdown. Bill shoots and kills Beckwourth before he can finish counting down, causing a gunfight to erupt. Love, Reeves, Pickett, and Cuffee kill most of Buck's gang, and the money is destroyed in another explosion. Escoe infiltrates Buck's house but is killed by Buck, while Pickett and Love are wounded.

title: Mosul
overview: When ISIS took their homes, families and city, one group of men fought to take it all back. Based on true events, this is the story of the Nineveh SWAT team, a renegade police unit who waged a guerrilla operation against ISIS in a desperate struggle to save their home city of Mosul.
plot:
Mosul is a 2019 Arabic-language American war film written and directed by Matthew Michael Carnahan, inspired by Luke Mogelson's New Yorker article about the 2016 Battle of Mosul, in which Iraqi government forces and their allies drove ISIS from the city it had held since 2014. Adam Bessa plays young policeman Kawa, with Suhail Dabbach as Major Jasem, Is'haq Elias as Waleed and Waleed Elgadi as an Iranian colonel.

During the battle, three Iraqi policemen who have arrested ISIS drug smugglers are overrun and run out of ammunition, and Kawa, a 21-year-old Feyli Kurd, loses his uncle in the fighting. They are rescued by the Nineveh SWAT team, a unit of Mosul natives who have lost relatives to ISIS, led by Major Jasem. Because his uncle was killed by ISIS, Kawa is invited to join, while his partner Jameel takes the uncle's body for burial. The unit presses on with a mission whose purpose no one will explain to Kawa. Resting in an abandoned building, Kawa and Jasem see Jameel guide an ISIS car bomber to their position, and the blast kills the team member Tomahawk, whose axe Jasem gives to Kawa. Distrusted as a traitor's partner, Kawa grows frustrated. Crossing into ISIS-held territory, the team loses Hooka to rooftop gunmen and a Humvee to an explosive drone.

An Iranian colonel commanding Popular Mobilization Forces in the city trades the unit ammunition for cigarettes, and Jasem finds Jameel among his prisoners. Jameel says ISIS forced him to betray them by threatening his grandson in Michigan, and as tensions rise between the two forces, Kawa kills Jameel with the axe. When Jasem finally begins to explain the mission, Kawa says he no longer needs to know. Friendly fire kills Youness and disfigures Kawa, and more men fall as the unit storms an ISIS camp, where Jasem is killed by a booby trap. Kawa rallies the shaken survivors, and Waleed leads them to an apartment, unlocks it with a hidden key and kills an ISIS fighter who has taken his wife and daughter. Kawa realizes the unit has been rescuing captured family members, and on learning that a comrade's son is nearby, he asks how far.

Shot in Marrakesh, the film premiered at the 2019 Venice Film Festival and was released on Netflix on November 26, 2020. It holds 84% on Rotten Tomatoes and 71 on Metacritic. After the film drew large audiences in Europe and the Middle East, cast members received death threats from people claiming ISIS ties.

title: Batman: Death in the Family
tagline: The fate of Gotham is in your hands.
overview: Tragedy strikes the Batman's life again when Robin Jason Todd tracks down his birth mother only to run afoul of the Joker. An adaptation of the 1988 comic book storyline of the same name.
plot:
Released in 2020 under the DC Showcase banner, Batman: Death in the Family is an animated interactive superhero film for adult audiences that imagines different outcomes for "A Death in the Family," the 1988 comics arc in which the second Robin, Jason Todd, was murdered by the Joker. Brandon Vietti produced, wrote and directed it, and the voice cast is led by Bruce Greenwood as Batman, Vincent Martella as Jason Todd and John DiMaggio as the Joker, with Zehra Fazal as Talia al Ghul and Gary Cole as Commissioner Gordon and Two-Face. It serves as a spiritual successor and tie-in to the 2010 film Batman: Under the Red Hood, and came out on Blu-ray on 13 October 2020.

The disc version lets the viewer choose at key moments, echoing the original comic's reader poll that decided Jason's fate; a choice must be made within ten seconds or a default is taken. Its branching paths lead to seven endings, while the digital release replaces the interactivity with four fixed story paths.

The story begins with Batman suspending Jason as Robin because of his growing brutality. Jason leaves Gotham, and the two meet again in Bosnia, where the Joker and Ra's al Ghul are stealing uranium for dirty bombs. The Joker captures Robin, beats him with a crowbar and leaves him in a warehouse rigged to explode. If Robin dies, the events of Under the Red Hood unfold, with Jason resurrected in the Lazarus Pit to return as the Red Hood. If he survives the blast, he emerges scarred and bandaged, kills a string of Gotham villains, and accepts Talia's offer to help him hunt the Joker in exchange for raising her son with Bruce, Damian. If Batman saves Robin, Bruce dies in the explosion and Dick Grayson takes up the cowl, and further choices follow. Jason may kill a seemingly reformed Joker in a diner and then either go to prison or become the murderous Red Robin, whose fate rests on a coin toss by Two-Face. Or he may take the Red Hood identity to capture the Joker alive, only to face a Bruce driven mad by the Lazarus Pit and revived by Talia, a confrontation that ends in either mutual destruction or Bruce's rescue and an attempt to cure him.

Most of the Under the Red Hood voice cast returned, with Martella also taking over the Red Hood role from Jensen Ackles. Critical response was positive, with seven of nine reviews on Rotten Tomatoes favorable.

title: Penguin Bloom
tagline: The true story of an unlikely hero.
overview: When an unlikely ally enters the Bloom family's world in the form of an injured baby magpie they name Penguin, the bird’s arrival makes a profound difference in the struggling family’s life.
plot:
Mother of three Sam Bloom accidentally falls off a roof due to a rotten wooden bracket during her family's summer vacation in Thailand. She breaks her T6 thoracic vertebrae, resulting in partial paralysis from her mid-back down. Back home in Australia, Sam, once an avid surfer, struggles to adjust to life as a paraplegic, but is supported by her husband Cameron, their three sons Noah, Rueben, and Oli, and Sam's overbearing mother Jan.
In the first months, Sam lacks motivation to interact, closing the curtains to sit in the dark, deliberately pushing a glass jar of honey on the floor, etc. She is encouraged by her mother and Cameron to leave the house, but she resists. One afternoon, the three boys find and bring home a magpie chick, which fell out of its nest, who they name Penguin.
Sam becomes despondent upon hearing one of the boys crying out for his father, having become violently ill from a bad oyster. Feeling useless, she cries with frustration. Noah asks Sam to work on getting Penguin to eat. Initially feeling too down to care for the bird, she musters the strength to help, understanding it is important to Noah. As time goes on, Sam bonds with Penguin.
Feeling guilty for being the one who asked his mum to go up to the roof in Thailand, Noah has withdrawn from her since the accident. Sam and Cameron's relationship also deteriorates as she struggles to find joy in daily life and wishes to forget who she was before the fall, since she can no longer live in the same way. She demands he never ask her how she is.
After several weeks, Penguin fully recovers and learns to fly, inspiring Sam to want to do something for herself; she starts kayaking lessons. For Sam's birthday, the Blooms go for dinner at Jan's house, joined by Sam's sister Kylie and Sam's kayaking instructor Gaye. While Jan and Cameron argue about Sam's new life and their responsibilities to her, Penguin is attacked by two larger magpies and then flies away.
Sam eventually confronts Noah about his guilt and tells him he is not to blame for what happened to her. She apologises for being distant and reveals she has found her strength, and the whole family reconcile. Sam requests Cameron ask her how she is, and when he does, she replies, "I'm better."
When Penguin returns home a few days later, Sam thanks her for helping her recover, before the bird flies away for good.

title: The Platform
tagline: There are 3 kinds of people; the ones above, the ones below, and the ones who fall.
overview: A mysterious place, an indescribable prison, a deep hole. An unknown number of levels. Two inmates living on each level. A descending platform containing food for all of them. An inhuman fight for survival, but also an opportunity for solidarity.
plot:
A man named Goreng awakens in a cell numbered 48. His cellmate Trimagasi explains that they are in a tower-style holding facility. Once per day, food arrives on "the platform" that lowers from level 0, stopping for two minutes on each level. Prisoners can eat only while the platform is stopped on their level, and are subjected to fatal temperatures if they keep any food. Prisoners are randomly reassigned to a new level each month. Trimagasi reveals that when assigned to level 132, he and his former cellmate cannibalized someone. One day, a woman named Miharu rides down the platform, whom Trimagasi explains regularly descends the pit to search for her child. Goreng explains that he volunteered to spend six months in the facility in exchange for a diploma, while Trimagasi confides that he is serving a year-long sentence for manslaughter.
The following month, they are reassigned to level 171. Trimagasi ties up Goreng and explains his plans to feed himself using Goreng's flesh. When he begins cutting into Goreng's leg, Miharu arrives, attacks Trimagasi, and frees Goreng, who kills Trimagasi. Encouraged by Miharu, Goreng eats Trimagasi's flesh and subsequently becomes haunted by hallucinations of Trimagasi.
The next month, Goreng wakes on level 33 with a woman named Imoguiri and her dog, Ramesses II. Imoguiri was the administration official who interviewed Goreng before sending him to the pit, having admitted herself after being diagnosed with terminal cancer. Imoguiri only eats every other day, letting Ramesses II eat on the days that she does not, and tries unsuccessfully to convince the pair below them to ration their food. One day, Miharu arrives injured. Goreng and Imoguiri nurse her back to health. That night, Goreng breaks up a fight between Miharu and Imoguiri to then discover that Miharu has killed Ramesses II. After Miharu leaves, Goreng mentions her child to Imoguiri, who says there are no children in the pit and Miharu came alone. The following morning, Goreng wakes to find that they have been reassigned to level 202 and that Imoguiri has hanged herself. He consumes her flesh, plagued with hallucinations of his former cellmates.
The next month, Goreng is assigned to level 6. His new cellmate, Baharat, is a religious man who has been attempting to escape the pit for months. Estimating that there are 250 levels, Goreng convinces Baharat to ride the platform down with him and ration the food. They forbid anyone on the first fifty levels to receive any, arguing that they get to eat every day, and fend off those who defy them. Fellow prisoner Sr. Brambang advises them that civility is more effective than violence and convinces them to send a symbolic message to the administration by leaving a single panna cotta untouched.
As they descend further, they hand out portions to the prisoners, attacking those who refuse to cooperate. They encounter Miharu being attacked and try to save her, but she is killed and they are both left severely injured.

title: Inside Man: Most Wanted
overview: An NYPD hostage negotiator teams up with a federal agent to rescue dozens of tourists held hostage during a 10-hour seige at the U.S. Federal Reserve.
plot:
Inside Man: Most Wanted is a 2019 American crime thriller film directed by M. J. Bassett and a sequel to Spike Lee's 2006 film Inside Man, made after plans for a sequel with the original cast were cancelled in 2011. It stars Aml Ameen as NYPD hostage negotiator Remy Darbonne, Rhea Seehorn as FBI hostage negotiator Brynn Stewart and Roxanne McKee as the bank robber Ariella Barash, with Jessica Sutton as her sister Ava, Urs Rechn as the robber Joseph and Akshay Kumar as FBI agent Ansh Ramachandra.

Five years after Dalton Russell's crew robbed the bank of Arthur Case and exposed him as a Nazi collaborator, a gang of robbers led by Ariella Barash seizes the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, taking everyone inside hostage. Their target is a large hoard of Nazi gold kept in the building. A joint task force headed by Stewart and Darbonne is deployed, and as the two negotiate with Ariella, who calls herself "Most Wanted", each begins separately to piece together her real motives. Arthur Case has died under house arrest, and his son Dietrich has taken Dalton, whose real name is David Barash, hostage, forcing his sister Ariella to stage the heist so that Dietrich can recover the fortune his father lost. Unknown to the negotiators and to the rest of her crew, Ariella and her sister Ava have engineered the robbery to look like a failure, leaving subtle clues for the investigators to find. Ava, outside the bank, gets close to Darbonne by claiming that her abusive ex-boyfriend is one of the robbers. Ariella leaves a family photograph in a safety deposit box that reveals the siblings' connection to David, and gives Stewart a mobile phone to guarantee Dietrich's arrest and the recovery of the gold. The FBI arrests Dietrich and recovers the gold, but not before he orders the execution of David, held captive by Nazis in Berlin. In the aftermath, Darbonne and Stewart wonder what has become of Ariella and Ava, and Darbonne predicts that Ariella is alive and that people will die once she learns her brother is dead. In a mid-credits scene, a disguised Ariella walks into a bar in Berlin and guns down Dietrich's men, avenging David.

Ameen was cast in November 2018, and the score was composed by Sonya Belousova and Giona Ostinelli. The film was released direct to video in the United States on 24 September 2019 and also made available on Netflix and other digital platforms.

title: Sweet Girl
overview: A man vows to bring justice to those responsible for his wife's death while protecting the only family he has left, his daughter.
plot:
Sweet Girl is a 2021 American action thriller directed by Brian Andrew Mendoza in his feature debut, from a screenplay by Philip Eisner and Gregg Hurwitz. Jason Momoa, who also produced, stars as Ray Cooper and Isabela Merced as his daughter Rachel, with Manuel Garcia-Rulfo as the hitman Santos, Amy Brenneman as Congresswoman Diana Morgan, Adria Arjona as Ray's wife Amanda, Justin Bartha as Simon Keeley and Lex Scott Davis as FBI agent Sarah Meeker. It was filmed in Pittsburgh.

In Pittsburgh, survival expert Ray and his teenage daughter Rachel train together in mixed martial arts at his gym. When Amanda is stricken with cancer, a promising drug from the company BioPrime might save her, but it is pulled from the market after CEO Simon Keeley pays to delay its production. Ray phones a live television interview and threatens Keeley's life. Amanda dies, and months later the journalist Martin Bennett offers Ray evidence of BioPrime's corruption. Their meeting on a subway train is cut short when Santos stabs Bennett to death, wounds Ray and knocks Rachel unconscious.

Two years later Ray, who has been tracking the company ever since, confronts Keeley at a charity auction, learns that chairman Vinod Shah is behind the scheme, and kills him. Fleeing with Rachel, he fights off mercenaries at a motel and plans to ambush Shah, only for Santos to shoot Shah first. Over a tense meeting in a diner, Santos agrees to a temporary truce and points them to his true employer, Congresswoman Morgan. Cornered by the FBI on the roof of PNC Park, the truth emerges: Ray died of his wounds on the subway, and Rachel, traumatized and suffering from dissociative identity disorder, has carried out the revenge herself. She escapes custody, kills Santos, records Morgan's confession of taking bribes and ordering the killings, and sends it to the FBI. Morgan is arrested, and Rachel leaves the country with a false passport.

Sweet Girl was released on Netflix on 20 August 2021. Critics were largely unimpressed: it holds a 24% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus faulted its action clichés and late twist while crediting its well-matched leads, and a Metacritic score of 46. The Hollywood Reporter praised its efficient action and use of Pittsburgh locations but found the violence increasingly mindless.
