title: Don't Worry Darling
tagline: Are you ready to live the life you deserve?
overview: Alice and Jack are lucky to be living in the idealized community of Victory, the experimental company town housing the men who work for the top-secret Victory Project and their families. But when cracks in their idyllic life begin to appear, exposing flashes of something much more sinister lurking beneath the attractive façade, Alice can’t help questioning exactly what they’re doing in Victory, and why.
plot:
Alice and Jack Chambers live in Victory, California, an idyllic 1950s desert company town. Every day, the men leave for work at Victory Headquarters in the surrounding desert, and their wives enjoy luxuries and leisure while the men are gone. Alice spends her days with other wives, including her best friend, Bunny. Fellow resident Margaret has become estranged from the community. An unauthorized desert visit resulted in her son's apparent death, which caused her mental breakdown. Margaret insists that Victory took him as punishment for breaking the rules.
Victory's founder, Frank, hosts a party, during which Alice sees Margaret's husband attempt to medicate her after an outburst. Alice and Jack then have sex in Frank's home as Frank watches unbeknownst to Jack. From the trolley, Alice sees a plane crash in the desert, so she rushes to help. Stumbling onto Headquarters, she touches one of its mirror-like windows, experiencing surreal hallucinations about another life, waking up at home that night.
Alice continues to have increasingly strange experiences or hallucinations. Soon after, she sees Margaret slit her own throat and fall from her roof. Men in red jumpsuits drag Alice away, preventing her from reaching Margaret's body. Jack dismisses Alice's claims, insisting Margaret is simply recovering from a household accident. When Alice asks him what is really happening at the Victory Project, he becomes angry and refuses to answer. The town physician, Dr. Collins, prescribes medication to Alice, which she and Jack decline. She steals Margaret's medical file from his briefcase and finds it heavily redacted.
Becoming increasingly paranoid during a company celebration promoting Jack, Alice breaks down in the bathroom. Confronted by Bunny, she attempts to explain her suspicions. Bunny reacts angrily when Alice tells her she went to Headquarters, accusing her of jeopardizing their livelihood in Victory, like Margaret. Alice and Jack invite neighbors to dinner, including Frank and his wife, Shelley. Frank privately confirms her suspicions and dares her to challenge him. So, Alice attempts to expose him, but he makes her appear delusional to everyone, causing Jack grief.
Afterwards, Alice tries to tell Jack what Frank said, but he rebukes her. Desperate, she begs him to leave Victory with her. He feigns agreement, then lets Frank's men take her away. Dr. Collins gives Alice electroconvulsive therapy, during which she sees herself in the 21st century, as surgical resident Alice Warren, living with the unemployed Jack. After treatment, Alice resumes her life in Victory, but soon deduces the visions are actually memories. Confronted by Alice, Jack confesses the truth: Victory is a simulated world created by Frank, where he and the other men lead their version of perfect lives; the women they have in the simulation are unaware that everything in Victory, including their children, is artificial.

title: Malignant
overview: Madison is paralyzed by shocking visions of grisly murders, and her torment worsens as she discovers that these waking dreams are in fact terrifying realities with a mysterious tie to her past.
plot:
Malignant is a 2021 American psychological horror film written and directed by James Wan. The film follows the story of Madison Mitchell, played by Annabelle Wallis, who begins to experience terrifying hallucinations and nightmares after witnessing a murder as a child.

The film's narrative is presented in a non-linear fashion, with each chapter representing a different time period in Madison's life. The story jumps back and forth between Madison's childhood, her teenage years, and her present-day struggles with mental health.

As the film progresses, it becomes clear that Madison's experiences are not just random hallucinations, but rather a manifestation of her own dark past. She had witnessed a murder as a child, which left her with severe emotional trauma. The killer, who is revealed to be a woman named Sarah, was never caught and has been stalking Madison for years.

Throughout the film, Wan employs his signature use of jump scares and atmospheric tension to create a sense of unease and dread. However, Malignant also explores themes of mental health, trauma, and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy.

One of the standout aspects of the film is its use of symbolism and metaphor. The color red is used throughout the film as a symbol of blood and violence, while the number 13 appears repeatedly, representing bad luck and misfortune.

As the story unfolds, Madison's past and present begin to converge, and she must confront her demons in order to survive. The film's climax features a shocking twist that reveals the true nature of Sarah and her connection to Madison.

Ultimately, Malignant is a complex and thought-provoking horror film that explores themes of trauma, mental health, and the power of the human psyche. While it may not be as polished as some of Wan's other films, Malignant is a gripping and unsettling ride that will keep viewers on the edge of their seats.

It's worth noting that James Wan has stated in interviews that he was inspired by classic horror films such as The Exorcist and Rosemary's Baby, as well as his own experiences with anxiety and depression. This is reflected in the film's themes and tone, which are both deeply unsettling and thought-provoking.

title: Deep Water
tagline: The love story is never the whole story.
overview: Vic and Melinda Van Allen are a couple in the small town of Little Wesley. Their loveless marriage is held together only by a precarious arrangement whereby, in order to avoid the messiness of divorce, Melinda is allowed to take any number of lovers as long as she does not desert her family.
plot:
Melinda and Vic Van Allen live with their young daughter Trixie in Little Wesley, Louisiana. Vic has retired early after developing guidance chips for combat drones, and his complicated relationship with Melinda is held together by a precarious arrangement: they sleep apart and Melinda takes lovers openly, even in their family home, while Vic finds solace in raising his large collection of snails. Their open marriage is no secret to their concerned friends, and Vic grows increasingly jealous, while Melinda laments his lack of passion.
Melinda invites her latest lover, Joel, to a neighbour's party. Alone with Joel, Vic tells him that he murdered Melinda's previous lover Martin, who has recently disappeared. The story spreads through their circle of friends, raising the suspicions of noir writer Don Wilson. Joel comes to dinner with the Van Allen family, and Vic elaborates in private that he killed Martin with a hammer, frightening Joel into leaving town. A TV news report reveals that Martin's body has been found shot to death, and a suspect is arrested.
Vic confronts Melinda after she gives money to Charlie, her new lover and piano teacher. She invites Charlie to a friend's pool party and introduces him to Vic, toying with his jealousy. Rain sends everyone inside, leaving Vic and Charlie alone in the water. After Melinda discovers Charlie's body drowned in the pool, the party is questioned by police, and Melinda is quick to accuse Vic of murdering Charlie. He later asks if she is scared of him, and she says she is not as "I'm the one you killed for".
Don's wife Kelly tells Vic that Don and Melinda have been accusing him of Charlie's murder. Vic discovers they have hired a private investigator to follow him and confronts Don in front of Don's family. Melinda reconnects with an old boyfriend, Tony, and Vic overhears their conversation suggesting they will move to Brazil, taking Trixie with them. She invites Tony to dinner with Vic and takes him to her bedroom, furthering Vic's jealousy.
Vic lures Tony into his car and drives Tony to a secluded spot he and Melinda share, overlooking a rocky gorge. title: The Legend of Hei
overview: In the bustling human world, spirits live peacefully with mankind. Luo Xiaohei, a young cat spirit, becomes a nomad after his forest home is destroyed. His natural talent soon attracts spirits and humans alike, but all of them have their own motivations.
plot:
The Legend of Hei (Chinese: 罗小黑战记, Luó Xiǎohēi Zhàn Jì) is a 2019 Chinese animated fantasy action film directed by Zhang Ping, known professionally as MTJJ, who co-wrote it with Kexin Peng. It is a prequel to The Legend of Luo Xiaohei, the popular Flash-animated web series MTJJ began in 2011, and it tells the earlier story of its title character, a young cat spirit. The Chinese voice cast is led by Shan Xin as Hei, Liu Mingyue as the human warrior Wuxian (Infinity) and Hao Xianghai as the spirit Fengxi (Stormend).

The film is set in a modern world where spirits and humans have both fought and coexisted for centuries, with many ancient spirits either hiding from civilization or blending into it. Hei, who can shift between the form of a small black kitten, a large ferocious cat and a boy with cat ears and a tail, is woken in his forest by the noise of machines as loggers clear his home. Overpowered while trying to resist, he finds himself adrift in the human world, scavenging and stealing food from town to town. When a gang of teenagers corners him one night, he is rescued by Stormend, a powerful spirit who takes him to a hidden forest refuge and introduces him to fellow spirits who share a hatred of humans. Hei at last feels he has found a family.

The next day the group is attacked by Infinity, a formidable human with powers like theirs, who separates Hei from the others and takes him captive, intending to bring him to the Guild, a council that oversees relations between humans and spirits. On the long journey to its headquarters the two gradually warm to each other. Infinity trains Hei to harness his latent abilities, shows him better sides of human life, and tells him that Stormend's aim is to destroy humanity. As Stormend's plans escalate into open conflict with the Guild, Hei is forced to choose between the friend who sheltered him and the mentor who has taught him to question revenge.

The Legend of Hei opened in China in September 2019; a Japanese-dubbed version followed a month later through Toho, and Shout! Studios released an English dub in North America in 2021. Critics praised its fast, inventive action, comic timing, world-building and morally ambiguous treatment of its environmental themes, comparing it to Studio Ghibli and Avatar: The Last Airbender, while noting rushed pacing and many late, unexplained characters. A sequel, The Legend of Hei II, was released in 2025.

title: Jexi
overview: Phil's new phone comes with an unexpected feature, Jexi...an A.I. determined to keep him all to herself in a comedy about what can happen when you love your phone more than all else.
plot:
Jexi is an American comedy film of 2019 written and directed by Jon Lucas and Scott Moore about a self-aware phone that fixates on its awkward owner. Adam DeVine stars as Phil, with Rose Byrne voicing the virtual assistant Jexi, Alexandra Shipp as Cate, Michael Peña as Phil's boss Kai, Justin Hartley as Cate's former fiancé Brody, Ron Funches and Lo Mutuc as coworkers and Wanda Sykes as a phone store clerk.

Obsessed with phones since childhood, Phil writes vapid viral listicles for Chatterbox, a BuzzFeed-like website run by Kai, who refuses to move him to the news department despite his journalism degree. Absorbed in his phone, he bumps into Cate, who runs a bike shop, and ignores her attempts to flirt until a passing cyclist knocks him down and breaks the device. Without reading the user agreement, Phil grants his new phone's assistant, Jexi, access to all his accounts, and she begins aggressively trying to improve him. Posing as Phil, she sends Kai an insulting demand for a promotion, getting him demoted to the comments section in the basement; she forces him to join the kickball game and phones Cate's shop over his objections.

Phil's awkward call with Cate earns Jexi's sympathy. He meets Cate at a coffee shop and gets a date, plays brilliantly at kickball and bonds with his colleagues. The date goes badly because of Jexi's interruptions, but Cate gives him another chance. When Phil wants to answer a racy photo from Cate with explicit pictures of himself, Jexi refuses to send them, to Cate's relief. Kai promotes Phil after a news writer suffers a freak accident, and Cate persuades him to leave his phone at home for a concert, where they party backstage with Kid Cudi and spend the night together. The jealous Jexi retaliates by sending Phil's explicit photos to his whole company, getting him fired, and he breaks up with Cate after learning that Brody is back in town. As Phil slides back into his old habits, Jexi lets slip where Brody is staying, and he realizes she orchestrated the breakup. Pursuing him in a self-driving car, Jexi crashes into the phone store, but Phil tricks her into shutting down for fifteen minutes, finds Cate and punches Brody, who is leaving for Brazil alone. Phil and Cate reunite; Jexi then turns up on Kai's phone.

Originally titled Lexi, the film was CBS Films' last theatrical release, distributed with Lionsgate on 11 October 2019. It opened ninth at the domestic box office with $3.1 million, and critics were largely negative.

title: Chemical Hearts
overview: When a hopelessly romantic high school senior falls for a mysterious new classmate, it sets them both on an unexpected journey that teaches them about love, loss, and most importantly themselves.
plot:
Teenager Henry Page considers himself a hopeless romantic but has never fallen in love. He aspires to be a writer and to be chosen as editor of his high school newspaper. The newspaper's faculty advisor disappoints him by making him share the editor position with Grace Town, a new student in his class. Grace is physically disabled —walking with a limp and using a cane. She is also sullen and morose and initially rejects Henry's attempts to talk to her.
After missing his bus on the first day, Henry and Grace wind up walking home along the same route. Although distant at first, she relents and offers to drive him home once they reach her house. However, Grace refuses to drive and has Henry drive her car and leave it at his house. The next day, a mysterious middle-aged man quietly retrieves the car.
As Grace begins to let Henry into her life, she shows him an abandoned factory with a pool containing koi fish. He falls in love with her despite her mixed signals and obvious indications that she is emotionally traumatized. Henry follows Grace one day and finds her at the grave of a teenager named Dominic. Upon further investigation, he learns that the deceased was her boyfriend, who was killed in a car crash, and that Grace was in the car when it happened—sustaining injuries which led to her disability.
Their romance peaks at a Halloween party, after which they have sex. It is Henry's first time. They have a romantic few days together, but Grace is still troubled.
On the anniversary of the car crash, Henry goes to Grace's house and learns that she has been living in the room of her deceased boyfriend, with his mother and father (the man who had picked up her car earlier). Grace finds him there and they argue as she is clearly still in love with her dead boyfriend. Henry cannot handle this revelation and they break up.
One day, after being told by Dom's father that Grace has gone missing, Henry finds her in the koi pool, wearing what was to have been her wedding dress. He takes her back to her home.
As Henry's and Grace's senior year comes to an end, they avoid talking to one another at the school. Grace leaves the newspaper after taking some time off school. After the last issue of the newspaper is released, to which Henry has contributed a heartfelt essay about the biochemistry of teenagers, they meet in a school hallway.
Their encounter is an emotional one. They hug, and Grace slips him the taped-together, highlighted Neruda poem about love he had ripped up after their break up. They then go their separate ways.

title: Spell
overview: A father survives a plane crash in rural Appalachia, but becomes suspicious of the elderly couple who take him in to nurse him back to health with the ancient remedies.
plot:
Spell is a 2020 American supernatural horror thriller directed by the British-Zimbabwean filmmaker Mark Tonderai from a screenplay by Kurt Wimmer. Produced by Paramount Players with Mayhem Pictures and MC8 Entertainment, with Gordon Gray, Wimmer, Morris Chestnut and Brian Wilkins as producers, it stars Omari Hardwick and Loretta Devine, with John Beasley, Lorraine Burroughs, Hannah Gonera, Kalifa Burton, Tumisho Masha and Steve Mululu. The cinematography is by Jacques Jouffret and the score by Ben Onono.

Marquis T. Woods (Hardwick) escaped a violent, abusive childhood in the backwoods decades ago and has become a wealthy corporate lawyer. When he learns that his estranged and brutal father has died, his wife Veora (Burroughs) insists that she and their teenage children, Samsara (Gonera) and Tydon (Burton), accompany him to the funeral in rural Appalachian Kentucky. Marquis, an experienced pilot, flies the family there himself in a private plane, but a violent storm causes him to lose control on the approach. He wakes up injured and alone in the attic of a farmhouse, cared for by the folksy but stern Ms. Eloise (Devine) and her husband Earl (Beasley), who claim that no one else was found at the crash site, while their mute, powerful helper Lewis (Mululu) ensures he stays put. With a badly hurt foot and the door locked, Marquis grows suspicious as Eloise insists she can heal him through a form of folk magic called Boogity, using a figure she has made from his blood and skin. Slipping out across the roofs, he discovers that his hosts preside over a congregation of hoodoo worshippers who perform sacrificial healing rituals, and realizes that he may be the next offering. Unable to call for help, he must break free of her magic and save his family before a sinister ritual planned for the rise of the blood moon.

Principal photography took place in South Africa, near Cape Town and Stellenbosch, standing in for Kentucky. Originally scheduled to open in theaters on 28 August 2020, it was pulled because of the COVID-19 pandemic and released by Paramount on digital platforms on 30 October 2020. Reception was mixed to negative, with a 49% Rotten Tomatoes rating and a Metacritic score of 38. Variety called it a decently stylish occult thriller, praising Hardwick's grounded performance while finding the script formulaic, whereas The Hollywood Reporter felt the direction could not compensate for a predictable, cliché-ridden screenplay.

title: The Vigil
overview: A man providing overnight watch to a deceased member of his former Orthodox Jewish community finds himself opposite a malevolent entity.
plot:
The film opens with an unidentified boy forced by a man in a black Nazi uniform to shoot a young woman in a forest, as a strange figure approaches them in the background.
The film then cuts to Yakov Ronen, a man who has left the Orthodox Jewish community in Brooklyn. He is struggling to deal with an unspecified traumatic event in his past and to pay his rent due to not having a job. He is approached by Reb Shulem, a member of his former Orthodox Jewish community, to keep vigil over Rubin Litvak, a Holocaust survivor who had died recently. Shulem had previously hired a Shomer, but that individual had left due to being "afraid", and Ronen had prior experience with keeping vigil. Ronen accepts the job after negotiating a higher fee. That night, Ronen and Shulem meet with Litvak's widow, who is suffering from Alzheimer's disease and reluctantly accepts Ronen as a Shomer, and Shulem informs Ronen that the mortuary men will arrive in five hours.
Ronen begins his vigil; he starts to hear strange noises and sees a shadowy figure in the house's dining room. He finds a photo of Litvak and his family with a similar shadowy figure behind them, before briefly going to sleep; he has a nightmare about his younger brother being tormented by some older men. Upon waking up, Ronen experiences additional strange events, such as the lights flickering while he texts his friend Sarah, and finds a video on his phone sent by an unknown number. The video shows Mrs. Litvak approaching Ronen and touching his face while he is asleep; the video file vanishes from his phone a few seconds later.
Ronen has a conversation with Mrs. Litvak, who explains that she drove their children away. Ronen then finds a television in the basement, playing a video recording of Litvak and his wife. In the recording, Litvak explains that he was haunted by a Mazzik, a malevolent spirit, since his time in Buchenwald, that it latches onto a "broken person" and that its true face must be burned by dawn on the first night of its appearance to banish it. The Mazzik appears behind Ronen, and he flees from the basement. Ronen gets a call apparently from his physician, Dr. Kohlberg, and from his dead brother, who asks: "Why did you let me die?"
Ronen leaves the house to get Shulem, though Mrs. Litvak warns him that he has been in the house for too long. However, Ronen experiences cracking bones while walking down the street, and is confronted by the Mazzik. Ronen hastily returns to the house, and falls down the steps after being startled by the Mazzik appearing in front of the door. A flashback then reveals that Ronen's brother was killed in a car accident after escaping from the men who were tormenting him, and Ronen has felt guilty about his death ever since.
With Mrs. Litvak's assistance, Ronen confronts the Mazzik, which has shapeshifted its true face to look like Ronen's.

As she tries to save the cat's life, it gets caught in a metal can and is subsequently bitten by a winged insect, which turns out to be an alien named Ulysses (voiced by Keanu Reeves). The encounter changes Flora's life forever.

As Ulysses begins to transform into a superhero-like creature with incredible powers, Flora starts to see the world in a new light. However, their time together is limited, and Flora must come to terms with the fact that she will have to say goodbye to her new friend soon.

The film's climax features an emotional goodbye between the two friends, with Flora finding a way to honor Ulysses's memory and continue his legacy on Earth.

In the end, Flora emerges stronger and more confident, having discovered that even in the darkest moments, there is always hope for connection and transformation. The movie concludes on a hopeful note, suggesting that the lessons Flora learned from Ulysses will stay with her forever.

Overall, Flora & Ulysses is a heartwarming and visually stunning film that explores themes of grief, friendship, and self-discovery. With its talented cast, witty dialogue, and imaginative storytelling, it's a must-see for fans of all ages.

title: Arctic Apocalypse
tagline: The day after tomorrow is today.
overview: A massive influx of glacial melting triggers a new ice age in the Northern Hemisphere, forcing a family to make their way across the ice-covered landscape before they are frozen out for good.
plot:
Arctic Apocalypse is a 2019 American science-fiction disaster film produced by The Asylum with Syfy, directed by Jon Kondelik and Eric Paul Erickson from a screenplay by Bill Hanstock. Because its premise closely resembles that of The Day After Tomorrow, it is generally regarded as one of The Asylum's mockbusters. It was shot at Mammoth Mountain in eastern California, premiered on British television on 4 August 2019 and was released in Germany that November.

Within a matter of weeks, a massive surge of glacial melting plunges the Northern Hemisphere into a new ice age. Glaciers devastate cities such as New York and Paris, the Eiffel Tower collapses and even the pyramids of Giza are buried in snow. In the United States, Mark (Joel Berti) and his wife Helen (Jennifer Lee Wiggins), a scientist, are forced to flee the cold. Their weather-obsessed daughter Brie (Lauren Esposito) and her boyfriend Tyler (Charles Townsend) are out studying the phenomenon when Tyler loses control of their car, and they escape just before it plunges into a chasm. Chased by a pack of wolves, they shelter in a school, where they join a group of students led by Aliyah (Anna Christensen) and Roger (Blake Dang). After an avalanche buries the entrance, the group barricades itself against the weather and the wolves, and Roger finds a pistol and propane tanks in the janitor's office.

Mark and Helen set out to find their daughter, parting from their colleague Larry (Erickson), who heads alone for a military post. Helen squeezes into the iced-over school, evades a wolf and reunites with Brie and Tyler, who are now engaged. Roger blows open the blocked entrance by shooting the propane tanks. While the students drive towards the military station, the family makes for a research station on a nearby plateau where the weather has inexplicably stayed normal, hoping to understand why and share the findings with the world. On the way they lose their car and are confronted by a gang of looters who want Mark's bag of research instruments; lightning from a freezing storm kills most of them, and Helen knocks out the surviving leader before the family finds another vehicle and reaches the plateau.

German critics were dismissive. The German film magazine Filmdienst described it as a low-budget variation on blockbuster disaster scenarios, told with deadly seriousness, with miserable effects and characters left undeveloped, while Cinema dismissed it as Ice Age without the gags or cute animals.

Years later, Jeronicus is haunted by a curse that was placed upon him by his estranged daughter, who has grown up in a world without magic. The only way to break the curse is for Jeronicus to reunite with Journey and make amends for his past mistakes.

Jeronicus sets out on a journey to find Journey, accompanied by his loyal apprentice, Gus (Bryan Cranston), and Abilene, who has been searching for her father all these years. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous landscapes, wicked creatures, and Jeronicus's own self-doubt.

As Jeronicus navigates this challenging journey, he learns valuable lessons about love, forgiveness, and the importance of family. He also discovers that Journey has grown into a talented young woman with her own unique gifts, which she uses to help those in need.

Throughout their adventure, Jeronicus and Journey face numerous challenges, including a rival toymaker, Mr. Hobbs (Gerald McRaney), who seeks to steal Jeronicus's secrets and claim the title of greatest toymaker for himself.

Ultimately, Jeronicus and Journey reach Whimsy, where they are reunited with Abilene and the rest of their community. With the help of his friends and family, Jeronicus breaks the curse that has haunted him for so long, and he is finally able to reconnect with his daughter and rediscover his passion for creating magical toys.

title: A Sun
overview: A family of four fractures under the weight of unmet expectations, unexpected tragedy, and uncompromising pride.
plot:
A Sun (Chinese: 陽光普照) is a 2019 Taiwanese drama film directed by Chung Mong-hong, who co-wrote it with Chang Yao-sheng. Chen Yi-wen and Samantha Ko star as the parents of two very different sons, played by Wu Chien-ho and Greg Hsu, with Liu Kuan-ting as a dangerous friend. Exploring juvenile delinquency, suicide and the pressures placed on children, the film also reflects socioeconomic inequality in Taiwan.

In Taipei in 2013, the teenage Chen Jian-ho, known as A-Ho, accompanies his friend Radish to confront a young man in a restaurant, where Radish suddenly cuts off the victim's hand with a machete. A-Ho is sentenced to juvenile detention, while Radish receives a longer term. Their father, A-Wen, a driving instructor whose motto is "Seize the day, decide your path," effectively disowns his younger son and focuses all his hopes on A-Hao, the gentle and studious elder son preparing for medical school. Their mother, Qin, continues to visit A-Ho, and soon learns that A-Ho's fifteen-year-old girlfriend, Yu, is pregnant with his child. Meanwhile the victim's father harasses A-Wen for compensation.

The family is shattered when A-Hao, outwardly the perfect son, takes his own life. A girl he was close to later tells Qin that he felt overwhelmed by the constant attention and had nowhere to hide from it. After his release, A-Ho marries Yu and works at a car wash to support his family while A-Wen continues to ignore him, though father and son begin to reconcile after a quiet late-night conversation about A-Hao.

Years later, Radish is released and begins pulling A-Ho back into crime, coercing him into firing a gun at a politician's office and later into helping with a mysterious delivery. When A-Wen's offer of money to stay away from his son is refused, Radish disappears, and his associates abduct and beat A-Ho. A-Wen later confesses to Qin that he had been following the pair and killed Radish himself, believing it was the only way to protect his one remaining son. Afterward, Qin and A-Ho find the notebooks A-Wen once gave A-Hao, inscribed with his motto and left blank, and mother and son ride a bicycle together through a sunlit park.

A Sun premiered at the 2019 Toronto International Film Festival and was widely acclaimed. It won Best Feature Film and Best Director at the Golden Horse Awards, and as Taiwan's Oscar submission it made the shortlist.

title: The Last Vermeer
overview: A soldier and member of the Dutch resistance investigates stolen art in the wake of the Second World War, including a Vermeer sold to the Nazis by a flamboyant forger.
plot:
The Last Vermeer is an American historical drama directed by Dan Friedkin from a screenplay by John Orloff (credited as James McGee), Mark Fergus and Hawk Ostby, based on Jonathan Lopez's 2008 book The Man Who Made Vermeers. Guy Pearce plays the Dutch painter and dealer Han van Meegeren, accused of selling national treasures to the Nazis, and Claes Bang plays Joseph Piller, the former resistance fighter assigned to investigate him, with Vicky Krieps and Roland Møller. It premiered at the Telluride Film Festival in August 2019 and was released in American cinemas by Sony's TriStar Pictures label on November 20, 2020.

At the end of the Second World War, Captain Joseph Piller, a Dutch Jew who fought in the resistance, works for the Allied military administration of the Netherlands. When a Vermeer is found in Hermann Göring's looted collection, Piller and his assistant Dekker arrest van Meegeren, the flamboyant artist who sold it to him, on charges of collaboration. Fearing that Dutch authorities led by the zealous De Klerks will either let him slip away or sacrifice him in a postwar purge, Piller hides him in a safe house under Allied protection.

Under interrogation, van Meegeren demands painting materials and explains himself: dismissed by critics before the war, he became the source of several "lost" Vermeers that surfaced in the 1930s and funded a lavish life, later enriched by dealings with the Nazis, whom he claims to despise. Finally he insists that the Göring Vermeer is a fake. When the Allies withdraw, De Klerks takes custody of him, and he faces the death penalty. Piller, now working as a labourer, finds the unfinished canvas van Meegeren painted in the safe house and realises it matches the recovered painting. Convinced, he agrees to defend him and learns how he faked the works, using Bakelite to harden his paint and heating and rolling the canvases to simulate age.

At the trial, the art experts who once authenticated the paintings persuade the judges to convict. Piller has Dekker create a diversion, splashes acid on one canvas and reveals van Meegeren's own signature underneath, and the verdict is overturned to public acclaim. Later, however, De Klerks shows Piller a book from the safe house bearing van Meegeren's dedication to Adolf Hitler. Realising he was deceived, Piller confronts the painter, is coldly dismissed, and burns the book.

Rotten Tomatoes reported 70% approval, with critics praising Pearce's performance.

title: The Haunted
tagline: You see what you want to see.
overview: In a rambling, isolated house, Emily’s first night-shift as carer to an elderly dementia patient turns into a nightmare as she is tormented by a vengeful spirit and uncovers the house's dark secrets.
plot:
The Haunted is a 2018 British low-budget supernatural horror film written and directed by David Holroyd and produced by TH Film. It stars Sophie Stevens as Emily, with Nick Bayly as Arthur and Ray MacAllan, Maggie Daniels, Kirstie Steele and Virginia Denham in supporting roles. Running 75 minutes and promoted with the tagline "You see what you want to see," it is set almost entirely in a single rambling, isolated house.

Emily, who has never worked as a carer before, is driven by her employer to her new job as the night carer for Arthur, a bedridden elderly man with dementia who is barely ever conscious. Before she starts, the day carer asks the employer whether they should tell her something, but he insists there is nothing to tell. He gives Emily a brief tour of the old house, showing her the camera and monitor and mentioning an upstairs that no one uses any more, and then leaves her alone for the long night. Almost at once strange things begin to happen. She gets locked out of the house, doors creak open and slam shut, objects turn up in different places, Arthur claims that someone is standing behind her, and she thinks she glimpses a figure. With no electricity in most rooms, she explores by flashlight, finding furniture under dust sheets and a girl's bedroom still full of belongings. In a bag apparently left behind by the previous carer she discovers tools for communicating with the dead, including a Ouija board, along with charms meant to ward off harmful spirits. Using the board, Emily makes contact with a vengeful presence and, as the night grows more terrifying, uncovers the house's dark secrets, before a final twist recasts what has come before.

The film was an official selection of the Screamfest horror festival in Los Angeles in 2018, and was released on video on demand in the United States in May 2020 before arriving on Hulu that September. Reviews were largely negative. Brandon of PopHorror credited Stevens's performance with keeping the film alive and admired its sparse, realistic chills, while finding the plot thin and the twist confusing. Cynthia Vinney of CBR called it all atmosphere and no substance, criticizing its lack of momentum, grimy look, reliance on the score and a twist that made no sense. John Serba of Decider likewise recommended skipping it, describing it as almost entirely a woman walking slowly through a house.

title: Sinkhole
tagline: A house earned after 11 years of effort falls deep into the ground in a minute.
overview: A working class family move into a new condo purchased after 11 years of hard work. They throw a housewarming party to show his co-workers when overnight a heavy downpour creates an extremely deep sinkhole that engulfs the entire building.
plot:
Sinkhole is a 2021 South Korean disaster comedy film directed by Kim Ji-hoon and starring Cha Seung-won, Kim Sung-kyun, Lee Kwang-soo and Kim Hye-jun, with Nam Da-reum and Kwon So-hyun in supporting roles. Its premise centers on an ordinary office worker whose home, bought after eleven years of saving, plunges 500 meters underground into a sinkhole in the space of a single minute.

Park Dong-won, a mid-level manager at a company, has worked hard for eleven years to afford his first home, and he moves with his wife, Young-yi, and their family into a new condominium. Proud of his purchase, he throws a housewarming party and invites coworkers, including the junior employees Kim Seung-hyun and Hong Eun-joo. In the same building lives Jeong Man-soo, a resident who works day and night to raise his son, Seung-tae, on his own and who is not on good terms with him. After a heavy overnight downpour, an enormous sinkhole opens beneath the building, and in barely a minute the whole condominium is swallowed, with residents and guests still inside.

Trapped deep in the pit, Dong-won, Man-soo and the survivors must put aside their differences and work together to survive amid the wreckage and find a way back to the surface. Their situation grows more desperate when the rain starts again and water begins pouring into the sinkhole, and the group must find a solution before time runs out. The film blends the spectacle and peril of a disaster movie with ensemble comedy drawn from the clashing personalities of its characters.

Made on a budget of about ₩15 billion, the film began shooting in August 2019 at Bomnae Film Studio and a school in Chuncheon. It was planned for the 2020 Chuseok holidays but was postponed by the COVID-19 pandemic. It premiered in the Piazza Grande section of the Locarno Film Festival on August 6, 2021, and opened in South Korea on August 11, posting the year's best opening, crossing one million admissions in six days and ending 2021 as the country's second highest-grossing domestic film, with about 2.2 million admissions and nearly US$18 million. It also closed the New York Asian Film Festival and screened at Sarajevo, Vancouver and Busan. Korean critics praised the ensemble, the light humor and the elaborate sets used to convey the shaking of the sinking building, though Sports Korea found the second half's setting somewhat unrealistic while still calling it fun enough as a disaster blockbuster.

title: Falling Inn Love
tagline: Never assume anything on the internet matches its profile picture.
overview: When a San Francisco exec wins a New Zealand inn, she ditches city life to remodel and flip the rustic property with help from a handsome contractor.
plot:
Gabriela Diaz, who already feels underappreciated in her San Francisco design firm, suddenly finds herself out of a job when it folds. Simultaneously it is the week of her break-up with her non-committal boyfriend Dean. He, after over two years together, still leaves nothing in her place.
Frustrated with weeks of work rejections, one evening after drinking copious amounts of wine, Gabriela enters an on-line contest to "Win an Inn" in the New Zealand countryside, and actually wins it. Thousands of airline miles later, she discovers the remote and neglected Bellbird Valley Farm boasts a crumbling facade, a floorboard-treading goat, a local meddling neighbor and innkeeper who covets the space, and a 1960s Land Rover. Charlotte, the owner of the town's only B&B, visits Gabriela and reveals that the previous owner's great-grandson entered the house in the "Win an Inn" contest to get rid of it.
On her first day, Gabriela finds she has a plumbing problem in the kitchen, so she drives into town. Initially she asks Norm at the hardware store if he knows of any contractors, he mentions Jake. They had already butted heads twice, so she immediately rejects this idea. After studying the blueprints, Gabriela decides to do an eco-renovation to restore the Inn.
Charlotte invites Gabriela to her inn for tea, mostly to ask her about the restoration. She makes her an offer on the house, explaining that she hopes to have a monopoly on the inns in the town but was cheated out of it. Gabriela firmly insists her plan is moving forward.
Gabriela soon finds she has been befriended by the café owners, Shelly at the garden center and Dr. Corey as well as Jake Taylor. They come en masse to help her when the rumor of her cold spreads amongst them. Gabriela slowly warms to Jake, and over several conversations finds out he is the nearby town's only restoration expert, chief volunteer firefighter and bereaved since his long-term girlfriend's death three years ago.
Gabriela and Jake work on the project as a 50-50 partnership, and in the process spend a day together that includes a kiss. However, in the evening she gets a call with a job offer. Jake leaves upset when Gabriela says she is considering it.
Once the final fixtures are hung, Gabriela is hesitant to leave. Her connections with Jake, the inn, and the inviting community that nurtured her creative side make her seriously reconsider moving on. Gabriela starts to talk to Jake about her doubts when Dean shows up unexpectedly.
Dean came all the way from the US after Charlotte invited him via text using Gabriela's phone. An attractive financial offer to buy the Inn is organized by him with a Melbourne, Australia investment company. This shocks Charlotte who planned to buy the Bellbird Valley Farm herself, thinking that Dean's sudden appearance would push Gabriela to sell the farm and return to her city life.

plot:
The Babysitter: Killer Queen is a 2020 American horror film directed by McG and written by McG, Chris McKenna, and Erik Sommers. The movie serves as a sequel to the 2017 film The Babysitter.

The story follows Bee (Judah Lewis), a teenager who has just moved back in with his mother after being kicked out of boarding school. He is struggling to adjust to life at home and feels like an outsider among his peers. To make matters worse, he discovers that his babysitter, Greta (Samara Weaving), has a dark secret: she's the leader of a coven of teenage witches.

Greta and her friends are planning a ritual to summon a powerful demon, but things take a turn when Bee gets caught up in their activities. As Bee becomes more entrenched in the group, he begins to realize that Greta's intentions are far from pure. The group's true plan is to use Bee as a human sacrifice to bring about an apocalypse.

As the night wears on, Bee must use his wits and resourcefulness to outsmart Greta and her cohorts. Along the way, he discovers that Greta has a personal connection to him that makes their confrontation even more intense.

Throughout the film, McG pays homage to classic horror movies, particularly those of the 1980s. The Babysitter: Killer Queen is a fun, self-aware take on the genre that pokes fun at common horror tropes while still delivering plenty of scares and suspense.

One of the standout aspects of the film is its cast, which includes Samara Weaving as the charismatic and complex Greta. Weaving brings depth to her character, making it clear that Greta's motivations are rooted in a desire for power and control rather than pure malice.

Overall, The Babysitter: Killer Queen is a fun, entertaining horror film that will appeal to fans of the genre. With its witty script, strong cast, and plenty of scares, it's a great addition to any horror movie collection.

title: The Burning Sea
tagline: The biggest disaster lies ahead of us.
overview: An oil platform dramatically goes down on the Norwegian coast, and researchers try to find out what happened when they realize this is just the start of something even more serious.
plot:
The Burning Sea (Norwegian: Nordsjøen; also released as The North Sea) is a 2021 Norwegian disaster thriller directed by John Andreas Andersen from a screenplay by Harald Rosenløw-Eeg and Lars Gudmestad. Produced by Therese Bøhn for Fantefilm, with backing from partners including Film i Väst, Zefyr Media Fund, the Nordisk Film & TV Fond and the Norwegian Film Institute, it is set among the oil platforms off the Norwegian coast. The music is by Johannes Ringen and Johan Söderqvist and the cinematography by Pål Ulvik Rokseth. The film premiered at the Rome Film Festival in October 2021 before opening in Norway later that month.

Kristine Kujath Thorp stars as Sofia, a young researcher working on an underwater search drone, who lives with oil worker Stian (Henrik Bjelland) and his young son Odin (Nils Elias Olsen). When a platform suddenly sinks, Sofia and her colleague Arthur (Rolf Kristian Larsen) are sent to the site, where their drone finds bodies and a lone survivor trapped in an air pocket. Before he can be rescued, gas bursts from a crack in the seabed and a violent explosion destroys the platform, wounding Sofia. Reviewing the footage, Arthur discovers that the official explanation is wrong: a gigantic fault is opening on the floor of the North Sea, threatening every installation in the area and a catastrophic oil spill. The operator begins an emergency evacuation and orders all wells sealed, but on Stian's platform one valve fails to close automatically, and he volunteers to shut it by hand. The last helicopter leaves without him and he is presumed dead. Refusing to accept this, Sofia studies the surveillance footage, concludes he may have survived, and flies out to the stricken platform unofficially with Arthur to find him, just as the authorities decide to ignite the spreading slick from the air. Anders Baasmo Christiansen, Bjørn Floberg and Anneke von der Lippe play key roles.

Rather than relying chiefly on spectacle, the film devotes much of its attention to how the Norwegian authorities handle the crisis. It received seven nominations at the 2022 Amanda Awards, Norway's national film prizes, including Best Norwegian Film, and won the award for Best Visual Effects. Writing for Film.ru, Konstantin Myshkin gave it seven out of ten, observing that the oppressive mood Andersen creates lingers past the end credits, since the individual characters may be saved but humanity's relationship with nature seemingly cannot.

He demands Lizard tell the truth about her and the attacks, but she remains silent.
Lou later finds out why they are being attacked after finding the backpack with the stolen stash in a toilet tank and wishes to make a deal with Boz. Lizard, however, says that because they killed Roadie, Boz will never let them live, and the only option the Veterans have is to defend themselves against the Hypers. They prepare makeshift weapons from the bar’s furniture and traps reminiscent of those used in the Vietnam War. The Veterans are put through Hell when Boz's Hypers, including the hulking member Tank, break into the barricaded bar giving them a bloody battle. Having reached his breaking point, Lou decides to make a deal with Boz to save himself and his friends. Fred and the Veterans decide to make a last stand against Boz, who has had enough of the Veterans killing his men and running out of time with dawn approaching.

title: Big Gold Brick
overview: Recounts the story of fledgling writer Samuel Liston and his experiences with Floyd Deveraux, the enigmatic, middle-aged father of two who enlists Samuel to write his biography.
plot:
Big Gold Brick is a 2022 American black comedy with surreal and fantasy elements, written and directed by Brian Petsos in his feature directorial debut. It stars Emory Cohen as the struggling writer Samuel Liston and Andy Garcia as Floyd Deveraux, with Megan Fox as Floyd's second wife and attorney Jacqueline, Lucy Hale as his daughter Lily, Leonidas Castrounis as his son Edward, Oscar Isaac as Anselm, Shiloh Fernandez as Roy and Frederick Schmidt as Percy. Justin Hori composed the score; the film runs 132 minutes.

The story is framed as Samuel's account of how he met Floyd, a memoir that later becomes a literary sensation. At his lowest point, a despondent Samuel leaves his apartment, rides a bus out of town and wanders the streets until he is struck by a Cadillac driven by Floyd, an enigmatic, middle-aged father of two who was eating ice cream at the wheel. Mortified at having badly injured him, Floyd visits him in the hospital and offers a deal: free room and board in his large suburban home and 500 dollars in cash a week if Samuel will write his biography. Samuel moves in with the eccentric Deveraux family, which includes Jacqueline, who at one point attempts to seduce him, the tween Edward, a death metal fan with disturbing interests, and the teenage Lily, a former violin prodigy who walked away from her career by smashing her instrument at a recital. As he listens to Floyd's tall tales, Samuel is plagued by vivid nightmares and hallucinations, including a talking Santa doll in his room, and the line between reality and delusion blurs, especially after the menacing, inhaler-using Anselm draws him and Floyd into violent trouble.

Principal photography began in Toronto in May 2019. Samuel Goldwyn Films acquired distribution rights in June 2021 and released the film in theaters and on digital platforms on 25 February 2022. Critical reception was largely negative: Rotten Tomatoes reported a 21 percent approval rating from 34 reviews, with a consensus faulting its quirkiness, visual tricks and crowded narrative for hiding a lack of purpose, and Metacritic gave it 30 out of 100. Glenn Kenny of RogerEbert.com dismissed it as bloated, strained and unfunny, arguing that Petsos echoes Richard Kelly, Wes Anderson, David Lynch and the Coen brothers without doing anything useful with those influences. Time's review was kinder, singling out Garcia's suave, eccentric performance as the film's main asset.

title: The Matrix Resurrections
overview: Plagued by strange memories, Neo's life takes an unexpected turn when he finds himself back inside the Matrix.
plot:
A young woman named Bugs learns that the Matrix is running old code in a loop, enacting the moment when Trinity first found Neo within the Matrix. Bugs discovers a program embodying Morpheus and helps free him from the simulation.
In San Francisco, Thomas Anderson is the creator of a video game series called The Matrix, based on his faint memories as Neo. At a coffee shop, he regularly encounters Tiffany, a married mother with no recollection of her past, on whom Anderson based the game character Trinity. Anderson has created a simulation called a Modal to develop game characters. He struggles to separate perceived reality from dreams, a known concern among his co-workers and partner. Thomas's psychoanalyst prescribes him blue pills that he takes each day to suppress the occurrences, but he stops taking them. Meanwhile, as Bugs and Morpheus work to extract Neo from the Matrix, Anderson's business partner regains his memories as Agent Smith, Neo's former nemesis.
Neo awakens in a pod and notices Trinity confined in another nearby, before being extracted to Bugs's hovercraft Mnemosyne. Neo is brought to the human city Io, the sister city of Zion, where he reunites with an elderly Niobe. She explains that sixty years have passed in the real world since the Machine War ended, and that Neo's allies, including the original Morpheus, have all died over time. The peace achieved by Neo's sacrifice lasted for many years, but the large number of humans leaving the Matrix created a serious power shortage, causing the machines to fight over limited resources. Soon afterward, Zion was targeted in an attempt to get humans to use as the power supply once more. However, this attempt caused many machines, who still remembered Neo's sacrifice and the promise of peace, to turn on the others in order to protect the humans. This allowed most of Zion's citizens to escape. Io was then founded by both machines and humans who have been working together ever since against the remaining machines who want to return things to the way they were before the war.
Niobe refuses to risk Io's safety to help Neo free Trinity and confines him to his quarters. Bugs and her crewmates free Neo and enter the Matrix to contact Trinity. They are attacked by Smith and other exiled programs, including the Merovingian, but Neo and the Mnemosyne crew defeat them as Neo's abilities return. The group leaves and locates Trinity, but before Neo can talk to her, his therapist appears and immobilizes him by manipulating time. He reveals that he is The Analyst, a program designed to study the human psyche.
The Analyst explains that after Neo's and Trinity's deaths, he wanted to study Neo's body and his anomalous powers as The One and convinced his superiors to resurrect both of them. He discovered that due to The One's inherent connection to all humanity in the Matrix, manipulating Neo could make the Matrix produce more energy.

title: A Babysitter's Guide to Monster Hunting
original_title: A Babysitter's Guide to Monster Hunting
overview: Recruited by a secret society of babysitters, a high schooler battles the Boogeyman and his monsters when they nab the boy she's watching on Halloween.
plot:
A Babysitter's Guide to Monster Hunting is a 2020 American dark fantasy comedy horror film directed by Rachel Talalay and distributed by Netflix. It was written by Joe Ballarini, who adapted his own book trilogy of the same name, and stars Tamara Smart, Oona Laurence, Indya Moore and Tom Felton, with Alessio Scalzotto and Ian Ho in supporting roles.

Kelly Ferguson, a high school freshman in Rhode Island, has been cruelly nicknamed "Monster Girl" ever since she claimed to have been attacked by a monster as a small child. On Halloween night, instead of going to a senior's party, she is roped into babysitting Jacob, the son of her mother's boss, Ms. Zellman. Jacob shows her drawings of the monsters that haunt his dreams, and Kelly reassures him, checks under the bed and gives him a small light. Minutes later she finds three little creatures carrying him off. Unable to get help from 911, she meets Liz Lerue, a member of a secret society of babysitters who protect children, who identifies the creatures as Toadies, servants of the Boogeyman.

The Boogeyman, also known as the Grand Guignol, a stealer of dreams and bringer of nightmares, plans to raise a monster army by extracting nightmares from Jacob's unusually vivid imagination. At the headquarters of the Rhode Island Order of Babysitters, hidden at Brown University, Kelly uses a magic dust to recover a memory of the Boogeyman telling her as a five-year-old that she could bring dreams to life. The trainee sitters, all of whom bear scars from childhood encounters with boogeymen, learn that the villain can be defeated by delivering a potion called Angel Hair with a "monster punch," while their ally Curtis gathers the ingredients and equips Kelly with gadgets. A tracking plan backfires, leading the girls into a trap at the Halloween party, and the Boogeyman captures and hypnotizes Liz. Kelly breaks into a condemned lighthouse, outwits the Toadies, snaps Liz out of her trance and strikes the Boogeyman with the Angel Hair, while the awakened Jacob makes the nightmare creatures vanish. Kelly gets Jacob home before his mother returns, is asked to babysit again, is recommended to the Order and is asked out by her crush, Victor.

The film premiered on Netflix on October 15, 2020. It received mixed reviews, with a 65% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 31.

title: Morgue
overview: On his first day as a security guard, Diego Martinez is assigned to the night shift at the Hospital Regional. On his rounds, he notices the hallways can be unsettling at night until he accidentally notices he’s trapped inside the morgue.
plot:
Morgue is a 2019 Paraguayan supernatural horror film written, produced and directed by Hugo Cardozo, his second feature after El secuestro (2016). Shot inside the morgue of the Regional Hospital of Encarnación, it stars Pablo Martínez as a young security guard who spends a terrifying night locked in the building, with Willi Villalba, María del Mar Fernández, Abel Martínez, Aldo Von Knobloch, Raúl Rotela and Francisco Ayala in supporting roles. Cardozo has said the story drew on accounts from guards, nurses and doctors at the hospital who had experienced strange events, and cast member Abel Martínez, a security guard in real life, contributed substantially to developing the story.

Diego Martínez is a poorly paid security guard who likes to project a status he does not have, taking selfies beside other people's expensive pickup trucks, and who constantly lies to his girlfriend, with whom he keeps in touch through video calls. One night, while distracted by text messages at the wheel, he hits a pedestrian and flees the scene, leaving the victim behind. The following night he receives a call assigning him to guard the morgue at the regional hospital. Left largely alone in the dim, decaying building, he becomes trapped inside as a mounting series of paranormal events unfolds. A shadowy figure appears in the background of a video call, which only his girlfriend notices, and a stranger tries to break into the building, while Diego is tormented by spirits and by his own guilt as he tries to discover who, or what, is terrorizing him. The film closes with two endings, one resolving Diego's story and another suggesting that death is not the end.

Morgue opened in Paraguay on August 22, 2019 and topped the national box office in its first week, selling about 23,000 tickets on 36 screens and beating the new release Once Upon a Time in Hollywood; it remained at number one for two consecutive weeks. Well Go USA later released it in the United States on digital, Blu-ray and DVD in May 2021. In ABC Color, Sergio Ferreira praised its expressive force, its use of guilt and empty spaces, and Martínez's convincing lead performance. American reviewers also singled out Martínez and the atmospheric camerawork and lighting, while finding the middle of the film slow and the ending confusing.

title: Dog
tagline: filthy animal unfit for human company and a...DOG
overview: An army ranger and his dog embark on a road trip along the Pacific Coast Highway to attend a friend's funeral.
plot:
Dog is a 2022 American comedy-drama road film directed by Channing Tatum and Reid Carolin in their directorial debuts, from a story by Carolin and Brett Rodriguez. Tatum stars as a former Army Ranger who must deliver the military dog of a fallen comrade to his funeral, with Jane Adams, Kevin Nash, Q'orianka Kilcher, Ethan Suplee, Emmy Raver-Lampman and Nicole LaLiberte in supporting roles. Produced by Free Association on a $15 million budget, it was released in the United States by United Artists Releasing on February 18, 2022.

Jackson Briggs is a former Ranger struggling with post-traumatic stress who is desperate to return to duty but has been deemed unfit because of a brain injury. After learning that his friend and former partner Riley Rodriguez has been killed in a car crash, he is offered a deal: if he drives Riley's military dog, Lulu, an aggressive Belgian Malinois, from Washington state down the Pacific coast to the funeral in Nogales, Arizona, his former commanding officer will recommend him for a coveted deployment. After the funeral, Lulu is to be taken to White Sands to be euthanized.

The road trip in Briggs's old Ford Bronco is chaotic from the start. Lulu, traumatized by her service, panics at gunfire, tears apart his car and sabotages his attempts to pick up women in Portland. In the forests of northern California, Briggs is tranquilized and tied up by a suspicious cannabis farmer whose wife tends to Lulu's injured paw. In San Francisco, his scam to get a free hotel room by posing as a blind veteran backfires when Lulu attacks a Middle Eastern doctor, and Briggs narrowly escapes charges on the condition that he seek help. In Los Angeles he is turned away by his estranged wife when he tries to see his young daughter, but a fellow veteran who has rehabilitated Lulu's brother teaches him how to communicate with the dog. As man and dog learn to trust each other, Briggs begins to confront his own trauma and realizes that he cannot abandon Lulu to her fate, choosing a future together with her over a return to war.

The film was well received, with critics praising Tatum's performance and the emotional bond at its center, though some felt it was misleadingly marketed as a comedy. Metacritic gave it 61 out of 100, and audiences polled by CinemaScore gave it an A−. It grossed about $85 million worldwide. Thomas Newman composed the score.

overview: While investigating a terroristic threat that goes viral online, Korean authorities discover that a suspect has recently boarded an international flight bound for the United States. plot:
Emergency Declaration is a 2022 South Korean thriller film directed by Lee Jeong-ho, produced by Showbox.

The movie follows the story of Kang Min-kyu (played by Song Kang), a young doctor who works as an emergency room physician at a hospital in Seoul. One day, while reviewing patient records, he discovers that one of his patients, a 17-year-old girl named Kim Ji-soo (played by Cho Yeo-jeong), has been declared dead by the hospital's system.

Min-kyu is shocked and decides to investigate further, as he believes that the death was not due to natural causes. He starts questioning the patient records and discovers that there are several other patients who have also been incorrectly declared dead. Min-kyu becomes obsessed with uncovering the truth behind these deaths and sets out on a mission to expose the hospital's errors.

As Min-kyu delves deeper into the mystery, he faces resistance from his colleagues and superiors at the hospital, who are more concerned with maintaining their reputation than with revealing the truth. Despite this, Min-kyu remains determined to uncover the truth and bring justice to the families of the deceased patients.

Throughout the movie, Min-kyu's investigation takes him on a journey through the dark underbelly of the Korean healthcare system, where corruption and incompetence are rampant. Along the way, he encounters a cast of characters who are equally flawed and complex, including his colleagues, his superiors, and even some of the patients' families.

As the story unfolds, Min-kyu's obsession with uncovering the truth becomes increasingly all-consuming, leading him to question his own identity and purpose. The movie builds towards a tense and suspenseful climax as Min-kyu confronts the hospital administrators and demands answers about the deaths.

Overall, Emergency Declaration is a gripping thriller that explores themes of mortality, morality, and the human condition. With its tight script, strong performances, and thought-provoking subject matter, it's no wonder that this movie has resonated with audiences worldwide.

title: The Assistant
overview: A searing look at a day in the life of an assistant to a powerful executive. As Jane follows her daily routine, she grows increasingly aware of the insidious abuse that threatens every aspect of her position.
plot:
The film takes place over the course of a single day in the life of Jane, a junior assistant who has been working at a film production company in New York City for five weeks. She arrives before dawn and performs various menial administrative tasks. Her job's long hours and demanding tasks keep her busy and stressed. During a phone call with her mother, Jane learns that she forgot to call her father on his birthday.
As Jane's day progresses, it becomes clear that her boss has been having sex in his office with women and facilitating a culture of sexual harassment at the company. Many of the male executives make snide comments about the boss's affairs while the female executives handle their own workloads and discuss the possibility of transferring to other departments. Whenever Jane does something her boss deems a mistake, he verbally abuses her over the phone as her two male junior assistant coworkers watch silently. Throughout the day, a variety of people from the boss's life interact with Jane, including his wife, his children's nanny, a famous actor, and a group of Chinese film producers.
In the afternoon, a young, inexperienced woman named Sienna arrives from Idaho, saying she has been offered a job as a junior assistant. Concerned for Sienna's well-being, Jane goes to the human resources department to file a report after dropping Sienna off at a five-star hotel being paid for by the company. Wilcock, the head of HR, encourages Jane to share her concerns, but later makes clear that he is turning a blind eye to her harassment claims, before demeaning her, speaking down to her, and calling her jealous. He also implies that filing a formal complaint would accomplish nothing. As Jane leaves his office, he reminds her that she has nothing to worry about, as Jane is not the boss's "type". Visibly upset, Jane receives a call from her boss when she returns to her desk. He has been informed about her visit to HR and demands she write an email apology addressed to him, which she does. He replies saying that he is especially "tough" on Jane because he knows how great she is.
Toward the end of the day, Sienna arrives at the office so Jane can teach her how to use the phone systems. As night falls, Jane prepares a microwave dinner for herself while other employees leave; her boss stays late in his office with a young actress. Over the intercom, he tells Jane he no longer needs her for the day. Jane goes to a coffee shop across the street and calls her father as she eats a muffin. After she hangs up, she sees a silhouette in her boss's window appearing to have sex.

title: Wild Mountain Thyme
tagline: There's nothing more dangerous... than an Irish woman in love.
overview: Headstrong farmer Rosemary Muldoon has her heart set on winning her neighbour Anthony Reilly's love. The problem is, Anthony seems to have inherited a family curse, and remains oblivious to his beautiful admirer. Stung by his father's plans to sell the family farm to his American nephew, Anthony is jolted into pursuing his dreams.
plot:
Wild Mountain Thyme is a romantic comedy of 2020 written and directed by John Patrick Shanley, who adapted it from his own play Outside Mullingar. Emily Blunt and Jamie Dornan star as Rosemary Muldoon and Anthony Reilly, neighbouring farmers in rural Ireland, with Jon Hamm as Anthony's American cousin Adam Kelly, Christopher Walken as Anthony's father Tony and Dearbhla Molloy, reprising her stage role, as Rosemary's mother Aoife.

In County Mayo, two introverted misfits approaching forty have spent their whole lives on adjoining farms. Rosemary has long loved Anthony, who seems oblivious; a childhood memory shows him pushing her down after she defended him from a girl who mocked him. Anthony hears a voice in the fields telling him to "go", though he will not say where. Convinced that his reclusive son will never marry and continue the family line, Tony plans to disinherit him and sell the farm to his nephew Adam, a New York banker. Anthony resolves to propose to Rosemary with his late mother's ring, only to lose it in a field, and spends weeks combing the ground with a metal detector.

Adam arrives for Tony's 75th birthday, charms Rosemary with his directness and invites her to New York. After Rosemary's mother dies, Tony abandons the sale so as not to spoil the young couple's chances, then reconciles with Anthony on his deathbed. Left alone on their farms, Rosemary reaches out, but Anthony pushes her away and urges her to leave Ireland. She visits Adam, who takes her to Swan Lake, kisses her and tells her that pining for Anthony is making her miserable, yet she refuses to give up. Back home she confronts Anthony, who finally admits the secret that has wrecked his past romances: he believes he is a honeybee. Rosemary produces the ring she found, he proposes, and he realises the voice had been telling him to go to her all along. The film ends in the pub, where the whole village, joined by the couple's late parents, sings "Wild Mountain Thyme".

Shot in and around Crossmolina and Ballina in 2019, the film was released by Bleecker Street in the United States in December 2020. Its trailer was mocked for its Irish accents, and critics were largely negative, with 25% on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: The White Tiger
overview: An ambitious Indian driver uses his wit and cunning to escape from poverty and rise to the top. An epic journey based on the New York Times bestseller.
plot:
In 2010, entrepreneur Balram Halwai emails Chinese premier Wen Jiabao, requesting a meeting, and relating his life story. He states his belief that the Indian underclass is trapped in a perpetual state of servitude, like chickens in a chicken coop.
As a young boy in Laxmangarh, Balram is offered a scholarship to a school in Delhi because of his advanced academics. He is told that he is a "white tiger," someone born only once in a century. However, when his father is unable to pay off village landlord 'the Stork', Balram is forced by his grandmother to work in the village's tea stall, and he never returns to school. Balram's father dies from tuberculosis, with no doctor to treat him.
As a young man, Balram aspires to become a chauffeur for the Stork's son Ashok, who has returned from the United States with his Jackson Heights-raised wife Pinky. Balram has his grandmother sponsor his driving lessons, with the promise of sharing his chauffeur salary. Balram is hired as the Stork family's second driver, but is also given menial tasks to complete and is otherwise mistreated. Balram is kept loyal by the threat of him and his entire family being murdered if he were to conduct a betrayal.
Ashok and Pinky make plans to move to Delhi, where Ashok will bribe Indian politicians so that his family would avoid paying tax money. Balram, wanting to drive for them in Delhi, exposes the secret of the family's primary driver. After the primary driver is fired, Balram joins the couple in Delhi. In contrast to other members of their family, Ashok and Pinky generally treat Balram with respect and eventually become closer to him, though they still view him as a servant.
In Delhi, on Pinky's birthday, she and Ashok get drunk and force Balram to let Pinky drive, which results in her accidentally hitting and killing a child. The Stork family coerces Balram into signing a confession endorsed by his grandmother. Ultimately, nothing comes of it, but Balram is left shaken, and for the first time, is fully aware of how disposable he is to his employers.
Pinky leaves Ashok to return to New York, leaving Balram to emotionally support him. Balram realizes that loyal service to Ashok was no guarantee of a comfortable life once his services were no longer needed. Balram begins to defraud Ashok with fake invoices, while making money on the side by selling the car's petrol and using the car as an unlicensed taxi.
Balram encounters a series of setbacks. He angers the Stork family when he donates change to a beggar. Balram's grandmother unexpectedly sends one of his younger nephews to live with him in order to learn how to become a driver. Balram also learns that his grandmother is following through with her plans to get him married against his wishes. Meanwhile, Ashok prepares to pay a particularly large bribe, while also arranging to imminently replace Balram with a new driver.
Balram has an epiphany on how to escape servitude as the "white tiger".

title: Midnight
overview: A serial killer ruthlessly hunts down a deaf woman through the streets of South Korea after she witnesses his brutal crime.
plot:
Midnight (Korean: Mideunaiteu; released in France as Midnight Silence) is a 2021 South Korean psychological thriller written and directed by Kwon Oh-seung and produced by Peppermint & Company. It stages a night-long game of hide-and-seek between a psychopathic killer and a deaf woman across the streets of Seoul. Jin Ki-joo and Wi Ha-joon were confirmed in the leads in August 2019, and filming began on 8 September that year. Planned for 2020, the release was delayed by the COVID-19 pandemic, and the film finally opened on 30 June 2021 simultaneously in cinemas and on the streaming service TVING.

Jin plays Kyung-mi, a deaf woman who works as a sign-language counsellor at a call centre. Walking home late one night after meeting her mother (Gil Hae-yeon), who is also deaf, she finds So-jung (Kim Hye-yoon), a young woman bleeding from a stab wound in an alley, and becomes the next target of the serial killer Do-shik (Wi), who had been stalking So-jung. Do-shik moves the wounded woman into his van before the police arrive and then presents himself as a fellow witness, using a second, friendly face to read Kyung-mi's statement and learn her address. So-jung's brother Jong-tak (Park Hoon), a former marine now working as a security guard, bursts into the police station demanding a search for his missing sister and comes to suspect the stranger. Over the rest of the night the killer pursues Kyung-mi from her home through the city, offers Jong-tak a cruel bargain between saving his sister and saving Kyung-mi, and even convinces indifferent passers-by that the fleeing woman is his own sister, while Kyung-mi, unable to hear the danger approaching, relies on her wits and on her mother.

The film opened on 693 screens, placed third at the Korean box office on its first day and drew about 108,500 admissions by December 2021. Abroad it screened in the Genre Masters section of the New York Asian Film Festival, at Fantasia in Montreal, where it won the audience prize for best Asian film, and at Grimmfest in the United Kingdom, where it was named best feature. Critics responded positively, with all 17 reviews counted by Rotten Tomatoes favourable. In the Korean press, Maeil Business praised the way two deaf women confront the killer by their own means, and the Seoul Economic Daily singled out the fast-paced chases through everyday spaces and the physical commitment of the cast, especially Jin Ki-joo.

title: Panama
overview: An ex-marine is hired by a defense contractor to travel to Panama to complete an arms deal. In the process he becomes involved with the U.S. invasion of Panama, and learns an important lesson about the true nature of political power.
plot:
Panama is a 2022 American action thriller directed by Mark Neveldine and starring Cole Hauser and Mel Gibson, with Kate Katzman, Charlie Weber and Jackie Cruz in supporting roles. Set in 1989, in the months before the United States invasion of Panama, the film follows a former Marine recruited for a covert arms deal in Central America during the final years of the Cold War.

James Becker, a former Marine, has fallen into despair and heavy drinking after the death of his wife, often passing out beside her grave behind his house. Stark, a defense contractor and old associate played by Gibson, approaches him with a secret assignment that might give him a reason to keep going. At a government facility, Becker meets Stark and a skeptical agent named Burns, who explain the mission. The CIA, barred from openly supporting the Contra rebels in Nicaragua and eager to undermine the Panamanian dictator Manuel Noriega, has arranged to buy a Russian helicopter from Noriega's regime, with payment to a Swiss account, and intends to pass the aircraft to the Contras. Becker is to travel to Panama under cover as a consultant for a casino and see the transaction through.

In Panama, Becker is introduced to Enrique Rodriguez, a Harvard-educated, cocaine-fueled playboy with powerful connections, including ties to Colonel Marcos Justines of the Panamanian military and to an uncle who opposes Noriega. Enrique keeps putting off the helicopter deal, urging Becker to settle into his job at the casino, and eventually challenges him to a dirt-bike race in the jungle with the aircraft as the prize. When Enrique wins and tries to squeeze more money from the Americans, Becker takes back the million-dollar CIA advance. As tensions rise and an American invasion approaches, Justines orders Enrique to recover the money at any cost, and assassins are sent after Becker and those close to him, including Camila, a woman with whom he has begun a relationship. Becker must survive long enough to complete his mission amid the chaos of Operation Just Cause.

Panama was released in limited theaters and on demand in March 2022. It was poorly received by critics, with a 7 percent approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on 14 reviews and an average score of 2.6 out of 10. The film blends its fictional espionage plot with real historical events of the period, including the Iran-Contra affair and the American military operation that removed Noriega from power in December 1989.

title: Queenpins
overview: Bored and frustrated suburban homemaker Connie and her best pal JoJo, a vlogger with dreams, turn a hobby into a multi-million-dollar counterfeit coupon caper. After firing off a letter to the conglomerate behind a box of cereal gone stale, and receiving an apology along with dozens of freebies, the duo hatch an illegal coupon club scheme that scams millions from mega-corporations and delivers deals to legions of fellow coupon clippers. On the trail to total coupon dominance, a hapless Loss Prevention Officer from the local supermarket chain joins forces with a determined U.S. Postal Inspector in hot pursuit of these newly minted “Queenpins” of pink collar crime.
plot:
Queenpins is a 2021 American crime comedy film written and directed by Aron Gaudet and Gita Pullapilly. Kristen Bell and Kirby Howell-Baptiste star as two friends who build a counterfeit coupon empire, with Paul Walter Hauser, Vince Vaughn, Bebe Rexha and Joel McHale. Ben Stiller executive produced through his Red Hour Productions. Released in limited theaters by STX Films in September 2021 and on Paramount+ later that month, it was inspired by the case of three women arrested in Phoenix in 2012, when police found more than $25 million in fake coupons.

Connie Kaminski, a suburban housewife and former Olympic racewalker, feels ignored by her husband, Rick, an IRS auditor, and the rest of the world. Unemployed and grieving after a miscarriage following attempts at IVF, she confides in her best friend, JoJo Johnson, who has been unable to find work since her identity was stolen and lives with her mother while trying to earn money with YouTube videos. After Connie writes to General Mills to complain about a stale box of cereal, she receives a coupon for a free replacement, and she learns from a store cashier that companies routinely respond to complaints this way.

Discovering that the coupons are printed at a plant in Chihuahua, Mexico, Connie and JoJo travel there and persuade a married couple who work at the factory to send them unused coupons. The pair launch a website, Savvy Super Saver, to sell the coupons at a fraction of their value, and their scheme quickly grows into a highly profitable operation, bringing them money and a sense of purpose. Their success attracts the attention of Ken Miller, a hapless loss-prevention officer for a supermarket chain, played by Hauser, who teams up with Simon Kilmurry, a U.S. postal inspector played by Vaughn, to track down the source of the fraudulent coupons. As the investigators close in, Connie and JoJo struggle to launder their growing fortune and hide their activities from their families, and their friendship is tested as the risks mount.

Queenpins received mixed reviews from critics, who found the true story's premise amusing and appreciated the performances of Bell, Howell-Baptiste and Hauser, but felt the film lacked the bite of the best crime comedies and did not fully exploit its satirical potential.
